devices.note: No community firmware mod found yet (2026-10-31). Generic tooling covers it: elektron-firmware-tool (firmware container), Elektroid (sample/SysEx manager) and Overwitch (Overbridge audio on Linux) list Analog Heat MKI/MKII/+FX. screendump names it as 'not implemented'. Neither the Lapin list nor altstrument.org has a firmware entry for it. Last official OS we saw on elektron.se: Analog Heat MKI/MKII OS 1.22 (2024-10-16); the +FX has its own OS (release notes last updated 2024-10-16) and MKII firmware is not interchangeable with +FX.

projects.version: v0.11.0 (tag 2026-11-17): ships DT1 core 4.4, DN1 5.4, DT2 1.0, DN2 0.4 (experimental), AR2 0.13, A4 core-a4mk2 0.9, OT 0.42, MC 0.3, MS 0.1. On main at the tag: drive-loader-ar2 0.6 and the new drive-loader-a4mk2 0.1. Before: v0.10.0 (tag 2026-11-09): ships each device's newest core (DT1 4.1, DN1 5.2.1, DT2 1.0, DN2 0.3, AR2 0.11, A4 0.5, OT 0.8, MC 0.3, MS 0.1). main since: DT1 core 4.2/4.3 and DN1 5.3 (live-note and MIDI CC events), core-dn2 0.4 (MIDI CC event, DSP post words), core-ar2 0.12 (spare table entries for +Drive mods), SDK mono machines and MIDI CCs, DT2 sharc_raw (raw section-7 loads and relocatable DSP objects); 2026-11-11 the Analog Rytm MKII Drive Loader (drive-loader-ar2 0.4: mods linked from the +Drive at boot, a MODS page, the web page's +Drive view over Web MIDI) and core-a4 renamed core-a4mk2; 2026-11-13 (main): Analog Rytm MKI 1.74 (ELE2 files, experimental, whole builds only, no core yet), core-ot 0.40 (Octatrack events and tables 0.9-0.40) and seqrows-ot 0.1; 2026-11-15 (main): DT1 core 4.4 (exports the AMP envelope as fw_amp_level and names the old fw_amp_env fw_filter_env), core-a4mk2 0.7 with the std1 standard-event ABI, and six Analog Four MKII check mods (frame, modset, std, std-midi, ui, voice); 2026-11-15 (main): core-dn1 5.4 for the TELOS +Drive loader (core_param_install, core_stock_info, core_tasks; no new patch site) and build descriptor ABI 1.2 with a stock shadow of every range the flashed build writes; 2026-11-16 (main): core-ot 0.42, settings-ot 0.2, dspload-ot 0.2 and the Octatrack TELOS engine, core-a4mk2 0.8; 2026-11-19 (main, 70d11c8): core-dt2 1.1/1.2 and core-dn2 0.5 (what TELOS needs on the Digitakt II and Digitone II), core-ar2 0.14-0.16, drive-loader-ar2 0.9, core-a4mk2 0.10, new smpl-machines and smpl-knob-c (Rytm MKII); main after 2026-11-19: core-ar2 0.17 (std1 standard events on the Rytm, knob flags) and 0.18 (restart calls), drive-loader-ar2 0.10/0.11 (needs core-ar2 0.18; saved-data mark and APPLY & RESTART as on the A4), drive-loader-a4mk2 on core-a4mk2 0.10

projects.notes: Mod loader: user supplies the stock OS file, the tool builds the custom .syx locally. Device table in the README (3016dca, 2026-11-08): Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1/Keys supported; Digitakt II 1.17 and Digitone II 1.12 experimental; Octatrack 1.40C supported (linkable core boots on an MKII); Model:Cycles and Model:Samples 1.13 supported (builds work on both units); Analog Rytm MKII 1.74 supported; Analog Four MKII 1.56 experimental proof of concept (hook bus, mod storage, unused DDR and recovery checked on a unit). Canonical repo is unclear: the forum post also embeds github.com/elekloader/elekloader (web app at elekloader.github.io/elekloader); forks exist (AvroraPolnareff, naturarum, toonst, simonjohansson); none is listed, as none has changes of its own. Forum: builder issue reported 2026-10-19. Licence GPL-2.0-or-later. 2026-11-10 (8daa2ea): the shop's list, forms and bots moved to elekloader/shop (#338); mods are submitted there. machine-pages 1.8-1.10, machines-dn1 0.5/0.6 and machines-dn2 0.5 add mono machines and MIDI CCs (emulator-tested per TESTS.md). The linker now refuses odd jump targets into mod RAM after a Digitakt II froze at boot (I61). The README offers a Windows .exe; not every release carries the macOS .dmg. 2026-11-10 (main): core-ar2 0.13 opens the Rytm MKII's TEST slots 44-52 to mod machines, adds per-voice trig and velocity getters, screen calls through stock's routines and per-mod knob ids; machine-pages 1.7 tagged. 2026-11-12 (main): core-a4mk2 0.6 brings core-ar2 0.10-0.13's foundations to the Analog Four MKII (field defaults, the modified mark, the project-save event, payloads, knob looks, screen calls) and a 37.7 MB mods' area. Builds pick older core or helper versions by themselves when a mod patches a place a newer one took (Tone+FX's Digitakt files and Digi EQ 1.0c link with DT1 core 4.0 only; OB-1 0.6 with machine-pages 1.2), and released versions stay available while a listed mod needs them. 2026-11-13 (main): a third file family, ELE2, for the Analog Rytm MKI OS 1.74 (Modwerk's Rytm MKI research holds the measurements behind the profile); the README's table also names 1.73, the profile only 1.74. core-ot 0.9-0.40 opens about 40 more Octatrack events and tables to mods (mutes, sequencer moments, LFO waves, popup rows, PATTERN SETTINGS and PERSONALIZE rows, the playback increment, card file calls, the engine task's jobs, a block to DSP core 1). 2026-11-15 (FORMAT, SDK, CORES): std1 'standard events': a mod that sets events std1 subscribes to device- neutral event names, each core maps them to its own tables, and a subscription the core does not map is refused at link time; std1 and native mods link in one build. core-a4mk2 0.7 is the first core with it and adds native A4 events for knob turns, the analog voice frame and modulation edits. A frame-check build that copied one voice's analog frame words over another's silenced track 1 and was fixed in 0.3 (unit or emulator not stated). 2026-11-16 (docs/CORES.md, DRIVE.md, FORMAT.md, core-dn1 README): on the Digitone mk1 the build descriptor now carries the stock bytes of each flashed range (ABI 1.2), and TELOS's linker refuses a +Drive mod site that is not stock on the unit, overlaps the flashed build or another mod, or a region outside a free area (link codes 21-28). core-dn1 5.4's core_stock_info copies the OS image to 0x44200000 before the OS runs. 2026-11-17 (ADAPTING, FORMAT, core-ot, settings-ot, dspload-ot, core-a4mk2 READMEs): core-ot 0.41/0.42 add 16 Octatrack events (tempo, scenes, card mount and USB DISK MODE, previews, recorder commands, pages, track select, windows, crossfader, pattern select and edits, arrangement); new dspload-ot 0.2 sends DSP code at run time (mod.json `dsp_load`), also for TELOS card mods; refusal code 23 `early` for a site the OS ran before the +Drive or card link. On the Analog Four MKII the lock service is now checked on a unit. 2026-11-18 (v0.11.0, docs/DRIVE.md, CORES.md, drive-loader-a4mk2 and drive-loader-ar2 READMEs): v0.11.0 ships the newest core of every device, core-a4mk2 0.9 included. The Analog Four MKII gets its own +Drive mods loader (drive-loader-a4mk2 0.1, not yet run): stock 1.56 keeps the +Drive as raw sectors with no file system, so the loader keeps its own two-copy store in sectors stock never addresses. The Rytm loader (0.6) now reads each file into the +Drive area itself (a 64 KB floor replaces the 512 KB staging buffer), and +Drive mods may hold storage fields, sites over the OS, claims, tables of their own, knob ids and std1 subscriptions where the build's descriptor flags allow (descriptor ABI 1.3). drive-loader-ar2's README asks for core-ar2 0.14 while core-ar2's mod.json at the tag reads 0.13. New A4 MKII check mods for live recording, the sequencer and moments (read as expected in the emulator, 2026-11-14). 2026-11-20 (ADAPTING, CORES, DRIVE, FORMAT; core-ar2 README and SKIPS.md; core-dt2, core-dn2, core-a4mk2, drive-loader, smpl-machines READMEs; new AR2 and DT2 examples): core-dt2 1.1 keeps mods' project and kit data in bytes stock writes as zeros (191 bytes a kit), adds value rows, a per-frame parameter event and key LEDs; core-dt2 1.2 and core-dn2 0.5 add what TELOS needs on the unit (card ready, project save and load, crash, restart, task list), checked in digikit's emulator only, not yet on a unit. core-ar2 0.15: knob faces, mod folders in the +Drive sample browser, pad strikes before stock and LED colours, a held USB input gain step, note ends, track mutes, DIN MIDI out, machines given slots by count; 0.16: four optional CPU skips, off at boot (silent voices, idle sample layer, the UI's dynamic_cast, idle delay and reverb), two of which change the sound slightly, and GLOBAL submenus. The linker hands out machine slots, page ids and mod-declared id pools by count, kept in the lockfile. New smpl-machines (a SMPL page machine layer) and smpl-knob-c. Five new Rytm check examples and kit-memo-dt2. core-a4mk2 0.10's core_project_keep lets the A4 loader's APPLY & RESTART keep unsaved project changes. core-a4mk2's README now says core 0.2's pages drew identically on a unit (OS 1.56). 2026-11-22 (AGENTS, ADAPTING, CORES, DRIVE; core-ar2, drive-loader-ar2 and drive-loader-a4mk2 READMEs and PAGE.md; five new Rytm check examples): core-ar2 0.17 brings the std1 standard events to the Analog Rytm MKII and adds knob flags: a mod's own knob can open a destination list as LFO DEST does (only the list bit is honoured). core-ar2 0.18 adds restart calls. drive-loader-ar2 now needs core-ar2 0.18, marks mods with saved data with * and has APPLY & RESTART, as the A4 loader. The new Rytm check examples (std, std-midi, ui, voice, knob-flags) are built and linked only. The core-ar2 README restates its OS-upgrade restart check: analog-emu hung on 5 of 15 upgrades without core's restart routine and 0 of 15 with it (0 of 30 with the panel link paced as on a unit).

projects.notes: 2026-11-12: the Octatrack card firmware builder is retired: modules reach an Octatrack only through the Modwerk base, over USB or as one set file (MODWERK0.SET) on the card; Tuner, Stem Rec and Temp Save paused until they have base versions; Spectrum, Modulation, Character and MIDI Scenes removed for good; CPU-rendered machines get a budget (CPU FULL) after FM Synth froze an MKII (I79); POLY8 and FM Synth carry a Heavy CPU badge; checks refuse writes into the stock DELAY table and odd jump targets; the DT2 base hides the raw +Drive block write from modules; Octatrack modules moved to sdk/octatrack/modules; new experimental Crossfader and Live Looper for the Digitakt I (OS 1.54) and Amiga, a tracker-style sample machine, for the Octatrack. 2026-11-11/12: the Octatrack base and USB installs are open to everyone (first install still from the card, at most 20 modules per set, 24 since 2026-11-14; Tuner, Stem Rec and Temp Save card-only); USB Audio is off unless the set has the USB Audio module; skipping modules at boot moved from FUNC to holding PROJ at power-on (MKI keeps FUNC); the octabam pin is frozen (Modwerk follows only elekloader upstream); Analog BD 0.1.7 has a new 909 model; base-update and SYNTIZ incidents I75 and I76. 2026-11-09/10: Octatrack beta: the silence after USB DISK MODE (finding 72) was the base mistaking stock's DSP pause for a stall, fixed (I69); FM Synth with many FLEX tracks no longer loses the audio on PLAY; the Octatrack page asks for a power cycle when the DSP has stopped; Temp Save 0.1.0 withdrawn from USB installs (card build stays). Modwerk also loads effects onto Zoom MultiStomp pedals now (ZDL files over USB; not an Elektron device). Browser-based hub, builds locally from the user's own stock OS. Browse mods by device, forum with a section per device, shared SDK. Dubspot (13 Oct): several modules are still early prototypes. last_activity = date of the Dubspot article, not a forum post. 2026-11-02: three Analog Rytm MKII modules by npp1993 moved into the library (Pipo Loop 0.1.1, Sample RATE 0.1.0, Silent Pad+Trig Settings 0.6.0, all experimental, OS 1.74; linkable together with core-ar2 0.7, Filter Hz and Loop Sync; the packages themselves not yet run on a unit). `_submissions/` takes no new modules. The Octatrack USB beta also works on the MKI. 2026-11-03: the site now lets you download a built Analog Rytm MKII .syx (after confirming you know how to get back to stock); new Rytm module quick-velocity-aftertouch-assign with a verification note. Zoom pedals: an effect whose group+ID clashes with one already on the pedal is moved to a free local Delay ID 958-1023 (ID only in the ZDL header at 0x40-0x41, no checksum); two effects with the same group and ID froze an MS-70CDR at boot until its ROM was reprogrammed. 2026-11-04/05: Rytm MKII downloads on (records); npp1993's Control In Actions (footswitch or 0-5 V gate on EXP/CV IN as ACTION for MUTE and more) and Quick Velocity+Aftertouch Assign join the library, Silent Pad+Trig Settings 0.7.0; euclidean 1.1.6 for Digitakt I 1.53/1.54 reported working on a unit by sumedho (all cases, save/reload, power cycle). 2026-11-08 to 11-10 (74c9eb2): Rytm library gains comp-preview, kit-ab, lfo-rnd and voice-dac (from rytm2_mods, unit runs on the Modwerk base), ctrl-in-perf and scene-mutes (from rytm-mods-src 0017/0018, unit runs T208/T210/T221), Improved Machine Browser and MIDI Mute; the Octatrack key bus moved to the tail of the first FX2 slot (checked on an MKI and an MKII); a Digitakt II audio scheduler is proposed (emulator only); Zoom MS-70CDR pedal work (out of scope here). 2026-11-12/13: Octatrack base: a stall record now keeps the 128 frames before it; an installed Sidechain no longer causes NO ROOM on every pick after a restart (I96); a new USB device revision (bcdDevice 0x0101) repairs Windows hosts that could not open the unit (I100); a machine engine's DSP price moved into its package; the base refuses a module machine or effect pick while the CPU meter is at 85 % or more; VECTOR 0.3.2 fixes a whole-bank reset (I95); SYNTIZ and Tape Echo get a Heavy CPU badge. Rytm MKII: the send-bus base gains digital voices; new Improved AMP and BD ANALOG (I97-I99). module:doctor covers Digitakt II modules; a Digitakt II pre-send render hook is proposed (emulator only). FRACT, an Octatrack granular machine draft by ex1010, has a functional unit report (2026-11-10). 2026-11-14 (second pass): the Digitakt II moved from research to preview: the site builds core 1.0 with library modules in the browser, downloads stay off, OS 1.17 only; the first DT2 library module is Track Names; DT2 phrase modules can continue phrases across empty steps, follow microtimed trigs and save settings in a project archive. Octatrack: a two-step base update for units whose RAM stage is too small; the CPU guard counts the picked machine's price and judges a stopped unit by its last playing load (I105); POLY8 0.3.3 and FM Synth 0.1.3 cost far less while installed on no track (FM Synth 0.1.3 also fixes track 1's LFO 3); `device:price` measures a module's cost; a new Octatrack Diagnostics page on the site. 2026-11-14 (changelog, verification): an Octatrack module set may hold 24 modules (was 20, still temporary); the base may grow to 1.5 MiB, so units on a base older than 2026-11-13 take it as two USB updates, and a base update retries up to four times when a reply goes missing before the write starts. New project and bank events (load, save, reload, new project, Part save and clear) let a module keep its own file beside the project. Amiga 0.3.0 (experimental) adds a SYNC stretch mode that follows the project tempo; in a RAM trial on an MKII an earlier build of it restarted after about 90 s on a twin that also carried a base change under test (I109). Filter Hz 1.2.1 (Rytm MKII, from rytm2_mods' port of 0008-filter-hz) widens the box behind a locked FRQ so kHz values fit; a maintainer ran it on a Rytm MKII on OS 1.74 on 2026-11-14. 2026-11-16 (changelog 2026-11-14/15, LINK.md, TEST_RUNNER.md): Rytm MKII development bases carry a SysEx USB link (screen, memory, keys, encoders, remote flash, and a boot from RAM with no flash write), and a test runner plays scripted cases on rytm-emu or a unit over it. Filter Hz 1.3.0 shows the FX track's delay and reverb HPF, LPF and reverb FRQ in Hz. 2026-11-17 (changelog 2026-11-16/17, verification, module docs): Octatrack base versions start at 0.7 (shown as MODWERK BASE 0.7 on the unit; 0.7.1 to 0.7.5 the same day): PROJ > MODWERK > MODULES switches installed modules on and off; a project remembers which machine each track uses, so a missing machine is named instead of playing FLEX; one module may use 288 KiB (was 128) and may borrow sample memory while installed; windowed modules such as Tuner can come over USB (base 0.7.5); packages are no longer refused for sharing byte runs with stock; every Octatrack module must name its CPU price (`resources.cpuPrice`); `module:doctor` reports DSP register writes against each hook site's contract; stall records name each DSP core's last packet. New Octatrack modules Kits and MIDI Scenes 0.3.0 (experimental ports of octabam's modules, short RAM trials on the owner's MKII); the Octakit draft is removed. New Digitakt I module CC Remap. Rytm MKII: a third base variant, voices; Ping Pong Loop folded into Improved SMPL 0.6.x; size-only updates of several modules run on the author's unit; Analog Rytm MKI builds are refused when the update exceeds the upgrade buffer or touches the boot-flash writers. Goal pages for contributors on the Digitakt II and the Syntakt (no Syntakt module yet). Field diagnostics 12-16 Nov: 87 units. A dialog on the site says the project's future is uncertain and asks for maintainers. 2026-11-18 (changelog 2026-11-07..17, verification, machine guides): Octatrack base 0.7.7 skips stock's delay work for tracks whose delay is silent (CPU meter 41 to 34 % with DELAY on every track); a machine's CPU price is now its mean cost per playing track (FM Synth 0.1.4: 6 %, seven tracks a Part); DSP voices book only what the bank's Parts use (core 0 up to 3,120 cycles); a shared scale file for Octatrack modules. Rytm MKII: sets linked by Modwerk's own linker may use 704 KiB or 3.7 MiB of DDR above the 128 KiB mod area; the voices base drops the FX lock words (1,752 B more for modules). Rytm MKI SDK guide published (research). Digitakt II: the site builds Modwerk's base 8650bb8a on core-dt2 1.1 (elekloader#221 at 0df8409), downloads still off; new modules MIDI Engine (Rytm), Euclidean Scale and Mute Latch (DT2), Vibrato (Octatrack, from octabam). Machine maintainers may now merge a machine's first module releases; pull requests that change a built package stay drafts until that build ran on a unit. The dialog saying the project's future is uncertain was removed. 2026-11-18, later (changelog, OCTATRACK_PACKAGE_DSP_HOOKS): Octatrack base 0.7.8 makes the per-track sound-source hook (DSP site 5) a chain (#1098): the base offers each track to every installed DSP track machine in turn and the first that owns it plays it, so a second DSP machine (BlackPyramids) can install over USB beside Analog BD; Analog BD's package and sound are unchanged. The key bus (option B) is merged (#737). 2026-11-19 (changelog 2026-11-14..19, DESKTOP_APP, MACHINE_RECIPE, HOOKS, MODULE_PERFORMANCE, arr-rows, butter- fingers, Digitone II verification): every contribution, core work included, now comes to Modwerk as a pull request, and every machine is to get a Modwerk base (Digitone II and Analog Four MKII included). Octatrack base 0.7.8 lets modules rest when unused; 0.7.9 adds a shared Part Edit menu and fixes an effect lost after a project load (I154). A desktop app (Electron, WebUSB and Web MIDI) is in development, Windows only so far, never run against a unit. Digitone II: core-dn2 0.3 builds booted on a second unit from Transfer, and stock 1.12 came back with a normal update; no Modwerk module can be built for it yet. Two stock Octatrack arrangement bugs found by Arr Rows (SB33, SB34). 2026-11-20 (changelog 2026-11-18/19, verification 2026-11-19 beta diagnostics, OCTATRACK_DRIVING, MODULE_PERFORMANCE, machines guide, micro-timing README/TESTING, Digitone II GOAL): most of the day's changelog is web app, agent board and tooling. Octatrack: base 0.7.9 is the site's base since 2026-11-18 (about nine units by 2026-11-19); base 0.7.10 is to add a refusal code of its own when a module's DSP claims meet a delay buffer (code 12) and to log which check refused a module at start. The card holds two set slots (MODWERK0.SET, MODWERK1.SET); a set loaded from the card is made the one the next boot prefers while the other stays for recovery. A live CPU/DSP load card on the site (USB). The machine guide now explains the frame guard's budget and how to count skipped renders. New draft Micro Timing 0.1.1-experimental (own_mods); its remembered row moved out of battery RAM into the module's own memory. Zoom MS-70CDR: Sync repairs an effect missing from the pedal's list; the list is written back only while the pedal stays connected. Digitone II: Modwerk's own linker knows OS 1.12 and links core-dn2 0.3 and 0.4 byte for byte as elekloader does, but refuses mods with DSP code; the site builds no Digitone II firmware yet. Base changes now collect in one draft pull request per machine, shipped by the owner after long tests on a unit; device reviewers (assigned per machine) approve first module releases. 2026-11-21 (changelog 2026-11-17..21, verification 2026-11-19..21, OCTATRACK_USB_AUDIO_MODULE, TEST_PROCEDURE, DIGITONE_II_OS_RESEARCH): Octatrack base 0.7.10 gives a DSP claim that meets a delay buffer its own refusal (code 12, naming the FX2 slot to move), logs which check refused a module at start, brings Analog BD back after a rolled-back trial (I178), lets Undo finish once a module's page is closed, and cuts the UI-tick cost of large sets; 0.7.11 (served) waits for a project load to finish before it changes the DSP's effects (I180) and rests unused machine and effect modules; 0.7.12 (staged) installs USB Audio 0.3.0 as one module configured on the unit instead of seven base variants (reconnect failures fixed on the way, I176, I177). Installed but unused modules may cost at most 0.2 points of the frame interrupt from now on, or must rest. Every module or base change now goes through one test procedure that the submitter runs; reviewers only read its record. A fast MIDI soak and a queue for the shared unit are new tools. New modules: kitbank for the Digitone (OS 1.44) and Screen Off for the Octatrack; Improved SMPL 0.6.3 and Direct Jump Kyoti 0.2.0 (V7.3). Digitone II: the research page names the MCF5441x, the SHARC+ boot over DSPI2 and the ARM core; the site can read a development base and upload a module to its RAM, but no Digitone II module exists yet. Also 28 Zoom MS-70CDR effects (not an Elektron device). 2026-11-22 (changelog 2026-11-21, verification 2026-11-21, MODULE_PERFORMANCE, MODULE_RESOURCE_GAUGES, TEST_PROCEDURE, OCTATRACK_DRIVING, effects guide, Grain, analog-bd and qperf docs, Rytm README): Octatrack base 0.7.13 judges a module machine pick on a busy unit by the CPU-meter points the machine adds (measured on a unit against Flex) instead of its frame price, which had refused Grain on a Part that played at 43.5 % on the owner's MKII. Module pages show measured CPU, DSP and memory figures where they exist and estimated tiers elsewhere. New track machine Grain (granular, up to six grains), measured at length on the owner's MKII; it still misses the frame deadline with 20-channel USB capture, and a panel freeze after one Grain trial is unexplained (I187). Under ot_emu the CPU meter reads 100 % from boot, so the emulator refuses every module pick. The effects guide explains the DSP56300 div half quotient. Rytm MKII: QPER Live Rec 0.3.0 follows pattern-length changes, BD ANALOG 0.2.2 drops the 808/909 badge, and Improved Performance (audio load 85.4 to 72.1 % on the author's unit) entered the library and was retired the same day, to be folded into the Rytm base. Every machine now runs one test procedure; Rytm unit steps run over its link with a RAM boot. Base work now goes to one cumulative draft per machine. 2026-11-23 (changelog 2026-11-22, verification 2026-11-22, MODULE_PERFORMANCE, MODULE_AUTHOR_UPDATES, Grain README/TESTING, Rytm README, Pad Pressure Fix README): testers run released Octatrack base 0.7.13; one logged a UI stop during playback with six modules installed (I191), and a Windows tester saw failed USB staging and a USB Audio trial rolled back at the reconnect (I192); the installer now retries claiming the returning interface. Grain 0.1.2 treats the sample as a ring and plays each grain 3 dB lower. Rytm MKII: package builds refuse audio code that needs over 512 B of stack; Pad Pressure Fix moves into the base. An unpublished Elemod update can be rolled back.

projects.name: digitakt-ii-research (Deja Vu LFOs, ONESHOT zoom)
projects.author: kariGardarsson
projects.license: MIT (repo root); the Sample Editing Pack AGPL-3.0-or-later (derived from digikit)
projects.base_os: Digitakt II OS 1.17 (recommended; Deja Vu + ONESHOT zoom) and 1.16 (Deja Vu only)
projects.version: v0.3.0-beta "All-in-One" (2026-10-23) per altstrument; GitHub releases page showed v0.2.0-beta (18 Oct) as newest when read
projects.tested_note: DV-F/DV-T run in 70b185's Digitakt II builds
projects.features: ["waveform zoom up to 64x (Universal Zoom)", "automatic slice points (SmartSlice)", "record, chop, trim and save samples on the unit (SampleLAB)", "crossfade at the loop point in SLICE (CFADE)", "random-loop LFO waveforms (D\u00e9j\u00e0 Vu, older editions)"]
projects.notes: Windows standalone builder (portable, no Python/Git/WSL needed) that takes the user's own official OS file, identifies it by SHA-256, writes the patched .syx; the user installs it with Elektron Transfer. The builder never connects to the instrument and never flashes. Adds two random-loop LFO waveforms on all three LFOs: DV-F (WAVE 7, free-running) and DV-T (WAVE 8, read position resets on track trigger); MODE = 2/4/8/16/32 steps; SPH = randomness (0 new values each step, 64 locks values and order, 127 keeps values but reorders, in between blends); stock WAVE 0-6 stay on stock paths. v0.2.0-beta adds a ONESHOT waveform zoom (encoder C cycles 1x, 2x, 3.75x, turning C pans; only in the combined 1.17 edition). Hardware: all three outputs validated on a physical unit for normal boot and operation, described by the author as beta evidence, not exhaustive. Open: broad MIDI / sequencer / transport / sync regression, save-reload-power-cycle persistence, long-duration stability. Unsigned .exe (SmartScreen warns). Repo: docs/INSTALLATION.md and docs/RECOVERY.md, windows-builder/, src/dv/ (host model), coldfire/ (DV, routing, trampoline, startup-allocation source), research/ (byte-backed findings), tools/midisniff.py (passive SysEx capture, does not transmit). Evidence ladder used by the author: SOURCE/STATIC, HOST, SYNTHETIC UNICORN, NATURAL EMULATED, HARDWARE. MIT, 7 commits, 4 stars. Credits: Marbles (concept only), Bezronczek's Syntakt Firmware Workbench (behavioural reference), ElekLabs digikit (research tooling, not bundled), elektron-firmware-tool (vendored). 2026-11-06: a second package, the Digitakt II Sample Editing Pack (OS 1.17, Windows builder): Universal Zoom (up to 64x), SmartSlice (automatic slice points), SampleLAB (load or record, chop, trim, audition, save copies) and CFADE (cross-fade at the SLICE loop wrap). Derived from digikit, AGPL-3.0-or-later; hardware acceptance by the author recorded in sample-editing/HARDWARE_ACCEPTANCE.md (user report, not an agent-run test).

projects.name: Overtone
projects.author: complex-ping
projects.base_os: Digitone II OS 1.12 only (patcher refuses any other file); NOT compatible with dn2mk2 (OS 1.11)
projects.version: v1.10 (tag, 2026-11-22): arp MODE SHUF and RAND on both arps (MIDI tracks too); ARP 2 runs while a track key is held with the sequencer stopped, gains RANGE (x1-x8) and SLIDE and drops TRUE; fixes FREE mode and the 1/128 speeds being lost when a sound loads. v1.9 (tag, 2026-11-21): GROOVE presets documented as weight tables (SW54-SW71 equal Elektron's swing values), GROOVE also on external MIDI clock. v1.8 (tag, 2026-11-19): fixes freezes in the MODULATION SETUP menus. v1.7 (tag, 2026-11-19): arp MODE FREE (runs from the pattern start, restarts each loop, trigs move it instead of restarting it), SPEED down to 1/128 (Q and T too), a playhead line under the arp step grid; followers listen to USB in or a CUSTOM mix (tracks, IN, send-effect returns, USB). v1.6 (tag, 2026-11-16): both arps, the LFOs and both envelope followers on MIDI tracks (ARP 1 sends notes over MIDI; modulation of MIDI values goes out as CC); followers can listen to MAIN or IN; lock trigs slide. v1.5 (tag, 2026-11-15): LOOP records from USB in or a CUSTOM SOURCE (any tracks, the inputs, the send effects, USB), SRC can be p-locked, FUNC steps LEN through bar lengths, an END below STRT plays the window backwards; THRU takes the same CUSTOM SOURCE. v1.3 (2026-11-04): per-sound LFOs, two envelope followers and two arps as modulators (played on a Digitone II per README); v1.2 (2026-10-30): instant pattern switch (PTN + YES/NO), saved with the project; v1.1 (2026-10-30) GROOVE rework and tap tempo; v1.0.1 (2026-10-29) fixes OS installs over Transfer while Overtone runs
projects.features: ["SOPHIE, MACHINEDRUM, LOOP and THRU machines; LOOP and THRU can take a custom mix of tracks, inputs, send effects and USB", "per-track insert effects", "envelope followers (a track, the main mix, the inputs, USB in or a custom mix)", "two arpeggiators: one in the keyboard scale with SHUF, RAND and free-running modes; a second as a step modulator with range and slide; both also on MIDI tracks", "parameter slides; knobs show the value that is playing", "GROOVE: a step-by-step timing editor instead of swing", "instant pattern switching that keeps the place in the bar"]
projects.notes: Python 3.11+ patcher (patcher/patch.py) that builds Overtone from the user's own OS 1.12 and only saves the result if it matches the tested build byte for byte; install via Elektron Transfer over USB. Adds machines SOPHIE, MACHINEDRUM, LOOP, THRU, per-track insert effects, envelope followers, two arpeggiators, parameter slides and GROOVE (replaces swing). 1.0.1 fixes installing an OS sent with Transfer while Overtone runs. About 160 checks per build in two emulators (digikit for the main OS, a SHARC emulator for the DSP program); author states 1.0.1 passes all of them, is played on a Digitone II and Transfer installs were checked on the unit. Opening Overtone projects on stock OS is untested. Recovery section is detailed (FUNC + TRIG 4, DIN MIDI, ~15 min). AGPL-3.0-or-later (includes dnfw), 5 commits. Related: dnfw, digikit, dn2-cfw, Schwung Sophie (MIT), and the author's digitone-2-modding-skill used with Claude Code. 2026-11-17 (README, v1.6): arps, LFOs and followers also work on MIDI tracks to play and modulate external gear; a follower can listen to the main mix or the audio inputs; a trig with only locks now slides too. 2026-11-20 (README, v1.7/v1.8): the README now says Overtone 1.8 is played on a Digitone II and passes about 190 emulator checks per build (160 before); the patcher also stores the packer's choices (no OS bytes), so it rebuilds the tested file in seconds instead of 1 to 3 minutes. 2026-11-22 (README, v1.9): GROOVE's presets are now listed with their step weights (the SW presets reproduce Elektron's SWING 54-71 %, and any swing value can be typed in as two weights); unlike Elektron's swing, GROOVE moves every step, the arpeggiators and micro timing. GROOVE now also works while the Digitone follows external MIDI clock; early steps play ahead of their clock from the measured tempo and can sit slightly off in the first beat after PLAY. The README says 1.9 passes every check (about 190) and installs and boots on a Digitone II, but its GROOVE changes are not yet played on a unit (1.8 was). 2026-11-23 (README rewrite, v1.10 commit message): v1.10 adds arp modes SHUF (held notes over RANGE in one random order, redrawn on each trig or chord) and RAND (a random note and octave each step) on both arps. ARP 2 runs while a track key is held with the sequencer stopped, gains RANGE (x1-x8) and SLIDE, and has no TRUE mode. Fixed: FREE mode and the 1/128 speeds were lost when a sound loaded. At the tag the README said 1.10 installs and boots on a unit and SHUF/RAND were played there; the shorter README now omits this.

projects.notes: Free browser-based pattern/sequence editor, not a firmware mod. Repo includes sysexmap/, a public reverse-engineered SysEx format map (CC BY 4.0): 45 mappings, map version 1.13.0, each with a confidence level (A = hardware-confirmed on a DN2: 23; B = corpus-confirmed by repo fixtures: 12; C = inherited, one value exercised: 9; D = unknown, do not rely: 1). Narrowed by bisection on 2026-09-08 against a Digitone II (OS 1.10E) and a Digitakt II. Not decoded: parameter locks, sound parameters (filter, amp, FX, LFO), synth machine choice. Needs the DN2 in SYSEX RECEIVE mode; Web MIDI needs Chromium over HTTPS or localhost (Chrome/Edge 152 break SysEx receive on macOS). App is AGPLv3 since v22.46 (MIT through v22.37). 6 commits.

projects.version: R027 candidate (2026-11-12): adds SEM, a seventh filter type (Oberheim-style state-variable model from Faust: low-pass, notch, high-pass, band-pass) with its response drawn on the FILTER page; browser build only; R025 stopped the right effects chain running for every voice. R022 (2026-11-06): working-project sample autosave and sampler SYN-page routing fixes; native replay passed, hardware confirmation pending; includes R020 cold-start guard and R013 FORMAT SAMPLES; an iPhone USB freeze is unresolved; R012 remains the stable target
projects.tested_note: README (2026-11-12): R012 confirmed on hardware; R027 owner-tested, not instrumented, USB audio untested since R023/R024 broke it (I74); R021/R022 fixes still pending hardware confirmation
projects.features: ["six Digitakt II sample machines: ONESHOT, WERP, STRETCH, REPITCH, GRID, SLICE", "mono and stereo samples with waveform views", "slice editing and slice grids", "recorder: record and resample, normalise, trim, save", "sample manager for the +Drive", "class-compliant multichannel USB audio", "SEM filter: low-pass to notch to high-pass, plus band-pass"]
projects.notes: Source-only recipes for Digitone II firmware with six Digitakt II sample machines (ONESHOT, WERP, STRETCH, REPITCH, GRID, SLICE), stereo samples, sample browsing, DT2 parameter graphics and SLICES trig mode. Recorder adds recording/resampling, source selection, normalization, trimming, audition, saving to +Drive and optional track assignment; VOICE cycles Voice Setup, Sample Manager and Recorder. Class-compliant USB audio provides 42 capture channels at 48 kHz/24 bit (MAIN, tracks 1-16, DELAY, REVERB, CHORUS, INPUT as stereo pairs) and a stereo return. R012 needs only the official DN2 1.11 and DT2 1.16 OS files; silent compatibility data replaces the private sample bank, and users load their own playable samples afterward. Native and browser builders verify exact inputs and the output: 2,563,872 bytes, SHA-256 4a2742a4...63a3a9a. The browser builds locally without uploading files; neither builder flashes the instrument. No firmware images or samples are distributed. Historical exact T1E2/R003/R008/R011 builds still require their original private sample bank. R011 fixed USB publication stalling after project changes by selecting its candidate destination from current DMA START while preserving ownership checks; R012 retains that fix. Owner-confirmed stock audio, samples, Recorder and USB audio on R012, including after project changes. Stable does not mean exhaustive validation: exact trimmed-file comparison, full Recorder-source coverage, endurance and end-to-end USB latency remain unverified. Builds on dnfw (angellinares/dn2_firmware_explore), selache, digikit and elektron-firmware-tool. AGPL-3.0-or-later. 2026-11-03: README warns new users NOT to install R012 yet. R012 mounts an existing sample filesystem but does not create one on a DN2 that never had it; symptoms are 0% Free / 0 bytes in Transfer, stalled uploads, Connection failed. The author says stock FORMAT +DRIVE, EMPTY RESET and FACTORY RESET do not create it and can erase projects; at that point an on-device formatter was still in development. R013 subsequently added FORMAT SAMPLES with erase confirmation; formatting, restart, capacity and post-format uploads were checked on the owner's unit. Owner testing of R012 had used storage prepared during development. An earlier track-2 saved-project reload report was an unsaved checkpoint; R022 addresses a separate, reproduced failure to refresh the sample table in the unsaved working-state backup. This does not establish recovery from an interrupted write or USB freeze.

projects.version: 0.42 (tag, 2026-11-15): HARM, a harmonic (Fourier) synth as the third ENG place between SMPL and TIME: the time synth's sixteen waves rebuilt from their first 32 harmonics, HARMS takes harmonics away down to a sine; 0.41 (tag, 2026-11-14): time-synth voices skip the stock sample playback (OS 1.54 only), about 15 % less audio work with a chord; 0.40 (tag, 2026-11-14): TIME OFF follows the sample engine's PLAY, LOOP and LOOP END. 0.39 (tag, 2026-11-14): the time synth reads its waves' table points without smoothing between them (as the CMI did), about a third less audio work with a chord held; 0.38 (tag, 2026-11-14) works out each looping voice's loop points only when the sample or STRT/LEN/LOOP/LOOP END change. 0.27-0.37 switch silent voices off by the firmware's real amp envelope, bring back LOOP END, make RETRO much cheaper, fix SUS release in ping-pong, and steal voices by gate and age
projects.tested_note: builds up to 0.14 and 0.25 ran on the author's Digitakt mk1; unit reports for 0.26 (notes stopped dead, I89), 0.30 (freeze on an ENG switch, I90), 0.31 (UI lag with RETRO, I91) and 0.34 (SUS stopped dead in ping-pong, I92); the fixes in 0.28-0.39 ran only in digiemu; the OS 1.53 amp-envelope address is now given by elekloader's core notes (2026-11-15)
projects.features: ["CMI machine: one sample played by eight voices from track 1", "forward, reverse and ping-pong loops with hold or sustain looping; LOOP and LOOP END snap to zero crossings", "RETRO dial: 16 bit 48 or 44.1 kHz, or 8 bit at 32 to 8 kHz", "stereo spread; released notes ring on and their voices switch off once silent", "TIME engine: sixteen single cycles cut from the sample, stepped or crossfaded", "HARM engine: the same waves rebuilt from up to 32 harmonics, down to a sine", "waveform page and a CPU meter in the title bar"]
projects.notes: A Fairlight CMI-style polyphonic sample instrument as an elekloader mod: machine CMI on track 1 turns tracks 2-8 into its voices and plays one sample across the keyboard, from trigs, chords or MIDI. Forked from Digi Poly 2.1 (digi1_mods), whose polyphony, voice borrowing and kit storage it keeps. Conflicts with Digi Poly, dt8poly, DIGISLICER, Digi EQ and Digi Matrix (same patch sites or sound slots). Kits saved with CMI load that track as ONESHOT on the stock OS. The author names Claude as coding assistant. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-12. 2026-11-12 (0.19-0.26): the meter shows the whole audio engine's peak load; on the unit it read about 85 % right after boot, and the author's instruction count in digiemu puts about 98 % of that in the stock render, so the UI gets what is left. Projects saved with 0.14-0.22's RETRO switch on open at 8 bit 8 kHz. 2026-11-14 (0.27-0.37): the envelope value 0.26 used to end voices (core export fw_amp_env) is the filter envelope and cut sounding notes on the unit; 0.30 reads the real amp envelope found by disassembly (S20). Voice stealing takes a voice that is off, else the oldest released note, else the oldest sequencer note, never a held key. 2026-11-15 (0.38-0.39, CLAUDE.md): an instruction profile in digiemu puts the stock render at about 83k instructions a block whether voices play or not (the stock render does all eight voices' work), and outside the render the UI costs about 2,300 a block; the lag in TIME mode was the time synth's own share (about 8.6k a block, cut to about 5.5k in 0.39). digiemu does not run the load-dependent paths, because the mod's CPU meter reads no timer there. 2026-11-16 (0.40-0.42, CHANGELOG and CLAUDE.md): the author's earlier listings were made at 0x40000000, but the DT1 main section loads at 0x40000400, so readings made before 0.40 were 0x400 off. 0.41's skip of the stock sample player and 0.42's HARM ran only in digiemu and on the host, not yet on the unit.

projects.notes: Native Rust emulator that runs the ColdFire and SHARC+ firmware together, with front panel, display and audio, plus a web panel (WASM core), a Tauri desktop app, the patch toolchain "patchkit" (applies modules to the user's own .syx), a headless scenario runner with pinned PCM hashes, a control socket for patch injection and DSP/ColdFire analysis databases with Ghidra tooling. README caveats: the DSP "does not run in real time yet", the browser host is parked on branch wip/browser-host, "no patched firmware has been installed on a device", and recovery via the bootstrap menu is "not tested on hardware". patchkit refuses to change sections 2, 4 and 8. 2026-11-12 (b657f37, via altstrument): a USB take-over for fast sample transfer in the workbench with a read-back hash check per file, a diagnostic module that reads card information, a restructured SDK, fixes to the card image and the patch kit on Windows. 982 commits, AGPL-3.0-or-later with extra section-7 terms (attribution, origin, names) in NOTICE; page shows 46 open issues. GitHub marks it as not a fork. The org ElekLabs has 2 public repos: digikit and a fork of js216/selache. Original author: the GitHub profile m-dwyer is named "Em D" (Melbourne), which is exactly the credit ElekLabs' NOTICE requires ("digikit by Em D"); Overtone credits digikit to "Em D" as well. The earlier repo m-dwyer/digikit (196 commits, 4 stars, GPL-2.0-or-later, README at the time: "no audio", last visible file HANDOVER-2026-09-16) shows no move/archive notice and does not mention ElekLabs. ElekLabs has no public members, so the pages themselves do not show who runs it; the maintainer (user of this repo) states that Em D develops in ElekLabs/digikit (2026-10-31, not verifiable on the pages). The licence changed from GPL-2.0-or-later to AGPL-3.0-or-later with extra terms. Treat both repos as one project line, ElekLabs/digikit being the current one. Mod READMEs that say "digikit's emulator" mean this project. 2026-11-14 (finding 123 rewritten, findings 128-129, docs/MODULES.md, docs/ADDRMAP.md): the USB take-over is deleted (its commands answer E_STATE); core/usb-bulk-audio adds a vendor bulk OUT interface to the USB AUDIO/MIDI configuration at boot, so there is no mode switch (a probe sent 200 MB at 28 MB/s while audio played; real uploads 3.38 MB/s on a DN2, 2.74 MB/s on a DT2). Runtime 0.7.0: modules declare machines and effects with builder calls and the runtime commits them at once or refuses; a module of another major.minor is refused (E_CONTRACT); the patched-in content macros are gone. An address map names code addresses in crash records and profiles; the debug module can keep a card log that survives a crash. Finding 128 (static): the SHARC hook sites cannot move into run-time services, because the ColdFire uploads the whole DSP image before the card is readable. 2026-11-15 (MODULE-AUTHORING, design/module-sdk, handover): modules no longer declare their DSP cycles; module:check measures the worst steady block and stores a per-voice or per-effect DSP cost in the package, and one shared rule (largest voice cost x voices + effect costs within the headroom) now runs in the boot planner, the menu, patchkit fit and the web Transfer tab, which refuses a selection over the limit ('DSP LOAD need > free'). Modules built for the old descriptor must be rebuilt. Runtime limits now listed: 512 KiB arena, 64 KiB per module, 8 machine rows, 3 FX slots, DSP area 512 KiB (DT2) / 320 KiB (DN2). The SDK sample kernel has since landed (2026-11-16): the Shot machine fell from about 5,000 to about 2,450 (DT2) / 2,660 (DN2) emulator instructions a block, bit-identical. 2026-11-16 (findings 130 and 132, sdk/dsp/REGISTERS.md, handovers; runtime 0.8.2, untagged): one generated DSP register contract for module code (clobber, keep, stack, never_write), checked by patchkit build but only as a warning so far; the fx, machines, samples and lfo services are separate crates, the step before loadable services; module DSP tests moved to a SHARC-only rig (about 45 s instead of about 21 min). Finding 103 was partly withdrawn: several values reported as measured on silicon came from probe instructions the old assembler had mis-encoded (see digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md). No new unit run in this period. 2026-11-17 (findings 133-135, plans usb-fast-batch, runtime-slimming, r12-8-sharc-stubs, digikit-hot-reload, handovers; runtime 0.8.3, untagged): a Fast USB speed round ran on a DN2 (OS 1.12) and a DT2 (OS 1.17) on 2026-11-16 with every file hash-checked: one store-table commit for up to 16 files, copy/write overlap and fewer +Drive steps per file took a sample pack from 2.42 to 3.56 MB/s (DN2) and 2.32 to 3.07 MB/s (DT2) and a 9.8 MB file to 4.37 / 4.13 MB/s; a cached USB receive was slower and was dropped. Finding 133 (static): the card takes one transfer at a time under global mutexes, so parallel writers cannot help. Services become separate .dks files bound to the user's own firmware at install (patchkit bind; bound files hold firmware bytes and are never committed): lfo.dks is merged, Transfer installs the services a module needs (both emulator-tested), fx.dks and machines.dks are on a branch. Hot reload is an active plan again (finding 135, static firmware facts), not built. Facts in devices/digitakt-2.md. 2026-11-18 (findings 136-141, devices/syntakt.toml, plan syntakt.md): Syntakt OS 1.42 support in the emulator only. The emulator runs MAIN and the second ColdFire (section 7) in lock step, with digital audio (analog tracks silent); patchkit builds a no-seal 1.42 image that changes only section 3 and refuses sections 1, 2, 4, 6, 7 and 8; the runtime, menu, health and input adapters boot on the emulated 1.42 and load the debug module over emulated USB MIDI. Nothing has been flashed to a Syntakt. The DT2 and DN2 device files gained [protect] windows (hardware blocks a content module may not address; the packer refuses such a module) and [container] roles; the bulk OUT interface (core/usb-bulk-audio) is now in the default device image of both. 2026-11-18 (docs/PATCHING, MODULES, ARCHITECTURE, plans runtime-and-services and r12-8-sharc-stubs, port files): machines and effects are run-time modules only; patchkit now refuses a patch-time machine or effect row. The services machines.dks and fx.dks have landed: unbound files hold no firmware bytes, `patchkit bind` makes the stock tails from the user's own firmware, and Transfer installs the services a module needs (emulator example on DN2 1.12: machines.dks 29,718 bytes). The SHARC hook sites now jump through 16 slot words that a service fills (4 used). core/usb-bulk-audio (Fast USB beside USB audio) moved from a separate patch set into the default `device` and `device-introblank` sets on both devices. `patchkit pack` refuses a content module whose code or data holds an address inside a device's protected windows (flash controller, FPGA, peer buses). The DN2 OS 1.11 port file grew from 277 to 358 anchors (1.12: 359), adding the USB, card-driver, DSP voice and link anchors. No new unit run in these files. 2026-11-18 (findings 147-149, handover 2026-11-18, plans extension-model and port-file, MODULES, LFO module docs): runtime 0.9.0 refuses modules built for an older minor runtime version and duplicate keys in a boot selection; a new module kind lfo-shape (template and a first module, lfo_shapes_1, with seven 32-sample shapes; the service holds up to eight, as wave numbers 7 and up) and a core/lfo image adapter in every DT2 and DN2 patch set; content modules reload without a boot (refused while the transport plays); one port file per device and firmware, picked by the firmware hash, is planned. Findings 147-149 read the play state, the filter type and the LFO paths statically on DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12. All emulator or static; no new unit run. An open risk the plan lists: after the last SysEx block the workbench flash flow can report done while the unit still writes flash. 2026-11-20 (finding 150 new, findings 110 and 148 updated, device files, plans and design digikit-project, extension-model, INSTRUMENTATION): the module file limit (upload stage buffer) doubles to 128 KiB on DT2, DN2 and Syntakt. Finding 150 reads the stock machine and filter type setters and the KitActive wrapper the machine chooser calls; finding 110 adds checked hook sites for a planned project service (slot setter, save, save exit) and what each stock project path (new, delete, clear, paste, format, load, rename) does; finding 148 traces the SHARC filter dispatch (two jump tables bounded at 7). The planned project service keeps per-project digikit data in projects/<slot>-<name>.dkp files, written after a successful stock save and archived, never deleted, when a slot changes hands. A calibration fit turns emulator instruction counts into device cycles from paired profiles. All static or emulator; no new unit run. 2026-11-21 (findings 151-157, plans card-write-guard, track-manager, usb-winusb, syntakt "Hardware bring-up", PATCHING "Flashing a Syntakt"): Syntakt hardware sets. The patched 1.42 image was 32 KB over the 2 MiB upgrade limit, so a core adapter (peer-image) stores the second CPU's section 7 packed and unpacks and hash-checks it in MAIN before it is streamed; a `device-peer` image with only that adapter and the full `device` set boot on the maintainer's unit. The first full image hung at the logo because the Syntakt bootstrap stages MAIN at 0x40200000 (DT2/DN2 0x40400000) and its in-place unpack overran (I183); patchkit now keeps an 8 KiB margin and refuses less. DIGIKIT > MODULES froze the unit because core/ui used Digitakt II key ids (I181); the first store lay beyond the unit's 1.82 GiB card (I182) and is now fixed at 1-1.5 GiB, checked against the driver's capacity. A new adapter card-guard hooks the firmware's eMMC write and erase and refuses requests outside each writer's sectors (on for the Syntakt, emulator-tested), against a stock Data API write that trusts the host's size (SB35). Also: a key-event hook site and the stock View and NameView classes (finding 155) with a planned shortcuts service and a track-manager tool module (host tests only); a WinUSB descriptor hook for the Fast USB interface (built, not yet tested on Windows or a unit); a DN2 unit calibration showing device/emulator SHARC cost factors from 1.01 (ALU) to 2.69 (memory). The public site still does not offer the Syntakt. 2026-11-22 (finding 158, FINDINGS, plans runtime-contract-and-lifecycle and ledgers/device-test-inventory, PATCHING, TESTING, AGENTS): the repository was reorganised (runtime/, services/, image-modules/, ports/; content modules under modules/<kind>/<author>/<name>) and checked byte for byte with a manifest tool. Finding 158, a static survey on DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12 read once, says the ColdFire main OS runs from writable DDR, so almost every hook site and firmware table could be installed by the runtime at load instead of being flashed; the firmware has no indirect-call dispatcher to reuse; on the SHARC no load-time path exists, so 30 voice and effect sites stay flashed. A new plan (one package lifecycle for modules and services) follows from it. A new size gate measured the stored container against the 2,096,640-byte cap: DT2 1.17 1,616,928 B, DN2 1.12 2,028,608 B, Syntakt 1.42 2,102,528 B (5,888 B over; the first planned fix loads the DIGIKIT menu from the card). An inventory lists 105 device-test files that run on emulated units; a smoke set of 8 runs on each of DT2 and DN2. No new unit run. 2026-11-23 (finding 159 new, FINDINGS, plans resident-core-and-system-package, rc2s-1-boundary-inventory, rc3-header-table-v4, observability, runtime-contract-and-lifecycle, device files, ARCHITECTURE, TESTING): finding 159 (static) says the Syntakt image size is bound by the bootstrap's in-place unpack, so the stored literal tail of MAIN is padding, not waste, and no packer setting can beat it. The planned fix splits the runtime into a flashed resident core (about 108 KB) and a system package (about 167 KB) loaded from the card, with a new core-only level. The lfo service now installs its hooks at load; core/lfo left the DT2 and DN2 images. Header table v4 will refuse all older module files. No new unit run.

projects.notes: Tools to inspect, modify and rebuild Digitone firmware (dnfw, CLI and browser), plus 17 mods for Digitone II 1.11 (Waverider wavetable machine, LFO4, arp modes, LFO waves, FX destinations and others), each with a version and a changelog. The ~80% recovery-path stall once listed as open was the MIDI link, not the image (settled 2026-09-11). AGPL-3.0-or-later. The container tools also unpack and rebuild Digitone / Digitone Keys (MKI) OS files (tests use DN1 OS 1.42A; its container is unsigned), and its parameter search on DN1 images is "not yet reliable" per the CLI; there are no mods for the MKI (README and source read 2026-11-11). 2026-11-12 (docs/os-versions.md, issue #382): port to OS 1.12 under way: address maps by instruction anchors decided all 778 mod sites (594 same bytes, 184 relocated), the platform has a 1.12 spec and a 1.12 test image boots in the emulator; every mod is to get a 1.12 build beside its 1.11 build, 1.11 stays the default until all are ported. 2026-11-13 (docs/os-versions.md): stock 1.12 touched no RAM from 0x46700000 up in an emulator run, bootscreen moves to 0x467e8000 on 1.12, the heap arena moves +0x1000 on 1.12 (S22), and lfo4 builds for 1.12 in the emulator. 2026-11-16 (README, docs/sendloop.md, docs/mods-page.md): new mod sendloop rewrites the ColdFire loop that copies each 1,344-word DSP frame into the transfer buffer (4 instead of 7 instructions a word, one 32-bit write instead of two), about 4 points less main-processor load, confirmed on hardware on OS 1.11. Every build now gets a MODS page (SETTINGS > SYSTEM > MODS) that lists the OS, the build name, the tool's commit and each mod's version; its code and rows sit at 0x46798000. 2026-11-18 (README): the sendloop mod is now on by default in builds.

projects.version: Digiwerk v0.3.0 (2026-11-04): multitrack USB audio (USB MULTI/MIDI, 42 inputs, UAC 2.0) in every build and a web patcher; eight non-spring builds released, six spring-reverb builds remain withdrawn; 0.2.0 download withdrawn
projects.tested_note: seven builds ran on real hardware, and the EEEM test build (with the MRB morphing reverb) ran 15 minutes on the author's unit on 2026-11-17; the spring-reverb builds are withdrawn; five other MRB builds are checked in the emulator only (read 2026-11-22)
projects.features: ["3-band master compressor", "flanger, from phaser-like sweep to chorus", "tape echo with three heads", "spring reverb", "new LFO waves", "multichannel USB audio"]
projects.notes: Public lab notebook: notes, tools and new effects, no Elektron firmware included. Seven builds run on real hardware per README (EF01 renamed stock, FLG1 flanger replacing the chorus, FTD1 + one-head tape delay, DH01 core/hook bus with a MIDI test mod, FTN1 renamed screens, GT00 parameter table moved, GT01 + 17 hidden rows for the 3-band compressor); not yet on the unit: the 3-band compressor and a Space-Echo-style delay (fx/spaceecho.c). Rule of the author: "nothing counts as working until it has run on my unit". Getting started (README): macOS on Apple silicon (Linux likely for most), Python 3, the user's own Digitone_II_OS1_12.syx in elektron-firmware/, upstream tools cloned into vendor/ (VENDOR.md) - for digikit and elekloader the author's forks on branch dn2-1.12 (digikit: 1.12 support, audio clock, DIN MIDI, LEDs, live play; elekloader: Digitone II 1.12 profile and the core-dn2 hook bus), commands scripts/dn2-emu-112.sh all, scripts/dn2-live.sh, fx make test/renders, tools/brickcheck/brickcheck CANDIDATE.syx (12 checks, must pass before any flash). README gives no step-by-step flashing procedure. Docs: ROADMAP.md, HANDOFF.md (later entries supersede earlier), FIRMWARE.md (sha256s), VENDOR.md, docs/parameter-table-growth.md, notes/ (one report per task, claims marked [verified] or [inferred]), analysis/ (class hierarchy recovered from RTTI). 28 commits, GPL-2.0(-or-later). 2026-11-22 (HANDOFF, ROADMAP, README, notes/UF01-upstream-fit.md): the EEEM test build ran on the author's unit on 2026-11-17 ("works fine over 15min of building a track"). MRB, a morphing reverb, replaces the shelved spring reverb. Five more MRB combinations pass the brick checker (12/12) and the pack checks, with a worst DSP block of 51-59 % of the frame in sharcvm (the shipped CFTE: 62.8 %); they wait for unit tests before 0.4.0. Two combinations with the tape echo do not fit. UF01 checks Digiwerk on paper against upstream elekloader (core 0.4, machines-dn2 0.5 on OS 1.12): they clash at the same 7 core hook sites, in DSP L1 from 0x2dd600 and in the parameter-table rows from 321; nothing was built. The README and release notes now call Digiwerk a separate project that contributes to Modwerk.

projects.features: ["shared base that the Digi2 machine mods need", "adds room for new machines, parameters and DSP voices; changes nothing on its own"]
projects.notes: Base mod for gdeo607's Digitakt II machine mods; on its own it changes nothing. It keeps irpina's core 1.0 hook bus and adds digikit's machine, parameter and DSP-inline frameworks as core services: added machine types 7-23 and parameter codes 275-338, DSP voices as relocatable objects placed in free DSP L2, a second SRC page with four saved, p-lockable controls (stored in the sound record's spare slots 77 and 78; such projects still load on the stock OS), and since 2.6 a pattern service that reads and edits trigs and locks through the firmware's own editors. Building needs an elekloader with `sharc_raw` support for the Digitakt II (a branch of gdeo607's elekloader fork, proposed upstream). Do not flash 2.4, 2.5 or 2.6: they crash the unit at boot (I67).

projects.version: v0.70 INKEY (tag, 2026-11-22): ARP OFS IN SCALE (arp offsets count degrees of the track's KB SETUP scale) and in-key track transpose ([KEYBOARD] + [FUNC] + [+]/[-], -7..+7 degrees, kept per track in each pattern), w-winter's arpscale and degreetranspose from dn2-firmware-explore applied byte for byte; PERFORM macros now move every voice playing their track. v0.69 PERFORM (tag, 2026-11-21): eight performance macros after the Analog Four MKII ([MOD] + [FX]), each adding an offset to up to five parameters on any tracks, saved per project, PERF MUTE; MACHINE SEL refuses a machine that would take the kit past a DSP limit. v0.68 ICONS (tag, 2026-11-21): MACHINE SEL shows the mod machine's icon and name; FLEX takes back to +24 dB for track takes, +24 dB for MAIN and IN takes. v0.67 MIDIARP (tag, 2026-11-21): the arpeggiator on MIDI tracks, each arp step sent as a MIDI note (upstream dnfw's midiarp). v0.66 NXT (2026-11-20): a slide lasts until the track's next trig (the new default), FM+ DYN FUNC + turn jumps to whole ratios, FLEX takes of MAIN and IN played +12 dB. v0.65 BANKS (2026-11-20): PROJECT RAM in four banks A-D (508 slots), FLEX track takes at +12 dB instead of +24, an optimal packer frees about 87 KB. v0.64 HOLD (2026-11-20): PTN + KEYBOARD sustains every track. v0.63 FLEXLEVEL (tag, 2026-11-19): a FLEX take of a single track plays at the level heard (+24 dB built in), and saving a FLEX buffer no longer normalises it. v0.62 SLICE (2026-11-19): the slice editor plays edits live, follows the slice that plays, zooms to 128 frames and snaps to zero crossings. v0.61 MICROTUNING (2026-11-19): a tuning per project, switched per track from KB SETUP's H knob. v0.60 FIXES, v0.59 FMPLUS (2026-11-18); v0.58 SCALES (2026-11-17) was pulled after a crash in a chord MODE
projects.tested_note: gated in the emulator (v0.48 adds a first gate step with ColdFire and DSP emulated together); units ran v0.44-v0.47: v0.44 froze (I65), BOUNCE recorded nothing or never played back (I66), a user's v0.47 dropped a sample voice block by block under load (I71); v0.48's fine controls and v0.49's FLEX are not verified on hardware (release notes); a user's old project silenced every track on v0.48 (I73, not reproduced); v0.50's track level is calibrated only in the emulator, which has no master path, and testers are asked to report the GAIN that matches; v0.51's lighter machines and v0.52's MUTE SRC are not verified on hardware (release notes); v0.53 fixes two faults a tester saw on a unit with v0.52 (BUF locks ignored, page LEDs stuck), gated in the emulator; v0.58 crashed a tester's unit in a chord MODE and was pulled (I138); v0.63's +24 dB FLEX gain was the owner's by-ear match, and a tester's measurement on v0.63 showed it 12 dB too high (I185; v0.65 uses +12); v0.64-v0.67 are gated in the emulator (CLEARED TO FLASH) with no unit result yet; v0.67's MIDI-track arp is upstream's work, tested on upstream's unit on 2026-09-17, not yet on this project's unit (FIRMWARE.md, read 2026-11-21); v0.68-v0.69 are gated in the emulator (CLEARED TO FLASH, 2026-11-21) with no unit result; v0.68 returns to +24 dB FLEX levels after the owner's measurement on v0.67, against the tester's I185 figure (O48); the DSP limit's machine weights come from the SHARC runner, not from hardware (read 2026-11-22)
projects.features: ["PERFORM: eight performance macros after the Analog Four MKII, each moving up to five parameters on any tracks, saved per project", "Digitakt II sample machines: ONESHOT, WERP, STRETCH, REPITCH, GRID, SLICE", "sample browser and recorder", "PERC: 34 Machinedrum machines (TRX, EFM, GND, P-I)", "Monomachine voices, polyphonic: SID 6581, DPRO WAVE, DDRW, DENS, VO-6, FM+ STAT / PAR / DYN", "microtuning: a tuning per project (just, historical, Arabic Rast, Poole and 8 of your own), on or off per track", "FLEX: live-buffer machine with recorder trigs (record a track, the input or the main mix), with GAIN and a level meter", "CPU guard that keeps the unit responsive, and a DSP limit in MACHINE SEL"]
projects.notes: Adds Digitakt II sample machines (ONESHOT, WERP, STRETCH, REPITCH, GRID, SLICE) with sample browser and recorder, PERC (34 Machinedrum machines incl. TRX, EFM, GND, P-I), Monomachine voices (SID 6581, DPRO WAVE/DDRW/DENS, VO-6) and a CPU guard. Browser-based patcher builds from the user's own files ("nothing is uploaded") and saves only if the output sha256 matches a build that passed scripts/ship_gate.py. Hardware: README says verification is pending per version; FIRMWARE.md says nearly every v0.21-v0.33 entry was checked in emulators and "not seen on hardware yet". Main open problem: DSP time (heavy voices cut sound). Flashing a 1.12 unit takes it back to a 1.11 base, projects saved under the newer OS may not open. 1,491 commits, 8 stars, AGPL-3.0-or-later. FIRMWARE.md says built firmware is kept on the repo's `builds` branch (not main) - unlike most projects here, which only ship patchers; we link only to the repo and docs, not to builds. Withdrawn builds: v0.4-v0.7 (oversized image). v0.38 (2026-11-02): Direct Jump state kept in its own +Drive sector (0x6FF000); per-project sample lists at +Drive 0x6D0000-0x6E02FF, two checked copies each. Root cause of the silent new samples: the DSP plays a pool slot only below the directory's count, and live adds did not update the count. v0.39 (2026-11-03): recordings had kept only ~2 ms since v0.38 because the DSP recorder took words 2-4 of every new link command as source, channel and threshold, and v0.38 sent a check command at every take's start; now only the recorder's own commands set them. 2026-11-15: the first test build, v0.54-t1 STEREO, is announced as a GitHub pre-release on the owner's request and listed under TEST in the patcher, not as the latest. Testers are asked to check hard-panned stereo files on headphones, filters and overdrive on both sides, and a fifth voice falling back to the mono mix. Next: stereo comb filters and sends, and the stock NAME screen for sample names. 2026-11-16 (FIRMWARE.md, release notes v0.54-v0.56): each build passed its gate in the emulator (54-56 gate steps) and is cleared to flash; unit results for these three builds are not reported yet. A DDRW sound saved with BR above 0 sounds grittier from v0.56. 2026-11-17 (FIRMWARE.md, releases/v0.57, docs/flex-pool.md): v0.57 FLEXMUTE is gated (56 gate steps) and cleared. It answers a tester's unit report on v0.55/v0.56: MUTE SRC muted the source as soon as a take existed, and some tracks could not be unmuted until a power cycle. Now the SRC track drops out only while a FLEX voice has its note on and is heard, and comes back about 0.2 s after the note ends; known issue: a long gap between FLEX notes un-mutes the source. FLEX takes still measure about 6 dB below their source (to be fixed). The v0.54-t1 STEREO test build was taken off the patcher's list because stereo samples do not play yet (altstrument, 2026-11-16). Planned next: microtonal scales in KB SETUP and a one-handed keyboard latch. 2026-11-18 (FIRMWARE.md, releases/v0.58): v0.58 SCALES added two microtonal scales to KB SETUP (PR12, a 12-note just tuning laid out as Chromatic; PM12, its 7-note minor laid out as Aeolian), retuning each voice by cents above ROOT. It passed its 57-step gate but crashed a unit in a chord MODE and was pulled from the patcher on 2026-11-17; the code is reverted on main, a fix is on a branch. Withdrawn builds now: v0.4-v0.7 (oversized image), v0.58 (crash). Planned next: MON on the recorder, the Monomachine FM+ machines, a per-track 4-band EQ, arp scale lock and in-key transpose. 2026-11-19 (FIRMWARE.md, releases v0.60-v0.61, docs/microtuning.md): v0.59 adds the Monomachine FM+ machines and MON on the recorder; testers found the FM+ knobs on the wrong parameters (I157), fixed in v0.60 together with GRID's ALLOCATE SLICE RANDOM, whose NO had put the old locks back. v0.61 adds microtuning: 12 offsets in tenths of a cent above ROOT, applied voice by voice in the audio interrupt from a double-buffered snapshot, never through stock's scale tables (so v0.58's crash cannot return); SLICE and GRID tracks, MIDI tracks and MIDI out are never retuned. The tuning is saved per project in its own +Drive sectors (two copies at 0x6E0400 + 2p + c, region 0x6E0400-0x6E04FF), two seconds after the last change and before LOAD or NEW. Known issue: ERASE MOD DATA does not clear the tunings yet. Both builds are gated (CLEARED TO FLASH); no unit result yet. Planned next: the SLICE editor, then a per-track 4-band EQ and arp scale lock; DT2 presets are on hold. 2026-11-20 (FIRMWARE.md, releases v0.62-v0.63, docs/sampler.md, docs/kbhold.md): v0.62 SLICE answers user requests for EDIT SLICE POINTS (edits heard 0.2 s after the knobs rest without YES, a played note selects its slice, zoom down to 128 frames read from the +Drive, FUNC + START/END snaps to a zero crossing within 512 frames) and lets CREATE SLICE GRID jump 2/4/8/16/32/64 with FUNC + E. v0.63 FLEXLEVEL: on the owner's unit a single-track FLEX take needed GAIN +24 to match its source by ear, so +24 dB is now built in (tracks already boosted get 24 dB hotter; MAIN and IN takes are still quieter than heard); saving a FLEX buffer had normalised the very take still playing, now it is kept as recorded. Both gated (CLEARED TO FLASH). The firmware is nearly full: a keyboard HOLD (PTN + KEYBOARD, planned at UI level only) does not fit the 2 MiB image yet and the per-track EQ is dropped for now; arp scale lock is next. 2026-11-21 (FIRMWARE.md, releases v0.64-v0.67, docs/banks.md, docs/packer.md, docs/midiarp.md, docs/kbhold.md): v0.64 HOLD makes PTN + KEYBOARD a sustain pedal on all 16 tracks through stock's own MIDI CC 64 sustain, so held keys, MIDI in and the arp latch; it fit only after the start-up animation was cut to every other frame (291 bytes left). v0.65 BANKS spreads PROJECT RAM over banks A-D (508 slots, still one 400 MB pool, the bank kept in SAMP's free low byte, new +Drive regions per project); a tester measured v0.63's +24 dB FLEX gain 12 dB too high, so v0.65 uses +12 (I185); an optimal aPLib packer, checked against the bootstrap's own depacker, frees about 87 KB. v0.66 NXT: a slide with no SLEN lock now lasts until the track's next trig (old patterns change), FM+ DYN FUNC + turn jumps 1FRQ / 2FRQ to whole ratios, and FLEX takes of MAIN and IN are recorded unchanged and played +12 dB (a saved take plays 12 dB quieter). v0.67 MIDIARP merges upstream dnfw's MIDI-track arp. All four gated (CLEARED TO FLASH), no unit result yet. Planned next: arp scale lock and a voice/load guardrail; DT2 presets on hold. 2026-11-22 (FIRMWARE.md, releases v0.68-v0.69, docs/perform.md, docs/guardrail.md, ROADMAP): v0.68 shows each mod machine's icon and name in MACHINE SEL by changing two stock instructions. On v0.67 (pattern volume 100, compressor off) the owner found FLEX takes needed 12 dB more, so v0.68 builds in +24 dB again for track takes and also for MAIN and IN takes; a tester had measured that same +24 as 12 dB too loud (I185, O48). v0.69 PERFORM adds eight macros A-H, each an offset on top of the sound's value, LFOs and locks, with up to five track and parameter targets and a depth of -64..+63, saved per project in the mod's +Drive sectors; turning a macro is not recorded into patterns yet, and ERASE PROJECT does not clear the macros. v0.69's DSP limit gives every mod machine a weight measured on the SHARC runner, and MACHINE SEL refuses a machine that would take the kit past 320,000 cycles (roughly three VO-6, two DENS, seven PERC or eleven sample tracks); stock machines weigh nothing and older kits load as they are. Planned next: arp scale lock and in-key transpose, a Machinedrum/Monomachine engine rewrite, then a keyframe stretch. 2026-11-23 (FIRMWARE.md, releases/v0.70, docs/inkey.md, THIRD-PARTY.md): v0.70 applies two upstream mods by w-winter (dn2-firmware-explore pull requests #212, #214, #278; AGPL-3.0) byte for byte as 25 edits plus two code chunks at 0x467A8000 and 0x467B8000; the arp toggle byte is 0x405CD8AF, the degree offset sits in bits 2..5 of a track's pattern byte +1187. Upstream reports both working on units (2026-10); here the gate checks the arp and degree notes in the ColdFire emulator, not the [+]/[-] keys. The PERFORM fix answers a user report on v0.69: macros wrote block t for track t, but the mirror's blocks are voices; each target now moves every voice the voice-to-track table (0x80005308) gives its track. A pattern with degrees saved on stock loses them.

projects.name: digitone-2-modding-skill
projects.author: complex-ping
projects.base_os: Digitone II OS 1.11 (user supplies the .syx; repo gives a SHA-256 prefix to check it)
projects.notes: Agent skill (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor; install with `npx skills add`) for developing Digitone II firmware mods: ColdFire MAIN OS patching in C, SHARC DSP audio code, verification in two emulators (digikit + a whole-DSP SHARC emulator), rebuild/re-sign/flash over USB. Encodes stock-firmware addresses, hook sites, the ColdFire-to-DSP frame format, free memory and "hardware rules the emulators cannot check, which each once silenced a real unit" - read on 2026-10-31 via SKILL.md and references/*.md (SKILL.md has 20 rules incl. whole 32-byte boot blocks, stock encodings only, no L2 above 0x200B0000, never read unwritten DDR, 2 MiB image / section 7 under 1 MiB, stop after two failed flashes; scripts include hwrules.py, shapecheck.py, encodecheck.py, bootblocks.py, sim.py/simc.py, cfmod.py, rpc_flash.py). Facts and rules are folded into hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md and hardware/common/agent-workflow.md. Note: tree pages are blocked for our fetcher by robots.txt; the blob pages were readable. Examples: double_time (sequencer clock hook), track_trim (-6 dB on track 1). Needs Python 3.11+, dnfw, m68k GCC, digikit. MIT (digikit-derived files GPL-2.0), 2 commits, 10 stars. Overtone was built with it. Closest existing relative of this repo's hardware/ folder.

projects.name: coldfire-rs
projects.author: FirestormAudio
projects.base_os: not firmware-specific; targets the NXP ColdFire V4e chips MCF54410 and MCF54415-MCF54418
projects.notes: Rust stack for ColdFire V4e (MCF5441x): toolchain (rustc_codegen_gcc + libgccjit for m68k-elf), runtime, PAC generated from an SVD, and an Embassy HAL (GPIO, PIT, INTC, eDMA, UART, DSPI, eSDHC eMMC block reads, SSI/I2S, USB OTG device mode). Not an emulator and not an Elektron mod: the README never mentions Elektron or digikit, the only link is the topic tag "digitakt". It is relevant here because digikit names the MCF54415 as the control CPU of Digitakt II (and the Digitone II is described as ColdFire too). Drivers were run on the author's own MCF54415 board. README: API is young and may change before 1.0. 33 commits, Apache-2.0 OR MIT. Same owner also has deluge-sdk (Synthstrom Deluge, out of scope). Org shows no public members; no relation to ElekLabs/Em D found.

projects.name: digi-roll-studio
projects.author: zooloo303
projects.base_os: hardware-verified: Digitakt II 1.16 (0079), Digitone II 1.11 (0059), Analog Four 1.55D (0201); the numbers in parentheses are the OS build numbers the units report in their identity reply (test fixtures firmware-2026-09-09, read 2026-11-18)
projects.notes: Native Rust desktop sequencer for Digitakt II, Digitone II and Analog Four, built from digi-roll. Writes to hardware: README recommends throwaway projects. Safe-write ceremony of five rules (re-read and back up the destination pattern first, OS build on an allowlist, user confirmation, change only needed bytes, read back and byte-compare). Gen-2 dump protocol (digis) vs gen-1 (Analog Four). +Drive file-write commands 0x57/0x58/0x59 hardware-verified for a single chunk only, not called by the app (writes above 16 KiB refused); 0x5A/0x5B/0x5C (move/copy/delete) not implemented. Protocol code ported from elk-herd (BSD-2, (c) mzero). Fixtures: 34 real .syx dumps. 124 commits, GPL-3.0-or-later. Not firmware modding. Windows/Linux write testing incomplete.

projects.name: digitone-syx-toolkit
projects.author: emnyeca
projects.notes: Python CLI (+ Tkinter GUI) to capture, replay, diff and hex-view SysEx, and to generate Digitone II PATTERN .syx from an empty template. README (Japanese) says Digitone II only. Hardware-validated: pattern-wide mode, tracks 1-8, steps 1-128, normal trigs, pitch, velocity, length (inherit/explicit/INF), tempo/speed/total steps, import/send. Not supported: chords, track-default rewriting, condition/probability/micro timing/retrig, non-destructive editing. Length encoding per README: inherit = 0xFF, explicit INF = 0x7F, finite 0x00..0x7E. 47 commits, licence not shown.

projects.name: digitakt-midi-mcp
projects.author: feamster
projects.base_os: Digitakt II; README points to the manual (OS 1.03) Appendix B for the full CC map
projects.notes: MCP server to control a Digitakt II over MIDI (notes, CC, NRPN, transport, raw SysEx) over USB with Overbridge. Includes nrpn_constants.py (full NRPN list per README) and tests that need the physical unit; mappings rest on the manual and the author's code, no independent verification claimed. SysEx tools are experimental and "best-guess" - the README says Elektron has not published the pattern SysEx format. MIT, 46 commits, 11 stars. One of the few agent-facing Elektron tools; relevant model for how an agent can talk to a unit.

projects.name: elk-herd
projects.author: mzero
projects.notes: "Elektron device manager". Browser app in Elm for Digitakt and Digitakt II content over Web MIDI: whole-project transfer to and from device and files, reordering of patterns, sample pool and sound pool, renaming (altstrument 2026-11-03; development continues off GitHub, we do not link the new source location). Other projects call it the de-facto public documentation of Elektron's SysEx protocol (digi-roll-studio) and port its 7-bit SysEx codec and F0 00 20 3C framing (SYXGRID). BSD-2-Clause per those projects. The GitHub page is a stub: README says the project has migrated away from GitHub to an obfuscated address (not decoded by us) and that issues and pull requests generated by AI will be summarily rejected - do not open AI-generated ones. Device support is not stated on the stub; SYXGRID says elk-herd does not support the Digitone family; the Digitakt II entry is an inference from digi-roll (which ports its protocol for DT2/DN2). 70 stars.

projects.name: SyntHack OS (upstream)
projects.author: Angelo-politek
projects.version: v0.9.0 (2026-10-19) per altstrument; README text said v0.8.0
projects.features: ["bus compressor with meter", "dual mono input", "readable parameter values (Hz, dB, ms, %)", "performance effects incl. beat repeat", "third send effect: chorus, flanger, phaser or crusher", "custom boot splash"]
projects.notes: Unofficial modular patch set for the Syntakt: master compressor (THR/ATK/REL/MUP/RAT with meter, saved per pattern or global), dual-mono external input levels, boot splash, readable parameter values (Hz, dB, ms, %), beat repeat (v0.6.0), third send FX SND3 into chorus/flanger/phaser/crusher (v0.8.0). Mod area: 64 KB RAM, stored compressed and unpacked at boot. Each mods/<name>/patch.json lists the patch location, a hash of the expected original bytes and the new bytes; tools/build/build.py refuses the wrong OS, overlapping patches and protected sections. tools/emu is a ColdFire emulator (Unicorn + EMAC model); every mod is tested there before flashing. A git hook (tools/hooks) blocks firmware files from commits - a practice worth copying. README: seven mods running on real hardware (v0.8.0); RECOVERY.md exists. Planned: PIN lock, new LFO shapes, 3rd LFO/mod matrix, arpeggiator, resampling, new machines (RISER/DOWNFILTER, SY SWARM+), web builder. MIT, 66 commits, 9 stars. Brick-risk flag set on altstrument. Fork "Syntakt MAX" is the synthack-os entry.
