facts.section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / ARP locks and MPE on the A4 MK1 (OS 1.56, ClaidArremer, 2026-11-15/16)
facts.text: Free per-step lock slots 101-108: the pattern already saves them and clears them the stock way, so ARP p-locks need no new storage. Stock writes p-locks through a temporary sound that has room only for sound parameters, so locks of ARP values must be written and shown straight from the pattern's lock words (0015 v0.1 went through the stock routines and never stored them). `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / ARP locks and MPE on the A4 MK1 (OS 1.56, ClaidArremer, 2026-11-15/16)
facts.text: The arpeggiator reads its settings through five `adda.l #0x4096ff52` (its track-data base); 0015 detours them to a per-track copy with the locked values in. `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / ARP locks and MPE on the A4 MK1 (OS 1.56, ClaidArremer, 2026-11-15/16)
facts.text: Empty knobs on the ARP page: knobs I and J have descriptor ids 9 and 10 with stock value 0; 0015 puts knob J on the blank placeholder parameter id 277 (`0x115`), a 4-byte patch at `0x40195050` (expect `00000000`). The knob draw's graphic call at `0x400231ec` (6 bytes, `20522f0c2f0b`) draws LEGATO's on/off switch for graphic id 15. `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / ARP locks and MPE on the A4 MK1 (OS 1.56, ClaidArremer, 2026-11-15/16)
facts.text: Kit-saved mod bytes: `0006-fx-slot` saves the FX track's spare storage with the kit; 0013-mpe's kit switch is byte 52 there (nonzero = on). The removed SLD switch used byte 26 + 6t + 5 for track t. `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / elekloader's lock service and 0.8 events on the MKII (core-a4mk2 0.5-0.8, OS 1.56, 2026-11-05/16)
facts.text: Mod parameter p-locks work beside stock's: set, copied, cleared, saved, loaded and played with Param Slide, RANDOMIZE, CONTROL IN, poly locks, another kit layout and an NRPN with a trig held; the value read matched stock's engine copy of a stock parameter on synth, FX and CV tracks. Not yet checked: track clear, SysEx dump out and in, a kit change's and CREATE NEW's clear of locks, a fine parameter, a sound-locked trig's pool sound. `[hw]`

facts.section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / elekloader's lock service and 0.8 events on the MKII (core-a4mk2 0.5-0.8, OS 1.56, 2026-11-05/16)
facts.text: Audio interrupt frame: vector 191 (`0x401013be`); its only exit uses a frame of `0xec` bytes (the Rytm's is `0xb4`). The Rytm's menu-item routines match on the A4 with addresses masked (`OP_NEW` `0x400653b8`, `ITEM_CTOR` `0x4005c7c4`, `MENU_ADD` `0x4005bffa`); the A4 has no manager for the Rytm's function-pointer type, and `0x40164940` is the only one with that code. `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / elekloader's lock service and 0.8 events on the MKII (core-a4mk2 0.5-0.8, OS 1.56, 2026-11-05/16)
facts.text: 0.8 on a unit (2026-11-16): the track-key event and the voice and SOUND SETUP events ran with two test mods. `[hw]`

facts.section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / elekloader's +Drive loader and new checks on the MKII (drive-loader-a4mk2 0.1, core-a4mk2 0.9, OS 1.56, 2026-11-14/17)
facts.text: The +Drive has no file system on 1.56: stock keeps it as raw 512-byte sectors under one slot store, with 128 project slots and 4,096 sound slots at fixed sectors and the power-off image at sectors `0x7a000` and `0x7c000` (the Rytm's slots too). Sectors `0x3000..0x7a000` (about 238 MiB) are addressed by no stock code and survive FORMAT +DRIVE (watched through boots, saves, loads, Data transfers and a format). drive-loader-a4mk2 keeps its store there: two directory copies of 320 sectors at `0x3000` and `0x3140` (header written last, so a torn write leaves the older copy), a scratch sector at `0x3280`, files from `0x3288` in runs aligned to 4 KB. `[emu]`

facts.section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / elekloader's +Drive loader and new checks on the MKII (drive-loader-a4mk2 0.1, core-a4mk2 0.9, OS 1.56, 2026-11-14/17)
facts.text: Raw sector I/O: read `0x400721a6`, write `0x40072376`; each takes the card mutex and goes through stock's DMA buffer. A write of part of a sector writes the buffer's leftovers after it, so write whole sectors only. `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / elekloader's +Drive loader and new checks on the MKII (drive-loader-a4mk2 0.1, core-a4mk2 0.9, OS 1.56, 2026-11-14/17)
facts.text: Stock's +Drive block writer swallows the footer of a multi-chunk upload: the write at `0x4001d9fc` takes at most the larger of the bytes still to write and the bytes still to accept; with up to a sector left in its ring between chunks, the last chunk also takes the data container's 12-byte footer, and WriteClose refuses the upload ("Footer was not processed"). A one-chunk upload closes. The loader's 2-byte site at `0x4001da16` makes the bound always the bytes still to accept; a write that fits behaves as before. Traced: an 18,466-byte upload in three chunks had 481 bytes in the ring at its last chunk. `[emu]` (2026-11-15)

facts.section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / elekloader's +Drive loader and new checks on the MKII (drive-loader-a4mk2 0.1, core-a4mk2 0.9, OS 1.56, 2026-11-14/17)
facts.text: Data routes: the route resolver's getter site is `0x40095ec8`; the handler add `0x40019596` moves one owning pointer (the Rytm copies a shared_ptr). An entry's slots: `+0x1c` sees the upload's payload size first, `+0x3c` runs just before stock makes the +Drive writer, `+0x6c` checks the header, `+0x4c` runs only after every byte was written and the content hash passed, and cannot refuse. Each std::function slot holds its own copy of the closure, so per-upload state must live outside it. `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / elekloader's +Drive loader and new checks on the MKII (drive-loader-a4mk2 0.1, core-a4mk2 0.9, OS 1.56, 2026-11-14/17)
facts.text: Boot hook: core-a4mk2's `ev_boot_drive` runs in main() at `0x401061e8`, before the boot project load `0x400f1b18`, the audio interrupt and the UI (not on a factory boot); SD init's result is at `0x41865e98` (0 = ok). `ev_drive_format` runs in FORMAT +DRIVE after the slot erases. `[doc]`

facts.text: Boot contract: The bootstrap unpacks MAIN to `0x40000400`, sets VBR = `0x40000000` and calls the word at `0x40000400` as an entry function pointer with one stack argument. It is not a reset SP/PC header. The stock entry sets SP to `0x48000000`, fills 256 vectors, sets up INTC/GPIO and caches (CACR `0xa50ce100`), then starts the kernel. `[hw]` (a from-source replacement OS booted on a unit)

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Platform (MKII, OS 1.74)
facts.text: Which ColdFire is open: rytm-fw-re builds with `-mcpu=54455` (MCF5445x), while analog-emu identifies the Rytm MKII as MCF5441x (same entry code, CACR/ACR values and peripheral blocks as the A4 MKII). Both are V4 cores with EMAC and no FPU, so code built for either runs; peripheral addresses are what to check. See CONFLICTS O14. `[?]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Platform (MKII, OS 1.74)
facts.text: A 16.3 MB unreferenced hole at `0x41ad0000` passed a memory probe on a unit (7 candidate regions all passed). `[hw]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Flash and recovery
facts.text: SPI NOR on DSPI `0xfc05c000`; layout: `0x00000-0x7FFFF` bootstrap + FPGA (never write), `0x80000+` the MAIN OS image. Images are staged in DDR at `0x3FF80008` with the same `size / checksum (i ^ word[i])` header as the small boxes. `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Flash and recovery
facts.text: The bootstrap supports several flash vendors and picks the geometry from the RDID: | Vendor | Page | Erase block | |---|---|---| | Spansion `0x01 2018` | 0x200 | 0x40000 | | Winbond `0xEF` | 0x100 | 0x10000 | | Macronix `0xC2` | 0x100 | 0x10000 | | ISSI `0x9D` | 0x100 | 0x10000 | | EON `0x1C` | 0x100 | 0x10000 | The geometry therefore differs per unit. This very likely explains the two geometries reported for DT2/DN2 (CONFLICTS O8) and why a Spansion-only protection command does nothing on a Winbond unit (O9). `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Flash and recovery
facts.text: The bootstrap also gates on a version-date field (image +0x10, 4 ASCII chars) per chip family, and refuses older versions. `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Flash and recovery
facts.text: Recovery is FUNC at power-on, OS UPGRADE, DIN MIDI only. The startup-menu receiver never enumerates USB (verified: no USB events while it shows READY TO RECEIVE). USB updates are received only by the running OS. Once a custom OS that does not implement the USB update is on the unit, the only way back is DIN ("one USB shot per custom-OS cycle"). `[hw]` rytm-fw-re rebuilt a DIN sender from an FT232RL (2 x 200 ohm) and streamed stock 1.74 back in about 10 minutes. `[hw]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Flash and recovery
facts.text: Rule for every device: a replacement or heavily modified OS should keep the in-OS USB update working, or the user needs a DIN interface. See rule A36 in [`../AGENT-RULES.md`](../AGENT-RULES.md).

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Analog Rytm MK1 (OS 1.73 / 1.74)
facts.text: Board (static analysis, `[doc]`): same CPU family and OS framework as the MKII; ELE2 file with one section (MAIN OS); 128 MB DDR, boot/config flash as parallel NOR on FlexBus CS0 (8 MB at 0); voice SPI on DSPI2 with eDMA ch 29 (492-word frame, as the MKII); codec on SSI0 + SSI1 (8 words each); 122x32 LCD, 1-bit LEDs; USB full speed only.

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Analog Rytm MK1 (OS 1.73 / 1.74)
facts.text: The bootstrap is inside MAIN OS, as on the A4 MK1 (rule A38): On 1.74 its version words are at `0x4028c768` and its image at `0x4028c770..0x402a1b84` (87,068 B, ending in its USB descriptors). On 1.73 the same image sat 0x60 lower. At every boot the startup code compares that version with the one in flash at `0x1fff8`. If the embedded one is newer, the OS shows BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE and rewrites the bootstrap sectors. `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Analog Rytm MK1 (OS 1.73 / 1.74)
facts.text: Container pitfall: elektron-firmware-tool padded ELE2 containers to 2 bytes; the stock MK1 file pads to 4. A "no change" rebuild therefore came out 2 bytes short and failed the null-repack check. hugz202 patches the tool to pad to 4. Always run a null repack of the stock file first (rule A23). `[hw]` ([I40](../INCIDENTS.md#i40-a-no-change-rebuild-came-out-2-bytes-short))

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Analog Rytm MK1 (OS 1.73 / 1.74)
facts.text: Load (measured with a probe build on a MK1, OS 1.73): Stock audio alone is about 77 % of the CPU with nothing playing. One readout showed CPU 78.3 %, the audio interrupt at 61.2 % average and 74.0 % peak. With a first chorus-plus-comb send on, the CPU reached 100 %. The CPU runs at roughly 120 MIPS. A one-to-one port of the A4's chorus (~8,000-9,000 instructions per block) would cost ~10 % of the unit and was rejected. Same lesson as A34: replace work, and keep added effects idle when no track sends. `[hw]` Idle mods add up (Modwerk, 2026-11-06, OS 1.74, sequencer stopped, block timed on DTIM0): in a 16-module set the idle block took 72.9 %; making three modules return early when they have nothing to do (Ping Pong Loop's voice gates in stock's sample prefetch, Sample Playback Rate's block handler, QPERF) brought it to 70.6-71.1 %. Each module's idle path is part of the budget. `[hw]` {modwerk-rytm-idle} ([I49](../INCIDENTS.md#i49-idle-paths-of-sixteen-mods-cost-two-percent-of-a-rytm-block))

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Analog Rytm MK1 (OS 1.73 / 1.74)
facts.text: Cached vs uncached DRAM: the chorus's delay line moved to a cached DRAM address (`0x428a0000`) in v2. The same rule applies as on the A4 MK1: don't touch uncached memory per sample. `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Analog Rytm MK1 (OS 1.73 / 1.74)
facts.text: RAM is not cleared at power-up in the regions the mods use: clear your own buffers before use. `[hw]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Analog Rytm MK1 (OS 1.73 / 1.74)
facts.text: Dead code to reuse: The machine table (53 entries at `0x402543d0` on 1.73) holds 19 hidden machines whose voice-mask byte is 0, so no list offers them. They look like earlier development versions of the shipped machines, and none has been played on hardware. TEST machines (SD/RS/CY/CB) also exist. hugz202 reuses their code space. Its only reference is its own table entry, which the mod repoints, and the build checks the stock bytes. A kit received over SysEx that names a hidden machine then plays the mod's machine or nothing. `[hw]` (the `full` image ran on a MK1)

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Mod machines in hidden slots (MKII OS 1.74, elekloader core-ar2 0.5; Modwerk's SDK guide, 2026-11-05)

Their records carry no MIDI, so core copies each used knob's CC and NRPN from slot 35's record at the same sound index; the records' list-kind word (+0x24) stays 0, so a knob there is not offered as an LFO, velocity or aftertouch destination. facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Mod machines in hidden slots (MKII OS 1.74, elekloader core-ar2 0.5; Modwerk's SDK guide, 2026-11-05)

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Mod machines in hidden slots (MKII OS 1.74, elekloader core-ar2 0.5; Modwerk's SDK guide, 2026-11-05)
facts.text: Fixed knob positions per slot (SYNTH page, sound indices): slot 40 A10 B13 C12 D11 / E14 F16 G15 H9; slot 41 A10 B13 C15 D11 / E16 F14 G12 H9; slot 42 A10 B12 C13 D11 / E16 F14 G15 H9. `knobs[k]` in `machines.h` is sound index 9 + k, not the panel order. Indices 9 (LEV), 10 (TUN) and 11 (DEC) keep stock's MIDI CCs. `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Mod machines in hidden slots (MKII OS 1.74, elekloader core-ar2 0.5; Modwerk's SDK guide, 2026-11-05)
facts.text: Where it appears in the machine list: a 34-byte section table at `0x40257d70` (read by `0x400df664`) files stock machines 0-33 under a section; slots 34+ have no entry and sort above every stock machine of their group. A machine with `home` -1 lands after DISABLE in slot order. Core 0.5 adds a 4-byte entry (slot, section, 0, 0) so a mod machine sits under its section's header. The SY comparators (`0x400bdc5e`, `0x400bde1c`) rank only SY DUAL VCO, SY CHIP and SY RAW, so a mod SY machine sorts after them. `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Mod machines in hidden slots (MKII OS 1.74, elekloader core-ar2 0.5; Modwerk's SDK guide, 2026-11-05)
facts.text: Driving a dual-oscillator voice (BD, SD, RS; control frame `0x800063c0`, TUNE1/TUNE2/LEVEL1/LEVEL2 at `+90`, `+98`, `+106`, as SY RAW `0x4011aa4c` writes them). Measured on a unit: A tune word is 16 x Hz after stock's trim `0x401197f4`. Write it every block and force it on the trig; without that the oscillator crawls at a few Hz. Below about 40 Hz oscillator 1 runs sharp and oscillator 2 flat. A LEVEL word acts within its block. Its loud end saturates mostly after AMP VOL, so it is not a drive control. An amp record at -128 still passes about -45 dB: write the LEVELs to 0 when a note ends. `[hw]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Mod machines in hidden slots (MKII OS 1.74, elekloader core-ar2 0.5; Modwerk's SDK guide, 2026-11-05)
facts.text: FUNC + turn drops its first detent on the sound page (flag `0x417e32b8`); jumps come from a std::function in the parameter's RAM record (`0x419a4888 + 84 * id`, manager `+0x4c`, invoker `+0x50`). `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / More from the MKII mod and research projects (rytm-mods-src OS 1.73, analog-rytm-mkii-research OS 1.72)
facts.text: A zero run is not a free cave until it survives a hard run on the unit. octatrack-mods had shipped code into a region that came from someone else's survey. The mod worked with the sequencer stopped and failed during playback, because the region was really `.bss` that the audio engine wrote. rytm-mods-src's check: fill the candidate with a known pattern, flash, run playback, sampling, Overbridge and +Drive access, then read it back. See rule A43. `[hw]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / More from the MKII mod and research projects (rytm-mods-src OS 1.73, analog-rytm-mkii-research OS 1.72)
facts.text: Pick the narrowest assembler target that assembles. The project went from `-mcpu=5407` (ISA_A) to `-mcpu=5475` (ISA_B + EMAC) only when a mod needed EMAC, and checked that the earlier mods rebuilt byte-identically. Too narrow a target fails at assembly time; too wide a one silently accepts instructions the chip lacks (rule A42). `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / More from the MKII mod and research projects (rytm-mods-src OS 1.73, analog-rytm-mkii-research OS 1.72)
facts.text: Sections 5, 2, 1 and 8 must come back byte-identical, and the bootstrap (section 2, 42,302 B at `0x07020000`) is checked by hash. Elektron's own bootstrap upgrade, which runs on the first restart after some OS updates, is the one moment the safety net is down: don't cut power then. `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / More from the MKII mod and research projects (rytm-mods-src OS 1.73, analog-rytm-mkii-research OS 1.72)
facts.text: The master compressor is analog (after the analog mix and the master distortion). The MKII firmware never reads its gain back (the MK1 did, through the on-chip ADC input AN1), so any gain-reduction display on the MKII is an estimate. A CC beyond an enumeration's last value makes the unit show ERR instead of clamping. `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / More from the MKII mod and research projects (rytm-mods-src OS 1.73, analog-rytm-mkii-research OS 1.72)
facts.text: Sample bit reduction is not done on the ColdFire. The BR knob becomes a per-voice command word, `0xB31407FF + ceil(BR x 0x40000 / 127)`, sent over DSPI1/eDMA to the external audio hardware. The main OS contains no mask or shift that would apply it to PCM. So sample playback processing on the Rytm MKII likely sits in the FPGA/voice hardware: a lead for research map T12. Static and emulator work only. `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / More from the MKII mod and research projects (rytm-mods-src OS 1.73, analog-rytm-mkii-research OS 1.72)
facts.text: A third reading of the CPU: analog-rytm-mkii-research models the Rytm MKII as MCF5441x (conflict O14), with MAIN at `0x40000400` (2,903,032 B on 1.72) and the stack at `0x48000000`. `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / More from the MKII mod and research projects (rytm-mods-src OS 1.73, analog-rytm-mkii-research OS 1.72)
facts.text: Porting MKII mods to the MK1: same code base, different data (gdeo607/rytm1_mods, OS 1.73) {rytm1-mods}: Most routines are byte-identical, but the parameter info record is 88 bytes on the MK1 and 84 on the MKII. UI glyphs and the screen differ (122 px wide on the MK1, 128x64 on the MKII), so anything that draws its own pixels needs a redesign, not new addresses. Every RAM address (`0x41xxxxxx`, `0x8000xxxx`) has to be found again. Each of these would have been a silent bug. `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Modwerk Rytm modules and stock behaviour (OS 1.74, 2026-11-10)
facts.text: Shared voices: the amp-envelope record is at `0x40109c24`, 18 bytes per voice per block. A pad's light is a running mean of its own voice's level, so a dropped trig leaves the pad dark. `[doc]`, the silencing route `[hw]` (Silent Pad+Trig 0.8.0, run AT04)

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / +Drive mods loaded at boot (elekloader drive-loader-ar2 0.4-0.6, core-ar2 0.12-0.14, OS 1.74)
facts.text: A third Data route. The loader adds a `/mods` route to stock's Data router (the one Transfer and Elektroid use for `/projects` and `/soundbanks`), registered at `0x400a005e` in the resolver's getter; uploads travel in stock's data container (31-byte header, 12-byte footer with CRC-32; a stock 1.74 project reads family 2, device 5). Folders go three deep; stock's rename moves a folder only within its parent, so a move elsewhere is mkdir plus one move per item, as SAMPLES' MOVE does. `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / +Drive mods loaded at boot (elekloader drive-loader-ar2 0.4-0.6, core-ar2 0.12-0.14, OS 1.74)
facts.text: Files on the +Drive need a 16-byte zero header. The files share the sample filesystem, and stock's SAMPLES browser lists every folder, `/mods` too. LOAD TO PROJECT reads a file's first 16 bytes as a sample header: a raw `.elemod` there hangs stock, and a project that holds one stalls the next OS upgrade at PREPARING until CREATE NEW (SB19). The loader writes 16 zero bytes in front of every file, which stock loads as an empty sample. `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / +Drive mods loaded at boot (elekloader drive-loader-ar2 0.4-0.6, core-ar2 0.12-0.14, OS 1.74)
facts.text: The link runs at boot in core's `ev_boot_drive` (from core-ar2 0.14; 0.4 used its own site at `0x401009e0` in `main()`), after the +Drive is mounted and before audio and the UI task start; it skips when [NO] is held at power-on, when the eMMC or filesystem did not come up, or when a crash flag `/mods/.armed` from the last start is there (deleted about 10 s after the mods' inits ran; after a boot that applied sites, not before 60 s and the MODS page closed). From 0.6 each file is read into the +Drive area itself (pass 1 at its start, pass 2 just under its end, longest file first), so a mod file may be as large as the area; a 64 KB floor replaced the 512 KB staging buffer. Its working memory (about 270 KB for the 4.3 MB area) comes from stock's heap. The area runs from the flashed build's RAM end to `0x47FFF000`. `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / +Drive mods loaded at boot (elekloader drive-loader-ar2 0.4-0.6, core-ar2 0.12-0.14, OS 1.74)
facts.text: Stock's Data router has no size cap on a RAM entry: stock 1.74 writes an upload's first chunk to the entry's address before the `+0x6c` header check (`0x4008c1c6`, traced 2026-11-11), so a route must refuse an oversized upload in `+0x1c`, where stock has already put the size in the entry. `[doc]

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / +Drive mods loaded at boot (elekloader drive-loader-ar2 0.4-0.6, core-ar2 0.12-0.14, OS 1.74)
facts.text: Writing sites over the running OS: the loader keeps each site's stock bytes, writes the site with interrupts masked (SR `0x2700`), pushes the data-cache lines, and sets CACR to `0xA40CE100` (stock's value without DCINVA) after the link; the V4 core's CPUSHL takes an index, not an address. `[doc]

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / +Drive mods loaded at boot (elekloader drive-loader-ar2 0.4-0.6, core-ar2 0.12-0.14, OS 1.74)
facts.text: Keep UI-task work small. Reading 13 files of 484 KB when a page opened held the key path and USB for over 5 s, and reading 257 small files for their sizes lost a key on a unit; the loader now reads 32 KB per tick, rests three times as long as it worked (timed with DTIM0) and waits 1 s after any key or encoder turn. Past 16 queued UI events, a remote key is refused as busy. `[hw]` (key loss) / `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / +Drive mods loaded at boot (elekloader drive-loader-ar2 0.4-0.6, core-ar2 0.12-0.14, OS 1.74)
facts.text: Stock's lists must never have no row: the label scroll reads the cursor's row without checking the count. On a list cleared to no rows it reads a freed row (a fatal halt in the emulator, DV2B runs); on a list never filled, a null row (the UI hung, build DLP7). Stock's own lists are never empty (`..`, or 128 RAM slots); a mod list needs a placeholder row. `[emu]` / `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Queued trigs: what a mod can see before a trig fires (Modwerk, OS 1.74, read from the code)
facts.text: The sequencer queues a track's next trig one step ahead, its probability already rolled, in the lowest free of three event slots per track (state at `0x42ac5fb0 + 224*track + 56*slot`, fire time at `0x8000fd50 + 12*track + 4*slot` on the clock at `0x8000fe54`, which moves 2 x tempo per block). A trig queued while an earlier one still waits (swing, micro timing) lands in the second or third slot. Pads, MIDI notes and the first trig after PLAY take a fourth slot at once and cannot be seen ahead. `[doc]` (a trig that will not play is not queued: rytm-emu at 50 %, a unit for FILL and 2:2 `[hw]`)

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Queued trigs: what a mod can see before a trig fires (Modwerk, OS 1.74, read from the code)
facts.text: Stock fires one event per track per block, so two due in one block take that block and the next. Mutes and a track's held word apply when the trig fires, not when it is queued. Retrigs are not queued: they run on their own tick counter. A pattern change clears queued events from the change on. `[doc]`

The waveform widget at view + 400 keeps its area in RAM (x0 +28, y0 +32, width +36, height +40; stock 2, 16, 123, 32), read at every draw, so a mod can resize it without a code site. `[emu]` {modwerk-rytm-smpl05}

facts.text: The waveform's slot follows parameter changes only: the page callback `0x400d253a(view)` sets the widget's slot from SMP, STA and END when a parameter or the track changes, and sets it to 0 (centre line) while SMP's slot has no sample name (`0x400b8192`). A slot gets its name (`0x41942350`, written at `0x4009e39e`) only when the sample loader `0x4009df72` has read its file whole, and the project's pool loads slot by slot (`0x400b739c`) from background jobs a few seconds after boot. A page that shows the waveform from boot must call `0x400d253a` again while the slot reads 0; seen on a unit with Improved SMPL 0.5.0 (the waveform appeared by itself after a few seconds). `[hw]` {modwerk-rytm-smpl05}

Stock applies a sound at `0x4011f60a` after the machine byte is written; the mixer call is `0x4012129a`, the block exit hook `0x401216c2`. facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Where a MKII mod can keep its own data (rytm-mods-src `re/subsystems`, OS 1.73, checked in 1.74 by byte match; static plus rytm-emu, nothing on a unit)
facts.text: Stored records are read only by their load serializers. In a cold boot watched over the whole stored project image (`0x405c8f20`, 0x1f9f32 B), the only readers were each record's loader, the project-load code, and whole-image copies. Dumps are serialised from live objects. `[emu]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Where a MKII mod can keep its own data (rytm-mods-src `re/subsystems`, OS 1.73, checked in 1.74 by byte match; static plus rytm-emu, nothing on a unit)
facts.text: 37 stored kit bytes stock never reads or writes: kit `+0x832..+0x841` (16 B) and `+0x902..+0x916` (21 B), on either side of the performance block (whose loader and saver start at `+0x842`). Mod 0018 keeps its scene mute masks there, behind a tag byte `0x53` at `+0x90c`. Whole-image copies carry them; kit copy/paste and SysEx kit transfer go through a live buffer and drop them. `[emu]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Where a MKII mod can keep its own data (rytm-mods-src `re/subsystems`, OS 1.73, checked in 1.74 by byte match; static plus rytm-emu, nothing on a unit)
facts.text: A 140-byte gap in the power-fail image: `0x405c8e84..0x405c8f0f`, between the end of the checksummed `COKI` global block and a saved random seed (`0x405c8f10`). The whole 2,096,059-byte image from `0x405c8e10` is written to eMMC (slots `0x7a000` / `0x7c000`) on power-fail and read back at boot. No code reference lands in the gap, and a marker survived a power-off and a cold boot in the emulator. Not yet checked: project and kit saves, OS upgrade, factory reset. Nothing initialises the gap, so give your data a tag (mod 0017 uses `CIPF`). `[emu]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Where a MKII mod can keep its own data (rytm-mods-src `re/subsystems`, OS 1.73, checked in 1.74 by byte match; static plus rytm-emu, nothing on a unit)
facts.text: "Loosened" bytes have a cost on stock: bytes that stock reads but always holds at one value (for example the 8 low bytes of the velocity and aftertouch route amounts, sound `+0x71/+0x74/+0x77/+0x7a` and `+0x8d/+0x90/+0x93/+0x96`) can carry mod data only if every stock reader is hooked. A project or dump using them is then not safe on unhooked firmware: a changed version long makes the record load at defaults, and a level LSB at 127 loads as 100. Bytes stock never reads are harmless there. See rule E3. `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Where a MKII mod can keep its own data (rytm-mods-src `re/subsystems`, OS 1.73, checked in 1.74 by byte match; static plus rytm-emu, nothing on a unit)
facts.text: Performance macros are engine state, not kit data: 12 words at `0x8000e57c + 2k` (0..`0x7f00`), glided each block (~22 ms) into `0x8000f774[0..11]`. Their setter `0x400b2bfe` raises no change notice, so the kit is not marked edited. CTRL IN 1/2 are ADC slots 0 and 1, smoothed and mapped each block by `adc_pedal_update` (`0x4013f1c8`). `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Where a MKII mod can keep its own data (rytm-mods-src `re/subsystems`, OS 1.73, checked in 1.74 by byte match; static plus rytm-emu, nothing on a unit)
facts.text: Track mutes belong to the project, scenes to the kit. Every UI and MIDI mute goes through `track_mute_set` (`0x400b786c`); Overbridge uses `track_mute_set_silent` (`0x400b6d6c`), which has no guard and bypasses hooks on the main setter. All scene engages (pads, CC 92, NRPN `0xE8`, Overbridge) go through `kit_scene_set_active` (`0x400a7d04`). `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Step records, locks and the stock write routines (trig-seedr, MKII OS 1.74, analog-emu only, 2026-11-14)
facts.text: Track record: 0x395 bytes a track: per step a 16-bit flag word (+0x000; 0x0001 trig, 0x0002 retrig, 0x0004 mute, 0x0008 accent, 0x0010 swing, 0x0020 slide), then 64-byte arrays for NOTE (+0x080), VELOCITY (+0x0C0), LENGTH (+0x100), MICRO TIMING (+0x140, -23..+23), RETRIG length, rate and velocity curve (+0x180/+0x1C0/+0x200), TRIG CONDITION (+0x240) and SOUND LOCK (+0x280); track length at +0x2C5, speed at +0x2C7. `[emu]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Step records, locks and the stock write routines (trig-seedr, MKII OS 1.74, analog-emu only, 2026-11-14)
facts.text: Stock write routines (track object first; steps past the length are refused): trig `0x400c2620`, flag bits `0x400c2482`, NOTE/VEL/LEN `0x400c0776`/`0x400c07f0`/`0x400c086a`, condition `0x400c03d6`, lock set `0x400c058c`, lock clear `0x400c05e2`, trig shift `0x400c1d7a` (one step a call, carries the 88-byte lock record). `[emu]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Step records, locks and the stock write routines (trig-seedr, MKII OS 1.74, analog-emu only, 2026-11-14)
facts.text: Lock limit without a warning: the saved pattern keeps locks in 72 rows of 66 bytes; past 71 used (a fine parameter costs 2) stock still sets a new lock, with no row and no warning. Such a lock was kept by SAVE PATTERN + RELOAD PATTERN and by a power cycle; whether the project file or a pattern SysEx dump keeps it is not measured. (The project's notes of 2026-11-14 said it lived only until the next save.) `[emu]` {trig-seedr-1116}

facts.text: Keys: stock 1.74 uses every FUNC + key combination; TRIG held + PAGE does nothing. A knob left for 2.5 s or more swallows its next turn, whatever its size (refined below from Modwerk's measurements). `[emu]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Step records, locks and the stock write routines (trig-seedr, MKII OS 1.74, analog-emu only, 2026-11-14)
facts.text: Version shift: sidecar's OS 1.73 addresses near `0x400c0000` sit 0x6c later in 1.74, its data tables near `0x401c5000` 0x218 later. `[emu]` sidecar-mods 0.5.0 gives finer steps, checked by its own tool: code near `0x4008xxxx-0x4012xxxx` +0x6c, tables at `0x401bfxxx` +0x2b0, `0x40288xxx-0x40290xxx` +0x360, `0x40002c14` unchanged. `[doc]` {sidecar-mods-1116}

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Step records, locks and the stock write routines (trig-seedr, MKII OS 1.74, analog-emu only, 2026-11-14)
facts.text: Knob value drawing (Modwerk Filter Hz 1.2.1): `0x40037a56` centres the value text and inverts a 27-pixel box for a locked value in the label row; Filter Hz widens it to 33 pixels at `0x40037bea`, and its value-text site is `0x400a86b4`. Ran on a Rytm MKII on 2026-11-14 with locked FRQ values from 440 Hz to 21.1 kHz. `[hw]` {modwerk-1115}

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Step records, locks and the stock write routines (trig-seedr, MKII OS 1.74, analog-emu only, 2026-11-14)
facts.text: The flag routine resets a step left without a trig: `0x400c2482` sets or clears any mask, and if the step ends up without the note trig (bit 0) it calls `0x400c0b18` (note, velocity, length to default, micro timing 0, retrig 46/9/0), `0x400c0624` (clears every lock of the step through the pool's `0x400ac86e`) and `0x400c070a` (sound lock to 0xFF). Write the flags first, then the fields, then the locks. `[emu]` {trig-seedr-1116}

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Step records, locks and the stock write routines (trig-seedr, MKII OS 1.74, analog-emu only, 2026-11-14)
facts.text: Sound lock: set `0x400c0670` (track, step, value up to 128; voice tracks only, otherwise it stores 0xFF), clear `0x400c070a`; both send the step's change notice. Lock set and clear (`0x400c058c`/`0x400c05e2`) leave the flag word alone; their length check lets step == length through. `[emu]` {trig-seedr-1116}

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Step records, locks and the stock write routines (trig-seedr, MKII OS 1.74, analog-emu only, 2026-11-14)
facts.text: Lock-row types: voice tracks map a sound index to a row type through the int32 table `0x401c5c7c` (42 entries, a permutation of 0..41; inverse `0x401c5d24`); the FX track (track 12) uses `0x401c5b4c` (38 entries; inverse `0x401c5be4`), chosen by `0x400075c8`/`0x40007602` on "track == 12" alone. A fine lock takes two rows (type and track, then one with track 0x80). The row is made from the change notice at the next UI tick, not inside the lock-set call. Measured on BD, MT and FX only. `[emu]` {trig-seedr-1116}

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Step records, locks and the stock write routines (trig-seedr, MKII OS 1.74, analog-emu only, 2026-11-14)
facts.text: Sound index to parameter (voice tracks): records at `0x401bfb2c`, 0x34 bytes each, index at +0x04: 1-8 LFO (MUL WAV MOD DST SPD FAD SPH DEP), 9-16 SYNTH (9 = LEV), 17-24 SAMPLE (TUN FIN SMP BR STA END LOP LEV), 25-32 FILTER (ENV ATK DEC SUS REL FRQ RES TYP), 33-41 AMP (ATK HLD DEC OVR VOL PAN ACC DEL REV). Words 42-43 of a step's 88-byte lock record hold the step's lock count (int32, rewritten by `0x400ac646`), not locks. `[emu]` {trig-seedr-1116}

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Step records, locks and the stock write routines (trig-seedr, MKII OS 1.74, analog-emu only, 2026-11-14)
facts.text: Euclid fields in the track record: PL1/PL2 at +0x2CB/+0x2CC; +0x2D1 holds 64 bytes, the pulse number Euclid mode plays per step (0xFF none; entries past the length keep old values). Euclid mode leaves the flag words alone. Stock's pattern for PL1 = p, LEN = n (no PL2, no rotation) has a pulse on step j when (j x p) mod n < p, which is not Bjorklund's start: 16/5 gives `x...x..x..x..x..`. `[emu]` {trig-seedr-1116}

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Modwerk development link and test runner (MKII OS 1.74, 2026-11-14/15)
facts.text: Boot from RAM without a flash write: a flashed development base lets stock's SysEx OS upgrade check the upload and save the working state; at the erase-and-write call (`0x4004dc14` -> `0x4009f404`) the base writes a mailbox over the 32-byte header of stock's upload buffer `0x403c8b00` and resets by software. A gate at `0x400008c6`, before stock fills SRAM, takes the mailbox only after a software reset (RSR bit 5), checks the CRCs, unpacks the image over the running OS and enters it. The unpacked image must stay under `0x3c8700` bytes and the flashed packed MAIN OS under `0x1c8b00` bytes, because the bootstrap reads it to `0x40200000` at every boot. A RAM boot takes about 16-21 s; a power cycle brings the flashed OS back. `[hw]` (A68)

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Modwerk development link and test runner (MKII OS 1.74, 2026-11-14/15)
facts.text: A software reset does not write the copyback data cache back: a mailbox written through the cache and pushed with `cpushl` alone was not in DDR after the reset (two gates came back as the flashed OS). Evicting by reads plus `cpushl`, then turning the data cache off in CACR before the write, fixed it. `[hw]` (A68)

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Modwerk development link and test runner (MKII OS 1.74, 2026-11-14/15)
facts.text: Remote flash over stock's upgrade: 0x50/0x51 messages in 2 KiB blocks, each block's CRC zlib crc32 seeded with 0xffffffff (O29). Started from GLOBAL > OS UPGRADE, stock answers every block with status 2, so the tool first presses NO three times. Nothing is erased before YES at UPGRADE OS NOW?. 916 blocks took 5.9 s and the unit was back after 13.1 s. A flashed image that hangs at boot needs DIN recovery. `[hw]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Modwerk findings (MKII and MKI, OS 1.74, 2026-11-16/17)
facts.text: Stock's UI queue has no full check (MKII): the UI queue is a ring of 1024 pointers that the UI task takes in order; stock's send and receive update its read index and count with interrupts masked. With 13 modules and BD ANALOG playing the queue held 1,931 messages, so stock overwrote its own unread messages (pad pressure, keys, a mod's events); the unit lagged and hits were lost (SB27, I131). `[hw]` {modwerk-rytm-1116}

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Modwerk findings (MKII and MKI, OS 1.74, 2026-11-16/17)
facts.text: Pad pressure floods the UI queue: with BD ANALOG 808 on one track and an RTRG hold in live recording (block load 86-89 %), the queue reached a depth of 205, almost all of it stock's pad pressure messages at 200-290 a second. A mod that posts to this queue must not count stock's backlog against its own budget. `[hw]` {modwerk-rytm-1116}

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Modwerk findings (MKII and MKI, OS 1.74, 2026-11-16/17)
facts.text: Stock's sample preview (FUNC + YES in a sample list): routine `0x400a0dac` (called from `0x400a5236` and `0x400e742e`) plays on the active track's voice with the sample in slot 129 (past the project's 127) and TUN and FIN at rest (`0x4000`); LFO modulation is added after it, so an LFO on FIN bends a stock preview. A mod that reads FIN as a rate must leave slots 128 and up at 1x (Improved SMPL 0.5.0 played previews silent, I132). `[emu]` (stock code) / `[hw]` (fix) {modwerk-rytm-1116}

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Modwerk findings (MKII and MKI, OS 1.74, 2026-11-16/17)
facts.text: More stock sites (Improved SMPL 0.6 with LOP PIPO and zero snap): shared OFF/ON value text `0x400fb56c`; LOP's maximum in the parameter table `0x401c04f8`; shared OFF/ON switch icon `0x400fedf4` (BD CLASSIC's WAV uses the three-position one); sample DMA source set by the prefetch at `0x4011c58a`/`0x4011c5e6` (voice 0) and `0x4011cb2e`/`0x4011cb98` (voices 1-7); voice 0 prefetch call in the audio interrupt `0x40121134`; encoder profile `0x4003a0de`, apply-delta call `0x4003a240`, lock call `0x4003a19c`, per-trig lock edit `0x40037f6c`; end of the waveform widget's draw `0x4006ce72`. Stock reads any nonzero LOP as ON; CC 30 writes its value into LOP unchanged. `[emu]` / `[hw]` (author's unit) {modwerk-rytm-1116}

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Modwerk findings (MKII and MKI, OS 1.74, 2026-11-16/17)
facts.text: MKI limits, reported and not yet checked on a Modwerk 1.74 image: BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE ends at `0x4011AA7A`; the flash erase and program routines every flash write uses lie at `0x40096A6C-0x40096B3E` (erases from `0x40096A6C` and `0x40096AC2`, program from `0x40096AF6`), and calling them can damage the boot sectors and the recovery menu. The in-OS upgrade decodes into a 2 MiB buffer at `0x40366570` with other statics behind it, so the decoded update (8-byte preamble plus container) must stay at or below `0x1F0000` (SB21); DIN recovery survives an overrun. Modwerk's build refuses both. `[?]` {modwerk-1117}

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / elekloader core-ar2 0.14-0.16: boot order, skips, pads, USB gain, SMPL machines (MKII OS 1.74, 2026-11-19)

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / elekloader core-ar2 0.14-0.16: boot order, skips, pads, USB gain, SMPL machines (MKII OS 1.74, 2026-11-19)
facts.text: Stock keeps calling idle voices: from a slot's first SYN trig on, the render (slot loop site `0x40121208`) calls each of the 8 slots' machine routines every block, sounding or not, and only a power cycle ends it (not STOP, a kit load or a project load). An idle machine call costs about 1,100-1,400 counted instructions a block per slot in the emulator. Ten machines leave a small negative gain stuck for good (gain words `0x80007000 + 8 x slot`). `[emu]`

facts.text: Stock's delay and reverb never reach 0: the FX block (`0x4010e6bc`) builds both send buses from all 8 slots and calls the delay (`0x4010da24`) and reverb (`0x4010d434`) every block at full cost, sends at 0 too. Once excited, the reverb settles in a limit cycle of about ±117 of 2^31 (main L stays at -1); the delay's output keeps a few hundred of 2^31. Delay line `0x4b400000` (4 MB), reverb lines `0x4b000000` (`0x98000` bytes). `[emu]` / `[doc]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / elekloader core-ar2 0.14-0.16: boot order, skips, pads, USB gain, SMPL machines (MKII OS 1.74, 2026-11-19)

The voice skip and the delay and reverb clears change the sound slightly (a skipped slot's next note starts from its power-on state); the sample-layer skip, the cast memo and the send trim are exact. A checked call costs about 5 % of a block, so core makes at most one per block: before that limit, a STOP put the slots in step and every 256th block overran its time (elekloader's test T238). `[emu]`

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Modwerk: EMAC pipeline, eDMA chains, delay lag, interrupt stack (MKII OS 1.74, 2026-11-22)
facts.text: EMAC pipeline: a `movclr.l` straight after the `mac` that feeds it waits for that MAC. On a unit 1,024 such pairs took 3,391 DMA timer ticks back to back, and 1,853 with two accumulators used in turn and other work between each `mac` and its `movclr`. In fractional mode the `<<`/`>>` scale factor of `mac` does nothing (ColdFire EMAC reference 5.3.5); add a product twice to double it. Unit and rytm-emu output matched the host's C only then. `[hw]` {modwerk-1123}

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Modwerk: EMAC pipeline, eDMA chains, delay lag, interrupt stack (MKII OS 1.74, 2026-11-22)
facts.text: Align hot data: m68k GCC aligns `int32_t` (and arrays and structs of it) to 2 bytes, so a static array can straddle 16-byte cache lines (seen in a link map). Give hot arrays and state `__attribute__((aligned(16)))`. `[doc]` {modwerk-1123}

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Modwerk: EMAC pipeline, eDMA chains, delay lag, interrupt stack (MKII OS 1.74, 2026-11-22)
facts.text: eDMA chains: while a channel's DONE bit is still set from its last transfer, the eDMA ignores a descriptor's E_SG, so only the chain's first descriptor runs. Write the channel number to CDNE (`0xFC04401F`) before loading the first descriptor; push descriptors out of the data cache (`cpushl dc`) and reach DDR through the uncached copy. rytm-emu runs and finishes every chain at once, so it shows neither this nor a transfer still in flight. OS 1.74 never names eDMA channel 46. `[hw]` / `[emu]` (emulator difference) {modwerk-1123}

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Modwerk: EMAC pipeline, eDMA chains, delay lag, interrupt stack (MKII OS 1.74, 2026-11-22)
facts.text: The delay's return lags the dry sound: on a unit the delay return reaches the main mix 3.2 ms (153 samples) after the track's dry sound (correlation 0.997 at that lag); rytm-emu lines them up. A send effect meant to sum with the dry sound (a phaser) then sits on a comb filter; build the dry part into its own return. `[hw]` / `[emu]` {modwerk-1123}

facts.text: Zeroing a voice's sample gain does not mute the sample layer: stock's `sample_render` (1.74 `0x4011c6b8`, 1.73 `0x4011c64c`) is the only writer of the layer's output S = `0x800067f8 + 128 x voice` (32 longs, every voice, every block). It runs after the machine engine loop, and `voice_output_mix` (1.74 `0x4010ea98`, called at `0x4012129a`) then adds S at a fixed weight. The gain word `0x80007000 + 8 x voice` scales buffer B only. So a mod machine cannot silence S from its own render; Sidecar zeroes S of its voices in a detour at the mixer call ([I195](../INCIDENTS.md#i195-stock-rytm-samples-played-under-sidecar-machines-rytm-firmware-044050)). `[emu]` / `[doc]` {sidecar-mods-1123}

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Sidecar 0.5.1.1 and Rytm firmware 0.5.1.1 (MKII OS 1.74, 2026-11-22)
facts.text: Inside `sample_render`: a voice loop over records `0x80005b30 + 92 x voice` (+40: playing a sample, set at a start, cleared at a stop or the sample's end; +44..+91: 48 bytes of filter state, cleared at a start). Per voice: the next voice's start (mask from the previous block, `0x80005868`) and DMA source (`0x80005820`/`0x80005824`), which must always run; the resampler (64 iterations); DMA bookkeeping (always runs); the filter (16 iterations) and output stage. Idle voices resample a silence buffer, about 1.7 M instructions a second per voice in the emulator. Sidecar 0.5.1.1 skips the resampler and filter for its voices with 6-byte detours at 1.74 `0x4011cc1a` and `0x4011cd46` (1.73 `0x4011cbae`, `0x4011ccda`); the routine is byte-identical between 1.73 and 1.74 except four absolute addresses. `[emu]` {sidecar-mods-1123}

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Sidecar 0.5.1.1 and Rytm firmware 0.5.1.1 (MKII OS 1.74, 2026-11-22)
facts.text: A skip must keep the accumulators clean: the resampler's first `macw`, the filter's first `macl` and the mixer start from ACC0/ACC1 as the previous voice left them; each voice ends with `movclr` into ACC0/ACC1 (1.74 `0x4011cf5a`). A skip that jumps past those two instructions leaves residue for the next voice. Sidecar's first build did that (found in review); the emulator's engine loop leaves the accumulators at 0, so it could not show the fault. `[doc]` {sidecar-mods-1123}

facts.section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Sidecar 0.5.1.1 and Rytm firmware 0.5.1.1 (MKII OS 1.74, 2026-11-22)
facts.text: Shared voices and the engine latch: a voice's engine pointer (`0x419ca110 + 4 x voice`, 1.73) is latched at a SYN trig. On the shared voices (RS/CP, MT/HT, CH/OH, CY/CB) a sample-only trig (TRIG page SYN off) from one track runs the engine of the last SYN trig, possibly the other track's machine. The voice flag cannot tell a Sidecar machine from a stock one. Sample table (1.73): `0x41329e70 + 16 x slot`, 131 slots (+0 PCM pointer, +4 rate, +8 length, +12 step); an empty slot points at a silence buffer, so SMP 0 plays silence; a trig starts the voice when its trig word has bit 8. `[doc]` {sidecar-mods-1123}

The pushed page title is a timed header of about 90 ms. `[emu]` {sidecar-mods-1123}
