facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 1. Two hangs on silicon that the emulator ran bit-exactly `[hw]`
facts.text: H-opt1, RINGS as a hand-written SIMD kernel: the DSP hung on the first block, and all audio died. ([I14](../INCIDENTS.md#i14-dag-registers-stored-through-their-own-dag-hung-the-dsp)) Cause, confirmed with a one-variable probe image: DAG registers stored through their own DAG (`DM(I7, M7) = M4` and similar, used to save I0/I1/M4/M6/L0/L1/L4). The PRM forbids it for Types 3 and 15. Stock loads such registers through their own DAG thousands of times but never stores one. The probe was `probe-samedag-store`, a single `DM(I4, M6) = M4` and no SIMD. Fix: push DAG registers through R0.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 1. Two hangs on silicon that the emulator ran bit-exactly `[hw]`
facts.text: SIMD-mode loads and stores (the implicit PEy access at +4 bytes) into L2 byte space have no stock precedent: stock does SIMD data accesses only in L1 normal-word space, and SIMD stores to DDR at most. The manual allows them, but they are unproven on silicon. The shipping kernel does SIMD compute only and moves every load and store in SISD, toggling PEYEN per sample as stock does. Cost: 125,766 -> 31,472 instructions per block versus the C version. The full-SIMD version would have been 27,404.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 1. Two hangs on silicon that the emulator ran bit-exactly `[hw]`
facts.text: Lesson: an instruction word with a stock precedent is necessary but not sufficient. How stock combines operands also matters: which registers go through which DAG, and which access mode in which memory region. The encoding gate now refuses same-DAG stores and any data transfer while PEYEN is set.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 1. Two hangs on silicon that the emulator ran bit-exactly `[hw]`
facts.text: Emulator gaps seen here: It wraps immediate-offset accesses circularly when L != 0, so own the L register of every I you use that way. It treats never-written L2 as unknown per 32-bit word, which halts code that legitimately reads half of such a word.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 2. Encoding traps (selas), each caught by a gate before it reached a unit
facts.text: `JUMP (PC, label)` assembled to a jump to itself; the kernel spun forever. Write `JUMP label` as selcc does.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 2. Encoding traps (selas), each caught by a gate before it reached a unit
facts.text: selas does not compress inside a DO loop. Under `.COMPRESS` it can merge or drop a statement after a loop end or a `(DB)` branch. Write delayed-branch code under `.NOCOMPRESS` and cross-check statements against instructions.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 2. Encoding traps (selas), each caught by a gate before it reached a unit
facts.text: `Rn = Rn + Rm` and `Rn = Rn XOR Rm` compress to 16-bit forms that stock never uses, so write integer adds under `.NOCOMPRESS`. Stock contains no plain XOR at all.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 2. Encoding traps (selas), each caught by a gate before it reached a unit
facts.text: A label defined in two sources resolves to one of them in the merged object. Each kernel's own test passed, but the merged image jumped into the wrong file. Use unique label prefixes per file.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 2. Encoding traps (selas), each caught by a gate before it reached a unit
facts.text: Delay slots: after a delayed branch, the two slots must not hold a branch, a DO, a PC-stack operation, IDLE, or a write of the indirect branch's I/M. After a conditional branch, they should also not hold a flag writer (stock does that, but it is avoided as a precaution).

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 2. Encoding traps (selas), each caught by a gate before it reached a unit
facts.text: The last 11 instructions of every DO loop are 48-bit, and the loop end is an instruction ([rule A45](../AGENT-RULES.md)). The other code can be compressed. Compression shrank the kernels by 10-30 %, which matters because the instruction cache is the bottleneck (section 3).

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 3. Where the cycles go on the SHARC+ (calibrated cycle model)
facts.text: Instruction-cache misses are the largest stall class (33 %). Every model touches 150-300 code lines (10-19 KB) of L2 code per voice block, near or above the 16 KB 2-way cache. The lever is code size (compression, kernels instead of selcc C, fewer calls), not code order.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 3. Where the cycles go on the SHARC+ (calibrated cycle model)
facts.text: DAG write-to-use stalls are 32 %, almost all in selcc C (`In = Rm` or `In = DM(..)` followed directly by a use). selcc has no optimiser, so only hand kernels remove them.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 3. Where the cycles go on the SHARC+ (calibrated cycle model)
facts.text: Data-cache misses are 18 % (cold) and only a few % warm: the tables mostly hit. Float forwarding is 14 %, taken branches 4 %.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 3. Where the cycles go on the SHARC+ (calibrated cycle model)
facts.text: This core has no load-to-use stall, and a cache miss stalls whatever the distance. Scheduling loads earlier only helps to free registers.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 3. Where the cycles go on the SHARC+ (calibrated cycle model)
facts.text: Fewer instructions are not fewer cycles. One kernel cut instructions by 46 %, but the calibrated load fell by only 1.2 points. Code-size changes alone move a measurement by about 1 point (layout noise).

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 3. Where the cycles go on the SHARC+ (calibrated cycle model)
facts.text: Stock 1.17 with one trigged track sits at ~48.6 % on the high bound. The calibration on the unit: 8 KICK tracks measured 91.7 %, and the sound turned choppy above ~87 %.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 4. Optimisation rules the project enforces (worth copying)
facts.text: Current Selache fork (pin 967c1d1e) build rules: a plain `.SECTION/DM` is laid out in 40-bit words, so digikit assembles DM data as `/DM/BW`; the assembler may set a DO loop's fast-loop F1 bit by itself, so turn that off and write `(F)` where it is meant; `Rn = Fm` is not a plain transfer, use `Rn = PASS Fm`; an undefined name (for example a register SHARC+ lacks) silently becomes an external symbol. The earlier assembler wrote 77 transfers without their width modifiers. `[doc]` {digikit-1116}

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 4. Optimisation rules the project enforces (worth copying)
facts.text: Lazy clear: skipping a large memory clear at init is exact only if the write-before-read structure is proven per delay line. It removed one model's 70k-cycle spike on the model-change block.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 5. Practical numbers
facts.text: The calibrated estimate of clean tracks (about 87 % or less) for 8 tracks of one model: SQUARE 10; ASYM-TRI and 2FM 9; KICK, NOISE and most DX7 banks 8; RINGS, HIHAT and ADDITIVE 7; most others 6; VA 5.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 5. Practical numbers
facts.text: The per-voice cost is 3.5-6.8 % of the DSP. Mixed kits add up per voice. `[emu]` calibrated

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 5. Practical numbers
facts.text: After flashing a build that adds machines, create a new project before testing: projects saved under an earlier image may not play. A project saved with PLAITS loads on stock 1.17. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
facts.text: L2 data is cached by a 16 KiB cache that maps lines 16 KiB apart to the same set. Buffers spaced at 16 KiB multiples thrash it, so pad or interleave them. Branches and calls are expensive: unroll small loops into hardware loops, avoid calls in per-sample code, and fill delay slots.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
facts.text: One block measured 666,582 cycles median on DT2 (666,784 on DN2), jittering by ±2.7 % (sd 0.5 %); the emulator does not jitter. With `digikit/remote` and `digikit/debug` loaded, a DN2 showed DSP 57 % average (61 % peak) and ColdFire 26 %.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
facts.text: Registers read on silicon (DT2 and DN2 alike): IMASK `0x8040801b`, MODE2 `0x42000021`, SHDBG_REVID `0x20`, CMMR_SYSCTL `0x6004`, SHL1C_CFG `0x00010101`, SHL1C_CFG2 `0xf0`; two non-cacheable ranges: `0x200fa000-0x200fe000` and `0x28240000-0x283a0000`, with exclusive end addresses. SHL1C_CFG2 `0xf0` enables ranges 2 and 3 with `RRnSEL = 1` (non-cacheable); L2 and DDR outside them are cached ([finding 103, section 4](https://github.com/ElekLabs/digikit/blob/main/docs/findings/103-dsp-facts-on-a-digitakt-ii.md#4-registers-read-on-silicon-d)); withdrawn 2026-11-16: the per-device core timer periods reported here were I0/I1 reads. The old assembler encoded the probe's TPERIOD, TCOUNT, MMASK and LIRPTL reads as other registers, so none of them was measured; of the probe's ID words only OSPID differs (DT2 `0x00224601`, DN2 `0x07674700`). {digikit-1116} Float and saturation rules the chip follows (some contradict the PRM):

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
facts.text: A float ALU operation with a NaN input returns `0xFFFFFFFF` with AI set and AN clear. Inf - inf also returns `0xFFFFFFFF`. The float multiplier's invalid result (NaN operand, inf x 0) is `0x7FFFFFFF` with MI set and MN clear.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
facts.text: The sticky bits (AIS, AVS, AUS, AOS) latch on every float ALU operation, so a NaN once produced leaves a mark you can read.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
facts.text: FIX of ±0.5 returns 0 and sets AUS.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
facts.text: With MODE1.ALUSAT, fixed add/sub/neg/abs saturate to `0x7FFFFFFF` / `0x80000000`. The short compute forms (Type 2c), the multifunction ALU halves and the dual add/subtract may still wrap; this is unmeasured.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
facts.text: Open again (2026-11-16): whether reading an MR word into a register keeps the multiplier flags. The probe's `MRF = R1 * R2 (SSFR)` was assembled without the rounding modifier, so its MV flag proves nothing; the "float multiply with parallel add" item measured only a plain multiply (see CONFLICTS S10). {digikit-1116}

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
facts.text: The RECIPS/RSQRTS seeds come from two 128-entry tables, all measured; the low 15 mantissa bits are zero. Stock's divide helper uses RECIPS plus Newton steps, so the last bit of a division depends on the exact seed. Diagnostic reply publication ([finding 101](https://github.com/ElekLabs/digikit/blob/main/docs/findings/101-module-step-word-on-hardware.md)): the DSP's SPI2 is a slave and its transmit DMA walks two descriptors. Timing of the suspected overlap between DMA and diagnostic writes on silicon remains unmeasured. {digikit-f101}

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
facts.text: On a real DT2 (OS 1.17), digikit's diagnostic word 25 arrived as 0 in 3,995 of 4,000 collected records. The old scheme delivered every second record in the emulator. `[hw]` {digikit-f101}

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
facts.text: Digikit's own `core/fx` and `core/dsp-voice` diagnostic clears overwrote the previous block's reply word. Removing those clears restored delivery in the DN2 1.12 emulator; this does not identify stock firmware as the writer or establish silicon DMA timing. `[emu]` {digikit-f101}

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
facts.text: Keep hook diagnostics in a static word and copy it into the reply at the block tail, after all module calls. The revised design clears the static word rather than either reply record and passes the emulator regression; finding 101 says it had not yet run on a real DT2. A mark stored in the call that hangs the DSP cannot reach a tail that never runs, so the fault record retains the last completed block's mark. `[emu]` {digikit-f101}

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 7. How a stock DSP interrupt saves registers, and what module code must never write (digikit findings 130, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Three pieces of stock code: a vector stub, the wrapper `0x1c02a4`-`0x1c066b` (byte-identical on both images, 968 words, return label `0x1c04b7`; it calls the handler through the table at `0x2404b0` with `JUMP (M13, I12) (DB)` at `0x1c04b1`) and a return stub. SEC vector stub DT2 `0x1c0b7b` / DN2 `0x1c0acd`, generic stub `0x1c0b1e` / `0x1c0a70`, return stub `0x1c0be5` / `0x1c0b37`: the DN2 stubs sit `0xae` lower. `[doc]` (both images' bytes, two decoders)

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 7. How a stock DSP interrupt saves registers, and what module code must never write (digikit findings 130, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
facts.text: What is saved: the stubs save R4, R8, R12, I6, I7, I12, B6, B7, PX and PCSTK; the wrapper saves the DAG, status, loop-stack and MR/MS registers and zeroes L0-L5 and L8-L15 for the handler. It picks its path by MODE1 bit 16 (RND32) of the interrupted code: with RND32 set it saves only R0-R2, R4 and S0-S15 and relies on the handler to keep the C callee-saved registers; with RND32 clear it saves R1-R15. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 7. How a stock DSP interrupt saves registers, and what module code must never write (digikit findings 130, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Never write these in module DSP code, not even with a save and restore: B7, L6, L7, M5, M6, M7, M13, IMASK, IMASKP, IRPTL, MMASK, TPERIOD, TCOUNT, FLAGS. The stock interrupt code may read them at any instruction, so an interrupt between the save and the restore sees the changed value. The wrapper needs a valid linear stack in I7 (L6 = L7 = 0) and M5 = 0, M6 = 1, M7 = -1, M13 = 0. digikit's `sdk/dsp/REGISTERS.md` generates one contract from this (classes clobber, keep, stack, never_write). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 7. How a stock DSP interrupt saves registers, and what module code must never write (digikit findings 130, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Finding 103 was partly withdrawn (2026-11-16): the old assembler mis-encoded several probe instructions, so the silicon run read MMASK as IMASKP, TPERIOD and TCOUNT as I0 and I1, LIRPTL (which SHARC+ lacks) as IMASK, and the cycle-counter reads of records 118-135 as LCNTR reads; it also dropped SSFR's rounding modifier and turned the dual multiply-plus-add into a plain multiply. The values listed in section 6 that came from these items are void; the non-cacheable ranges, REVID, IMASK, MODE2, the 59 value items and the block cycle counts stand (A41). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / What the stock SHARC kernels look like (digikit finding 72, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, static)
facts.text: Calling convention: a delayed `CALL` with a frame; arguments in R4, R8, R12, more on the stack; result in R0. Most kernels come as a pair: `reset(record)` and `process(record, in, out, n)`, one 32-sample block per call. The prologue and epilogue cost ~20 instructions, about 0.6 per sample.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / What the stock SHARC kernels look like (digikit finding 72, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, static)
facts.text: Every sample loop is a hardware `DO ... UNTIL LCE`. The loops are software-pipelined (the last stores come after the loop) and have a fast exit for n = 0 or 1.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / What the stock SHARC kernels look like (digikit finding 72, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, static)
facts.text: Idioms worth copying: multiplier + ALU + data move in one instruction; post-modify DAG access with constant M6 = 1 and M5 = 0; RECIPS/RSQRTS seed plus Newton steps, using FAVG to halve; branch-free CLIP/ABS/MIN/MAX; FEXT to wrap an index; SIMD around copy loops; parameter ramps as "accumulator += step per sample"; MODE1 saved and restored around RND32 or SIMD.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / What the stock SHARC kernels look like (digikit finding 72, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, static)
facts.text: Same code, different address: the shared kernels are byte-identical on DT2 and DN2 but sit at different addresses (biquad DT2 `0x1ccbd8`, DN2 `0xb81368`). Only the float divide `0x1c06ba` has one address on both. Calling a stock kernel therefore needs a per-device address row.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / What the stock SHARC kernels look like (digikit finding 72, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, static)
facts.text: Hidden dependencies of stock kernels: The envelope reads a rate table at a device-specific absolute address. powf reads three tables and writes error words. Divide and rsqrt flip MODE1 bit 16 and restore it, so don't call them with SIMD or a loop active.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / What the stock SHARC kernels look like (digikit finding 72, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, static)
facts.text: The DSP sections are byte-identical between DT2 1.16 and 1.17 and between DN2 1.11 and 1.12 (digikit finding 53), so SHARC code and addresses carried over between those OS versions. `[doc]` {digikit-f53}

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / What the stock SHARC kernels look like (digikit finding 72, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, static)
facts.text: digikit's recommendation: write your own kernels for the hot path; they can be faster (its estimate: interpolated delay 41 -> 15 instructions per sample, half-band 25 -> 10). Call stock only for the divide.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 1. Timing - the numbers that matter
facts.text: The core runs at 1.000 GHz (DSP clock against the host's wall clock: 1000.1 MHz median). A block is 32 samples at 48 kHz = 666,667 cycles, 1,500 blocks/s. Earlier "~650k / ~975 MHz" figures were a unit error (counted in units of 1,024). Guards built on 650k are about 2.5 % too strict. `[hw]` {own-dt2-notes}

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 1. Timing - the numbers that matter
facts.text: Stock load with nothing playing: about 43-49 % (word 0 ~280-320k cycles, idle-task measure 48.6-49 %). `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 1. Timing - the numbers that matter
facts.text: On the Digitakt II, reply word 0 is a true load figure. It tracks an idle-task measure second by second, about 6.5k cycles/block below it (interrupts, RPC, timers outside the frame handler). This differs from the Digitone II, where dn2_firmware_explore found word 0 misreading. Add ~6.5k for the whole DSP. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 1. Timing - the numbers that matter
facts.text: Device cycles are about 2x the emulator's instruction count for this project's own code, which reads samples from DDR. The emulator models no memory stalls. Stock render code is reported at ~9 cycles/instruction on the DN2. A hard stop that the emulator showed overshooting by ~25k overshot by ~75k on the unit. `[hw]` ([I36](../INCIDENTS.md#i36-the-emulator-undercounted-dsp-time-by-2x-to-12x))

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 1. Timing - the numbers that matter
facts.text: Free budget with one plain stock track: about 330k cycles per block (calibration burn builds). `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 2. FreeRTOS on the DT2 SHARC (static, confirmed by a task-switch hook on the unit)
facts.text: Priorities 2-4 and 6 are unused, probably with configMAX_PRIORITIES = 7. A task at priority 2-4 runs only after Audio finishes its block and is preempted by the next one, so it cannot make Audio miss a block. Only work inside Audio, or at priority 6, can. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 2. FreeRTOS on the DT2 SHARC (static, confirmed by a task-switch hook on the unit)
facts.text: Kernel globals: `pxReadyTasksLists` `0x2ca2e8` (20 bytes each), `pxCurrentTCB` `0x2ca3e0`, `uxCurrentNumberOfTasks` `0x2ca3e8`, `uxTopReadyPriority` `0x2ca3f0` (bit mask, `31 - leftz`), `xSchedulerRunning` `0x2ca3f4`, `uxSchedulerSuspended` `0x2ca414`. The TCB is 88 bytes and statically allocated (`xTaskCreateStatic` sw `0xb86014`). Stack overflow check method 2 (`0xa5a5a5a5`). No run-time stats are compiled in. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 2. FreeRTOS on the DT2 SHARC (static, confirmed by a task-switch hook on the unit)
facts.text: `prvIdleTask` is at sw `0xb863ca` with no idle hook; its back edge is at sw `0xb863df`. `vTaskSwitchContext` sw `0xb85af7` stores `pxCurrentTCB` at sw `0xb85b6b`. Both are workable hook points for an idle counter or a task map, at ~250 device cycles per switch (~0.1 %). L2 code loads at byte `0x20000000` (sw `0xb80000`). "Audio" and "RPC" are created from internal-memory code (sw `0x1c3f6a`, `0x1c7775`). `[hw]` (hooks ran on the unit)

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 3. Missed blocks, overload and "bitcrush until reboot" (what the runs showed)
facts.text: A late block is always a whole missed block. Audio is locked to the block interrupt. If one block's work runs past the next interrupt, that interrupt is lost and Audio runs one block later: an exactly one-block dropout, never drift. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 3. Missed blocks, overload and "bitcrush until reboot" (what the runs showed)
facts.text: The stock engine governs its own per-block load. With 8 heavy stock tracks the Audio task ran at 99-100 % for whole 4 s windows and missed no block. Misses happen only when extra code inside the Audio task adds work the stock governor doesn't know about. So a custom engine must stop on a per-block deadline measured from the block start, with margin, not on an average budget. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 3. Missed blocks, overload and "bitcrush until reboot" (what the runs showed)
facts.text: Provoked missed blocks (54 in one boot, three back to back) did NOT cause the sticky bitcrush. Neither did stock overload, nor sample loading at low load. The sticky "everything bitcrushed until reboot" appeared only with several custom-engine tracks at extreme settings. An emulator write audit showed no stray stores, so the cause is still open. Proven causes of a sticky whole-mix bitcrush from earlier builds: a render call much longer than a block with interrupts off; NaN/Inf reaching stock FX feedback; a value routed through a "free" stock parameter slot; overrunning the L2 area. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 3. Missed blocks, overload and "bitcrush until reboot" (what the runs showed)
facts.text: Reading load by sampling word 0 (~17 reads/s = ~1 % of blocks) misses single late blocks. Count late blocks on the DSP side instead (task-switch gaps > 1.25 blocks). `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 4. The ColdFire <-> SHARC reply record
facts.text: The SHARC writes two copies, at DM `0x266220` and `0x267220`. A selector at `0x261ca4` picks the copy being written (`0x266220 + (sel << 12)`), so write both. The ColdFire copies it every frame to `0x8000488C` (2,748 bytes, at most 687 words). The 16-bit halves arrive swapped. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 4. The ColdFire <-> SHARC reply record
facts.text: Word k is at `0x266220 + 4k`, not `+ k`. Two test builds wrote to the wrong place because of this; copy addresses from the compiler's disassembly. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 4. The ColdFire <-> SHARC reply record
facts.text: Which words are free (DT2 1.17, measured): 670-676 arrive untouched. heavylight's engine uses 672-676. Words 1-6 are rewritten by the firmware after the block, so writes there never arrive. Word 5 is the firmware's while a track plays (unlike the DN2). 677-686 are the firmware's. From word 7 on there is a per-track table: 21 words per track at `0x8000488C + 0x1C + 84*track`. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5. STRETCH machine contract (measured in the emulator, used on the unit)
facts.text: Render `FUN_1c5576 -> FUN_1c5615`, only caller `FUN_1c642a` (selector 2). Replace the body. Do not patch the call at `0x1c6af1`. The stock renderer costs ~1,720 instructions per 32-sample call. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5. STRETCH machine contract (measured in the emulator, used on the unit)
facts.text: Call: R4 = voice record (`0x2412cc + v*0x1d8`, 32 records), R8 = output (32 floats, 48 kHz, int16/32768 scale), R12 = 32. Voices are rendered in ascending order 0..31, so a new block starts when v <= last v. Record words: w00 sample pointer (int16 mono, L = voice 2t, R = 2t+1), w62/63 length, w64/65 loop start, w68/69 end (Q31), w6a/6b step (Q31, 96 kHz units), w6c/6d phase, bytes 0x1b8 active / 0x1b9 stop / 0x1bb reverse / 0x1bc loop, w72 = a (tempo fit, float) and w73 = b (pitch ratio). A trigger is visible as w70 == w71 == 0. +4 is a 96 kHz work buffer and +0x104 is decimator state, not scratch. Tempo is a float BPM at DM `0x252d50`. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5. STRETCH machine contract (measured in the emulator, used on the unit)
facts.text: Stock STRETCH: fixed 2,048-sample grains, 128-sample crossfade, linear interpolation. `a = BPM*(end-start)/(96000*120*2^bars)`, grid speed `clamp(a, 0.125, 4) + P - b`. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5. STRETCH machine contract (measured in the emulator, used on the unit)
facts.text: Knob frame working copy: short at `0x2558dc + 0xde + 0x60*track` (the hidden CFADE slot, 0..0x7f00). Routing a value through this "free" slot also feeds a stock per-voice flag that acts on the delay feedback (`FUN_1c24e9`, slot struct `0x2506ec + v*0xdc + 0x10`). That leaked into the delay and once caused a sticky bitcrush. Check every reused slot with a memory-write diff of the stock chain. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5. STRETCH machine contract (measured in the emulator, used on the unit)
facts.text: The SHARC upload in MAIN OS checks only `length <= 1 MiB` (no fixed size). Insert new boot blocks before FINAL. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5b. How a sample reaches a SHARC voice (digikit finding 15, DT2 1.16, emulator)
facts.text: Samples go to the DSP over link port 0 (LP0_CTL `0x30FFE000`; SEC sources 81/82/168), not over the frame link. LP1 is unused. One transfer is 0x401 words: a tag and 1,024 payload words. Tag `0xFFFFFFFF` means a slot header: slot, startL, startR, rate, len. Stereo means startL != startR. A tag below `0x19200` is a page number into the 400 MiB DDR sample pool at `0x8422B9C8`. This is the RPC-task work the owner saw while samples load.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5b. How a sample reaches a SHARC voice (digikit finding 15, DT2 1.16, emulator)
facts.text: Slot table: 0x14-byte records at DM `0x257810 + slot*0x14` (start L/R relative to the pool, length, ...), at most 0x401 slots.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5b. How a sample reaches a SHARC voice (digikit finding 15, DT2 1.16, emulator)
facts.text: Track t owns voices 2t and 2t+1, with no dynamic allocation (unlike the DN2). The frame's trig mask is at payload `0x22` (bit t = track t). `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 6. Memory rules learned the hard way
facts.text: L2: the static analysis says `0x2001ab7c..0x20100000` minus `0x200fa000..0x200fe000` is free, but going past `0x200f5a74` gave clicks and leaks into the delay on the unit. Keep your data at or below that. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 6. Memory rules learned the hard way
facts.text: External DDR: the stock output buffer (`0x8045b3c0`) and the sample data are in DDR. Per-sample stores to the DDR output buffer crashed the unit (continuous tone), although the emulator was bit-identical. Render into L2 and copy once per block. Read int16 samples two at a time. `[hw]` ([I17](../INCIDENTS.md#i17-per-sample-stores-to-the-ddr-output-buffer-crashed-the-unit))

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 6. Memory rules learned the hard way
facts.text: DM and PM data caches are not coherent on DDR (DN2 finding). Don't write through one bus and read through the other. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 6. Memory rules learned the hard way
facts.text: Keep long calls short with interrupts off: a watchdog of at most ~1M cycles per call. Burns of ~1.27M with interrupts off left no lasting harm; longer calls knocked the audio stream out of step for good. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 6. Memory rules learned the hard way
facts.text: Save MODE1 on entry and restore it on exit. A changed MODE1 alters the whole stock DSP until reboot. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 6. Memory rules learned the hard way
facts.text: Never let NaN/Inf/huge values leave the machine: per-sample guard `!(|x| < 1e6)` -> 0 and restart the voice, clip to ±2. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
facts.text: `double` is 32-bit float. A read position in float loses resolution from ~22 s into a sample, which sounds like sample-rate reduction. Use Q32.32 fixed point for positions. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
facts.text: No integer `/` or `%` where the operand can be 0 (`___umod32` runs LCNTR = 32 - leftz(x); 0 means a hang).

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
facts.text: No loops with early exit (`break`/`return`): they become DO loops left by a jump.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
facts.text: `int more = a < b; while (more)` compiled into an endless loop. Write a counted `for` with an `if` body.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
facts.text: Large initialised `static const float` tables arrive as garbage, so compute them at run time. Complex float expressions passed as arguments lost terms. `static int a = 1, b;` lost `b`. Keep compound conditions simple. Pass at most 3 arguments (stack arguments are passed wrongly) or a struct pointer.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
facts.text: selas: multifunction (MUL+ALU) and dual-load forms are encoded wrongly; `Ia = MODIFY(Ib, ..)` becomes `Ib = ..`; system registers (MODE1, LCNTR, EMUCLK) moved in 48-bit form are wrong, so use compressed code. Negative shift immediates are wrong (`023e 0000` vs stock `023e 7800`: ILOPI on the unit). Shift by a register.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
facts.text: selcc treats R3, R5-R7 as scratch where the ADI ABI preserves them: save them at the bridge.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
facts.text: A selcc peephole bug (frame-reload forwarding clobbering the reload register) was patched locally. The patch also added a `SELCC_SAFE=1` switch that skips the post-allocation peepholes. If code misbehaves only when optimised, try that.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
facts.text: DAG registers moved via the same DAG's addressing hang the unit; move them through R registers. Same rule as the DN2 skill.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 8. Measuring on the unit without a debugger
facts.text: Read-only USB SysEx probe in MAIN OS (heavylight's dt2-keyframer, derived from irpina/digihealth via dn2_firmware_explore): `F0 00 20 3C 7D 00 <pack7> F7`. Commands: HELLO 1 (returns word 0) and PEEK 3 (address, up to 256 bytes). There is no write command. It hooks the SysEx router at `0x40120006` (router `0x4011ffda`, header `0x4021e5d2`, send `0x40121d2a`, USB port 2), and the router itself drops device id 0x7D. It fits in 532 bytes of a free 896-byte run in MAIN OS 1.17 (`0x402e4f64`, `0x402e609c`) and coexists with Deja Vu V5.1, Musical V4 and Zoom V11. It also went into an elekloader-built image. It is built with plain binutils (`m68k-linux-gnu-as -mcpu=5475`). Overbridge suspected of conflicting: keep the probe build separate. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 8. Measuring on the unit without a debugger
facts.text: Telemetry as audio: a DSP track outputs one constant level per block (frame of 47 blocks with sync levels), recorded via an Overbridge track output. Overbridge applies a DC-blocking highpass (one pole, a = 0.9981 at 48 kHz) that the decoder must undo. About 50 % of frames decode. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 8. Measuring on the unit without a debugger
facts.text: Load display build: show peak cycles per call on the playhead. This is the only figure that includes real DDR stalls without a probe.

facts.section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 8. Measuring on the unit without a debugger
facts.text: Recovery used throughout: FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4, stock `.syx` over DIN. Bootstrap 0x0201 is the same on 1.16 and 1.17, so the 1.16 <-> 1.17 update is reversible. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Bootstrap/recovery facts

facts.section: Digitakt II / Bootstrap/recovery facts
facts.text: The startup-menu recovery has been used on a real DT2 (dt2-machine-lab, 2026-10-06): An experimental build crashed at startup. The owner restored official OS 1.16 through Transfer's recovery mode over DIN MIDI, sent from a Novation Launch Control 3's DIN out. Normal boot and audio came back. A generic "USB2.0-MIDI" cable adapter (VID 1a86, PID 752d) showed no reception at all. Use a known-good MIDI interface and test it before you need it. `[hw]` {dt2-lab-coldfire-fix}

facts.section: Digitakt II / Hardware test evidence for the mods
facts.text: dt2-machine-lab's Sketch/BUF R8 (OS 1.16; four live performance buffers, next-bar or immediate capture) works on the user's unit; the README calls it an experimental checkpoint. Its OS 1.17 reimplementation, trial R1, ran on a unit on 2026-11-12: a new project worked, a project used with the 1.16 Sketch hid the buffers (I94). `[hw]` (user reports) {dt2-lab-sketch}

facts.section: Digitakt II / Hardware test evidence for the mods
facts.text: digikit's flash rungs on a real DT2 1.17 (finding 47, 2026-10-18/19): each step was flashed through SETTINGS > SYSTEM > OS UPGRADE with Transfer and logged over USB SysEx. `[hw]` {digikit-f47} Rung A, the runtime in section 3 only, booted with a DIGIKIT menu. Rung B added the DSP link and voice hook (sections 3 and 7) and played stock audio. Rung C, a machine loaded at run time (pluck, 4,484 B uploaded over SysEx), halted the SHARC at the first trig. Breadcrumbs narrowed it to the step after the type match. The fix (C3d2) was to route 17 DAG-register stores through an R register, the same-DAG rule. With it, pluck played at ~1,500 dispatches/s with DSP load 41.5 -> 42 %.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Hardware test evidence for the mods
facts.text: A second SHARC stop on a real DT2: `fx/freqshift` on the send route froze the unit at boot; the emulator showed nothing (findings 77, 91). Two causes were found. `[hw]` {digikit-f91} ([I15](../INCIDENTS.md#i15-a-frequency-shifter-froze-the-unit-at-boot)) A selas defect left the end of a nested hardware loop compressed (VISA). The last 11 instructions of every hardware loop must be 48-bit ISA, so wrap nested loops in `.NOCOMPRESS` ([rule A45](../AGENT-RULES.md)). Code copied into L2 at run time was not written back from the data cache. After both fixes, freqshift ran on the send and master routes (2026-10-30).

facts.section: Digitakt II / Hardware test evidence for the mods
facts.text: An LFO at large depth on a run-time machine's TUNE drove Inf/NaN into the send FX and silenced every track until reboot, while the DSP kept running. The fix was a parameter clamp plus a per-voice guard in the wrapper; the guarded build ran on a unit with 0 faults. `[hw]` {digikit-f51}

facts.section: Digitakt II / Hardware test evidence for the mods
facts.text: PLAITS port (digitakt-ii-research All-in-One): 25 models flashed step by step on a unit, plus one SIMD kernel that hung the DSP. Lessons: [`digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md`](digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md). `[hw]` {dt2-plaits}

facts.section: Digitakt II / ColdFire facts from digitakt-ii-research's research notes (DT2 **1.16**, emulator)
facts.text: LFO tick `0x40139342` (caller `0x4002e912`): Parameter rows relative to A3: SPD -6, MULT -4, FADE -2, DEST 0, WAVE +2, SPH +4, MODE +6, DEP +8. WAVE is clamped to 0-6 at `0x401393c6`. WAVE 0-5 dispatch through a 6-entry table at `0x4022231c`; WAVE 6 is RAND. The table cannot be extended by appending: the RAND slew data sits right after it. The shared RNG is `(A,B) -> (B, A+B)` at `0x402b62c8/cc`. The phase increment is in D5 (signed); the stored phase is in D2. Raw WAVE 7/8 clamp to 6 and play RAND on stock. This is why Deja Vu needs two paired hooks, not one dispatch hook. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / ColdFire facts from digitakt-ii-research's research notes (DT2 **1.16**, emulator)
facts.text: Firmware heap: `malloc` at `0x4011e674` (size at `4(A7)`, pointer in D0, mutex `0x44e08654`), `free` at `0x4011e87a` (it checks bounds and 16-byte alignment with `illegal`). The heap is a 32 MiB buddy heap `0x44f39c40-0x46f39c40` with metadata at `0x402b406c`. It sits inside the reset clear and initialises on first call. An 8 KiB block allocated once stayed untouched for 10 M emulated instructions. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / ColdFire facts from digitakt-ii-research's research notes (DT2 **1.16**, emulator)
facts.text: A persistent flashed cave `0x403117c4-0x40312000` (2,108 B) ends exactly at the reset clear and survives boot. `0x4031be59-0x4031ff60` is inside the clear and cannot hold flashed code. The priority-6 task entry `0x40133646` is a candidate one-shot startup hook, after the heap is initialised. `[emu]` Deja Vu, the All-in-One, dt2-machine-lab and 70b185's private project all use it; who holds which bytes: [memory-maps.md](../common/memory-maps.md); one freeze report: [CONFLICTS O18](../CONFLICTS.md).

facts.text: These are 1.16 addresses; resolve them on 1.17 before use (rule C1).

facts.section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
facts.text: SHARC part: ADSP-21569. Section 7 holds ADSP-2156x loader/application records (104 records mapped). FreeRTOS, an Audio task and a recurring block loop are traced. The hand-off from the boot kernel to that startup is not.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
facts.text: The ColdFire <-> SHARC frame is the same shape as on the Digitone II: A full-duplex `0xabc`-byte DSPI2 frame carries a `0x802`-byte state payload: 16 records of `0x60` bytes, track n to SHARC unit n. ColdFire eDMA29 sends and eDMA28 receives; the SHARC uses SPI2 with completed-image double buffering. The send is driven from a level-5 interrupt that a level-6 eDMA-completion path forces in software. Link settings: SPI mode 1, 16-bit MSB-first, one `0x55e`-word window. The meaning of the SHARC-to-ColdFire return content is open. Compare the DN2's frame and reply words in [digitone-2-internals.md](digitone-2-internals.md). This is a second, independent reading of the shared design (research map T19).

facts.section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
facts.text: Project samples reach the SHARC over a different path: ColdFire Rapid-GPIO byte/strobe/ready endpoint -> SHARC link port 0 (LP0_RX, DMA30). Samples are described by five-word resource descriptors with 4 KiB pages. This agrees with digikit finding 15 ([digitakt-2-sharc-measured.md](digitakt-2-sharc-measured.md)). The physical bridge between the two endpoints is not identified.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
facts.text: Audio output: two 64-word banks are selected, then sent by a two-bank circular DMA descriptor (DMA10) to SPORT4 half A. Codec and pin are not identified.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
facts.text: Update path: MAIN validates checksum, minimum version and the cryptographic trailer before it erases and programs the staged ELE3 slot at flash `0x80000`, then requests a reset. Which updater copy runs after reset, and whether recovery is independent of it, is marked opaque.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
facts.text: Offline modifications proven in the simulator only: a byte-exact selector reroute, and a 3-byte change that turns an output-bank negation into pass-through. Re-encoding a modified section and running it on hardware are explicitly unproven.

facts.section: Digitakt II / What happens on a ColdFire fault (digikit finding 37, DT2 1.16/1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12, static, checked by a second agent) `[doc]`
facts.text: The main OS's default exception handler prints `EXCEPTION ...` with the vector, format, PC and twelve stack words, then executes `halt` with interrupts masked. It never returns.

facts.section: Digitakt II / What happens on a ColdFire fault (digikit finding 37, DT2 1.16/1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12, static, checked by a second agent) `[doc]`
facts.text: The core watchdog is not used anywhere in the main OS, so a fault hangs the whole device until the power is cycled. Messages like the DT2's `V04 M0 P40311A64` (dt2-machine-lab) are this handler's output.

facts.section: Digitakt II / What happens on a ColdFire fault (digikit finding 37, DT2 1.16/1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12, static, checked by a second agent) `[doc]`
facts.text: digikit's runtime counts bad boots: the counter is raised at boot start and cleared only after 30 s of stable running. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
facts.text: The intro is its own task, priority 7, created once by the installer before the main-OS task (DT2 `0x400d1448`, DN2 1.12 `0x400d3920`) and woken by a PIT3 tick. A higher number is more urgent here, so the intro preempts the main-OS task (priority 6). A frame callback that never returns starves the main OS until power-off.

facts.section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
facts.text: Five scene tables at `0x402a1b64`, `0x402a1b74`, `0x402a1b84`, `0x402a1b94`, `0x402a1ba4`. Each boot picks one with an LCG; the first is picked about 99.9 % of the time and has 175 frames. An entry is `{callback, frame count}`, ended by a 0.

facts.section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
facts.text: One pointer drives it: the current entry is at DT2 `0x43153a00`, DN2 1.12 `0x42c4cacc`, DN2 1.11 `0x42c4bacc`. Only the setup function (DT2 `0x400d1832`, DN2 1.12 `0x400d3d0a`) and the tick function (DT2 `0x400d18f0`, DN2 1.12 `0x400d3dc8`) touch it. Each frame calls `callback(index, count, bitmap)`; count 0 ends the intro the normal way: the pointer is cleared, PIT3 stops and semaphore `0x43149550` releases the main-OS task.

facts.section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
facts.text: Swapping the intro: a hook before the setup function's argument load (`move.l (0x24,SP),D0; movea.l D0,A0`, DT2 `0x400d183a`, DN2 1.12 `0x400d3d12`, DN2 1.11 `0x400d3bae`, the same 6 bytes on all three) can point it at an own table. In digikit's emulator the UI was then reached after 115 audio blocks instead of 5,973 (DT2) and 6,180 (DN2). Stock's frame clear is `0x40113700` (DN2 1.12 `0x40115074`, DN2 1.11 `0x40114d94`), called as `(bitmap, 0, 1)`. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
facts.text: Frame rate unresolved: digikit's timer model gives 30 Hz (175 frames = 5.8 s); its earlier emulator notes derived 15 Hz. Open conflict [O20](../CONFLICTS.md). Module code first runs at about frame 53-57 of the intro (emulator); almost all of that delay is stock setup.

facts.section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
facts.text: Faults during the intro reach stock's halting handler (see the section above): digikit installs its own crash handler only from the UI loop.

facts.section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
facts.text: Frame layout on the panel (measured on one DT2 1.17): with y = 0 at the top, the intro bitmap holds pixel (x, y) at byte `8*x + (63-y)/8`, bit `7 - (63-y)%8`, flipped vertically only. digikit's emulator shows these frames the other way up. `[hw]` ([I53](../INCIDENTS.md#i53-boot-screen-frames-were-upright-in-the-emulator-and-flipped-on-the-panel))

facts.section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
facts.text: Safe mode is digikit's, not stock's: REC (key `0x13`, state byte 2 bit 2; key state array at DT2 `0x44dc8644`, DN2 `0x445a2e30`) held from power-on skips all modules. On one DT2 1.17 it worked, and a custom boot screen started about 1.8 s after the stock intro. `[hw]` ([I54](../INCIDENTS.md#i54-safe-mode-by-rec-at-power-on-tested-on-a-digitakt-ii))

facts.section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
facts.text: ColdFire heap: a 32 MiB buddy allocator at `0x44f39c40-0x46f39c40` (16-byte minimum, power-of-two blocks), parameters at `0x402b406c`.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
facts.text: Allocating from the stock heap at startup (digitakt-ii-research, OS 1.16, emulator, byte-verified sites) {dt2-research-heap}: `malloc` is at `0x4011e674` (size at `4(A7)`, pointer in D0, mutex at `0x44e08654`, lazy init on first call). `free` is at `0x4011e87a`. It traps with `illegal` on a pointer outside the heap or not 16-byte aligned, the same rule as the Digitakt mk1's operator delete. The OS clears `0x40312000-0x47e28470` at reset, so static data placed there does not survive boot. A startup hook at `0x40133646` (`link.w` + `movem`) made exactly one 8 KiB allocation that stayed untouched for 20 M instructions. This is the cleanest way to own memory without a cave.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
facts.text: Sample pool: Logical range `0x400-0x19000400`, 400 MiB, allocations rounded to 8 KiB. The ColdFire's allocation records decide admission; no SHARC malloc is involved. In the SHARC's view the pool is a window at DSP byte address `0x8422b9c8 + (offset - 0x400)`, ending at `0x9d22b9c8`. Capicola reserves the top 8 MiB.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
facts.text: Recorder: the main OS fetches recorder data in chunks of at most `0x800` bytes over DSPI1 from a service whose physical owner (ColdFire, SHARC DDR or a third part) is not established. Staging buffers are at `0x4fe79340` / `0x4fe7a340`.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
facts.text: SHARC side: Sample-slot table at `0x257810 + slot*0x14`: 1,025 entries, slot `0x400` is the preview. Voices at `0x2412cc + lane*0x1d8`, 32 lanes: `+0` PCM pointer, `+0x188` length, `+0x1b8` active. Link-port 0 receive staging at `0x268220` (descriptor) and `0x268240` (a tag plus 4 KiB of payload).

facts.section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
facts.text: Once published to the SHARC, PCM keeps playing after the ColdFire source is freed, as long as the stock allocation stays owned. Saving, however, needs the source, and no read-back path from sample memory was found.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Three Digitakt II mod routes side by side (T21, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: digikit's patchkit (used by digitakt-ii-research's All-in-One and dt2-machine-lab), elekloader's core-dt2 (used by digitakt2-perform) and the hand-placed builds share the flash cave `0x403117c4-0x40312000`. elekloader's RAM `0x47f00000-0x47f40000` lies inside digikit's `cf.expansion` `0x47e8b000-0x47fe0000`. Full table of ranges and hook sites: [memory-maps.md](../common/memory-maps.md). `[doc]`

facts.text: A decoded section 7 over 1 MiB crashed a unit (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16): [firmware-container.md](../common/firmware-container.md), rule A46. `[hw]` {dt2-lab-capicola} ([I16](../INCIDENTS.md#i16-a-decoded-section-7-over-1-mib-crashed-the-unit))

facts.section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
facts.text: Reading a track's Sound parameter words needs no fixed address: get the project singleton, its ProjectSettings at project + `0x30` (static analysis only), the selected track from `view_track` (clamped 0-15), then `native_track_sound(active kit, track)` = kit + `0x6c` + `0x3c0` x track; vtable slot `0x28` of that Sound object returns the record pointer `*(sound + 0x10)` (0 when none is bound), and word i is a big-endian s16 at record + `0x14` + 2i. Anchors: settings `0x40041d18` (DT2 1.17) / `0x4003e40e` (DN2 1.12); `native_track_sound` `0x40035cca` / `0x40030e66`. The array holds 71 words on the DT2 and 101 on the DN2. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
facts.text: On the DN2 a track's Sound record can sit at an odd address (kit stride `0x48b`), so read it byte by byte. A parameter code maps to its array index through the descriptor table (rows of `0x3c` bytes, index as s32 at row + 4, -1 = no word); the same index means another parameter on another machine. P-locks, sound lock, LFO and MIDI CC writes go through other paths, and a latched parameter of a run-time machine changed no word in the array (where it is stored is open). `[doc]`/`[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
facts.text: Track overdrive (stock): the curve clamps to +-1 and applies y*(2-|y|) three times; the blend is x + mix*(y-x) with stock ramps for drive and mix. OVR Routing is parameter `0x103` (Sound mirror index 68; 0 = pre, `0x100` = post). The per-track stage is called twice per track from the voice chain. `[doc]` {digikit-overdrive}

facts.section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
facts.text: Run-time machines: on the DT2 they can use knob slots B C E F G H; a parameter on the seventh slot replaces LEV, whose level is then fixed at 100. The run-time module stage is limited to 64 KB; a TB-303 port costs about 8,000 SHARC instructions per 32-sample block. `[doc]` {digikit-tb303}

facts.section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
facts.text: ColdFire jump targets must be even: a jsr/jmp to an odd address faults with an address error on the unit while the emulator runs on; a byte-aligned mod section froze a DT2 at boot (I61). `[hw]` {elekloader-oddjump}

facts.section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
facts.text: Modwerk's DT2 base: a combined image booted on a DT2 (OS 1.17, 2026-11-08) and restored saved module kit data after a project reload. Its audio scheduler (grid callbacks and phrase replacement at the stock audio submission call `0x400d82f8`) is a proposal checked only in digikit fixtures. `[hw]` / `[emu]` {modwerk-dt2-base}

facts.section: Digitakt II / +Drive file writes from mod code (digikit finding 120, DT2 1.17)
facts.text: The firmware's own file calls can write samples: open (`0x40158902`, mode "w"), write (`0x4015866a`), reserve, hash (`0x4015b3aa`), close (`0x401588c0`), info, delete (`0x40157078`), mkdir and rename (`0x40156f6c`, which keeps the inode, size and stored hash). Each takes the recursive filesystem mutex itself and blocks, so call them from a task, never an interrupt. The sampler's recorder `0x40153c70` is a complete stock caller. `[doc]` (static)

facts.section: Digitakt II / +Drive file writes from mod code (digikit finding 120, DT2 1.17)
facts.text: Open does not truncate: an existing file opens at position 0 with its old size and data; stock deletes first. Whole 32 KiB pages at multiples of `0x8000` are written straight from the buffer, the rest goes through the page cache. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / +Drive file writes from mod code (digikit finding 120, DT2 1.17)
facts.text: The 16-byte trailer: files carry 16 zero bytes after the data, and the stored hash covers them; the C calls do not add them (the recorder and stock's MidiRpc close do), so a writer adds them before the hash. File info reports size minus 16. `[emu]` (card read back on the emulator) Elekloader's Rytm loader meets the same 16 bytes as a header at the start of each file on the Analog Rytm MKII ([analog-rytm.md](analog-rytm.md)).

facts.section: Digitakt II / +Drive file writes from mod code (digikit finding 120, DT2 1.17)
facts.text: Power cut: a cut mid-write leaves a visible file with a partial size and no hash; the mount was not seen to repair it. Delete refuses an open file (open-file bitmap at `0x46f4ded0`). Only `/factory` is RAM-backed; user files always go to the card, and a failed card write is not reported. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / +Drive file writes from mod code (digikit finding 120, DT2 1.17)
facts.text: On a unit (2026-11-11) digikit's bulk uploads through these calls left only complete files after a pulled cable, and the stock sample browser did not list the staging folder `/.dkstage`. `[hw]` {digikit-usbfast}

facts.section: Digitakt II / Projects, sample rows and the recorder (dt2-machine-lab Sketch, OS 1.16 and 1.17, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: Whole-sample-clear hook on OS 1.17: the entry `0x40154634` starts with push A2, push D2, `clr.l D2` (6 bytes); a hook resumes at `0x4015463a`. INIT NEW and a full project LOAD both pass it. It is a notice, not a promise that the recorder, loaders or DMA have stopped: drain your own work before stock frees the backing. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Projects, sample rows and the recorder (dt2-machine-lab Sketch, OS 1.16 and 1.17, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: OS 1.16 project LOAD: the stock clear runs once per sample slot, so it marks no project boundary; the post-clear sample-batch entry does. The load-and-select callback (caller `0x40046c8e`) saves a recovery copy to internal slot 128 before its asynchronous sample batch completes; a mod that blocks that save makes LOAD report LOAD ERROR although decoding succeeded (I93). `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Projects, sample rows and the recorder (dt2-machine-lab Sketch, OS 1.16 and 1.17, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: Sample rows are shared: digikit's `core/sample-pool` reserves the top sixteen rows (H112-H127); Sketch uses H124-H127 for live buffers and H116-H123 for FREEZE, so the two declare a conflict. A user sample in those rows also blocks the reservation. Two mods that reserve sample rows need one owner. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Projects, sample rows and the recorder (dt2-machine-lab Sketch, OS 1.16 and 1.17, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: OS 1.16 recorder editor (static): the waveform service `0x4001266a` issues recorder command 3 for four signed extrema; encoder handling at `0x40020960`; trim endpoints at view +`0x9a0`/+`0x9a4`; the accepted-range copy is command 4 at `0x4001282e`. facts.section: Digitakt II / Projects, sample rows and the recorder (dt2-machine-lab Sketch, OS 1.16 and 1.17, 2026-11-13)

facts.text: Pointer returns: the firmware returns pointers in d0, while GCC's m68k ABI reads them from a0; a C prototype returning a pointer froze the UI. Declare such routines as returning a 32-bit integer. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
facts.text: USB mode switch: `FUN_40006c16` has the same address and bytes on DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12. It takes no lock and cuts a MIDI reply in flight; USB restarts after a 30-tick counter (about 1 s in the emulator; counter DT2 `0x40965a38`, DN2 `0x4058f280`). The stored USB CONFIG byte (0 MIDI, 1 Overbridge, 2 AUDIO/MIDI; DT2 `0x4099d5c4`, DN2 `0x405ce898`) is written only by the menu actions (DT2 `0x4010331a`/`30`/`48`, DN2 `0x40104dc2`/`d8`/`f0`), never by the switch, so a reboot returns to the stored mode; an Overbridge disconnect (`FUN_400f2ce0`) is the only path that re-applies it by itself. DT2 connection-state word `0x40965a40`. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Take-over on units (2026-11-11): digikit's Fast USB switched both units from USB AUDIO/MIDI to USB MIDI in RAM for an upload over its bulk interface and back (SysEx TAKEOVER `0x1e`, RELEASE `0x1f`); the stored mode byte stayed unchanged and USB audio was heard working afterwards. Longer loops later lost a unit from USB (I80, next section). `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
facts.text: +Drive internals: close hash `0x4015b1e8` under the filesystem mutex `0x46f4deb0` (recursive lock `0x400015a0`, unlock `0x400016d2`); inode get/put/write `0x4015b92a`/`0x4015b846`/`0x4015b868`; extent lookup `0x4015813c`; hash-table rebuild `0x4015b0ee` (about 300 ms per file on a unit); event post `0x4015a6aa`. Data page 0 is card sector `0x5ee180` (page p at base + p x `0x40`), the first hash page sector `0x5ee980`. Every file write reaches the card before the call returns. The eSDHC read/write is clamped to 64 KiB (DT2 `0x4012e3c4`, DN2 `0x4012ca8a`). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Measured ceilings (8 MiB, 2026-11-11): DT2 +Drive file write 2.6 MB/s with 64 KiB calls, 7.8 MB/s with 256 KiB, 10.3 MB/s with 1 MiB; the firmware's close-hash re-read 4.2 MB/s; store writes DT2 about 7.2 MB/s, DN2 6.3 MB/s; raw card reads 15.3 MB/s on both; CPU hash 16-18.7 MB/s. A whole 8 MB upload: DT2 2.99-6.15 s (varies a lot between runs), DN2 1.75 s. Per file about 0.18-0.19 s fixed cost. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Fast close: digikit hashes from a card read-back and then runs the firmware's own close steps, byte-identical to the stock close, falling back to the firmware close if the read-back fails. After such uploads the stock browser listed the files, a sample loaded and played, and a project that referenced an uploaded sample reloaded and played it. Creating the staging folder `/.dkstage` cost about 420 ms and removing a file from it about 150 ms, so it now stays for the session. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
facts.text: SHARC cycle counter: each image has exactly one EMUCLK reader, the block handler (DT2 `0x1c74cd`, DN2 `0x1c9d6b`), which keeps a low-word delta for reporting only; nothing branches on it. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
facts.text: eMMC EXT_CSD copy in RAM: DT2 1.17 `0x4fe69100`, DN2 1.12 `0x4e6f9100`; bytes are reversed within each 32-bit word because the eSDHC runs little-endian. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: The USB mode take-over is not reliable on a unit: switching a Digitakt II from USB AUDIO/MIDI to USB MIDI in RAM and back lost the unit from USB in cycle 5 of a 20-cycle loop, and in cycle 11 after digikit added a 2 s restart hold and parked the PHY's line during the stop. The host saw no disconnect, the unit no longer answered, a cable replug did not help and only a power cycle did; both failures came on TAKEOVER, never on RELEASE. digikit now keeps the take-over off by default; with USB CONFIG set to USB MIDI in the menu its fast transfer ran fully reliably (I80, rule A55). `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: External ULPI PHY: the USB controller drives an external ULPI PHY (PORTSC.PTS = ULPI, set at init `0x40006d1c`-`0x40006d2c`). The stock firmware writes no PHY register: its only ULPI_VIEWPORT (`0xFC0B0170`) use is a read of PHY register 0 every 300 calls of a periodic function (`0x40006af8`), which resets the controller (not the PHY) when the read never finishes. It never sets PORTSC.PHCD. The VBUS interrupt (`0x40005e14`, OTGSC.BSVIS) starts or stops the controller; the restart `0x40006bc6` starts it only while OTGSC.BSV is set. Same code on DN2 1.12. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: The USB clock comes from the PHY: the stock init clears MISCCR.USBSRC (`0xEC09000E` bit 0), so the PHY's 60 MHz ULPI output clocks the controller's USB side. A PHY whose clock stops freezes USB while the rest of the unit runs on. The documented way to restart a stopped PHY clock is a viewport wake-up (WU set, RUN clear). Same code on DN2 1.12. `[doc]` {digikit-f123-bulk}

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: Stock controller reset: `0x40006ada` (same on DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12) stops the controller with restart type 2; after 30 ticks `0x40007104` sets USBCMD.RST and spins on it with no bound, runs the USB init `0x40006c52` and restarts if VBUS is valid. The firmware's own viewport watchdog uses this path. Each reset leaks one of the 16 shared timer slots (SB20). `[doc]` {digikit-f123-bulk}

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: How a failed take-over looks: after RS is set again PORTSC shows line state SE0 (`0xa0000005`; good switches show J), no SOF arrives and the host never addresses the device; after a controller reset OTGSC.BSV reads 0. Failures came on take-over and on release, with audio idle: 1 in 76 and 1 in 200 switches on two builds; parking the PHY line during the stop made it about 1 in 15. A replug never helped, a power cycle always did; a stop/hold/restart and the stock reset did not revive it. A viewport wake-up was never tried on a unit (I80). `[hw]` {digikit-f123-bulk}

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: USB AUDIO/MIDI port entry 5: the port table has 0x28-byte entries; entry 5 is at table + 0xC8 (DT2 `0x4029f048`): +0 connect `0x400040a6`, +4 disconnect `0x40004054`, +0xC configuration pointer, +0x10 length 0x148. The configuration has 5 interfaces (UAC2 on 0-2, MIDI on 3-4 with the EP1 bulk pair); EP2 IN is the iso feedback and EP2 OUT is unused. A bus reset clears ENDPTCTRL1-3 and every queue head, and SET_CONFIGURATION calls connect again. DN2 1.12 has the same code at other data addresses. `[doc]` {digikit-f123-bulk}

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: A bulk OUT endpoint fits beside live USB audio: digikit hooks the USB init entry `0x40006c52` (6-byte prologue, same on DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12; it runs at boot and again in interrupt context after a controller reset), copies the configuration, appends interface 5 (vendor class, EP2 OUT bulk, 512 bytes), sets wTotalLength 0x158 and repoints entry 5; connect and disconnect touch only the receive half of ENDPTCTRL2. Replies go back over SysEx. A probe sent 200 MB at 28 MB/s while audio played; real uploads on 2026-11-13: DN2 3.38 MB/s (6.5 MB) and 2.09 MB/s (146 MB in 200 files, audio clean), DT2 2.74 and 1.50 MB/s. macOS keeps audio and MIDI; Windows does not bind it without an MS OS 2.0 descriptor. Not yet tested: long runs, host sleep, a bus reset during a transfer. `[hw]` {digikit-f123-bulk}

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: eMMC: both units carry an eMMC 5.1 of 23.05 GiB with identical EXT_CSD: enhanced reliable write supported but not forced, 1 MiB cache off, background operations off, optimal write size 32 KiB. Card clock 37.71 MHz (75.43 MHz divided by 2) on a 4-bit bus in high-speed timing; the eSDHC has no 8-bit mode. `[hw]` (read on the units)

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: Stock card driver: data moves by eDMA channel 59 to the eSDHC data port, 16 bytes per request; every write uses CMD23 with the reliable-write bit. The block write and read split every transfer into 64 KiB commands: `cmpi.l #0x10000,D2` at offset 0x14 (entry) and 0x22 (chunk loop) of each function, same bytes on both images: DT2 1.17 read `0x4012e1b6` (sites `0x4012e1ca`, `0x4012e1d8`), write `0x4012e39c` (sites `0x4012e3b0`, `0x4012e3be`); DN2 1.12 read `0x4012c87a` (`0x4012c88e`, `0x4012c89c`), write `0x4012ca60` (`0x4012ca74`, `0x4012ca82`). The 64 KiB bounce buffer for unaligned buffers is the likely reason; the eDMA's 15-bit count allows at most 1023 blocks (511 KiB) a command, which digikit's sdhc-large uses (1022) for 16-byte aligned buffers it registers. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: Raw card rates (DN2, 8 MiB, median of 3): write 11.4 / 13.3 / 15.3 MB/s and read 13.8 / 15.6 / 16.1 MB/s with 32 KiB / 64 KiB / 511 KiB commands; reliable write and the card cache change nothing within 2 %. A copy in RAM runs at 18 MB/s, USB alone at 20.9 MB/s (13.5 MB/s while the CPU copies). An upload that reads every file back is capped at about 7.2-7.8 MB/s by the card. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: Cost per file: on the DN2 store the cost of an upload grows by about 0.46 ms for each file already stored (the store table is rewritten and read back at every commit), on top of about 95 ms; on the DT2 +Drive about 195 ms a file, with no growth across folders. For sample packs of hundreds of files this matters more than the transfer rate. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: +Drive ids at or above `0x1000000` never reach the card (DT2 1.17): the inode write-back `0x4015b868` and page write-back `0x40155c34` call the block write only for inode ids and page numbers below `0x1000000`; higher ones are copied into RAM tables (inodes at `0x47d73ed0 + n*0x80`, pages at `0x46f63ed0 + n*0x8000`, n counted from `0x1000000`). `[doc]` {digikit-f120}

facts.section: Digitakt II / MIDI notes from whiplash (DT2, OS 1.17 manual, 2026-11)
facts.text: NRPN numbers disagree between the OS 1.17 manual and midi.guide's data for track mute and level, pattern mute, master overdrive, filter env depth, filter base/width and portamento; all CCs agree (CONFLICTS O24). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / MIDI notes from whiplash (DT2, OS 1.17 manual, 2026-11)
facts.text: CC 80 (amp HOLD) at 127 switches HOLD to NOTE; it is not the longest hold. A sound ends on note-off only with AMP MODE = ADSR or HOLD = NOTE. Note 60 plays a sample at its own pitch only with TUNE 64 and the preset OCTAVE unchanged. No CC or NRPN selects the machine type. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Pre-send render hook proposal (Modwerk, OS 1.17, emulator)
facts.text: Modwerk's proposal guards the SHARC send-driver entry `0x1c18a6` (short-word PC), displacing one 6-byte instruction and resuming at `0x1c18a9`; the stock caller is at `0x1c3090`. A sidechain prototype (16 sources x 16 destinations) ran 9,060 SHARC instructions a block in digikit's emulator; with the hook off the PCM was byte-identical to stock. Not on a unit. `[emu]`
