facts.section: Digitakt II / USB MIDI callbacks and Shot's cost (digikit handover, 2026-11-15)
facts.text: The function at `0x4000434a` stores two USB MIDI callbacks into .bss slots: `0x409659d0` / `0x409659d4` on the Digitakt II (1.17), `0x4058f218` / `0x4058f21c` on the Digitone II 1.12. USB MIDI that arrives before they are set leaves the link dead while the CPU runs (an emulator-only failure in digikit's tests). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB MIDI callbacks and Shot's cost (digikit handover, 2026-11-15)
facts.text: digikit's Shot sample machine costs about 5,057 (DT2) / 5,266 (DN2) instructions per 32-frame block; 16 voices use 91 % of the DN2 headroom. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / ColdFire task switches, main-OS entry and the bus timer (digikit findings 07 and 132, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Every ColdFire task switch passes through `vector_32_handler` at `0x40000410` (20,760 entries on DT2 and 17,778 on DN2 over the probe window). Vector 205 is the switch entered from an interrupt, always from stacked IPL 0; vector 32 (`trap #0`) is a task yielding, with SR 0x2700; vector 191 does not occur, and no switch is entered from a handler at IPL 2 or higher. So code reachable from a task needs an entry/exit counter before it can be unloaded while running; code reached only from interrupts can be unloaded after masking interrupts and clearing its slot. `[emu]` (PC probe)

facts.section: Digitakt II / ColdFire task switches, main-OS entry and the bus timer (digikit findings 07 and 132, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Main-OS entry comes at instruction 299,258,200 on DT2 and 298,782,809 on DN2. `param_code` runs before it, from the boot project decode loop (caller DT2 `FUN_400e64dc`, return `0x400e6546`; DN2 `FUN_400e7eb0`, return `0x400e7f1a`), and saw only stock machine types even with a saved project that uses digikit's types 16/17: the saved project loads after main-OS entry, so hooks installed there are early enough. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / ColdFire task switches, main-OS entry and the bus timer (digikit findings 07 and 132, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
facts.text: DTIM0's counter `DTCN0` at `0xfc07000c` runs at the 132 MHz bus clock, 88,000 ticks per 32-sample frame, and is already running before the main OS. digikit uses it read-only as its profiling clock (`span_clock` in the device files). The rate was measured on the owner's unit on 2026-11-07 (the source does not say which device). `[hw]` The Analog Rytm MKII's DTCN0 runs at the same rate ([analog-rytm.md](analog-rytm.md)).

facts.section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
facts.text: One card transfer at a time: the eSDHC has one command and one data channel, no command queue and no packed commands; it supports SD Host 2.0 and MMC 4.2 only (no DDR), and the 8-bit pins are not bonded. The reference manual gives 40 MHz as the eSDHC maximum; the firmware runs 37.7 MHz (SDCLKFS=1, DVS=0, DT2 setup `0x4012d78e`). A command without data (CMD13) can go out during a data transfer, but errata SECF214 says it may see a spurious CRC or index error. FIFO 128 x 32 bit; the controller stops the card clock on FIFO under- or overrun. Wire ceiling about 18.5 MB/s payload, about 9.3 MB/s for write plus full read-back. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
facts.text: Stock card driver locking: every block transfer runs under one global mutex (DT2 `0x47de3cac`) plus a second mutex `0x44e4ae98` taken through `0x401344dc`; a request above 64 KiB is cut into 64 KiB chunks, each locked on its own. The caller starts eDMA channel 59 and waits with `sem_pend` on `0x44e3fec8` (command complete) and `0x44e3fec0` / `0x44e3feb8` (data); the eSDHC ISR `0x4012d5ba` (vector 223) posts `0x44e3fec8` on CC/CTOE and `0x44e3fec0` on TC or a data error (the poster of `0x44e3feb8` was not found). The task sleeps during DMA and card busy, so other tasks get the CPU. Reads use CMD18 with auto-CMD12 and no CMD23; writes send CMD23 with the reliable-write bit before every CMD25, no auto-CMD12. Setup: CMD6 HS_TIMING=1, BUS_WIDTH=1 (4 bit), ERASE_GROUP_DEF=1, CMD16 512; no cache enable or flush, packed commands or command queue seen. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
facts.text: RTOS primitives (DT2 1.17; the DN2 1.12 mutex functions sit at the same addresses): priority-preemptive, a larger number is a higher priority; task switch by `trap #0` (`0x40000410`); no tick that rotates tasks of equal priority was found `[?]`. Binary semaphores `sem_init` `0x40001398`, `sem_pend` `0x4000141a`, `sem_post` `0x4000155c` (a counting variant at `0x4000148c`, `0x400014fc`, `0x4000172a`). Mutexes `0x400015a0` / `0x400016d2` are recursive for the owner with FIFO waiters and no priority inheritance. No task delete, yield or event flags were found. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
facts.text: +Drive serialises as well: every `file.*` and `path.*` call runs under the file-system mutex `0x46f4deb0`, and the close (`0x4015b3aa` -> `0x4015b1e8`) holds it through the whole read-back and hash-table work. Several files can be open (open bitmap `0x46f4ded0`), but they share static scratch buffers (`0x4066d8c0`, `0x406658c0`, `0x44f2bc68`). So several writers (tasks, files or pieces of one file) cannot raise card throughput; a pipeline (one task waits on the card while another copies or hashes in RAM) is safe and helps. Keep middle-priority work from delaying the task that holds the card mutex. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
facts.text: +Drive page allocation (DT2 1.17): `file_reserve` `0x40158810` calls `0x40158448(id, 0, bytes, 0)`: inode get, missing-page count `0x40158326`, free-page count `0x40155f84` (bit by bit over the 0x14010-byte bitmap, no I/O), then `0x401581dc(inode, 0, pages, 0)` and the inode write-back `0x4015b868`. `0x401581dc` allocates first fit with `0x40155974` from page `0xa7a`, then from 0, writes the touched bitmap pages and adds one extent per allocation (`0x40157c68`); it stops silently when no page is free and does not write the inode back. Call it under the file-system mutex with an inode from inode get, hint 0. `[doc]` {digikit-f120}

facts.section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
facts.text: Where upload time goes (2026-11-16, every file hash-checked on the unit): one 9.8 MB file: DN2 3.66-3.73 MB/s (card writes 710 ms = 13.8 MB/s, copy from the USB buffers 710 ms, END with read-back, hash and commit 1100 ms); DT2 3.46-3.52 MB/s (BEGIN 141 ms, card writes 988 ms = 9.9 MB/s, copy 558 ms, END 1009 ms of which read-back 940 ms = 10.4 MB/s). A 309-file pack (1.05 MB a file): on the DN2 the END per file grew from 386 to 550 ms between two runs as the store filled (about 300-480 ms of it is the store-table commit); on the DT2 per file `file_reserve` 94 ms (also 90 ms for the 9.8 MB file), `path_open "w"` 52 ms, rename 56 ms, read-back hash 92 ms (32 KiB pages), the 16-byte trailer write 13 ms. The DT2's fixed cost of about 200 ms a file stays flat up to 618 files in one folder. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
facts.text: Cached USB receive is slower: reading the USB receive buffers through the cached window (with a cache-line invalidate before the read) gave 3.47-3.50 MB/s against 3.66-3.73 MB/s uncached on a DN2; the copy time stayed about 0.71 s, and the extra 0.19 s is likely the about 600,000 line invalidates per 9.8 MB. Why the copy runs at only about 14 MB/s is open. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
facts.text: What did help (all kept since runtime 0.8.3): one store-table commit for up to 16 files took a DN2 100-file pack from 2.42 to 3.25 MB/s, and 3.56 with copy/write overlap; overlap alone (a helper task copies into one 512 KiB half while the card writes the other) took a 9.8 MB file from 3.67 to 4.37 MB/s (DN2) and 3.53 to 4.01 MB/s (DT2). On the DT2, read-back in runs of up to 128 KiB, the trailer in the last write, page allocation without the free-page count and new files written at their final name (no rename; a power cut can leave one partial unhashed file visible) took a pack from 2.32 to 2.49 MB/s, and 3.07 MB/s with every lever; the 9.8 MB file reached 4.13 MB/s with read-back runs, trailer and overlap. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
facts.text: CACR and the by-address flush: both images write CACR once, at `0x4000055a` (`move.l #0xa50ce100,d0`: SPA=1, IVO=0, DDPI=0, IDPI=0, instruction and data cache on). With SPA=1, `cpushl bc,(ax)` searches by physical address and clears the line in both caches (RM Table 6-10), so one `cpushl` per 16-byte line is a correct flush for new code. Do not write CACR yourself. Whether a pipeline sync is needed after the last `cpushl` is open. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
facts.text: The task that loads a project: DT2 entry `0x400caff0` (created at `0x400cc7ce`, TCB `0x4039be58`, priority 2, stack `0x4039beac` + `0x4000`); DN2 entry `0x400cd5f2` (created at `0x400cec02`, TCB `0x40386e48`). It reaches `write_live_project` `0x400df95a`, `fx_array.load` `0x400daf54` and the sound-load exit; `fx_array.save` is reached from the UI side (`0x400dbdca`). This is call-graph reachability only (vtable calls are not edges). `[?]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
facts.text: The UI task and its queue: DT2 `main_os_task` `0x400337ba` (created at `0x40033280`, TCB `0x40966ee8`, priority 6, stack `0x4096775c` + `0x28000`) waits on queue `0x40966f3c` (wait function `0x40001928`) and switches on the message byte; the UI-loop site is `0x40033d06`. DN2: entry `0x4002ed34`, created at `0x4002e902`, TCB `0x4059e1c0`, queue `0x4059e214`, site `0x4002f17e`. No other code reads that queue, so modal pop-ups and browsers run inside message handlers and a UI-loop hook runs once per message. A7 inside one of the two stacks tells which task runs a hook. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
facts.text: Two level-7 interrupts (not maskable): INTC0 ICR2 (`0xfc048042`, set at `0x40001cbe`): EPF2, vector 0x108, handler `0x40001a10`, a 516-byte leaf with no callees. INTC1 ICR40 (`0xfc04c068`, set at `0x400d346e`): EDMA_INTR, its handler installed at run time into vector 0x2a0 from pointer `0x43153a2c` (DN2 sites `0x400d56c6`, `0x400d5996`); which code it runs is open. An IPL-7 mask therefore does not keep these two out. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
facts.text: Empty machine rows and the name table: stock `mf_dispatch` `0x400c89a4` uses `type < 7 ? 0x4293b960 + 0x2c * type : 0x4293ba68`, and the compare is unsigned (so -1 is out of range too); the fallback `0x4293ba68` is the row of type 6, the last stock machine, not type 0 (finding 135 as rewritten 2026-11-18 {digikit-1119}; the earlier reading "plays as type 0" is wrong, S24). No code keeps a pointer to a name-table row (only `lea` in the accessors); the machine list is fetched once into the view at boot. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
facts.text: The boot intro drops stock MidiRpc: after a restart digikit's runtime answered at once, but the firmware was still on its boot intro and dropped stock MidiRpc file requests; digikit's host now probes read-only for up to about 30 s and never resends a write (I114). `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Card concurrency, upload phases and hot-reload facts (digikit findings 133-135, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-11-16/17)
facts.text: Encoder input needs fast detents: digikit reports that the firmware encoder needs fast detents (12 detents moved a value about one or two steps); its test helpers send 4-detent events 30 ms apart. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings: MANUAL SLICE tests, menu font, DSP slot stubs (DT2 1.17, 2026-11-18)

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings: MANUAL SLICE tests, menu font, DSP slot stubs (DT2 1.17, 2026-11-18)

facts.section: Digitakt II / Modwerk's Digitakt II plan (GOAL.md, OS 1.17, 2026-11-16)

Switching mutes with the counter at the last step already changed steps 127-128; at step 2 it missed step 1; on the second UI tick (about 30 Hz) of step 1 the last step stayed and step 1 played switched. `[hw]` (author's reports, 128 steps, 140 and 200 BPM)

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 147-149: play state, filter type, LFO paths (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: Play state is two words: u32 at `0x43164f94` and `0x43165010`, each 0 stopped, 1 playing, 2 paused; the firmware's own test ORs the two (`0x400d688a`). Live record = playing and the byte at UIStates + `0x271`. `[doc]` (checked against the image bytes by a second reader)

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 147-149: play state, filter type, LFO paths (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: Filter type is a byte at sound + `0xa3`, right after the machine type byte. The accessor `0x400c89c6` takes types up to 5 and otherwise a fallback row; the stock sound loader resets a type of 6 or more to 0 (bound at `0x400db484`); the setter and the chooser apply no bound. Over MIDI the filter setter sends parameter `0xea`, which is parameter row 6 "Machine Type", the same id the machine setter sends (finding 150; corrected 2026-11-20, see O39); what a receiving unit does with it is open (H54). Names (table `0x4020ef30`): MM, LP4, EQU, COMB-, LEG, COMB+. On the DSP side the per-track type maps through DM `0x2567a0` (types 0-5 give 1, 3, 2, 4, 5, 6), read once in the emulator. On the DT2 the filter rows and the machine rows are one contiguous array. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 147-149: play state, filter type, LFO paths (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: LFO paths: tick `0x4013961e`, function table `0x402227d4`, and a second reader of that table at `0x401392d4`: a new waveform has to patch both. A third compare with 6 sets the RAND start phase; a wave byte of `0x80` or more is clamped to 0 and plays as TRI; the sound and p-lock loaders do not clamp the wave value. The LFO state belongs to a voice slot, not a track; the final LFO output is in the DSP transmit frame at `0x80005348` + `0xda` + stride x slot, so the live row alone is not enough. Graph tiles are 28 x 15 pixels. The claim that wave 7 "jumps into data" is wrong (digikit); the 1.16 facts above (the table cannot be extended by appending) stand. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 147-149: play state, filter type, LFO paths (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: Parameter table rows: MIDI CC and NRPN are halfwords at +`0x18`, the slot at +`0x1c`, template words at +`0x20`/+`0x24`, name +`0x28`, short name +`0x30`, formatter +`0x34`; range accessor `0x400da368`. `[doc]` (same layout on the DN2, see O37)

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 147-149: play state, filter type, LFO paths (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: Brain and the boot check: Brain pointer global `0x44f37098`; its view manager at Brain + `0x40` is a list of views. The boot "FILE SYSTEM OK" confirm window runs when the card superblock (eMMC sector `0x5D8000`) has state 3 or its checked word is 0; digikit's own card builders wrote 0, so every card they built ran the check at first boot (fixed). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 147-149: play state, filter type, LFO paths (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: Project hooks (planned, not checked): project setter `0x400c11ca`, project save `0x40043a30`. `[?]` (checked against image bytes on 2026-11-20: see the next section)

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 147-149: play state, filter type, LFO paths (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: Flash flow risk: after the last SysEx block a host can report "done" while the unit is still writing flash, and the old image can still answer INFO (digikit plan; not fixed yet). Wait for the unit's own restart before you call a flash finished (A23). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 110, 148 and 150: project paths, SHARC filter dispatch, machine setter (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-20)
facts.text: Project hook sites: slot setter `0x400c11ca` (first bytes `73 39` = `mvs.b (abs).l,D1`, 6 bytes to displace, slot argument at SP+4; callers `0x400424a2` and `0x400c0d90`); save `0x40043a30` (`(Project*, slot, progress)`, prologue `4f ef ff cc 48 d7 7c 1c`, 8 bytes); save exit `0x40043b1e` (save + `0xee`, the only `rts`; D0.b nonzero on success, slot in D3; a `before` hook must keep D2-D4/A2-A6). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 110, 148 and 150: project paths, SHARC filter dispatch, machine setter (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-20)
facts.text: Slot `0x80` is the live mirror: the save wrapper `0x40043b78` sets the slot, saves the real slot through `0x40043b28` (rejects slots above `0x80`), then saves the mirror slot `0x80`, then sets the slot again. New project (`initializeNewProject` `0x400465e2`) saves only the mirror; the wrapper saves the real slot. A save-exit hook sees D3 = `0x80` on the mirror save and must skip it. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 110, 148 and 150: project paths, SHARC filter dispatch, machine setter (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-20)
facts.text: Card write result: `0x400f5150` returns 0 for a slot above `0x80`, else the record flush `0x400f4d8c`: D0.b = 1 when written, 0 on failure, for a null record, or when the record is not loaded or not dirty (only the low byte is defined). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 110, 148 and 150: project paths, SHARC filter dispatch, machine setter (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-20)
facts.text: Project name: at most 16 bytes; the name entry's character table `0x4025dea9` holds `A-Z`, `Å Ä Ö Ü ß Æ Ø Ç Ñ` (bytes `c5 c4 d6 dc df c6 d8 c7 d1`), `0-9`, `~!@#$%^&()_+-=`, space; no lower case. The live name stores bytes of `0x80` and up as 0; the slot listing record (`MmcFs + 0x10 + slot * 0x1c`, name +8, save stamp +`0x18`) keeps them. Rename (callback `0x400a1246`) writes the name into the slot record, card-writes it and, for the current slot, calls `ProjectDataChangeInfo` `0x40042140`; it does not check other slots' names. Whether a rename keeps the save stamp is open. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 110, 148 and 150: project paths, SHARC filter dispatch, machine setter (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-20)
facts.text: What each stock project path does (slot setter S, save stamp at slot record +`0x18`): Delete (callback `0x400a13f0`) clears the record's valid byte (`0x400f4d58`) and erases the card slot, S(-1) only if the deleted slot is current, no save. Clear (`0x400a131e` single, `0x400a1376` several slots) resets the record through `0x4004234e` (name "NEW PROJECT", bulk regions from +`0x200`) but keeps the save stamp. Paste (`0x400a12f8` -> `0x400f548e`) copies `0xdd9604` bytes from the clipboard to the destination record from its start, stamp and name included. Unload calls `initializeNewProject(-1)`. Format (`0x40131276`) calls S(-1) only when a Project exists; its first erase loop covers `0x400000` bytes in `0x800` chunks (whether every later loop stays below digikit's store at `0x457FFF` is open). Load from card: wrapper `0x40046c38`, `loadProjectFromMmc` `0x40046906`, S at `0x40046ca0`, then a mirror save. `0x40041c96` is a change notification, not the stamp builder (corrects digikit's earlier plan). `[doc]` (DT2 traced; Move (cut) `0x400f539e` has no static callers; what triggers load from memory `0x40043f74` is open)

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 110, 148 and 150: project paths, SHARC filter dispatch, machine setter (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-20)
facts.text: Filter type graph: the response graph is x 21..71, y 7..23 (51 x 17 px); a type outside 0..5 draws no response curve and leaves that box blank, while the filter envelope graph (x 21..71, y 34..50) and the page dots still draw. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 110, 148 and 150: project paths, SHARC filter dispatch, machine setter (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-20)
facts.text: SHARC filter dispatch: the converter `0x1c24e9` maps the track's filter-type frame word through DM `0x2567a0` to S3 and stores it at word +31 of the per-voice record (base `0x2506ec` + voice x `0xdc`; the machine selector goes to +16). `0x1c642a` then jumps on S3 twice, both bounded at 7: a coefficient stage (table `0x8055c858`, bound at `0x1c66be`, skip at `0x1c66d8`) and a process stage (table `0x8055c874`, bound `0x1c6c0d`, skip `0x1c6c13`). Process routines: S3 1 `0x1cdbb2`, 2 `0x1cd286`, 3 `0x1cc79e`, 4 and 6 `0x1cbf07`, 5 `0x1ccd96`; all but 5 run in place on the voice buffer, 5 writes to `0x8045c3c0`. Static cost per 32-sample block (upper bound, no stalls): about 640, 1,140, 2,300, 1,635 and 490 instructions. `[doc]` The `0x2567a0` table is filled at run time (not in the image). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 110, 148 and 150: project paths, SHARC filter dispatch, machine setter (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-20)
facts.text: New filter types: a type of 16..31 reads other data from `0x2567a0` words 16..31, so S3 is 0 or 7 and up, both stages skip and the voice plays unfiltered without a fault (`[?]`, an emulator check is still to come). Types 8..14 map to stock filters: never store them. The filter envelope and key tracking are added on the SHARC in the coefficient stage; LFOs and MIDI modulators are added on the ColdFire before the frame is built. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 110, 148 and 150: project paths, SHARC filter dispatch, machine setter (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-20)
facts.text: Machine type setter `0x40051712` `(track object*, type, track, flag)`: refuses a type the track does not permit (`0x400da514`), writes sound + `0xa2` only when a settings mode (`0x4004c6f8`) is not 2, posts a SoundParamChangedInfo, and with flag set sends parameter `0xea` (type << 7, `0x40121c74`) or (`0xf`, type) (`0x40121c2c`) depending on another setting. The chooser calls the KitActive wrapper `0x40036798` `(KitActive, track, type, 1, 1)`, which for type 5 (probably the MIDI machine) sets bit `track` in the mask at KitActive + `0x552e` and addresses track objects at KitActive + `0x6c` + track x `0x3c0`. The filter setter `0x40051886` is a copy without the permit check and sends the same parameter `0xea`. Never write the type byte directly: a raw write to sound + `0xa3` did not reach the DSP (finding 148). How code outside a view gets KitActive was open (answered in the digikit-1121 section below); the Project singleton comes from `0x40198b7e` (global `0x44f370a0`). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / elekloader core-dt2 1.1 and 1.2: frame values, key LEDs, TELOS sites (DT2 1.17, 2026-11-19)
facts.text: Per-frame parameter values: at `0x4002e90c` the frame interrupt has rebuilt each track's values from the smoother (block `0x80005b50`, 71 values a track, from +0x22) and is about to call the per-track modulators (`jsr 0x400d9508`); values added there are heard but never saved, since the kit and pages are untouched. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / elekloader core-dt2 1.1 and 1.2: frame values, key LEDs, TELOS sites (DT2 1.17, 2026-11-19)
facts.text: Key LEDs: the LED frame (`0x4003117c`) clears every LED, then the views set theirs and the first setter wins. A handler sets an LED through the stock setter with layer 2 (value's high nibble a colour; layer 1 turns it off); trig keys are key code + 1, the page keys TRIG to MOD key code + 19. A redraw is asked for with the view controller's byte +0x21 (Brain + 0x40). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / elekloader core-dt2 1.1 and 1.2: frame values, key LEDs, TELOS sites (DT2 1.17, 2026-11-19)
facts.text: Kit copies: a kit is `0x5574` bytes and the OS copies kits in RAM with `memcpy` (`0x40136388`): pattern copy and paste, PASTE KIT, undo, the clipboard. A mod keeping data in a kit record's unused tail must follow those copies. Stock keeps the unused header and kit bytes when it re-saves a project it loaded. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / elekloader core-dt2 1.1 and 1.2: frame values, key LEDs, TELOS sites (DT2 1.17, 2026-11-19)
facts.text: Sites a loader on the unit needs (core-dt2 1.2): card bring-up status stored at `0x400cccbe`; after the file system mount (`0x4015a72c`) at `0x400ccd6c`; project slot write entry `0x40043a30`; project load entry `0x40046c38`; crash printer installed as exception hook at `0x4011d4a2`; MIDI task SysEx router at `0x40120006` (message a1, length d1, source d2); SysEx sender `0x40121d2a`. Project events run in a background worker; slot 128 is the working copy, saved at boot and after each load, and the boot's own load of it is not a project-load call. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / elekloader core-dt2 1.1 and 1.2: frame values, key LEDs, TELOS sites (DT2 1.17, 2026-11-19)
facts.text: Restart and tasks: the firmware's restart `0x40005608` turns interrupts off, drains the console, clears DDR word 0 and asks the reset controller for a soft reset. A cold boot of 1.17 creates fifteen static tasks through `0x400012c8` (saved SP at TCB+72); the init task (`0x400cc9c8`) is the one that brings up the card. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / elekloader core-dt2 1.1 and 1.2: frame values, key LEDs, TELOS sites (DT2 1.17, 2026-11-19)
facts.text: No room for a stock copy: unlike the Digitakt mk1, the Digitakt II has no free RAM for a copy of its 3.2 MB OS, so a +Drive loader reads stock bytes from RAM as the OS has them. All of the above ran in digikit's ColdFire emulator with TELOS; not yet on a unit. `[emu]` / `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 152, 155, 156: bootstrap stage, key event path, NameView, eMMC entries, EP0 (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: Bootstrap stage: the DT2 and DN2 bootstraps (1.16, 1.17, 1.11, 1.12) stage packed MAIN at `0x40400000` (constant at `0x800005cc`, `0x800005ec`, `0x8000063c`, `0x80001d3e`, `0x80001d5e`) and unpack in place to `0x40000400` with no bound or checksum; 1.15C and DN2 1.10E staged at `0x40200000`, as the Syntakt still does. So an unpacked MAIN may reach `0x3FFC00` bytes before the margin matters; check it anyway (A14). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 152, 155, 156: bootstrap stage, key event path, NameView, eMMC entries, EP0 (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: KitActive outside a view: call the active-kit getter `0x40041d24` with the Project singleton (`0x40198b7e`); the MachineSelectionView constructor stores exactly that at +`0x84` (`0x40061268`-`0x4006128e`). digikit's debug SETUP command commits machine and filter types through the chooser's own calls (`0x40036798`, filter `0x4003696e`, both `(KitActive, track, type, 1, 1)`), and the firmware's MACHINE_CHANGE followed each change in the emulator. `[doc]` / `[emu]` (answers the open question in the section above)

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 152, 155, 156: bootstrap stage, key event path, NameView, eMMC entries, EP0 (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: Key event path: the UI task pops a key record (caller `0x40033d94`) and calls the runner `0x40030bd0` `(Brain*, KeyEvent*)`, which calls an idle reset (`0x40030b50`), the listeners at Brain + `0x94`, then tail-jumps to the walker `0x4011c79c` `(ViewController*, KeyEvent*)`. The walker runs the release callbacks of the key on a release, then offers the event to the views from the top (offer loop `0x4011c41a`, vtable slot 2); the first nonzero answer stops it. Every view sees keys only through it. KeyEvent: +`0xc` key code, +`0x10` flags (bit 0 press, bit 1 FUNC held, bit 4 release). Chords have no event: views ask `key_down` (`0x4011e150`, bitmap at `0x44dc8644`). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 152, 155, 156: bootstrap stage, key event path, NameView, eMMC entries, EP0 (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: A clean hook site for key events: the walker entry, 8 bytes `4fef ffa0 48d7 7cfc` (`lea -0x60(sp),sp; movem.l`), same bytes on DN2. Consume with `moveq #1,d0; rts`: views and release callbacks are skipped, the runner's listeners still ran. D0, D1, A0, A1 are live at the tail, so save them. Swallow the release of a swallowed press and pass the release of a passed one; never swallow TRK. Run no module code inside the walker; queue it for the UI pass. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 152, 155, 156: bootstrap stage, key event path, NameView, eMMC entries, EP0 (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: Menus and NameView act on release: YES and NO act on the key's release, the arrows on the press. A view pushed from a YES press therefore receives that YES's release as its own key: push after the release. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 152, 155, 156: bootstrap stage, key event path, NameView, eMMC entries, EP0 (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: Key codes (table `0x4020afb8`, `key_down` bit map `0x4020b084`): 1 TRIG, 2 SRC, 3 FLTR, 4 AMP, 5 FX, 6 MOD, 7 PRESET, 8 SETTINGS, 9 TEMPO, 10 YES, 11 UP, 12 NO, 13 LEFT, 14 DOWN, 15 RIGHT, 16 TRK, 17 FUNC, 18 KEYBOARD, 19 RECORD, 20 PLAY, 21 STOP, 22 PAGE, 23 PTN, 24 SONG, 25-40 TRIG 1-16, 41-48 encoder pushes A-H, 49 LEVEL, 50 SAMPLING. On the Syntakt the same keys have other ids (see syntakt.md). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 152, 155, 156: bootstrap stage, key event path, NameView, eMMC entries, EP0 (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: View class: ctor `0x4011b06e` `(this, name)` (does not clear +`0x14`, +`0x16`, +`0x17`, +`0x30`: allocate zeroed), vptr `0x4021dfd8`, 17 slots, size `0x4c`; +`0x14` dirty, +`0x16` opaque (views below the top opaque view are not drawn; set it before the push), +`0x28` name (not copied), +`0x2c` manager. `invalidate` `0x4011b126`; render `0x4011bc96` runs only when VC + `0x20` is set; push `0x4011c08a` (shared_ptr) / `0x4011c2a6` (raw pointer). Lifetime: a raw-pointer block's dispose calls slot 1 (deleting dtor), a make_shared block's dispose calls slot 0 (no free), so keep the slot the block type uses valid. View stack: Brain `0x44f37098`, manager at + `0x40`, list sentinel at + `0x14`, node next +0, prev +4, view +8. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 152, 155, 156: bootstrap stage, key event path, NameView, eMMC entries, EP0 (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: NameView (the stock naming screen): 8-argument ctor `0x40117ac2` `(this, prompt, initial, number, maxlen, show_number, number_fmt, done)`, 7-argument wrapper `0x40117c70`, key function `0x40118260`; object `0xa0` bytes (make_shared block `0xb0`). `done` is a `std::function<void(std::string,int)>` at +`0x7c`, called on YES before the close; NO closes without calling it; an empty text is refused unless byte +`0x94` is set. No lower case; FUNC + YES inserts a space, FUNC + NO deletes, SETTINGS gives a random name. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 152, 155, 156: bootstrap stage, key event path, NameView, eMMC entries, EP0 (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: Fonts: stock UI font `0x402a9be0` (box height 6), a large ROM font `0x402a764c` (height 15, A-Z, 0-9 and a few symbols; reached only through RAM wrappers); text width `0x4011467a`. Header word 0 is not the glyph width. Text y counts from the screen bottom. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 152, 155, 156: bootstrap stage, key event path, NameView, eMMC entries, EP0 (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: eMMC block write `0x4012e39c` and erase `0x4012e0ce`, capacity getter `0x4012ddd6`: same code as on the Syntakt and DN2: the write is bounded only by the capacity, the erase by nothing (count 0 ends at `sector - 1`). Many callers on the DT2 (27 for the write, mostly the +Drive folder filesystem); how the DT2 Data API sizes a sample write is not read. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 152, 155, 156: bootstrap stage, key event path, NameView, eMMC entries, EP0 (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: EP0: the setup dispatcher `0x40005ff6` gives a BOS request (GET_DESCRIPTOR type `0x0F`) no answer at all (the host times out); unknown vendor requests stall; DEVICE_QUALIFIER stalls; free `0xC0` vendor codes are 3 and 6-255; it has no string index `0xEE`, so Windows binds no WinUSB driver by itself. The setup packet is at `0x47db4198`; EP0 send `0x40005f30` returns at once for more than `0x1000` bytes. digikit built a hook that answers BOS and the MS OS 2.0 set in USB AUDIO/MIDI mode only (bcdUSB `0x0201`); emulator and unit checks are open. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit findings 152, 155, 156: bootstrap stage, key event path, NameView, eMMC entries, EP0 (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: Project hook sites (exits): paste exit `0x400f55aa` (D0.b nonzero when the copy reached the card write, D6 the slot), clear-one exit `0x400a1368`, clear-many exit `0x400a13e6`; paste and clear run on the BgWorker thread (`0x400f0abc`) and finish their card write inside the job, so a hook at their entry sees the old listing. The slot listing is in `MmcFs` (getter `0x4019dbda`): slot s at + `0x10` + s x `0x1c`, name +8 (16 bytes, no terminator), save stamp +`0x18`; slot `0x80` is the live mirror. The slot byte `0x4099d5c5` holds the last persisted slot. A menu rename of the current project gives it a new save stamp (DN2 emulator). `[doc]` / `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit finding 158: service entry survey (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-22)
facts.text: Main-OS code and tables are writable at run time: ACR0 maps `0x40000000-0x47ffffff` copyback and not write-protected, and no MMU write protection was found; "flashed" only means patched into the .syx before boot. A code write still needs a cache push (`cpushl`). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit finding 158: service entry survey (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-22)
facts.text: No firmware dispatcher to reuse: every hooked site on both CPUs is a direct call, a jump or a mid-function address. The LFO function table `0x402227d4` can only replace waves 0-5 (wave 6 branches to RAND before the table; slot 6 is the first long of the slew table); new waves need the six compare sites, tick `0x40139804`/`0x4013986c`/`0x4013977e` (vector 191 only) and reader `0x401394dc`/`0x4013954a`/`0x4013944e` (task). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit finding 158: service entry survey (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-22)
facts.text: Vector 191's slot `0x400002fc` is RAM, written at boot by `0x4002d4f2`; redirecting it moves the whole handler. Whether its interrupt level is below 7 is open. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit finding 158: service entry survey (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-22)
facts.text: Order in the main OS task: the TimerManager, Brain and MmcFs constructors run first, then the MainScreenView constructor, then the queue wait; the machine list is built after the task entry, so tables filled at the task entry are seen by stock's builders. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit finding 158: service entry survey (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-22)
facts.text: Machine tables (const data in DDR, no slack): list order `0x401f5458` (read by `0x40052a08`, `0x40052c98`), names `0x4020ef78` (3 accessors bounded by `moveq #last`), permit mask `0x4020f0ce` (read in `0x400da514`), per-type byte `0x401eda30` (12 references). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit finding 158: service entry survey (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-22)
facts.text: Parameter table: `0x4020f59c`, 275 rows of 60 B, count `0x113` at `0x400c8932`; the next object starts at `0x40211a68`, so no slack. Readers use absolute addresses at 110 sites (56 references plus 54 `cmpi.l` bounds): a larger table means patching all of them or a copy. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit finding 158: service entry survey (DT2 1.17, static, 2026-11-22)
facts.text: SHARC entries: render entry `0x1c4ecf` (called at `0x1c6b00`); the switch tables in `0x1c642a` (`0x8055c840`, `0x8055c858`, `0x8055c874`) are read-only boot-stream data; FX entry `0x1c80f2`, send `0x1c207b`; block handler `0x1c74cd` with command table `0x25f7b0`; RPC command table `0x2577c4` (11 entries). No load-time path can reach them, so SHARC sites stay flashed. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit runtime plans and LFO hooks at load (DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, emulator and plans, 2026-11-22/23)
facts.text: First ColdFire hooks installed at load, not flashed: the image module `core/lfo` (six interrupt stubs at the LFO tick and reader compare sites) is gone from every DT2 and DN2 patch set; `lfo.dks` on the card now installs the six interrupt hooks and the MOD page hooks when it loads. It follows finding 158 (main-OS code is writable DDR). The hook names carry `_dt2` / `_dn2` until the next table version. Emulator device tests; the `lfo` device test still fails on main for a harness reason. `[emu]` {digikit-1123}

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit runtime plans and LFO hooks at load (DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, emulator and plans, 2026-11-22/23)
facts.text: Boot counter trap: digikit's runtime counts a boot as stable only after 30 s, counted from the first UI-loop pass. Three restarts in a row without 30 s of running put the unit into safe mode by counter (no modules), even when nothing crashed. digikit's test harness hit this and now sets a 1 s period for its tests. Let the unit run for 30 s between restarts. `[emu]` {digikit-1123}

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit runtime plans and LFO hooks at load (DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, emulator and plans, 2026-11-22/23)
facts.text: Planned split (approved, not built): a flashed resident core (about 108 KB: reset installer, platform hooks, boot counter, safe mode, crash and hang records, DSP hang watch, store, the Transfer repair commands, a 2-3 KB stage-1 loader) and a card system package (about 167 KB: package manager, full loader, DSP loading, DIGIKIT menu). Stage 1 streams the package through the 128 KB stage with a SHA-256 check and puts it at the top of the 512 KB arena. A missing, broken or wrong-version package gives a new core-only level (stock firmware plus Transfer, no DIGIKIT UI), not counted as a crash. `[doc]` {digikit-1123}

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit runtime plans and LFO hooks at load (DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, emulator and plans, 2026-11-22/23)
facts.text: Stack size of the boot path: building the runtime object in place cut the boot frame from 60 KB to about 7 KB (6,740 B); the worst boot chain of the package manager is about 24 KB. The runtime text grew to about 252,900 B (+41 KB) with the package manager. A mod that runs large Rust code from a firmware task should measure its frames: the main task's stack depth is not measured anywhere we know. `[doc]` {digikit-1123}

facts.section: Digitakt II / digikit runtime plans and LFO hooks at load (DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, emulator and plans, 2026-11-22/23)
facts.text: Module files will break: header table version 4 (runtime 0.12.0, decided 2026-11-22) refuses every older `.dkm` and `.dks` file (E_CONTRACT, "built for an older runtime"); cards in the field need repacked modules. `[doc]` {digikit-1123}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Where the audio runs (Digiwerk prior-art survey, 2026-10)
facts.text: The Digitakt mk1 renders all its audio on the ColdFire itself, in the render interrupt (vector 191). It has no DSP chip. New machines and filters (DigiFilter, digistring, digisophie, digineighbor, digislicer) are ColdFire C built with `m68k-elf-gcc -mcpu=54455`, hooked in the render ISR through elekloader. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Render path, injection point and key tables (digigrain's platform skills, OS 1.53, Ghidra plus digiemu)
Digitakt (mk1) / Render path, injection point and key tables (digigrain's platform skills, OS 1.53, Ghidra plus digiemu)
facts.text: The cleanest place to add a machine: each voice's mono block at `0x80001a18 + 128*v` (32 x int32, Q31). Anything written there before the per-voice processing step gets the stock filter, amp, pan, level, mute and effects for free, and resampling records it too. Bit reduction acts *inside* the stock voice synth, before that point. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Render path, injection point and key tables (digigrain's platform skills, OS 1.53, Ghidra plus digiemu)
facts.text: Samples: table at `0x403193a0`, 16 bytes per slot `{PCM ptr, ?, length, ratio Q30}`, valid slots 0..130 (`0x82` is the audition slot); PCM is s16 mono. A voice advances its position by 32 x the pitch ratio per block. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Render path, injection point and key tables (digigrain's platform skills, OS 1.53, Ghidra plus digiemu)
facts.text: Parameter descriptors: `0x401a9d9c + 52*id`. 44 code sites clamp ids >= 164 to 0, so new parameters must fit below 164 or every one of those sites needs a patch. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Render path, injection point and key tables (digigrain's platform skills, OS 1.53, Ghidra plus digiemu)
facts.text: Heap: `operator new` is `0x400d4180`. Never free a firmware-owned buffer: operator delete halts on a non-heap pointer. Never write message `+0x48` (the next link). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Render path, injection point and key tables (digigrain's platform skills, OS 1.53, Ghidra plus digiemu)
facts.text: Bound the worst case, not the average: an early granular engine froze the UI at low pitch, because fixed-length source grains became long, the pool filled up and every voice ran its worst case. The fix made grain length independent of pitch and capped overlap. `[hw]` ([I24](../INCIDENTS.md#i24-a-granular-engine-froze-the-ui-at-low-pitch))

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Render path, injection point and key tables (digigrain's platform skills, OS 1.53, Ghidra plus digiemu)
facts.text: Recorder (static reading, not yet run in an emulator; digigrain's recorder skill): the record buffer holds 1,584,000 frames (33.0 s at 48 kHz mono) as two planes written together, the top 16 bits at `0x4237DF90 + 2n` and bits 8-15 at `0x421FB410 + n`, so the reassembled sample is 24-bit. The source selector fills a mono capture block at `0x800032c4`; sources 9-16 (TRK1-8) are a straight copy of the voice block `0x80001a18 + 128*(t-1)`, so a machine that writes the voice block can be resampled for free. Sample slot `0x82` is the recorder's preview slot; a sample-table setter at `0x400763b4` fills a slot and, below `0x80`, its 255-entry slice table. `[doc]` {digigrain-skills}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Render path, injection point and key tables (digigrain's platform skills, OS 1.53, Ghidra plus digiemu)

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Ecosystem snapshot, Digitakt mk1 (altstrument 2026-10-31: 13 firmware entries + screendump; elektronmods lists 20 Digitakt entries)
facts.text: digiemu - emulates the Digitakt mk1 firmware on a ColdFire CPU with a patched Unicorn (six patches: three fix ColdFire flags and the multiply-accumulate unit, three make it fast enough for live audio); clickable panel, screen, keys, LEDs, sequencer, +Drive, live 48 kHz audio; tested on OS 1.53 (SHA-256 `9bdd44bb...29bcc92`), other mk1 releases offered as untested; runs about 2.5x faster than the hardware needs; first boot installs the factory project (~25 s, once per firmware); limits: factory sample library absent, 44.1 kHz pitch unverified, interrupt controller approximated, loading samples restarts the firmware (~15 s); its README still says Digitone mk1 is not supported although the directories list it. A content guard in CI rejects firmware, snapshots, card images and files over 1 MB. GPL-2.0-or-later. `[doc]` {digiemu-readme}

facts.text: digislicer (1.2 README; 2.5 per altstrument) - hold YES ~1 s on a SLICE track's SRC page to open the editor; slices keyed to the sample content and saved to the +Drive about one second after the editor closes (`/cfw/slices.a`, `/cfw/slices.b`; a `/cfw` folder appears in the sample browser); max 64 slices per sample; GRID gets a step past 64 = AUTO (transient slicing); a kit saved with AUTO plays the 64-slice grid on stock firmware; 1.1 and 1.2 "not yet tried on a unit" (an earlier combined build 1.8J ran on one); cold-boot comparison vs stock showed one 1 ms silent block from hook-bus timing. `[hw]/[emu]` {digislicer-readme}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Ecosystem snapshot, Digitakt mk1 (altstrument 2026-10-31: 13 firmware entries + screendump; elektronmods lists 20 Digitakt entries)
facts.text: DigiFilter - patches three sites (widen Filter Type range 7->11, re-point the TYPE label formatter, hook the per-voice filter call; stock types tail-call the stock filter); DSP is integer-only, no FPU, no libgcc; BP/BP2 = trapezoidal state-variable filter, COMB/TRASH = two feedback combs; coefficients smoothed per block; per voice per block (digiemu): stock TYPE 1 ~2,400 instructions, BP/BP2 ~2,800, COMB/TRASH ~1,750 (the README claims "at or below stock" - contradicted by its own BP figure); BP can clip at high RESO (no output saturation); response curve cosmetic; needs core 2.1; emulator-tested only in the README (later versions: v1.1b lowers per-voice cost, v1.2 caps Digitakt OB resonance at 75 %). `[emu]` {digifilter-readme}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / elekloader core 4.1-4.3 and compatibility (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Core 4.2 adds a live-note event (live notes before the voice; a handler can take them). Stock NOTE_ON/NOTE_OFF are at `0x400d53dc`/`0x400d575e` on 1.53 and `0x400d5604`/`0x400d5986` on 1.54; digipoly, digislicer and OB-1 hook these routines themselves. Core 4.3 adds a MIDI CC event at `0x400158ec` in the CC router `0x400158d2` (same on 1.53 and 1.54). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / elekloader core 4.1-4.3 and compatibility (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Core 4.1 patches the master-output sites itself, so Digi EQ 1.0c and Tone+FX's Digitakt files (3.2a3, 4.0c), which patch the same places, refuse to link with it; the builder falls back to core 4.0 for them. Tone+FX and Digi EQ also cannot go together: both take the master view's draw, the render site `0x400721e6` and kind-0 pages. `[doc]` {elekloader-cores} {tonefx-dt-port}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / elekloader core 4.1-4.3 and compatibility (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Up to Tone+FX 4.1a its author found no spare per-pattern MIDI block on the DT1 (4.3b then used a saved MIDI-track record, below); the kit spare at kit + `0x530` and the pattern spare bytes are already used by Digi Matrix, Digi Poly and Digi EQ, so Tone+FX up to 4.1a keeps its Digitakt data in RAM, lost on power cycle or project load. `[doc]` {tonefx-pattern-storage}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / elekloader core 4.1-4.3 and compatibility (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Tone+FX 4.3b keeps its Digitakt settings in MIDI track 8's saved kit record at kit + `0x8ba` (the track reserved on channel 16, block magic "DGX4"), so the stock serializer saves them and they survive a pattern switch, a project load and a power cycle. Users must leave MIDI track 8 alone; another mod using that record clashes. Not yet tested on a unit. `[doc]` {tonefx-43b}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / elekloader core 4.1-4.3 and compatibility (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Kit MIDI-track records: the DT1 kit holds eight MIDI-track records at kit + `0x59a` + t x `0x70`, each `0x6c` bytes; the stock pattern serializer carries only the first 41 words of each to the +Drive, and elekloader rewrites the byte at record +8, so Tone+FX's block starts at record +`0x10` (+`0x10`..+`0x51`). On OS 1.54 save runs `0x4007a300` -> `0x40079d22` and load `0x40079f86` -> `0x40079cc2`. `FW_TEMPO` is at `0x4020db60` on 1.53 and `0x4020df10` on 1.54. `[doc]` {tonefx-records}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / elekloader core 4.1-4.3 and compatibility (2026-11-10)
facts.text: GLIDE (ClaidArremer) stores PORT and LEG in the MIDI chord-note fields NOT3 and NOT4 of the pattern, which audio tracks never play, so stock saves, locks, copies and clears them like any trig parameter, and old patterns open with both OFF. Another mod using NOT3/NOT4 on audio tracks clashes. 0.4 tested on a Digitakt mk1, OS 1.54. `[hw]` {glide-dt}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / elekloader core 4.1-4.3 and compatibility (2026-11-10)
facts.text: elekloader Digitakt cores and Tone+FX 4.3b: core 4.0 lacks the `fw_tempo` export the stutter needs and cores 4.3 and 5.0 claim its master sites (render `0x400721e6`), so the release ships its own core-4.0.1 (S21). On 1.54 the Digitakt file takes `.run` 20,352 and `.bss` 104,300 bytes. `[doc]` {tonefx-43b}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Stock compressor, read by Synfact (OS 1.54, 2026-11-20)
facts.text: Stock compressor routine (OS 1.54, from Synfact's Syntakt port study): the master compressor is `[0x4007425e, 0x4007472a)` (1,228 bytes), initialised by `0x400741d8`; the GR meter is drawn by `0x40038f80` (half-dB steps, 50 pixels for 31.5 dB, at x = 126) and reads GR from `0x400784e0`. In Unicorn with EMAC it costs 3,860-4,015 instructions per 32-frame block; the gain calculation alone 2,896-3,051. The detector works per sample. `[emu]` {synfact-1121}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Stock compressor, read by Synfact (OS 1.54, 2026-11-20)
facts.text: SCF control (OS 1.54): parameter record `0x401ab34c` ("SCF" / "Sidechain Filter"); its dial is the 27-frame bipolar filter animation `0x421fa2fc`, drawn by `0x400601f0` (low-pass at frame 0, flat at 13, high-pass at 26). Digitakt's SCF uses three coefficients interpolated per sample (6 MACs a frame) and also low-passes. `[doc]` {synfact-1123}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Modwerk Digi Perform (OS 1.53/1.54, 2026-11-11)

Mod data kept in a kit's spare bytes needs its own path through a power cycle (I77). `[hw]` (power cycle) / `[emu]` (the cause)

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Modwerk Digi Perform (OS 1.53/1.54, 2026-11-11)

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Digi CMI on the unit (OS 1.54, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: The stock render already takes about 85 % of the audio interrupt: Digi CMI's meter (render entry to exit over the block period, timed with PIT0's counter `0xFC080004`, read only; 0.485 µs a tick, about 1,375 ticks a block of 667 µs) read 85 % peak right after boot. In digiemu the render (`0x40077428`-`0x400784c8`) runs about 85,000 instructions a block, 98 % of them stock's; at about 1.6-1.7 cycles an instruction that fits the 85 %. The UI gets what is left, so a few percent more load show as lag everywhere. `[hw]` (meter) / `[emu]` (instruction count)

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Digi CMI on the unit (OS 1.54, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: Voices that never switch off cost load: released voices kept looping silently and took the meter from 86 % to 94 % (I81). Switch a voice off only by the real amp envelope (below), and clear its on flag (voice + `0x28`), not only its end flag. Digi CMI 0.30 switches a voice off after the amp envelope stays below -90 dB for 64 blocks; 0.26's -72 dB rule read the filter envelope and cut sounding notes (I89, S20). `[hw]` (load) / `[emu]` (rule) {digicmi-026} {digicmi-037}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Digi CMI on the unit (OS 1.54, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: Voice internals (digiemu): voice + `0x00` is the PCM pointer of the sample playing, + `0x10` the gain, + `0x14` the sample length, + `0x28` voice on. AMP kit slots: attack 38, hold 39, decay 40, overdrive 41, delay send 42, reverb send 43, pan 44, volume 45. digiemu does not model the PIT counters. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Digi CMI on the unit (OS 1.54, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: The real amp envelope is at `0x4199ed64 + 8*v` on OS 1.54 (8 bytes a voice: +0 phase, +4 value), updated by the render's amp stage `0x400716c0` from kit slots 38-40 (attack, hold, decay). Phase 2 attack (value rises as negated Q31), 1 hold, 0 decay (|value| / 2^31 is the level, 0 when idle). After a release it matched the output level within about 5 %. On OS 1.53 it is `0x4199dd64` (elekloader's core notes, 2026-11-15; the filter-envelope export is `0x4199df54` there). Core 4.4 exports the amp envelope as `fw_amp_level` and names the old export `fw_filter_env`. `[emu]` (1.54) / `[doc]` (1.53) {digicmi-037} {elekloader-1115}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Digi CMI on the unit (OS 1.54, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: elekloader's `fw_amp_env` export (`0x4199ef54` on 1.54) is the filter envelope, despite its name: `0x40073304` fills it from kit slots 29-32 and 35; it fell to -135 dB while a held looping note's output stayed constant. Do not use it as a voice's level (S20). `[emu]` {digicmi-037}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Digi CMI on the unit (OS 1.54, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: Velocity is a square law in stock: both sample players pass the clamped velocity to `0x40074c60`, which returns gain = (vel/127)^2 x (VOL/127). `[emu]` {digicmi-037}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Digi CMI on the unit (OS 1.54, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: Count divisions in per-sample code: a `rems.l` costs about 20-35 cycles on this ColdFire but one instruction in digiemu's profile; a per-sample remainder in Digi CMI's RETRO made the UI crawl on the unit (I91). `[hw]` (lag) / `[emu]` (fix) {digicmi-037}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Digi CMI on the unit (OS 1.54, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: The DT1 main section loads at `0x40000400` (`main_load` in elekloader's profile), not `0x40000000`; Digi CMI's listings made at `0x40000000` before 0.40 were 0x400 off. `[doc]` {digicmi-042}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Digi CMI on the unit (OS 1.54, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: The stock per-voice player (OS 1.54): all eight voices go through one loop (`0x400758b8-0x40076234`, voice records from `0x8000EDC4`, 94 bytes each, `a3 += 94`), idle or playing. Per voice: the resampler `0x40075eac-0x40075efa` is an EMAC loop of 64 steps (about 1,024 instructions), then `0x40075f00` stores the position (V+0x1c/V+0x20) and adds the step to the playhead V+4; a voice's player costs about 1,800 instructions a block (about 2.1 % of the render) whatever it plays. Digi CMI 0.41 jumps over this work for its own voices at `0x40075ea2`, `0x40075f8c` and `0x40076164`, keeping only the playhead advance and gain: the render fell from 88,640 to 75,403 instructions a block with a chord held. `[emu]` (not checked on the unit) {digicmi-042}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Modwerk CC Remap: the incoming-CC path (OS 1.54, Core 2.1, 2026-10-29 to 11-12)
facts.text: Stock CC routing to MIDI tracks: the MIDI input task matches a CC's channel against the sixteen track channels (TRACK 1-8, TRACK A-H; A-H default to 9-16) and the auto channel, then calls the per-track CC handler `0x400d6c80` (track, CC number, value). On a MIDI track only CC 70-77 do anything: they set CC VAL 1-8 through the same parameter setter a knob turn uses (`0x400e0b94`), so the value reaches the pattern, the screen and MIDI OUT (as VAL's CC SELECT number on the track's CHAN). `[emu]` (digiemu c1b5735)

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Modwerk CC Remap: the incoming-CC path (OS 1.54, Core 2.1, 2026-10-29 to 11-12)
facts.text: Parameter page sites: parameter read `0x4000fe10` and write `0x40010b62` used by the pages; the title copy in the parameter pages' getTitle `0x40030954`. A page's sub-pages are a list in its view (pressing the page key steps the index; the title gets " (n/m)"); a MIDI track's AMP page has one sub-page, CC SELECT. VAL1 is set as parameter id 25; SEL1-8 are local ids 33-40. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Modwerk CC Remap: the incoming-CC path (OS 1.54, Core 2.1, 2026-10-29 to 11-12)
facts.text: Page copy, paste and clear read through the page's getter: a page copy (hold AMP + RECORD) on a page that a mod redirects copies the mod's values, and a later paste on the stock page writes them into stock parameters. MIDI OUT and pattern/track copy do not go through it. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Modwerk CC Remap: the incoming-CC path (OS 1.54, Core 2.1, 2026-10-29 to 11-12)
facts.text: Stock quirk: after an audio track's page, TRK + a MIDI track keeps the previous title until the page is opened again. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Modwerk CC Remap: the incoming-CC path (OS 1.54, Core 2.1, 2026-10-29 to 11-12)
facts.text: CC Remap 0.1.0 (four 6-byte `jsr` sites above, 423 B in DDR) ran on the author's Digitakt I with an Allen & Heath Xone:1D for about 20 minutes, alone and beside FX Track, CC Assignment Names and CC Recall; its table resets to 70-77 at every power-on. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Modwerk FX Track and stock CC input (OS 1.54, 2026-11-17)
facts.text: FX Track needs RECEIVE CC/NRPN {modwerk-1118}: stock's MIDI task drops CCs, including the FX CONTROL CH ones a mod hands over as MIDI IN, unless SETTINGS > MIDI CONFIG > PORT CONFIG ticks RECEIVE CC/NRPN with INPUT FROM set. facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / T9-KeyScale: addresses for an OS 1.53 port (OS 1.54, 2026-11-20)
facts.text: Sequencer pointers move by `0x1000` between OS 1.53 and 1.54: the playing-pattern pointer is `0x4199ec38` on 1.54 and `0x4199dc38` on 1.53, the transport word `0x4199ec2c` / `0x4199dc2c` (both confirmed by elekloader's seq-events-dt1 `SQ_PATTERN_PP` and `SQ_TRANSPORT`). The mutes pointer is `0x421fab90` on 1.54 (CC 94 handler); `0x421f9b90` on 1.53 is the author's guess from the same shift, not checked. The stock eMMC read `0x400e2c14` and write `0x400e2dfa` are 1.54 only; their 1.53 addresses are still to be found by byte pattern. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / T9-KeyScale: addresses for an OS 1.53 port (OS 1.54, 2026-11-20)
facts.text: eMMC blocks past `0x60000` in use by mods: on a fresh digiemu `plusdrive.img`, `0x60000-0x6005f` is all zero; FLEXMODS uses `0x60040-0x6004c`, T9-KeyScale `0x6004e`, ledcolors `0x60000` (above). A fresh drive being empty does not show that stock never writes there. `[doc]`

facts.text: Proven room for added DSP code: 83,838 B over four regions (L1 block 1 17,974 B, three code regions 9,798 / 31,606 / 24,460 B). Each function is placed first-fit. facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / DSP code room and load on the DN2 (Digiwerk DT01, DC01/DC02, SC01)
facts.text: selcc output is about 10 % larger than needed (field accesses cost 5 instructions). Digiwerk's peephole pass saves ~5-6 KB.

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / DSP code room and load on the DN2 (Digiwerk DT01, DC01/DC02, SC01)
facts.text: Their safety lesson: stock code never puts a load into an I register directly before a 48-bit instruction that uses it (0 of ~14 cases; there is always work in between). The SHARC emulator does not model the pipeline, so the cautious pass refuses that pairing. Copy the rule: do not create instruction pairings the stock code never has. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / DSP code room and load on the DN2 (Digiwerk DT01, DC01/DC02, SC01)
facts.text: Where DSP code may live, after the probe study (Digiwerk PB01 findings, static, 2026-10-23) {dn2-cfw-pb01}: L1 block 1 above `0x2e4f46` gives about 12 KB, not the 45 KB of the static map, because the build keeps the edge for a 32 KB DM cache. Block 3's tail is the 16 KB I-cache. `0x315f8c-0x318000` in block 2 depends on whether the PM cache there is 16 or 32 KB. Code placed there stopped the DSP on a unit (CMP2's LOW MUP stop), so builds refuse it. L2 candidates: `0x2008823c-0x200918c0` (38,532 B) and `0x200c2000-0x200fa000` (229,376 B). `0x200918c0-0x200c2000` is kept free of data by the build. Other projects use part of that range on units: [CONFLICTS O19](../CONFLICTS.md). Section 7 can grow ~150 KB before its 1 MiB limit. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / DSP code room and load on the DN2 (Digiwerk DT01, DC01/DC02, SC01)
facts.text: Code running from L2 in dead stock FX spots stopped the DSP on a unit (Digiwerk SC01, 2026-10-21): knob turns and random idle moments, while the UI stayed fine. 74 minutes of the same recipes in the SHARC interpreter gave 0 faults, so the cause is something the interpreter doesn't model. facts.text: Bound every feedback path's output. A held three-head runaway of a tape echo reached 4.24 (18 dB over stock's delay), so Digiwerk added a soft ceiling (linear to 0.5, at most 0.7). Stock's own runaway peaks at 0.526. `[emu]` {dn2-cfw-t53}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / DSP code room and load on the DN2 (Digiwerk DT01, DC01/DC02, SC01)
facts.text: How far the cycle model is off on a unit (dnfw Waverider 0.3.8, DN2 1.11, USB-probe idle measure, 2026-10-29) {dn2-waverider-perf}: A change that the cycle model put at 0.6-0.7 load points for 16 voices measured 2.0 points on the unit, roughly 3x. The unit runs about 1.26x slower than the emulator assumes in general, which leaves ~2.4x unexplained (memory waits are suspected, not checked). With 16 voices of a custom wavetable machine plus a 16-note FM chord, the unit read 60-68 % with no missed frame (peak 71.8 %). Same lesson as rule A35: budget from unit measurements. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / DSP code room and load on the DN2 (Digiwerk DT01, DC01/DC02, SC01)
facts.text: Measuring per-stage cycles on the unit (dnfw `waverider-loadmap.md`): Chosen jumps and calls go through a 12-byte stub that reads EMUCLK and adds the cycles since the previous mark to the running segment. A null segment measures the marks' own cost. Results publish through reply word 2, half a record per block. A reusable recipe for any DSP mod. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / DSP code room and load on the DN2 (Digiwerk DT01, DC01/DC02, SC01)
facts.text: Load model used: load = (1.30 x emulated instructions + 11k) / 666,667. For one build it predicted ~74 % where the unit showed ~50-60 %, so the model overestimates. `[?]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Frame: 0xa80 bytes from `0x80005e60`, sent by DSPI2 (16-bit DMA, 1,374 halfwords); the reply arrives at `0x800053a4`, every block (1,500/s). All send-FX, compressor, external-input and master parameters are one block of big-endian words at `0x9fa + 2*(k-25)` (`k` = the parameter row's mirror index; chorus is k 25-31). Compressor routing is at `0xd4` (track bits) and `0xd6`. 16 per-voice rows of `0x92` bytes start at `0xda`. A row is a voice, not a track: a track parameter goes to every row whose owner (`0xa5a + 2r`) is that track. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Audio clock: SSI0 with eDMA 48 (RX) / 50 (TX), 96,000 requests/s. One major loop is one 32-sample block, and vector 170 forces vector 191 (the frame handler). The emulator needs this clock for PLAY to run the sequencer. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Panel and MIDI: Panel MCU on UART8 at 156,250 baud, sent through eDMA 35. LED messages: `B9 i v` (LED i, palette entry v) and `B5 i r g b` (palette entry); see also [`../common/sysex-and-midi.md`](../common/sysex-and-midi.md). DIN MIDI on UART9 at 31,250 baud: out by eDMA 37 (bulk) plus direct writes for realtime bytes, in by eDMA 36. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Notes: MIDI tracks have no voice limit in the output engine; the "4 notes" are only the UI's NOT2-NOT4 rows. A pattern's note pool holds 8,192 notes, with at most 16 notes per step. The MIDI note-output length is a byte counter over a 1,024-byte buffer. Stock 1.12 plays more than 4 notes per trig from a modded project. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
facts.text: DSP free memory (static): L1 block 2 is never written by the stream (128 KB), the L1 block 1 tail `0x2dd52c-0x2effff`, and L2 from `0x2008823c`. Correction: the startup turns on all three L1 caches, so `0x39c000-0x39ffff`, `0x2ec000-0x2effff` and `0x31c000-0x31ffff` are cache, not free. dnfw's proven code area is `0x2dd600-0x2e7000`. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
facts.text: The frame is longer than its data (elekloader core-dn2 0.3). The driver sends a 0xabc-byte frame but writes data halfwords only for the first 0xa80 bytes; for the rest it writes only command halfwords. So the tail from byte 0xa80 keeps whatever you write there before the call, and stock leaves it zero and ignores it on the DSP side. The driver's transmit queue is at `0x80002510` (one 32-bit entry per frame halfword, command half first); the frame sender calls the driver at `0x40025e9e`. The DSP reads tail word k as halfword 2k+1 above halfword 2k. `[hw]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Reply word 2 (record offset 8) is free on DN2 1.12: no stock code writes or reads it. elekloader's DSP peek uses it (one halfword per block, ~3 KB/s), and so do digikit's `core/dsp-link` and the `sharc` branch's metrics core, so only one of them can be in a build. `[hw]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
facts.text: DSP load on a unit (DN2 1.12, elekloader's idle-task meter, Nov 2026): 666,706 cycles per block measured (the nominal figure is 666,667). Time outside FreeRTOS's idle task: about 80 % with nothing playing, 65 % with 64 notes held. Stock's own block-handler span (reply word 0) shows the same pattern (79 % and 68 %). Neither figure is headroom. Stock's audio task holds the DSP for most of each block and holds it *less* under load, so the share counts waiting. Do not read "80 % busy at idle" as "20 % left". `[hw]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
facts.text: elekloader DN2 machine budget (core-dn2 0.3, experimental): each SHARC machine kind gets 64 KiB of L2 and its own guarded 4 KiB L1 stack. The callback may declare at most 2,048 stack bytes; the rest is shared with interrupts. The peek reads only L1 blocks 0-3 below their caches and L2 below the special window. On a unit, it read the machine stacks' guard words and its own code back exactly. `[hw]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2} {elekloader-adapting}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Emulator pitfall: digikit's Unicorn got EMAC fractional mode wrong (MACSR F/I = 1). The frame handler uses it, so values that pass through EMAC can be off in the emulator. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / How much of a Digitakt II is inside a Digitone II (dnfw `dt2-machine-port.md`, DN2 1.11 vs DT2 1.16)
facts.text: SHARC: 1,038 of 1,228 DT2 functions (85 %) have a relocation-tolerant twin in DN2 (which SHARC findings hold on both units: [`../common/dt2-dn2-sharc-crosscheck.md`](../common/dt2-dn2-sharc-crosscheck.md)). facts.text: The DT2 ONESHOT render (`0x1c4ecf` + `0x1c4f81`, 4 functions and 611 instructions with its callees) was extracted from the user's own DT2 file, relocated into DN2 1.11, and ran bit-identical to the DT2 for all four play modes in the emulator. dn2mk2 and armio's T1E2 later shipped full DT2 sample machines on DN2 1.11. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / How much of a Digitakt II is inside a Digitone II (dnfw `dt2-machine-port.md`, DN2 1.11 vs DT2 1.16)
facts.text: Trap for new machine types: the firmware's per-type voice setup dispatch (`0x8052db90[type]` at `0x1c91ad`) has only five entries. A new type 5 triggered from idle reads past the table and jumps to 0. Extend every per-type table, not only the render loop. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The three ColdFire <-> SHARC layers (dnfw `audio-dma.md`, `dsp-control-block.md`, lalzart cross-check)

facts.text: MAIN OS = section id 3 of the ELE3 container; load address `0x40000400` on Digitone II and Digitone mk1; big-endian; 16-byte header, first instruction `46 FC 27 00` (`MOVE #$2700,SR`) at `0x40000410`. facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Hardware map and budgets (OS 1.12 unless noted)

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Hardware map and budgets (OS 1.12 unless noted)
facts.text: The in-place loader is the hidden size limit. Section 4's loader (`0x8000357c`, stage `0x40200000`) has a stock margin of +31,182 bytes; elektron-firmware-tool's default compression level (`-l 3`) gives -39,318 and corrupts the image. Every build needs a margin >= 0 at both loader stages; elekloader's default packer produced a container too large for the receive buffer, so the DN2 build uses a dense packer (`codec/dense.py`). Stock Digitakt II 1.17 also fails the in-place path (margin -31,912). `[hw]` {dn2-cfw-handoff} ([I39](../INCIDENTS.md#i39-the-default-compression-level-corrupted-a-dn2-image))

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Hardware map and budgets (OS 1.12 unless noted)
facts.text: Elektron's own streams keep the furthest match within a 1 MiB window and the longest match at 2,048 bytes; a packer that exceeds them is refused by the build tool. Compressed streams are padded to a multiple of 4 B. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

Section 8 (a shared ARM Cortex-M image, probably for the Outbox 8; see [firmware-container.md](../common/firmware-container.md)) must also stay stock. The bootstrap holds the recovery menu and signing-key material. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-handoff} {dn2-ele3}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Hardware map and budgets (OS 1.12 unless noted)
facts.text: Boot sequence: DSP boot -> eMMC -> boot record -> project decode -> mount -> frame interrupt -> main-OS task. A boot-time hook can sit at the main-OS task entry. Safe mode is triggered by a boot counter plus a flag; the counter clears after 30 s of the firmware's block counter; a CPU exception halts the device. `[doc]` {digikit-findings}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Audio/DSP side
facts.text: DSP effect entry points (SHARC, 1.12): chorus `0xb84d5c`, delay `0xb8482c`, reverb `0xb836bc`, compressor `0xb8541d`; FX bus `0x1c1738`; render `0x1c2712`; effect parameters at TX frame offsets `0x9fa-0xa53`. Stock per-block cost about 5.4k instructions (delay) and 16.6k (compressor); the replacement versions measured 18.6k and 47.7k, so hand-assembling five loops is needed to get below stock. Stock DSP load measures 63-65 % on the unit. `[hw]` {dn2-cfw-handoff} {dn2-cfw-roadmap}

facts.text: SHARC tooling facts: the ADSP-214xx Ghidra SLEIGH cannot parse this stream (wrong core generation, VISA-compressed); a project emulator had no semantics for 48.7 % of instructions; dn2-cfw's `sharcvm` passes 2,036 of 2,039 selache test cases (the 3 failures are selcc output problems); selcc miscompiles `fx_exp2` and `fx_log2` at every `-O` level and re-evaluates a local initialised with a comparison at each use. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-handoff}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / ColdFire / MIDI side findings
facts.text: The 4-note MIDI limit is code only (NOTE/NOT2-NOT4 rows, `FUN_40055606`, a 4-byte default chord, 4-note SHAPE chords); the engine and pattern format are not limited; the note pool is 8,192 six-byte entries. Traps: the lock-clear path writes -1 to notes 1-4; the 8-bit MIDI output counter at `0x44600ca0` can wrap on large note-off bursts and leave notes stuck. The arp is kept off MIDI tracks by structure (not fully confirmed). `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-handoff}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / ColdFire / MIDI side findings
facts.text: Hook events in dn2-cfw's core: `ev_midi_step` (sequencer, interrupt level), `ev_midi_note` (MIDI task before note-on); `ev_tick` at `0x4002e464`, `ev_key` at `0x4002f20c`. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-handoff}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / ColdFire / MIDI side findings
facts.text: Machine dispatch: Digitakt II limits an added machine to one SRC page (a second page is not possible); Digitone II supports an added machine with its own SYN page at run time. A run-time unload is refused with code -26 on both. `[doc]` {digikit-findings}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / +Drive and storage (digikit findings 14, 23-24, 35, 43-47)
facts.text: +Drive block records are 128 bytes; the real filesystem uses 32 KB extent-mapped pages with hierarchical directories; MmcFs has fixed-capacity project, sound and kit pools; its bitmaps at sector `0x800` are write-protect bits, not occupancy; a panel SAVE lands in project slot 0 and does not update the MmcFs bitmaps. digikit's card module store uses sectors `0x38000-0x3E000` (blank on a real DT2 card when checked); DT2 modules can live as files in a `/digikit` folder; the USB SysEx store is version 2 with a static receive ceiling of 1.0-1.4 MB/s (about 100 instructions per byte; measured on a DN2 in 2026-11: 0.857 MB/s, see "USB transfer speed on the units"). `[doc]` {digikit-findings}
