facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / More from dnfw's notes (read 2026-11-02)
facts.text: The SHARC's filter accelerators, read on a DN2 (accelprobe, 2026-10-17). The ADSP-21569 has IIR0 and FIR0; the DN2 1.11 engine uses neither. Only 22 of 76 result words matched the models built from the hardware reference; the chip differs in three ways: IIR0 feeds stored word 5 of a biquad into the output: y = A0 x + s1, then s1 = (A1 x + s2) + B1 y and s2 = A2 x + B2 y, each step rounded to float32 (all 40 outputs and 4 states match). FIR0 adds its four partial sums in pairs, (acc0 + acc1) + (acc2 + acc3). In ACM mode the chip writes `0xFFFFFFFF` to a TCB's INIDX and 0 to OUTIDX after a window, the other way round from the hardware reference. Speed bounds, including setup: at most about 22 cycles per biquad-sample and 4.5 per tap-sample. ADI's application note gives the theoretical rates as 6 cycles per biquad (one MAC unit) and about 0.25 cycles per tap and sample (four MAC units), and says the coefficient and state preload dominates small jobs, which fits these bounds from jobs of 8-16 samples {adi-ee408}. The INIDX/OUTIDX write-back in ACM is not described there. digikit's models were corrected to match all 76 words. Same silicon on the DT2 ([crosscheck](../common/dt2-dn2-sharc-crosscheck.md)). `[hw]` {dn2-accel}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / More from dnfw's notes (read 2026-11-02)
facts.text: ColdFire tasks on a unit (DN2 1.11, read with the USB probe): The context switch is at `0x40000410-0x40000458`; the ready table at `0x4664ac9c` holds one list head per priority; higher numbers run first. Prio 0 never runs; prio 1 is the real idle loop (entry `0x400cec98`, parked at `0x400cf0e2`); the MIDI task (prio 7) answers the probe. Stack high-water marks after a busy pattern and a save: the fullest is a 2,048-byte prio-10 stack at 27 %; the main application's 160 KiB stack peaked at 1.5 %. Interrupts run on the current task's stack. ColdFire CPU 58-61 % whatever plays, almost all of it the audio ISR; a pattern raises the ISR's worst frame (75-83 % in a busy one), and SAVE PROJECT takes 100 % for about a second. `[hw]` {dn2-cftasks}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / More from dnfw's notes (read 2026-11-02)
facts.text: Stock 1.11 trusts a stored song row count. The song LOAD (`0x400dea6a`) copies `count` stored 29-byte rows into 37-byte live rows without checking it. One project held 21,503 instead of at most 99 and crashed stock and modded builds alike when opened; the damage had entered between two exports. A mod that writes project data must keep every count in range, and a repair tool must use the storage-version-4 offsets (row count at record `+0x147`). `[hw]` {dn2-oldproject} ([I2](../INCIDENTS.md#i2-stock-song-load-trusts-a-stored-row-count))

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Disassembly pitfalls (agents will hit these)
facts.text: Reference disassembler: `m68k-linux-gnu-objdump` 2.42, `-m m68k:cfv4e -z`; objdump prints indexed-mode displacements in hex without `0x` and `d16(An)` displacements in decimal - confirm against raw bytes. Padding `0x0000` words appear as clusters. Bootstrap needs `--adjust-vma=0x800003fc`. `[doc]` {dn2-mainos-image} {dn2-cfw-handoff}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Disassembly pitfalls (agents will hit these)
facts.text: Capstone has no ColdFire mode: 98.95 % of boundaries right over `0x40001000` + 64 KB with 201 divergences (it assigns two bytes to each failed instruction and desyncs; it decodes `00 00 2f 0a` as `ori.b`, which ColdFire removed). Stock Ghidra `68000:BE:32:Coldfire` reached 99.76 % over 512 KB but lacks `movclr.l ACCy,Rx` (flow stops at words `a1c0 a3c1 a5c2 a7c3`, so decompilations of the frame ISR and modulation module may be truncated) and gets MSAC-with-load wrong (accumulator selection inverted). digikit's `68000:BE:32:ColdfireEMAC` module fixes this - re-import rather than switching language on an existing program. Auto-analysis of the 3.19 MB 1.11 MAIN OS takes about 128 s; close the Ghidra GUI before headless runs; some large switches report "Could not recover jumptable" and must be read as assembly. `[doc]` {dn2-mainos-image}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 findings v0.45-v0.48 (OS 1.11, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: Front-panel LEDs: the LED driver `0x40132148(id, value)` remembers the last value per LED and sends only changes; `LedManager` (pointer `0x446478e0`) is the only route to it, and on each refresh (`0x4002c854`) the first write to an LED wins. Trig keys are logical LED ids 26-41. The palette is uploaded in three sets (one per LED INTENSITY): index 0 off, 1 backlight white, then eight hues of 16 levels each (red 2-17, green 18-33, blue 34-49, yellow 50-65, cyan 66-81, magenta 82-97, white 98-113, orange 114-129), 130-135 special. Modes: 1 unlit, 2 steady, 3 and 4 blink. `[doc]` (read from disassembly) {dn2mk2-leds}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 findings v0.45-v0.48 (OS 1.11, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: core-dn2 0.4 (elekloader main): its MIDI CC event sits at `0x4003f106` in the CC router at `0x4003f0ec` (OS 1.12); `core_dsp_post` puts up to five numbered 25-bit words per frame in the frame tail, and since the DSP receives frames alternately at `0x2c29d0` and `0x2c39d0` the posts land at `0x2c3460` and `0x2c4460`. The TRK SETUP PLAY MODE and MONO NOTE PRIO setters are `0x4004b6d6` and `0x4004b786`. `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2} {elekloader-machines-dn2}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 findings v0.45-v0.48 (OS 1.11, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: Coupled emulator (v0.48): dn2mk2 now runs the ColdFire image (digikit's emulator) and the SHARC image together, one audio block of 32 frames at a time: the audio interrupt once per block, the sequencer timer at its exact rate but up to one block late in phase, one ColdFire packet per block to the DSP and the DSP's status one block later. Its own audit calls this faithful in order and content, not in timing: an interrupt never lands mid-UI code, a DSP overrun is not modelled, and the default "fast" mode runs the UI's 60 Hz tick about 90x too often (the "faithful" mode gets 59 of 60 ticks a second). The unit's ColdFire spends about 56 % in the audio interrupt with the sequencer stopped. `[emu]` {dn2mk2-v048} (I66)

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 findings v0.45-v0.48 (OS 1.11, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: Load guard: a guard that drops a sample voice for one block and retries it in the next makes it flicker; dn2mk2 v0.49 is to render sample voices first and keep a dropped one stopped until its next note. `[hw]` (user report) {dn2mk2-v048} (I71)

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / USB transfer speed on the units (digikit, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: The SysEx route is CPU-bound. On a Digitone II (OS 1.12, high-speed USB) the firmware's receive chain in the deferred-call task (priority 9) takes at most 0.857 MB/s of SysEx bytes even when nothing handles the message; digikit's store reaches 0.60 MB/s of payload, two requests in flight gain nothing, and its card VERIFY runs at 7.4 MB/s. Receive work and MIDI-task work do not overlap. About 53 M instructions a second are left free. `[hw]` {digikit-usbfast}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / USB transfer speed on the units (digikit, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: A vendor bulk interface fits beside USB MIDI. In USB MIDI mode the port uses EP0 and EP1 only, so a patched configuration descriptor can add an interface with a bulk pair on EP2; in USB AUDIO/MIDI mode EP3 and EP2 IN are taken but EP2 OUT is free, so a bulk OUT endpoint fits there too (devices/digitakt-2.md, {digikit-f123-bulk}; earlier text: EP2 and EP3 are taken (audio and its clock feedback), and the controller has only EP0-EP3. Stock serves the configuration from a pointer in its port table, so a copy in free flash space needs no code change. `[hw]` (enumerated on macOS) {digikit-usbfast} {digikit-f42}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / USB transfer speed on the units (digikit, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: Program IN endpoints for 64-byte packets. The controller's transmit buffer is 64 bytes per endpoint: two 512-byte IN packets back to back wedged it until a power cycle (I70). Stock declares bulk 512 but programs its IN queue heads for 64. `[hw]` {digikit-usbfast}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / USB transfer speed on the units (digikit, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: Measured over the bulk route (64-byte IN packets): echo about 2.3 MB/s each way on a DN2 and 2.9 MB/s on a DT2; an 8 MB sample 3.86 MB/s on the DN2 (0.68 over SysEx), 0.94-1.60 MB/s with verify on the DT2 (0.11 over SysEx); for many small files the per-file overhead dominates. A cable pulled mid-file left only complete files. On the DT2 a sample loaded on a track keeps playing while its file is replaced, since it plays from sample RAM. `[hw]` {digikit-usbfast}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.49 FLEX (OS 1.11, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: FLEX replaces BOUNCE (machine type 17, BOUNCE's, so older projects open their BOUNCE track as FLEX with no conversion code). Recorder trigs record a track, IN or MAIN into one of 8 buffers for R.LEN steps; the FLEX track plays the take. BOUNCE had two faults FLEX fixes: its engine read three sound slots the panel never wrote, so a take ignored its panel, and it waited for a +Drive pool directory that a unit with nothing ever sent to the +Drive never has, so every take was refused there. `[emu]` (gated; not verified on hardware)

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.51-v0.52 and the DN2's per-track chain (OS 1.11, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: The per-track chain is mono: on the SHARC runner (stock section 7), after a machine renders into its 32-float block, `0x1c8ef1` calls seven stages on that one buffer in place (`0xb8251b`, `0x1cdb56`, `0xb80c39`, `0xb8265b`, `0xb81368`, `0xb82342`, then the amp `0xb80345`), each with its own state block per track (track 0 at `0x250020`, `0x24fa20`, `0x24f320`, `0x250160`, `0x2533e0`, `0x2505a0`, `0x2547a0`). Mono becomes stereo only at the output (`0x1c244d`), which pans the block into `0x259f68 + 0x100k`. Unlike the Digitakt II's stereo voices, so stereo samples would need the chain run twice with a second set of states. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.51-v0.52 and the DN2's per-track chain (OS 1.11, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: A TRK recording takes the block after the amp, before LEVEL, pan and the sends: setting a voice's LEVEL and three FX sends to 0 in the frame leaves the recorded block unchanged (SHARC runner). dn2mk2's MUTE SRC does this from the frame ISR's first copy after its voice loop (`0x400275b0`, `jsr 0x40134490`): voice LEVEL at frame word `116 + 2v`, sends at `168 + 2s + 146v` (s = 86-88). `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.51-v0.52 and the DN2's per-track chain (OS 1.11, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: Exactness costs DSP time: giving up bit-exact Monomachine and Machinedrum emulation (oversampling 4x instead of 12x for SID, 1x reads for DDRW and DENS, float instead of 24-bit products for filters) cut those machines' cost by 9-64 % while holding level within 2.5 dB and every octave band within 20 dB of the originals; the guard then allows more voices. The sound on the unit is not yet verified. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.51-v0.52 and the DN2's per-track chain (OS 1.11, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: Page LEDs: the eight page LEDs are logical ids 42-49 (two rows of four under FX and MOD). In grid recording stock lights them in mode 2: the edited page palette 33 (bright green), the pattern's other pages 10 (dim red), pages past the length 2 (near-off); outside grid recording no page is green. A mod that turns its own page without passing PAGE to stock leaves stock's green on the old page (seen on a unit with v0.52, I87). `[emu]` (palette, read from stock's code) / `[hw]` (photos) {dn2mk2-v053}. A sound's slot s sits at `sound + 20 + 2s`. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.51-v0.52 and the DN2's per-track chain (OS 1.11, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: DSP budget: about 666,667 cycles a frame on the DN2 (dn2mk2's handoff for a second firmware); the SHARC engine task's stack lives in the FreeRTOS heap at `0x2d08b8`-`0x2dd0b0`, so mod data starts above `0x2dd600`. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Pattern change, the PTN view and the settings block (dnfw directjump, OS 1.11, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: Stock prepares each step one step before it sounds. The sequencer prepares its next events at `0x400d9e10`; a cued pattern is armed by the tick routine (`0x400da406`) on tick 2 only, and the switch (`0x400da6e6`) takes its start step from the change counter `0x42c5a91c`. So a change made "now" still plays one step of the old pattern unless that step's queued events are freed. `[doc]` `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Pattern change, the PTN view and the settings block (dnfw directjump, OS 1.11, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: Stock's discard at a pattern change only marks queued records; a marked record keeps its lock until its old time. Rapid cues with sixteen arpeggiated tracks emptied the lock and record pools (`0x40138992`, `0x401389dc`) on builds that only marked old events, not on one that unlinks and frees them. Stock queues an arp request (type 9) for every audio track on every step, arp on or off. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Pattern change, the PTN view and the settings block (dnfw directjump, OS 1.11, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: PTN view: its key handler is in the vtable at `0x402008cc` (stock handler `0x400fa6be`); stock does nothing with [UP] and [DOWN] there. The cue is posted by `0x400fa11e`. The LED colour cache is at `0x466b7420`, one byte per panel channel. `[doc]` `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / OS release history (dn2-cfw `notes/dn2-release-history.md`, dnfw `docs/os-versions.md`)
facts.text: Porting: 1.11 and 1.12 MAIN images share only their first 28 bytes; about 48.7 % of 48-byte windows from 1.11 appear verbatim in 1.12 but at 535 different offset shifts - fixed-address patches do not port; locate hook points by masked byte patterns (`find`/`expect` fields) and pin every mod to its build by hash. Units already at bootstrap 0x0201 will not be upgraded again. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-release-history} {dn2-os-versions}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / OS release history (dn2-cfw `notes/dn2-release-history.md`, dnfw `docs/os-versions.md`)
facts.text: Rules for a new OS version (dnfw): compare decoded content (`dnfw diff`), never compressed bytes; use `--strings` as a filter only; read the densest change blocks first (a relink gives many small blocks, a rewrite one large one); check bootstrap and updater separately (the updater matters for recovery); re-locate every patch via `find`/`expect` and name the target build; examine unfamiliar sections (id 8) before relying on the image; mangled storage-struct names show which persisted state changed. The compression and signing scheme was unchanged in 1.11 and the codec limits were measured on 1.11. `[doc]` {dn2-os-versions}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Bootstrap and the recovery path (dnfw `docs/bootstrap.md`, 1.10E image)
facts.text: Section 2 is 30,302 bytes; header `[u32 payload_size = 0x7656][u32 0x80010000]` (the second word is not the load base); load base `0x800003fc` incl. the 8-byte header, payload runs at `0x80000404`; status strings READY TO RECEIVE `0x80006603`, RECEIVING... `0x80006614`, UPGRADING... `0x800065e6`, "BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE" at payload offset `0x602c`. `[doc]` {dn2-bootstrap}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Bootstrap and the recovery path (dnfw `docs/bootstrap.md`, 1.10E image)
facts.text: Receive phase: start marker `0x7F` (kind 1) records the total packet count and starting sequence number; data packets `0x7E` are sequence-checked, their checksum verified over 119 bytes and 101 decoded bytes copied to the buffer; end marker (kind 2) verifies totals. The progress bar measures reception only (`received * 128 / total`). A bad sequence number or checksum sets the state to 0 and the transfer silently stops - no retransmit. Transport is one-way DIN MIDI at 31,250 baud. `[doc]` {dn2-bootstrap}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Bootstrap and the recovery path (dnfw `docs/bootstrap.md`, 1.10E image)
facts.text: Write phase: the receive buffer is RAM at `0x40000000` holding `[u32 size][u32 checksum][container]`; the container check sums `(word_index ^ word)` over `size/4` words from `0x40000008`; flash is erased in 256 KB blocks from `0x80000` and the raw container is written in 512-byte chunks. No decompression happens here - the updater and MAIN OS decompress sections on the next boot (which is why the in-place loader margin matters). The page does not mention any seal/signature verification in this path. A different routine (`FUN_80011844`) flashes a single small section with a CRC (residue `0xDEBB20E3`) and 64 KB caps - not the recovery path. `[doc]` {dn2-bootstrap}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Arpeggiator vs MIDI tracks (dn2-cfw `notes/T2.2-arp-midi-v2.md`, OS 1.12, static analysis only)
facts.text: The arp is part of the voice interrupt; its only output is the internal voice allocator `FUN_4002a6a2`, nothing on that path creates a MIDI event. Barriers: UI gating by `FUN_40031274` (isMidiTrack) at the ARP key `0x4005f9b6`, menu auto-close `0x400187ea`, LED `0x40060dde`; the step handler `FUN_400d99de` sends MIDI tracks to `FUN_400d8cbe`; live keys on a MIDI track go straight to the MIDI task via `FUN_4012bb90`. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-arp}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Arpeggiator vs MIDI tracks (dn2-cfw `notes/T2.2-arp-midi-v2.md`, OS 1.12, static analysis only)
facts.text: Data: arp settings per track sound record at `kit+0x34+t*0x48b` (`+0x15f` mode, `+0x160` speed, `+0x161` range, `+0x162` note length, `+0x164` step mask, `+0x166..0x175` offsets); track MIDI mask s16 at `kit+0x5cda`; events are 0x6c bytes (alloc `FUN_40138cb6`, schedule `FUN_40138e3c`), MIDI events 0x60 bytes, MIDI task queue `0x445ff870`, free list head `0x4460f4b8` (2,048 entries), MIDI output byte count `0x44600ca0` (8-bit). The arp self-tick is a type-9 event every 90,000 units (1/60 step); one interrupt pass is ~0.67 ms. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-arp}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Arpeggiator vs MIDI tracks (dn2-cfw `notes/T2.2-arp-midi-v2.md`, OS 1.12, static analysis only)
facts.text: Hazards for any MIDI-generating mod: the event allocator `FUN_4012a6e8` does not check for an empty free list (test `0x4460f4b8` first); MIDI events take the untransposed note (the task transposes); source byte `[0xd]` 1 = sequencer (subject to mute/solo), 2 = live; length `0x7f` (INF) hangs notes in the MIDI task; the 8-bit output count wraps above 255 bytes per message; latency ~one pass plus DIN serialisation (~0.96 ms per 3-byte note); vector 191 (voice interrupt) is not modelled by the emulator by default. Design options range from UI-only (~0 bytes) to sequenced trigs with p-locks (~850 bytes). `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-arp}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Frame send loop, MODS page and the ColdFire task switches (dnfw sendloop and MODS page, OS 1.11; digikit finding 132, OS 1.12)
facts.text: The frame send copies 1,344 words a frame, 1,500 times a second: before each transfer to the DSP the ColdFire's audio interrupt copies every 16-bit frame word into the transfer buffer beside a fixed 16-bit command word (`0x8001`), 7 instructions and two writes a word in stock. dnfw's `sendloop` mod puts the command word in a register's high half once and stores each entry with one 32-bit write (4 instructions a word; 5,376 instead of 9,408 per frame, same 24-byte loop, same bytes out), about 4 points less ColdFire load, confirmed on hardware on OS 1.11. `[hw]` {dn2fe-sendloop}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Frame send loop, MODS page and the ColdFire task switches (dnfw sendloop and MODS page, OS 1.11; digikit finding 132, OS 1.12)
facts.text: dnfw's MODS page (SETTINGS > SYSTEM > MODS) lists the base OS, the build name, the tool's commit and each mod's version, built from stock's own menu parts by one hook at the end of the SYSTEM menu's start-up code; its code and rows (a count, then 32 bytes a row, at most 64 rows) are a chunk at `0x46798000` in the platform's area. Checked in the emulator from reset on 1.11 and 1.12. `[emu]` {dn2fe-sendloop}

facts.text: ColdFire task switches, main-OS entry and DTCN0: see the section of the same name in [digitakt-2.md](digitakt-2.md); the findings cover DN2 1.12 too. {digikit-1116}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / RIFT v0.4 ORGAN and dn2mk2 v0.57 FLEXMUTE (OS 1.11, 2026-11-16)
facts.text: SHARC arithmetic traps: there is no exact divide (FASCIA's `recip`: a seed plus three Newton steps, about 4e-8 relative error), so a port of C code is bit-exact only to a tolerance where it divides; ORGAN ends the chiff's decay at 1e-30 (about 2.3 s) to keep out of denormals. ORGAN's SHARC code is 8.6 KB. `[emu]` {dn2-rift-v04}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / RIFT v0.4 ORGAN and dn2mk2 v0.57 FLEXMUTE (OS 1.11, 2026-11-16)

A FLEX voice's take keeps looping silently on the DSP after its release, so DSP play positions do not show when a note ends; dn2mk2 v0.57 uses the trigger words plus the frame LEVEL > 0 instead, with a 300-frame (about 0.2 s) hold (I133). `[emu]` {dn2mk2-v057}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / RIFT v0.4 ORGAN and dn2mk2 v0.57 FLEXMUTE (OS 1.11, 2026-11-16)

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / RIFT v0.5 BREATH and v0.6 SILT: records, DDR delay lines, DSP budget (OS 1.11, 2026-11-17)

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / RIFT v0.5 BREATH and v0.6 SILT: records, DDR delay lines, DSP budget (OS 1.11, 2026-11-17)
facts.text: Budget figures RIFT plans with: frame 666,667 cycles; the silent stock frame about 416,000 (62 %); its guard keeps RIFT's voices inside 0.8 of the frame, about 117,000 cycles for all RIFT voices together. Cost model: instructions + 4 x L2 + 10 x DDR accesses (run-mode estimate: instructions + 0.9 x (4 L2 + 10 DDR)). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / RIFT v0.5 BREATH and v0.6 SILT: records, DDR delay lines, DSP budget (OS 1.11, 2026-11-17)
facts.text: SILT cost (emulator, after hand-written register loops): FIBER SOLO about 22.5k, SKIN about 30k, SILT SWARM about 43k, FIBER MASS DEEP about 44k (109k before the lean pass); the plan's target was about 27k (4 % of the frame) for the worst case. For scale: a P-I drum 21-33k, VO-6 about 48k, a heavy FASCIA voice at its attack about 51k instructions before memory. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / RIFT v0.5 BREATH and v0.6 SILT: records, DDR delay lines, DSP budget (OS 1.11, 2026-11-17)
facts.text: Per-voice DDR delay lines: `SILT_DELAY_DDR = 0x82400000`, slot t at `+ t x 0xC000` (48 KB a slot, 16 slots = 768 KB, to `0x824C0000`), above the Machinedrum P-I delay lines at `0x82200000` (128 KB) and below the sample pool at `0x84000000`; RIFT's tables live at `0x81000000`. The span was measured clear of stock's init and is checked by a gate step that reads every added span back after init. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / RIFT v0.5 BREATH and v0.6 SILT: records, DDR delay lines, DSP budget (OS 1.11, 2026-11-17)
facts.text: DDR is garbage at power-on and too big to ride in the image: 768 KB of zeros cannot go in the DSP image (1 MiB upload buffer, about 947 KB used unpacked), and clearing 12,288 words in one block would cost about 120,000 cycles, so a slot clears its lines over 24 blocks (512 words a block, about 5,000 cycles) when it becomes SILT (machine change, project load, power-on) or after the output guard wipes it; a note waits for the clear, at most 16 ms. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / RIFT v0.5 BREATH and v0.6 SILT: records, DDR delay lines, DSP budget (OS 1.11, 2026-11-17)
facts.text: Delay reads by block bursts: the delay pointers advance one sample at a time, so a block reads 32 consecutive words per line; one burst per line per block into L1 scratch replaces about 960 single DDR accesses (planned guardrail). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / RIFT v0.5 BREATH and v0.6 SILT: records, DDR delay lines, DSP budget (OS 1.11, 2026-11-17)
facts.text: DSP image room: fascia.asm moved to L2 `0x200c4000` (the former room of the PERC code; RIFT's perc.asm is 7.7 KB there) and is 84 KB; the DSP program is 981,144 of 1,048,575 bytes. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / RIFT v0.5 BREATH and v0.6 SILT: records, DDR delay lines, DSP budget (OS 1.11, 2026-11-17)
facts.text: Planned guardrails for every engine: a cap of 4 SILT voices across tracks (a fifth note steals the oldest with a 32-sample fade); slow coefficients on alternate blocks; when the guard's clock says the frame is full, a voice first drops its ensemble size, then goes SOLO, before it is left out; a gate stress step that must stay under 0.8 of the frame and a negative control (cap off, 8 voices) that must exceed it. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / RIFT v0.5 BREATH and v0.6 SILT: records, DDR delay lines, DSP budget (OS 1.11, 2026-11-17)
facts.text: Note-off for a custom voice: SILT's DSP voice takes the note-off from frame mask word 36 (as measured for FLEX); a released voice under -80 dB rests. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / RIFT v0.5 BREATH and v0.6 SILT: records, DDR delay lines, DSP budget (OS 1.11, 2026-11-17)
facts.text: Old sounds and new records: ORGAN v0.5's 16 new controls ride FASCIA's other records (PHRM a choice on WAV2; TURB, BREK, BDEP, PRES on the 0..100 PD and OFS records read as 0..127; BLOM, EDGE, PVEL on FM Tone records 235..237, so no LFO). A v0.4 ORGAN sound holds stock's record defaults there; the DSP reads that set as "both pages at 0", and the ColdFire writes v0.5's defaults on the first turn of one of those knobs. Reusing a record for a new meaning changes old sounds: in v0.6 a v0.5 sound's PHRM and VELO words read as MTUN and MCHR. `[doc]`

facts.text: A SHARC floor bug: ORGAN's `o_sint`/`o_sinf` called `_floor` with the integer and its scratch both in R12, so floorf gave 0 for 1 <= x < 2 and the sine left its polynomial's range for phases 0.75..1 (up to about 1e-4 off, inaudible; caught only by a 400-block tremolo test, longer than v0.4's 124-block gate). v0.5 fixes it. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / digikit findings 152, 155-157 on DN2 1.12: addresses and a SHARC calibration on a unit (2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: Device cycles against emulator instructions (SHARC, one unit, DN2 1.12): five synthetic kernels of about 20,000 instructions a call, one call per block, 3 x 5 s captures each: ALU 1.01, data moves 1.08, a mix 1.46, branches 2.10, memory access 2.69 device cycles per emulator instruction. One factor per device mis-estimates a module by up to 2.7x; ALU-heavy code costs about its instruction count, memory and branches 2-3 times. One real analog machine module: 5,723 mean / 6,811 max cycles a call against 4,642 emulator instructions (about 1.23). Stock load: about 249k cycles a block (one note, `light`) and 420k (every track, long release, all sends, `heavy`); 443k mean in the kernels profile. The emulator's stock engine runs the same ~337k instructions in both stock profiles, so stock load must be measured on the unit. `[hw]` (confirms I36; A35)

facts.text: RIFT's frame guard order: it renders its voices in ORDER and leaves out, then steals, those that do not fit. ORDER was newest first, so a melody over a held chord (or a re-struck note under voice mode REUSE) took the time and the held notes were stolen (a user report; the REUSE case did not reproduce at the emulator's CPU level). v0.11 marks a voice released at its note-off (frame mask word 36) until its next note and orders every released voice after every held one, newest first within each group (I161). `[emu]` (fix) / `[?]` (report)

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.64-v0.67 and RIFT v0.13-v0.14 (OS 1.11, 2026-11-20/21)
facts.text: Stock's sustain (MIDI CC 64) holds note-offs per track: a flag byte per track at `0x445fe6e0`, set by the CC handler `0x40122f56` through `0x40126d4a(track, on)`. Every live note-off (the KeyboardView's key up, the MIDI note-off entries `0x40121aae` / `0x401219ac`, all notes off) goes through `0x4012182a(track, note, source)`, whose first call `0x40126e30` stores the note-off in the track's list at `0x445fe6f0 + 8 x track` while the flag is set. `0x40126d4a(track, 0)` clears the flag and sends every stored note-off. dn2mk2 v0.64's keyboard HOLD calls it for all 16 tracks, so held keys, MIDI in and the arp's keys latch without a UI-level latch. `[emu]` (gate step `kbhold`; HOLD with the arp not yet tried on a unit)

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.64-v0.67 and RIFT v0.13-v0.14 (OS 1.11, 2026-11-20/21)
facts.text: Stock takes the KEYBOARD key before any view sees it: in the emulator, KEYBOARD pressed with PTN held turned KEYBOARD mode off and the PTN view's key handler never saw it, so a PTN + KEYBOARD combination has to be caught in the UI item queue ([O46](../CONFLICTS.md)). The PTN view (class `0x402008c4`) stays open after PTN alone and after PTN + YES / NO, and the next [TRIG] then picks a pattern; dn2mk2 closes it by sending NO before PTN's release. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.64-v0.67 and RIFT v0.13-v0.14 (OS 1.11, 2026-11-20/21)
facts.text: The upgrade image's room is the compressed size of sections 3 and 7: dn2mk2 v0.63 had 89 bytes left of the 2 MiB, v0.64 291 bytes (after shipping every other frame of its start-up animation). An optimal aPLib parse (a dynamic program over every byte; same token format, offsets at most 1,044,480 inside the 1 MiB window, lengths at most 2,048) packed v0.64's section 3 from 1,291,136 to 1,219,072 bytes and section 7 from 653,056 to 637,984, about 87 KB freed. The bootstrap's own depacker (`0x80000432`, run in the emulator) returns exactly the packed bytes; a stream with one byte flipped does not. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.64-v0.67 and RIFT v0.13-v0.14 (OS 1.11, 2026-11-20/21)
facts.text: A sound value is a 16-bit word `coarse << 8 | fine`, and stock stores a p-lock as the record's whole word, so a coarse-only record such as SAMP has a free low byte that survives sounds, kits, presets, locks and copy and paste. dn2mk2 v0.65 keeps a sample bank there (`0x00`/`0x40`/`0x80`/`0xC0` for A-D); its DSP reads the bank as `(low byte + 0x20) >> 6`, so an LFO's small offset never changes bank. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.64-v0.67 and RIFT v0.13-v0.14 (OS 1.11, 2026-11-20/21)
facts.text: The playing pattern is at `0x42C5A9A0`: 16 tracks of 1,701 bytes, each step's flags a big-endian u16 at track + 2 x step; bit 0 is set on a note trig (`0x0381` seen) and on a lock (trigless) trig (`0x7801`). dn2mk2's gate checks that stock's own track objects (vtable +40, read by the step test `0x4004e95a`) hand exactly these pointers for all 16 tracks. v0.66 uses it for slides that last until the next trig (SLEN NXT, the Analog Four manual's rule). `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.64-v0.67 and RIFT v0.13-v0.14 (OS 1.11, 2026-11-20/21)
facts.text: Arp on MIDI tracks (upstream dnfw's `midiarp`, merged into dn2mk2 v0.67): a MIDI track with the arp on is sent down the synth path at the three forks (sequencer trig, key down, key up); at the ISR's voice trigger `0x400268f8` its note becomes a MIDI record on the batch the ISR already hands the MIDI task, its length the arp's N.LEN (INF sent as the longest finite length), and the engine's voice trigger `0x400db524` is never called for it. In the emulator stock still sets the voice slot's note-on bit for that note; on upstream's unit a MIDI track's slot made no sound. Compare the static reading under "Arpeggiator vs MIDI tracks" above. `[hw]` (upstream's unit, 2026-09-17) / `[emu]` (dn2mk2 v0.67 gate; not yet on dn2mk2's unit)

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.64-v0.67 and RIFT v0.13-v0.14 (OS 1.11, 2026-11-20/21)
facts.text: FLEX takes of MAIN and IN clip when GAIN makes up their level, because GAIN is applied before the recorder's int16 clamp (the owner and a tester). dn2mk2 v0.66 and RIFT v0.14 record such takes unchanged, mark them in bit 15 of the buffer entry's steps word, and play a marked take +12 dB; the owner heard MAIN needing close to +24, so +12 is still to be checked on a unit, and a take saved as a sample loses the mark (12 dB quieter). `[hw]` (symptom) / `[emu]` (fix)

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.64-v0.67 and RIFT v0.13-v0.14 (OS 1.11, 2026-11-20/21)
facts.text: Monomachine FM+ DYN frequencies are continuous: 1FRQ = 2 x knob / 128 and 2FRQ = 4 x (knob / 128)^2, as the Monomachine manual describes; STAT's and PAR's are its listed ratios, one a detent. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.64-v0.67 and RIFT v0.13-v0.14 (OS 1.11, 2026-11-20/21)
facts.text: dn2mk2's +Drive map grows (v0.65): bank lists for projects 0..63 at `0x6E0600-0x6EE5FF` and for 64..127 at `0x6F0800-0x6FEFFF`. The project's own memory-map table had left out the tuning records and the library extension (`0x6F0000-0x6F0700`) and counted them as free until the banks were placed. facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.64-v0.67 and RIFT v0.13-v0.14 (OS 1.11, 2026-11-20/21)
facts.text: RIFT v0.13-v0.14 ports dn2mk2 v0.60-v0.63 (slice editor, FLEX level, FLEX save), v0.59's recorder MON and v0.61's microtuning (the same record at `0x6E0400-0x6E04FF`); RIFT's machines read the note word as note + fine / 256, so all of them retune (SLICE and GRID never). facts.text: `load = exec * 2 + 0x28000000`. Code addresses count 16-bit parcels (VISA), and the entry `0x001c12e2` lands exactly on a loaded region; all 591 of 591 `0x1c`-space jump targets fit. The `0xb8` space (1,025 targets) needs the other mapping (L2 code at `0x20000000`, see the firmware map). `[doc]` {digikit-sharcmap}

facts.text: Regions (DN2 1.11, section 7 836,956 B): L2 `0x20000000-0x2001e880` code (125 KB), `0x2001e888-0x2008823c` data; L1 `0x282403f0-0x2826f000` and `0x282c0000-0x282dd52c` rodata, `0x283825c4-0x2839bffc` code (105 KB); DDR `0x80000018-0x8052fbe0` 5.4 MB, almost all fill. About 240 KB of the 837 KB section is code. `[doc]`
