facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / A Model:Cycles firmware on a Model:Samples (Modded Cycles Techno Edition v1.6.2, OS 1.13, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: Same hardware: the Techno Edition's Cycles firmware, packed inside the official Model:Samples OS 1.13 file (the Modded-Cycles packing; Elektron's code checked by SHA-256 only), turns a Model:Samples into a modded Model:Cycles; bootloader, startup menu and signature stay Elektron's. Installed through the startup menu over MIDI IN (FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4, READY TO RECEIVE), whatever OS the Samples runs; the unit restarts by itself 1-3 minutes after the transfer. `[hw]` (2026-11-16 and 2026-11-18)

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / A Model:Cycles firmware on a Model:Samples (Modded Cycles Techno Edition v1.6.2, OS 1.13, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: After that Transfer cannot update it; use the startup menu. A Model:Cycles running the Samples OS would take such a file and then refuse Cycles firmware over USB until the Cycles OS is reinstalled over MIDI. Going back: the official Samples OS through the startup menu, after moving tracks off added machines. `[doc]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / A Model:Cycles firmware on a Model:Samples (Modded Cycles Techno Edition v1.6.2, OS 1.13, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: Stereo samples played an octave low on SAMPLER, GRANULAR and WAVETABLE (half speed); v1.6.1 mixes stereo to mono on load (a slot holds about 35 s of stereo, 71 s of mono). `[doc]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Mute, LFO waves and the 707 (Modded Cycles Techno Edition v1.6.3-v1.9, Model:Cycles OS 1.13, 2026-11-19)
facts.text: The Cycles' mute only holds back the sequencer's trigs: a voice that sounds without a trig (the Techno Edition's ATMOS drone with GATE on) kept playing on a muted track, even across a pattern change. v1.9 ends such a drone on mute and fades its reverb tail in about a second; trig-played notes ring out as usual (I162). `[doc]` (user report; fix tested in emulation only)

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Mute, LFO waves and the 707 (Modded Cycles Techno Edition v1.6.3-v1.9, Model:Cycles OS 1.13, 2026-11-19)
facts.text: Stock OS 1.13 reads an LFO WAVE value it does not know as RND: the mod's Turing Machine waves (T3-T16, past RND) saved in a sound play as RND on the official OS. `[doc]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Mute, LFO waves and the 707 (Modded Cycles Techno Edition v1.6.3-v1.9, Model:Cycles OS 1.13, 2026-11-19)
facts.text: Lo-fi by rate and bit depth, not samples: the 707 machine synthesises its six parts at 24 kHz and 8 bits (cymbals 6 bits), the original's grain, with no 707 sample. Tested in emulation only. `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Silicon
facts.text: CPU: ColdFire MCF5445x (board photos read MCF54454VR266 or MCF5445AVR266), 32-bit big-endian. The firmware stores 264 MHz; internal bus 132 MHz (UARTs, PIT, DSPI), FlexBus 66 MHz, 24 MHz crystal. 128 MB SDRAM at `0x40000000`; NOR flash on CS0, 8 MB decode. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Silicon
facts.text: Audio DSP: Freescale Symphony DSP56721, two DSP5636x cores in one chip, 200 MHz each, with no external memory. Each core has its own P memory. A 64 K-word shared window at `$030000` is reachable by both cores; P, X and Y alias there. Tracks 1-4 run on core 1 and tracks 5-8 on core 0 ("inverted from old assumptions"). Each track's FX1 and FX2 run on its own core. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Silicon
facts.text: Storage: CompactFlash (FAT16/32) through an ATA stack (PIO task-file registers at `0x90000000`).

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Silicon
facts.text: The kernel is a proprietary preemptive microkernel (banner "ElektronOctatrack DPS-1"), not FreeRTOS.

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
facts.text: 4,532 cycles per sample per core at 44.1 kHz (199.9 MHz measured). The older 4,160 / 183 MHz is retracted.

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
facts.text: About 3,120 cycles/sample are usable for DSP work; stock takes ~1,410.

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
facts.text: Planning number: ~500 cycles on top of the current reverb with 4 FX1 FILTERs, ~900 with 2. One FX1 FILTER costs 192 cycles/sample. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
facts.text: Stock FX2 costs per sample (one MKII, 1.40C), dearest first: DJ EQ ~340, LO-FI ~310, SPRING ~300, CHORUS ~295, FILTER ~285, DARK ~255, PLATE ~250, PHASER ~240, EQUALIZER ~190, FLANGER ~145, COMB ~125, COMPRESSOR ~100, SPATIALIZER ~80, DELAY ~0. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
facts.text: Words are not cycles: `move x0,a` 2 cycles, a one-word displaced `move x:(r7+$15),a` ~4, a two-word displaced ~6. Static word counts are a floor; only a burn sweep measures the ceiling. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
facts.text: ColdFire access costs (one unit, 132 MHz, inside the frame interrupt, stock cache settings): register/SRAM/cache hit ~2.9 ns, uncached SDRAM store 36 ns, load 69 ns, cache miss ~80 ns, `cpushl` 46-80 ns. SRAM is 12-28x cheaper than SDRAM, and caching a transmit buffer does not help. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
facts.text: USB costs: one recording buffer is about 6 points of the ColdFire's frame share, USB streaming about 12. Six buffers plus streaming drop frames. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / FX slots
facts.text: Every track runs `FX1 -> FX2 -> gain`. FX1 has 3,072 words of Y, FX2 16,384, which is why reverbs and delay are FX2-only.

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / FX slots
facts.text: Both menus share one DSP dispatch table indexed by the raw id. A module on a stock effect's id replaces that effect in both slots, and removing an effect from a menu frees no space. The reclaimable pool is FX1's ten effects, 3,384 words. `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
facts.text: Elektron ships the same OS as `.bin` and `.syx` (the MKI and MKII files are byte-identical for 1.40C). `.bin` = ELUP header + seed + XOR-feedback-obfuscated `[len] + ELEK(aPLib(MAIN OS))` + checksum. `.syx` = SysEx-packed ELEK container. The MAIN OS is 1,112,560 B. No cryptographic signature in any layer. `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
facts.text: Validation on update returns: -1 IO, -2 not a valid OS, -3 length (more than 1 MB + 12 B), -4 checksum, -5 MK1 not allowed (version code below "0156"), -6 cannot downgrade (below "0178"). octabam images keep code 0178. `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
facts.text: The card path: OS UPGRADE lists `/*.BIN` on the CF, validates, programs NOR from `0x4000` and verifies it word by word. Stock then shows "PLEASE REBOOT!" and never resets the unit itself.

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
facts.text: Recovery: hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 3 = MIDI UPGRADE (not TRIG 4 as on the small boxes), send the stock `.syx` over DIN MIDI. `TRIG 2` (EMPTY RESET) clears battery-backed RAM and settings, not the card. Pace about 7,460 messages at DIN rate. Filter MIDI clock on that port and merge nothing else into it: a MIDI-hub preset caused a CHECKSUM ERROR. If the unit loses sync, send again slower (60-300 ms between messages). The unit may update its bootstrap after the flash. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
facts.text: How stock writes NOR (1.40C, Modwerk's reading, `[doc]` {modwerk-ot-traps}): OS UPGRADE reads the whole card file into RAM, then erases and programs NOR from there (sector erase `0x40020628`, 256-byte page program `0x400206f4`, the 37 sector starts listed at `0x400a95c0`). The layout is 8 KB boot sectors from `0x4000`, then 64 KB sectors up to `0x1f0000`. Both routines poll the chip themselves and mask interrupts only around the command bytes, so a mod can call them from a task without breaking the frame interrupt. The bootloader below `0x4000` is never written. It depacks NOR from `0x4012` without checking anything, so an image that doesn't boot is recoverable over DIN MIDI only. The startup menu's MIDI UPGRADE checks the received file, not NOR. `[hw]` (testers' units)

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
facts.text: Don't verify a running image against its own RAM: once running, stock rewrites bytes inside its bootloader copy (`0x400e201e-0x400e2108`) and reuses the RAM after the image. Compare against digests taken before stock started. `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-traps}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
facts.text: After flashing a build that changes an effect's parameter layout, old projects need their stored values stamped. A select value outside its count stalls the sequencer on first play. `[hw]` ([I28](../INCIDENTS.md#i28-a-select-value-outside-its-count-stalled-the-sequencer))

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Memory and code placement
facts.text: The free ROM is small: zero runs in `0x400c0000-0x400d8000` total ~8.4 KB, shared by every mod. The zero region above `0x400d8000` is the PROJECT subsystem's RAM. A menu table placed in a 15 KB zero run at `0x401087e4` crashed a unit. ([I48](../INCIDENTS.md#i48-a-menu-table-in-a-free-zero-run-crashed-the-unit)) Larger code goes to a loader-copied area: octabam's loader is a stub at `0x4010fdf0`, right after the OS image, reached from the boot site. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Memory and code placement
facts.text: DSP code that does not fit a core's P memory (ends `P:0x1fff`) runs from the shared window `P:0x30000-0x3ffff`. This was proven on a unit (PEXT probe, 2026-10-25). `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Memory and code placement
facts.text: DSP scratch: r7 scratch `$00-$83` is the per-instance block, and `$84+` hangs the unit. Stock effects scratch `X:0x20-0xff`, and the hardware dispatcher passes the audio block at X:0. `[hw]` ([I29](../INCIDENTS.md#i29-dsp-scratch-at-84-and-up-hung-the-unit))

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
facts.text: `dsp_asm` silently mis-encodes: `tfr a,b` as `rnd b`, and any `mpy` operand order it does not know as `mpysu` (the same trap put garbage on AERIA's headphones, I158). `lua (rN+d),rM` takes d in -64..63 and silently wraps larger values. Labels resolve by prefix, so a new label may not have an existing label as its prefix.

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
facts.text: DSP56300 semantics: A logical op on an accumulator leaves the extension byte stale, so the next store saturates to full scale. `move a,b` limits; `tfr a,b` moves all 56 bits. A Tcc pair sharing one compare breaks with any arithmetic in between. `asr #n,a,a` shifts into a0, and Z is set only when all 56 bits are zero. Reading a0 exposes the fractional left shift that a1 hides.

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
facts.text: No `rep` in an effect's init or proc (it cannot be interrupted, and the host-command handlers need to run). No dense X work in a DMA's 8K block.

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
facts.text: Instruction-form rule, as on the SHARC: a DSP form ships only if a stock payload runs it or a hardware probe approved it. Since 2026-11-15 octabam's gate also accepts a form used by a module proven on a unit (level UNIT). {octabam-1115}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
facts.text: Stock Unicorn halves every ColdFire fractional-mode multiply and adds where `msac` subtracts (the firmware runs EMAC with MACSR = 0x20), and its MAC-with-load decode has three defects. MACSR S/U is bit 6, and in fractional mode it selects 16-bit rounding. These are the same EMAC pitfalls as on the Syntakt and DN2 (rule G-series, `common/toolchain-and-emulators.md`). `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
facts.text: The emulator (`ot_emu`) charges one step per instruction, with no cache or memory timing. A change can be cycle-identical in the port and several percent worse on the unit.

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
facts.text: `div` is a fractional divide: for positive integers N and D (N in a1:a0, D in x0, carry cleared), 24 `div x0,a` steps leave floor(N/(2D)) in a0, not floor(N/D). Double N first. A module's tempo-synced loop lengths came out half as long until this was fixed. `[emu]` {modwerk-1122}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / USB device side (both octabam and Modwerk, measured on units)
facts.text: No EP0 reply or OUT data stage may be a whole multiple of 64 bytes. A reply of 64/128/192/256 bytes left a stale zero-length packet, and the next request returned 0 bytes (once, the unit froze). Stock leaves zero-length termination on in the EP0 OUT queue head, so a 128- or 192-byte OUT stage never completed. Send one byte less, or clear ZLT when priming. `[hw]` Rule A39. ([I5](../INCIDENTS.md#i5-ep0-data-stages-of-a-multiple-of-64-bytes-stall-or-freeze-stock-usb-driver))

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / USB device side (both octabam and Modwerk, measured on units)
facts.text: About one EP0 OUT stage in 50-100 goes unanswered on a MKII: completed inside the ISR after stock's poll, or stopped part-way. Modwerk runs a 60 Hz tick that finishes a completed stage, or stalls EP0 after 0.5 s so the host resubmits. `[hw]` ([I6](../INCIDENTS.md#i6-about-one-ep0-out-stage-in-50-100-goes-unanswered))

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / USB device side (both octabam and Modwerk, measured on units)
facts.text: DMA reads RAM, not the copyback cache. A value the CPU stores rarely stayed stale for minutes in USB replies, while values stored every frame looked live. Copy a reply through the uncached alias and send it from there. `[hw]` (Same idea as A28 on the SHARC.) ([I35](../INCIDENTS.md#i35-usb-replies-stayed-stale-for-minutes))

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / USB device side (both octabam and Modwerk, measured on units)
facts.text: A soft reset leaves the USB controller and PHY as they were: one RAM boot in about six came back with no USB until a power cycle. Stop the controller (USBCMD.RS = 0) and wait ~50 ms before resetting; that gave 20 of 20 good boots. `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-traps} ([I7](../INCIDENTS.md#i7-a-soft-reset-leaves-the-usb-controller-running))

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / USB device side (both octabam and Modwerk, measured on units)
facts.text: Never post key events into stock's queues directly (two crashes minutes later). Feed the panel parser its own bytes instead. `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-traps} ([I30](../INCIDENTS.md#i30-key-events-posted-into-stocks-queues-crashed-the-unit-minutes-later))

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
facts.text: The Modwerk base with nothing installed shows ~42-47 % CPU. That is mostly stock's own tasks; there is no clean stock baseline yet. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
facts.text: An FM synth module costs ~8 points just by being installed, plus ~5 while a track plays it. Small effects cost 0.5 points or less on the ColdFire, but their DSP cost lands on their core (BBD on T6: core T5-8 went from ~44 % to 54 %). `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
facts.text: Uncached module code is expensive: Analog BD on one track cost ~20 points. 93 % of each call was a write lease whose owner check read the module header through the uncached alias (~0.6 µs a read). With one lease per frame it dropped to ~10 points. Lesson: take locks only where a call writes, at most once a frame, and keep uncached reads out of hot paths. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
facts.text: UI-task edits can cost milliseconds: a 64-step MIDI rewrite took 3.9 ms per knob turn, mostly stock's lock-index rebuild. Updating only the own track's bits brought it to 0.5 ms. Audio frames stayed ~406-417 µs apart throughout, because it all ran on the UI task. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
facts.text: The DSP peak meter shows the busiest single frame of a 1,024-frame window. A self-test or sync leaves it at ~99.7 % while the mean is flat and the audio fine. Judge overload by the longest frame of a real load, not the peak. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
facts.text: Frame budget from the field (Modwerk beta, 2026-11-08): audio frames are 363 µs apart (16 samples), and the DSPs starve once a gap passes about 515 µs. A unit left stopped and connected for about 23 hours with 6 modules showed 42 % CPU and a longest gap of 423 µs, with no freeze. `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-beta}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
facts.text: Settled: the silence after USB DISK MODE was Modwerk's, not stock's (finding 72, 2026-11-10): stock pauses the DSP while USB DISK MODE is open; Modwerk's base took that pause for a stalled DSP, and its recovery kept the audio stopped until a power cycle. Fixed in the base; on the owner's MKII (1.40C) PROJ > USB DISK MODE, about 10 s, NO, PLAY now plays. Not tested: the walk on a flashed base, a file copy in that mode, an OS upgrade from the card. A mod that watches for DSP stalls must tell stock's own pauses from a stall (rule C12: it was never reproduced on a stock unit). `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-unit-1110}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
facts.text: Field stalls with modules (Modwerk beta, 8-10 Nov): stalls still come within about a minute of installs or restores, before any module code is placed (finding 71), and on a heavy self-test Part (FILTER and DELAY on every track plus FLANGER and PHASER) 1 run in 21 stalled on the live base, 0 in 5 on the lighter Part; only a power cycle recovered. The base's longest fully masked span measured about 14 µs, far under the roughly 200 µs that stops core 0, so masked ColdFire code is unlikely but not ruled out for the stall itself. One field crash record: vector 3 inside a module's ColdFire code. A unit with 6 modules stayed up 70 hours (longest frame gap 424 µs). `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-beta-1110} {modwerk-ot-unit-1110}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / More DSP and boot traps (measured on units)
facts.text: An effect's `init` must preserve r1: the FX1 dispatcher keeps the effect id there and calls `proc` through it. An init that moved r1 jumped to the reset vector and killed the core at project load. octabam's build refuses an init that writes r1/n1/m1. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / More DSP and boot traps (measured on units)
facts.text: A persistent slot that `init` does not clear holds the previous effect's leftovers. The emulator boots with zeroed RAM and cannot show it. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / More DSP and boot traps (measured on units)
facts.text: Resident window code must sit in `0x33da3..0x33fff` or `0x37da3..0x37eff`: payload B's boot loop clears `Y:0x37f00..0x3ffff`, and DARK REV on an FX2 slot writes from the slot base up to base + `0x3da2` (O31). The FX2 slots start at `0x30000`, `0x34000`, `0x38000` and `0x3c000`, so `0x34000..0x37da2` is the next slot's reverb buffer, not free space (octabam's correction, 2026-11-22, [I188](../INCIDENTS.md#i188-window-stubs-placed-inside-dark-revs-buffer-stopped-the-dsp-octabam-test-images)). `[emu]` (both cores faulted at boot in the port) `[hw]` {octabam-1122}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / More DSP and boot traps (measured on units)
facts.text: A DSP frame counter past `$7fffff` saturates in `move a,nN`, which stopped a frame engine after 50.7 minutes. Mask counters to 23 bits. `[hw]` ([I32](../INCIDENTS.md#i32-a-dsp-frame-counter-saturated-after-507-minutes))

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / More DSP and boot traps (measured on units)
facts.text: Core 1's load-meter counter is at `X:$2840` on Modwerk USB bases; module state there gave a jittery pitch. `[hw]` ([I33](../INCIDENTS.md#i33-module-state-on-a-load-meter-counter-gave-a-jittery-pitch))

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / More DSP and boot traps (measured on units)
facts.text: Cold starts: an early-startup change passed emulator boots and quick power cycles but stalled at the logo after several minutes powered off. Keeping the activation helper resident in the OS image fixed it; the mechanism is unknown. Qualify startup changes after a long power-off (rule A40). `[hw]` ([I34](../INCIDENTS.md#i34-a-startup-change-stalled-at-the-logo-after-a-long-power-off))

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / More DSP and boot traps (measured on units)
facts.text: A write-watch on cached addresses is blind to a clear through the uncached alias. A "free 8.8 MB" region turned out to be the stock delay rings. Before trusting a null result, ask what the instrument cannot see (rule A31). `[emu]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / From KYOTI (Zac-Kyoti/octatrack-kyoti-fw, OS 1.40C)
facts.text: A core's crash threshold, found on hardware in KYOTI's own cost model: stock's heaviest effects plus the sidechain compressor model at ~3,516 cycles per sample. The core crashed somewhere between ~3,760 and ~3,830. With DJ EQ in both slots on T5-T8, one extra REPITCH voice (~240) was clean; adding a second (RPS9 ~77 or RPSP ~240) crashed. KYOTI's bar: a feature must not break any configuration that is clean on stock. So beside stock's heaviest effects a core has room for about one heavy voice. Note that these "modelled cycles" are KYOTI's estimate, not octabam's measured 4,532 cycles per sample. Compare figures only within one model. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / From KYOTI (Zac-Kyoti/octatrack-kyoti-fw, OS 1.40C)
facts.text: The DSP shared window in work RAM is volatile: at boot, `0x401086f4` is copied to `0x80000000` (`0x3e88` bytes) and the rest is zero-filled up to `0x80004000`. Nothing of yours survives there across a boot. `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / From KYOTI (Zac-Kyoti/octatrack-kyoti-fw, OS 1.40C)
facts.text: One image for MKI and MKII: the OS probes `0x46c8d18c` and shows 15 (MKI) or 16 (MKII) PERSONALIZE items. `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / From KYOTI (Zac-Kyoti/octatrack-kyoti-fw, OS 1.40C)
facts.text: KYOTI keeps a merged, confidence-tagged 1.40C address map (`reference/kb/memory-map.md`) that cross-references octabam. It is a good second reading. `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Debugging on the unit by writing a log to the CF card (OctaMax, MKII, OS 1.40C)
facts.text: When the emulator cannot run the code you need to see (here, the EMAC-heavy frame builder), log from the unit itself. OctaMax added two detours that call the firmware's own file primitives (open `0x40016864`, write `0x400166b8`, close `0x4001677c`, sprintf `0x40013a08`) and write `/HOTDBG.TXT` to the CF card. Pull the card and read it. It works on hardware, and it showed that values seeded in the emulator had been guessed wrong (a voice type byte of 1, not 4). `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Debugging on the unit by writing a log to the CF card (OctaMax, MKII, OS 1.40C)
facts.text: The DSP never plays on its own: every frame the ColdFire builds a per-voice packet in shared RAM (double buffer at `0x80000000`, selector `0x800000e0`) and pokes the DSP. A voice that stops being fed goes silent without any "stop". `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Debugging on the unit by writing a log to the CF card (OctaMax, MKII, OS 1.40C)
facts.text: Recorder buffers live in a paged RAM pool (base `0x40a955e0`, ~89 MB) that survives a project change; the voices are torn down and rebuilt by the load. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Debugging on the unit by writing a log to the CF card (OctaMax, MKII, OS 1.40C)
facts.text: Restoring state every frame is safe only for CPU-side bookkeeping. Overwriting data the DSP reads corrupted the audio. `[hw]` ([I31](../INCIDENTS.md#i31-restoring-dsp-read-state-every-frame-corrupted-the-audio))

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Debugging on the unit by writing a log to the CF card (OctaMax, MKII, OS 1.40C)
facts.text: An Octatrack emulator built on QEMU (ColdFire MCF54455) plus dsp56300, octemu by markandrus, targets firmware development including USB MIDI and audio; PassOS uses its 20-channel USB audio work. `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Where code and data may go: KYOTI's cave ledger (OS 1.40C, `reference/kb/caves.md`)
facts.text: The parameter-page descriptor table is live data, zeros included. It is 31 entries of `0x192` bytes at `0x400d2e52-0x400d5f00`, and a zero entry means "the default". Never place code or data there unless the entry is proven unreachable. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Where code and data may go: KYOTI's cave ledger (OS 1.40C, `reference/kb/caves.md`)
facts.text: The canary test (from octalab) before anything ships in a new region: 1. Fill the range with a pattern, or a 32-bit counter so that partial overwrites show. 2. Use the unit for a full session: load, record, change patterns, save, power-cycle, load again. 3. Read the range back and compare. octamax lost tables to a heap tail and probe counters to a region restored on every load. See rule A43. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Where code and data may go: KYOTI's cave ledger (OS 1.40C, `reference/kb/caves.md`)
facts.text: Scratch RAM `0x80006a40+` is not safe under live audio: a magic word at `0x80006a60` was overwritten by the next key press on a real MKI while recording; the emulator, which runs no DSP/audio path, kept it forever. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Where code and data may go: KYOTI's cave ledger (OS 1.40C, `reference/kb/caves.md`)
facts.text: Past the image's ceiling, two routes: append a runtime after the OS image (octabam's loader stub; proven on an MKI); put a position-independent payload with a relocation table on the CF card and load it at run time. octemu does this for USB audio (four UAC2 descriptors, iso servicing and a 36 KB ring against ~408 B of slack). `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
facts.text: AMP envelope: the DSP's AMP envelope restarts from zero at every trig START, so with any ATK above 0 a sound that plays across trigs drops out and fades back in, a click on every note. A ColdFire machine holds the DSP at ATK 0 / HOLD INF / REL INF and shapes AMP itself, as SYNTH MACHINE does. Measured laws (Tim Hastie): ATK is a linear ramp of 3.85 ms x 2^(ATK/8.53), at least 16 frames; REL is exponential with tau 0.295 ms x 2^(REL/8.53). `[hw]` {octabam-wavecf} (I58)

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Crossfader: stock maps the crossfader through one table of 128 Q15 values at `0x400bcd90`; the panel handler `0x40061e40` and the MIDI CC 48 handler `0x400626ba` rebuild the per-track weights at `0x80003c60` from it. Replacing the table changes scene locks, XVOL and the morph alike; MIDI SCENES mixes linearly on its own. `[hw]` {octabam-xfcurve}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Demand loading: the loader copies a whole effect block (MODULATION, 1,561 words, an estimated ~31k of the 72,512 cycles in a frame) inside one DSP frame hook; the DSP-busy meter reads 99.7 % in that window `[hw]`. The frame interrupt has two waits with no time limit (the loader's wait before each host word, and stock's spin at `0x4000ab26` until the DSP takes the frame's `0x8c` host command); if the DSP stops taking host words, the ColdFire can spin forever `[?]` {octabam-dl} (I57, H22).

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
facts.text: CF write throughput (STEM REC, MKII): write time per KB grows with the number of files written at once: 54-92 us/KB for one file, 423 us/KB for eleven (212 after writing whole 32 KB clusters only). Samples streamed by Static machines from the same card slow writes further (252 -> 387 us/KB for ten files); eleven 24-bit files need 2.9 MB/s. `[hw]` {octabam-stemrec}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Test host: octabam's hardware tools run on Linux and on WSL2 with usbipd; MIDI, transport and the load meter work there, but USB-audio capture over usbip delivered only about a quarter of the frames. `[hw]` {octabam-hwtest}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Key bus (Modwerk): the key bus moved from Y `$800-$9FF` to Y `$7E00-$7FFF` on each core, the tail of the first internal FX2 slot, which frees Y `$7F0-$9FF` for a DSP machine's voice. An FX2 effect that fills the whole 16,384-word buffer is then refused on T1/T5; Mini Verb, E-Verb (15,870 words) and BBD still fit. A keyed duck lands within one 5 ms window of the kick, on the same core and across cores; in the DSP simulator the cross-core key arrives exactly two blocks late. Four RINGMOD SC plus four BBD while playing: CPU 85.1 %, core peaks 66/74.5 %. `[hw]` (MKI 2026-10-30, MKII 2026-11-10), memory survey `[emu]` {modwerk-ot-keybus}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Module cost (Modwerk survey): module DSP code runs at 1.4-1.7 cycles per instruction against about 1 for stock, and installed but unused modules add frame-interrupt time (23.3 % -> 28.2 % stopped with 26 installed). `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-options}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Internal SRAM has no free holes: `0x80000000-0x80008000` is the program's `.data`/`.bss`, filled at boot from the image tail; `0x80006964-0x80007574` is the work buffer of the stock audio-analysis task, which writes up to 768 words from `0x80006974`. This explains the KYOTI scratch-word loss at `0x80006a60`. OCTAMAX keeps patch state in DDR at `0x40af0000-0x40af0600`, inside a reserve stock never references, cleared by its boot stub. `[hw]` {octamax-notes} (I59; boot-fill extent disputed, CONFLICTS O23)

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Sequencer state: current bank/pattern at `0x800065bd/be`, the cued pair at `0x800065bf/c0` ("nothing cued" when both pairs are equal); cueing the playing pattern cancels in stock, and a switch to the same pattern is a restart with no Part reload. Active bank `0x80000002`, active Part `0x80000003` (disputed, O23); whole-Part apply `0x40009094`. `[hw]` {octamax-notes}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Step timing (KYOTI): the sequencer schedules each step one step ahead, so a Part change sent to the engine in the landing tick sounds a step early; a per-track apply must wait one of the track's steps `[hw]`. The whole-Part apply posts a kernel message and belongs on the UI task; a storage job's done-callback runs on the UI task, which ticks at 1/60 s `[emu]`. Copies with interrupts masked click (I60). {kyoti-reload}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Sample pool: paged in 6 KB pages (MEMORY shows 85.5 MB); KYOTI V1.7 takes 11 pages on DRAM units, octabam reserves 10 MiB when any module runs from DRAM, 18 MiB with STEM REC. `[doc]` {kyoti-build}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam findings (2026-11-11)
facts.text: Audio-interrupt budget (CX OSC on a MKII): with nothing playing the ColdFire idles at 44.7 % with a mean audio interrupt of 125 us (max 212 us); four CX OSC tracks: 21.8 % idle, 272 us; six: about 12 %, 309 us mean but a 376 us maximum past the 363 us frame; seven: 0 % idle and MAIN clipped. The module now refuses a seventh instance. `[hw]` {octabam-cxosc}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam findings (2026-11-11)
facts.text: Stock icon blit (`0x400128a8`, a 13-row column word with mask `0xfff80000`): bit 31 is the bottom row and bit 19 the top, so a left shift moves the picture down. Five flashes went into one pixel before this was written down. `[hw]` {octabam-traps}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam findings (2026-11-11)
facts.text: FLEX slices (DRUMMER, OS 1.40C): in slice mode the voice start `0x4000f450(track, slot, flags)` plays slice `min(STRT >> 1, count - 1)`; the slice table is 64 entries of 12 bytes from +312 of the FLEX slot record `0x100b14f0 + 0x448*slot` (octabam's own STORAGE note said 20 bytes; the code multiplies by 12). `[emu]` {octabam-drummer}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam findings (2026-11-11)
facts.text: Adding and moving trigs: the sequencer builds each step about 912 samples after the step counter changes, one step ahead; a detour right after the builder (`0x400a2d82`) can add a trig on an empty step or rewrite its micro-timing (one unit is 1/24 of a step). Locks staged for an added trig are ignored, and its lock block holds zeros at boot unless the mod fills it (all 32 lane values of the track went to 0 until DRUMMER wrote `0xff` there). `[emu]` {octabam-drummer} DRUMMER ran on the author's MKII from these sites; two bugs found after the first unit test are I72. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam findings (2026-11-11)
facts.text: Scene locks sit at Part `+0x662 + (scene*8 + track)*32`, one byte per parameter, `0xff` for none. Retrig time RTIM is exponential: half a step at 79, doubling every 12. `[emu]` {octabam-drummer}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: Boot keys (OS 1.40C): FUNC held from power-on opens Elektron's startup menu; PROJ held at power-on is ignored by the bootloader and the unit starts normally. Modwerk therefore moved its "skip modules" gesture from FUNC to PROJ on the MKII (the MKI keeps FUNC). `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-base}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: Scene keys take the encoders: pressing a scene key writes stock's scene-lock knob handler `0x40053498` into every encoder slot of the table at `0x46c7dede + 20*enc` (writer `0x40031406`, dispatch `0x40031944`), so a page editor's hook sees no turn while a scene is held. `[emu]`, seen by a user {octabam-traps}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: Stock calls clobber scratch registers: the CC sender `0x4009eec8` saves only d2-d7/a2-a5; any `jsr` into stock can change d0, d1, a0 and a1. `[emu]`, seen by a user {octabam-traps}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: Render after stock's trig work: in SYNTIZ, a render in the same frame after stock's trig handling cost up to 2.25x a first render (33.6 % vs 14.9 % of a frame); stock's own work reached 84 % of a frame at pattern transitions. Modwerk refuses a RAM boot or trial while the sequencer plays. `[hw]` {modwerk-syntiz}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: An installed module that never plays can cost margin: on an MKII, FM Synth 0.1.2 installed beside SYNTIZ gave light crackle and one sample track less of headroom; removing it cured both (one A/B, cause unknown). `[hw]` {modwerk-syntiz}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: Removing a module in use left the loader stuck in recovery until a power cycle (I75, rule A54); a base update over USB once reported Done and did not stick (I76). `[hw]` {modwerk-syntiz}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: USB base: Modwerk's Octatrack base is open to everyone since 2026-11-11; the first install still goes through the CF card, a module set holds at most 20 modules (24 since 2026-11-14, still a temporary limit {modwerk-1115}), and USB Audio is off (USB MIDI only) unless the set has the USB Audio module. `[doc]` {modwerk-ot-base}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: Analog BD 0.1.7 (909 model): tables and voices in DSP X `$2841-$3200`, next to the core-1 load counter at X:`$2840`; glue plus engines take 1,003 P words per core. On an MKII a voice on T5 (core 2) was refused even alone with every core-2 effect slot off, and the DSP `meter` command did not answer on that base. `[hw]` {modwerk-analogbd}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: A recorder started on the first PLAY after power-on (MIDI mode, T1 idle), probably from a quantized REC start left staged at `0x800018be`/`0x800018de` (QREC branch of REC_POST `0x40005178`); a double STOP before PLAY avoided it (I78). `[hw]`, cause `[?]` {octabam-freeloop}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: The stock DELAY's coefficient table `0x400d1ce0-0x400d2cdf` is not free space: its upper half is zero in the stock OS and looks unused, but DELAY reads it. Code that card builds placed there dulled DELAY repeats; Modwerk's checks now refuse any package or base site that writes into it. `[doc]` {modwerk-1112}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: CPU-rendered machines need a budget like DSP effects: on the owner's MKII, three FM Synth tracks beside a busy eight-track pattern froze the unit (I79). Modwerk's base now prices machines (first estimates: 45 % of the CPU for added machines, 12 % for one that names no price), refuses a pick over the limit (CPU FULL) and drops a voice instead of freezing. Seen on development builds; the release base was not run on a unit. `[hw]` {modwerk-1112}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: Modwerk dropped its card firmware builder (2026-11-12): Octatrack modules now reach a unit only through the Modwerk base, over USB or as one set file (`MODWERK0.SET`) on the CF card. `[doc]` {modwerk-1112}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: FREE LOOP and RELOAD_FROM_PROJECT can share the UI tick: both detour the UI task's 1/60 s tick `0x40056c28` (the toast countdown's read), which made them a listed conflict. octabam's HOOKS now chains the site (FREE LOOP first, then RELOAD_FROM_PROJECT); the chain passed four cases under Unicorn, not flashed yet. `[emu]` {octabam-hooks}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Frame-interrupt timing and MIDI scenes (octabam, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: Frame grid: the DSP raises the frame interrupt once a frame (362.8 µs) and the ColdFire answers with the next frame; the handler's entry is `0x4000aad0`. At START and at a program change one frame interrupt runs 475-585 µs on every image measured, so the next one enters late. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Frame-interrupt timing and MIDI scenes (octabam, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: Late-entry window: measured on an MKII, an entry 128-149 µs late is followed by one back-to-back frame interrupt and the unit runs on; 155-223 µs late, one frame is skipped and it runs on; the two stalls logged entered 149 and 155 µs late, after which the DSP took no more frames (sequencer held at step 1, panel and USB alive, power cycle needed). A USB audio capture adds 25-30 µs to the START frame. octabam's FRAME GUARD waits out entries 110-190 µs late until 190 µs; the DSP-side mechanism is inferred (I82, rule A56). `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Frame-interrupt timing and MIDI scenes (octabam, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: Open: on a test image with 60 µs added to every frame interrupt and a 20-channel capture (the frame interrupt at 91 % of the ColdFire), 7 of 16 STARTs froze the whole unit 8.2 s later, at the pattern's wrap; not seen on shipping images. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Frame-interrupt timing and MIDI scenes (octabam, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: Scene lock view (stock): the audio pages draw scene locks from a view byte `0x460d1694` (1 scene A, 2 scene B), set only by the hold-and-turn paths and the scene press handlers `0x40054c80` (A) and `0x40054c5c` (B), which return at once in MIDI mode; the MIDI key's handler (`0x40055548`-`0x40055676`, tail `jmp 0x4007e998` at `0x40055670`) does not set it. So a scene held while switching from the MIDI to the audio tracks shows no locks on stock; octabam's MIDI SCENES hooks the tail to fix that. `[emu]` {octabam-msc}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / AERIA OS findings (own OS on the MKII, 2026-11-09..13)
facts.text: Audio codec: the converter on one MKII board was read as a Cirrus Logic CS42432 (marking read off the board). `[hw]` (one unit)

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / AERIA OS findings (own OS on the MKII, 2026-11-09..13)
facts.text: Stock does not set up the codec over SPI; its only SPI traffic is the real-time clock (stock's code traced, every hardware write logged in octabam's emulator). `[emu]`; disputed by AERIA's register reading below (O44), so treat it as `[?]`.

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / AERIA OS findings (own OS on the MKII, 2026-11-09..13)
facts.text: The analog outputs stayed silent under an own DSP program that copied every DSP register write stock makes; inputs worked. Bisecting put the switch-on in a ~40 ms slice of stock's start-up where its frame exchange with the DSP begins, and the outputs came alive once the engine used a DMA-driven audio ring restarted by a DMA interrupt, as stock does. `[hw]` What actually un-mutes them is `[?]`: the CHANGELOG names the codec's DAC mute, the log the DMA ring. {aeria-changelog}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / AERIA OS findings (own OS on the MKII, 2026-11-09..13)
facts.text: DSP memory per core: a probe on core 0 measured 48K words of private Y and 36K words of private X (core 1 assumed the same). `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / AERIA OS findings (own OS on the MKII, 2026-11-09..13)
facts.text: Running code from the shared window costs about 2x, and the two cores slow each other there. Moving AERIA's engine into core 0's private P memory cut its worst case from ~700 to ~370 instructions a sample and a sequencer stress test from 89 % to 50 % of core 0. `[hw]` {aeria-changelog}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / AERIA OS findings (own OS on the MKII, 2026-11-09..13)
facts.text: Shared-window memory is not zeroed at a cold boot, unlike in the emulator; core 1 ran a garbage effect from an uninitialised slot table and crashed (I84). Clear any table there before use. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / AERIA OS findings (own OS on the MKII, 2026-11-09..13)
facts.text: A crashed core 1 blocks a DSP reload over USB; only a power cycle clears it. A memory probe that wrote past the end of core 1's private memory did the same. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / AERIA OS findings (own OS on the MKII, 2026-11-09..13)
facts.text: Feeding sample audio to the DSP word by word over the host port starved it (about 4,000 frames a second instead of 44,100); taking the data by interrupt, later by DMA sorted once a frame, held full rate. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / AERIA OS repair facts (MKII, v0.9.5-beta, 2026-11-19)
facts.text: Output words of core 0's ESAI TX0 (8 slots a frame): 0/1 CUE, 2/3 MAIN, 4/5 headphones, 6/7 unused; the headphones have their own DAC pair. On the MKII stock's output loop writes the headphones' right channel to word 4 and left to word 5; a cable test on the unit (2026-11-12) agreed. Inputs arrive in RX0 as words C, D, A, B. `[doc]` (read in stock's DSP payload A, P:`$30a-$359`) / `[hw]` (phones order)

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / AERIA OS repair facts (MKII, v0.9.5-beta, 2026-11-19)
facts.text: Stock headphones are a DSP crossfade of main and cue (MIX page PHONES MIX). AERIA found no stock code that reads a headphone pot or writes a codec volume, so the headphone knob is taken to act after the DAC (no schematic). `[?]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / AERIA OS repair facts (MKII, v0.9.5-beta, 2026-11-19)
facts.text: Codec mute at boot: the specification says the bootstrap writes the CS42432's register 07 := FF (all DACs muted) at every boot and the OS must write 07 := 00 (register read by the owner, 2026-11-10). This disagrees with the earlier emulator trace above (stock's only SPI traffic is the real-time clock). `[?]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / AERIA OS repair facts (MKII, v0.9.5-beta, 2026-11-19)
facts.text: DSP clock at a cold start: both cores run from the crystal until core 1's first stage writes the shared PLL (`x:$ffff7d = $2960b0`); bit 18 of `y:$fffff9` / `y:$fffffa` is needed for a cold ESAI start. AERIA's likely cause of silent headphones after flashing: core 0 started the ESAI and lined its rings up with the converter before the PLL was set, the lock then stalled it, and the eight output words could land shifted (a shift of two puts the phones copy of main on the main jacks and unused words on the phones). Every bench test was a RAM boot with the PLL already locked, so none saw it. v0.9.5 makes the engine wait for a host flag raised 20 ms after core 1 and the PLL are set; not yet tested on the unit (I159). `[doc]` (clock recipe) / `[?]` (cause)

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / AERIA OS repair facts (MKII, v0.9.5-beta, 2026-11-19)
facts.text: Level lamp ids above the REC keys: A 62/63, B 60/61, C 56/57, D 58/59 (even and odd are the two dies; stock drives both for green, yellow, red); stock also drives 128-131 on the MKII. `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / AERIA OS repair facts (MKII, v0.9.5-beta, 2026-11-19)
facts.text: DIN MIDI out carries about one message a millisecond; when several tracks' notes fall due together the last leaves up to about 5 ms later (worst seen 6.4 ms). Servicing the DIN queue only between screen updates (the LCD flush takes up to 5.7 ms) let notes wander up to about 10 ms against their sound. `[emu]` (AERIA's simulator)

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / AERIA OS repair facts (MKII, v0.9.5-beta, 2026-11-19)
facts.text: AERIA's simulator (`aeria-os/sim`) runs the real image and both DSP programs on octabam's ColdFire and DSP56300 emulators, with panel, codec writes, DIN MIDI, CF card and battery RAM modelled. It does not model the DSP's cold-start clock, the analog stage, real panel timing, USB with a host or DSP wait states, so loads read low: 29 % worst frame for AERIA's default chain against 36-45 % (worst 55 %) measured on the unit. `[emu]` / `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk findings (2026-11-12/13)

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Findings 2026-11-14/15 (KYOTI RELOAD, octabam DLCOPY, Modwerk)
facts.text: Landing a reloaded track in phase (KYOTI, OS 1.40C): the scheduler builds each step a step ahead, so a track switched on the tick that starts a step is heard a step late. Landing it one tick before the boundary, with its counters set for that boundary and the old sequence's pending events for the track cancelled a tick early, puts it exactly in phase, as stock's own landing and DIRECT JUMP do. Confirmed on an MKI on 2026-11-14 (every item of KYOTI's walk-through). `[hw]` {kyoti-reload-clyps}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Findings 2026-11-14/15 (KYOTI RELOAD, octabam DLCOPY, Modwerk)

Stock STOP (`0x400a12b8`) calls COND_RESET(-1) after clearing RUNNING; PLAY never calls it. `[emu]` (logged in the emulator) {kyoti-reload-clyps}

A core in the illegal-instruction trap answers host commands with P:`$04`. Copying a block takes core B to about 80 % of a frame. `[hw]` {octabam-1115}

facts.text: Borrowing sample memory (`ot_sample_memory`, base 0.7.4): the base takes a module's pages from the top of stock's sample-pool free list on the engine task, as stock's track recorders do, so FREE MEM, sample loads and recorders see that much less until the module is removed. Room for one borrower only. Pages keep their contents through LOAD PROJECT, but not through a power cycle. `[doc]` (contract) {modwerk-1117}

facts.text: Analog BD's 808 has no rest path: it runs its whole sample loop every block, triggered or not; a never-triggered 808 voice was reported at about 152 DSP instructions per sample (emulator). The 909 rests at 3. `[emu]` {modwerk-1117}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / TELOS and dspload-ot: boot order, card mount, run-time DSP code (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-14/16)
facts.text: Boot order on stock 1.40C (instruction counts in octabam's emulator): the boot site `0x4000050c` calls `0x40001e50`, the DSP bootstrap upload, before the OS (4.27 M); SRAM init `0x40000512` (4.35 M); RTOS handoff with 10 tasks (10.2 M); main's last init call `0x4001fc96` (44.9 M); USB controller init `0x4001e030`, run once (45.3 M); the card's first mount `0x40061734` in the sys task (45.8 M); first UI tick that shop mods hook `0x4005595c` (45.9 M); remount (57.6 M); LOAD PROJECT, the engine task's first job (57.6 M); first audio frame (101 M). `[emu]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / TELOS and dspload-ot: boot order, card mount, run-time DSP code (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-14/16)
facts.text: Files read correctly at the first mount: a probe opened and read a 16-byte and a 256 KB file with core's file calls there; the engine task had not run a job yet. USB is composed at the controller's init, before the mount, so USB mods cannot be loaded from the card. `[emu]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / TELOS and dspload-ot: boot order, card mount, run-time DSP code (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-14/16)
facts.text: Code run before the mount: USB init `0x4001dfbc..0x4001e042` and its descriptors `0x400e2000..0x400e21e0` run or are read once; main's bank-pointer store `0x4001fbd0` once; `0x40025aa2` / `0x40025ac2` (the defaults routine) also in every project load; `0x4009d1de` again later. The OS changes data in its image before the mount, so a loader that needs stock bytes keeps its own copy of `0x400b9000..0x400e2324` from boot (I118, A69). `[emu]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / TELOS and dspload-ot: boot order, card mount, run-time DSP code (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-14/16)
facts.text: The DSP payloads are gone from RAM by the mount: A (`0x400e2324`, 79,563 bytes) and B (`0x400f59ef`, 77,061 bytes) are uploaded before the OS starts; by the first mount 76,702 and 73,982 of their bytes read `0xFF`. A payload patch applied later changes nothing. `[emu]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / TELOS and dspload-ot: boot order, card mount, run-time DSP code (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-14/16)
facts.text: Tasks: main (TCB `0x46c7ae84`) and ten others with fixed TCBs and stacks (voice, p2a, p2b, p2c, engine, p1b, sys; sys creates storage, keyrepeat and ui); task create `0x400005fc`, current TCB at `0x800068fc`; a TCB keeps its SP at +72. The sys task's own stack holds return addresses into the card-mount path (`0x40061648`). `[doc]` (read from octabam's RTOS model)

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / TELOS and dspload-ot: boot order, card mount, run-time DSP code (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-14/16)
facts.text: Other routines: FAT opendir `0x46c8240e` and readdir `0x46c8244e`; stock YES/NO dialog `0x4006d57c`; the ColdFire soft reset is RCR `0xFC0A0000` = `0x80`. Stock never restarts itself (an OS upgrade asks for a power cycle); whether a unit comes back from that soft reset is not tested. `[doc]` / `[?]` (reset)

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / TELOS and dspload-ot: boot order, card mount, run-time DSP code (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-14/16)
facts.text: Sample arena: 14,602 pages of 6,144 bytes; TELOS's area (2 MB), staging (256 KB) and heap (768 KB) take about 3 MB of it. `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / TELOS and dspload-ot: boot order, card mount, run-time DSP code (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-14/16)
facts.text: Run-time DSP code (dspload-ot 0.2, from octabam's demand loader): code goes in the window gap `P:0x33dab..0x33fff` (597 words for all mods), after four slot pairs at `x:$33da3`. The ColdFire pump sends 100 halfwords a frame, only on frames whose ping word `0x800000e0` is 0, to core 1's `X:0x2901..` and rings `0xa55a` at `X:0x2900`; each block goes three times, 30 quiet frames apart. Core 0 is never written (a transfer there stalls its chain). Core 1's copier sits in SPATIALIZER's words `P:0x868-0x96c`, hooked at payload B's frame head `P:0x76`; core 0 calls bound slots from `ev_dsp_rx`. `[emu]` (not run on a unit)

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / TELOS and dspload-ot: boot order, card mount, run-time DSP code (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-14/16)
facts.text: A reverb past its default knobs can write above `0x33da3`: the gap is above everything stock effects write with default settings only; dspload-ot puts a guard word (`0xc0ffee`) at each end of a block and unbinds the slot when one changes. A write that lands inside a block without touching either guard is not caught. `[doc]` (O31)

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / TELOS and dspload-ot: boot order, card mount, run-time DSP code (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-14/16)
facts.text: Compiler and emulator disagree on two ColdFire patterns: for `move.b (a0)+,(0,a0,a1)` GCC assumes the destination uses the old a0, ot_emu the new one; for a byte push to `-(sp)` GCC assumes SP moves by 1, ot_emu by 2. Which one the CPU takes is not checked; TELOS avoids both (`-fno-ipa-sra`, `dl_memcpy` out of line). `[emu]` (I117)

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Custom LFO design in the Part (Octatrack Manager user guide, 2026-11-16)
facts.text: Each audio and MIDI track's custom LFO shape is 16 steps, each a value -128..127 and a mode, smooth or stepped (the Part's interpolation mask). A smooth step slopes linearly to the next, and step 16 slopes into step 1. On the device a step is made smooth by holding its trig and pressing TEMPO. `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Custom LFO design in the Part (Octatrack Manager user guide, 2026-11-16)
facts.text: Stock Invert maps v to -1 - v (127 becomes -128, 0 becomes -1) and keeps the modes; stock Clear sets every value to 0 and every step to stepped. The tool copies both behaviours; its hardware comparison cases (PE356/PE357) have no published result yet. `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
facts.text: Banks in RAM: all 16 banks are resident. Bank n at `0x400e21e0 + n*0x9b340`, pattern p's slab at `+ p*0x8ed8`: 8 audio track records of `0x91a` B at `t*0x91a`, 8 MIDI records of `0x8b0` B at `0x48d0 + m*0x8b0`. Slab trailer: `+0x8e50` master length (u16, -1 = INF), `+0x8e52` master scale, `+0x8e53/54` pattern length / scale, `+0x8e55` scale mode, `+0x8e56` CHAIN AFTER (< 0 = the project's `0x8000004e`; steps from table `0x400d80dc`), `+0x8e57` Part link, `+0x8e58` tempo. The 4 working Parts (`0x18b2` B each) start at bank `+0x8ed80`, SAVE PART copies at `+0x9504a`, Part-saved flags `+0x9b312`, Part-edited byte `+0x95048`, bank-changed `+0x9b332`. `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
facts.text: Track record: self-contained; stock's track paste copies it anywhere. P-locks at `+0x59` (64 x 32 B, `0xff` = none) hold scene-parameter indices and the sample lock is a slot number, so a moved sequence plays through the destination's Part. Trig words `+0x89a`, own length / scale `+0x50/+0x51` (MIDI `+0x28/+0x29`). Byte `+0x899` and the slab tail `+0x8e5c..+0x8ed7` are never written to the bank file (TRAC is 2,329 B on the card): leave them out when you compare RAM with a card copy. `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
facts.text: Part slice of an audio track (what stock TRACK COPY carries, 136 B): FX1 / FX2 id `+0x00+t` / `+0x08+t`, levels `+0x12+2t`, machine `+0x22+t`, machine pages `+0x2a+30t` / `+0x1da+30t`, AMP/LFO/FX page 1 `+0x11a+24t`, page 2 block `+0x2f2+30t`, slot record `+0x2ca+5t`, recorder setup `+0x602+12t`. Not carried by stock: scene locks (`+0x662+(s*8+t)*32`, per-scene bytes `+0x1662+10s+t`) and the LFO designer (`+0x1702+16t`, slope `+0x1782+2t`; MIDI `+0x1792+16m` / `+0x1812+2m`). MIDI slice: `+0x3e2+32m` (pages) and `+0x4e2+36m` (channel, bank, program). `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
facts.text: Applying Part data: `0x40001f18(bank, part, t)` publishes one track (engine state and memcpy, no kernel call); set the restart bit `0x8000184c` bit t first when the machine changed, as stock's machine edit `0x400973b4` does. The whole-Part apply `0x40009094` (1,492 B, parameters only) snaps in-flight slides on every track. At a pattern switch the engine runs the light apply `0x40009e00`: Part-wide bytes (the engine's bank / Part `0x80001828/29`, scene table, UI block) and, per track, only the LFO setup and only with LFO AUTO CHANGE (`0x80000050`) on; every other new setting reaches a voice at its next trig. `[emu]` (every byte compared)

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
facts.text: Sequencer tick `0x400a1eea` (IPL 2): phase D `0x400a1f72`, E builds one step ahead (`0x400a2d7e` audio, `0x400a39c6` MIDI), F `0x400a3ca4`, G master `0x400a3f94`; master step `0x800065b2`, master tick `0x800065b6`; change gate `0x400a42fa`. The wrap body `0x400a43a0` commits a pending pattern whenever one is set and then runs the full switch, whose COND_RESET(-1) call is at `0x400a4850`. A:B pass counters `0x46107918[t]`. `[emu]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
facts.text: Stock switch timing (measured tick by tick): the new pattern's first step still runs at the outgoing master rate (`SCALE_IX` `0x8000663d` follows a step later); track reload counters stay 0 until the new pattern's first master wrap; MASTER_STEP reads 0 during the last audible step of the master cycle. An A:B pass starts at each track's own wrap (`0x400a536c`) and at the master restart, once when both coincide; FIRST trigs fire only in pass 1. `[emu]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
facts.text: Landing a track in phase: land one tick before the boundary with the first-fire bit (`0x80006624`) and reload `0x800065d3[t]` = tps - 2, and cancel the old boundary event a full tick ahead. Landing on the boundary tick itself left the old step in place now and then on the unit, because the sample clock and the old event's time are a frame apart there; the emulator's exact clock never showed it (I120, A70). Clocks: audio `0x4610757c` (127,008,000 a second; a tick at 120 BPM is `0x285ff0`, ~21 ms), MIDI `0x46107564` (a tick 16,800). The sequencer runs about a tick ahead of the audio; the engine places events 16 to a frame. `[hw]` (landing) / `[emu]` (values)

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
facts.text: SILENCE TRACKS is `0x8000004f` (setter `0x40065a96`, battery copy `0x100b14af`; per-track START SILENT at track record `+3`, -1 = the project's). At a pattern switch the engine hard-kills each silenced voice (`0x40006820`, from the loop at `0x4000d446`) instead of using the declicked note-off `0x40008f84(t)`. On stock a trig on the new pattern's step 0 restarts the voice in the same frame and hides the cut; a DIRECT JUMP landing mid-pattern popped on an MKI until the jump released the silenced tracks with the note-off a tick before the switch (V7.2.2, 2026-11-15, I119). Stock probably pops the same way when a ringing silenced track has no trig on step 0 (H32). `[hw]` (pop, fix) / `[emu]` (mechanism, ot_emu render)

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
facts.text: Bank files on the card: chunk lengths are exact (error -51) and a 16-bit checksum covers every byte (-54), so there is no spare byte for mod data; keep it in a sidecar file in the project folder (Clyps' `clypsNN.work/.strd`, 2,568 B per bank, survived SAVE / RELOAD, EXPORT TO SET and DELETE PROJECT on an MKI with hooks at `0x400914de` and `0x4008ed5e`). Direct seek, checked on 816 real files (versions 0x14-0x17): PTRN n at `0x16 + st*n` (st = `0x8eec` from version 0x17, `0x8ee8` before), PART p at `0x16 + 16*st + 0x18bb*p`; OctaLib's table fits 0x17 only. A `.strd` holds 16 PTRN, 4 working PART and 4 SAVE PART chunks. Stock's buffered seek `0x4001660c` keeps a partly read buffer and the parser then finds no tag: seek the filesystem (`0x46c8243e`) to the block and drain the rest. `[doc]` / `[hw]` (sidecar)

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
facts.text: Battery mirror: the UI bank's slabs are mirrored at `0x1001614e` (MIDI part `0x1001aa1e`), its Parts at `0x100a4ece`; that is what returns after a power cycle. Stock's `0x4000faf0` writes a whole bank (~620 KB) there; writing only changed records cut a one-track load from 36,568 to 2,466 B. `[emu]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
facts.text: Key layers: push `0x40031494`, pop `0x4003146c`, head `0x460d165c`; the last layer that lists a key wins (`-1` passes down, `0` swallows), but a key's sub-maps chain across layers (rebuild `0x4003125c`), so stock's FUNC sub-map `0x400bfa1e` still links above yours, and encoder records are copied as they are (no `-1` pass-down). A key held across a rebuild keeps its old handlers (`0x400312e2`). Copy T1's hold delay / repeat (`0x400bfc10`) into every key record you override: a key pressed under one layer and released under another with a different delay leaves its timer in the repeat list `0x460d1660`, and the UI task hangs at its next press. Held flags `0x46c7d8ee + code*24` ([FUNC] `0x2d` at `0x46c7dd26`); TRACK keys select on release; a double tap is a second press while `0x460d5de0` <= 14. Codes: UP `0x33`, DOWN `0x20`, LEFT `0x34`, RIGHT `0x21`, [PAGE] `0x1b`, [CUE] `0x2a`, PLAYBACK..FX2 `0x22..0x26`. `[emu]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
facts.text: Windows: `0x4005829c(w, h, dx, dy, prio, close_cb)` has five slots; opening priority P closes every window of priority >= P (toasts and SELECT 10, name editor 5, menus 3, project lists 2, Parts menu 1), and close_cb is never cleared. Window `+32` bit 0 is "visible" (the compositor `0x40013ad8` skips it), bit 5 "linked"; the manager finds a free slot by the linked bit, so hide a window by its visible bit, never by unlinking it (I121). Toast font `0x400ba862` (widths `0x400c205c`; a toast line holds 113 px), interface font `0x400ba876` (3x5 glyphs, 4 px advance, widths `0x400c246a`). `[hw]` / `[emu]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
facts.text: Track tabs and LEDs: three routines paint the main screen's track tabs on every UI pass, each with its own active-track test (`mvzb 0x80000000`): `0x4004bd48` (lower half), `0x4003fed8` (upper half) and `0x40044804` (a `!`-shaped status mark); they repaint only tabs whose cached state changed (side caches `0x400c0c50` / `0x400c0c94`). Redirecting fewer than all three gave half tabs and a stray `!` on a unit (I122). Trig LED buffer `0x460ba98c` (trig n = red die 2n, green 2n+1; stock dims to 7), LED layer table `0x460e7628`, push `0x4007e760`, pop `0x4007e81c`. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
facts.text: ColdFire build traps (KYOTI): a duplicate `.equ` lets the last one win without a warning (cost one flash round on a unit); hooks placed mid-function must save d0-d7/a0-a6 and replay the displaced instruction last, because stock branches on its flags; `-mcpu=5407` refuses cmpi to memory, `not.b`, `exg`, `cmpa.w`, movem with `-(sp)` / `(sp)+` and d16 offsets past 32767. The OS VERSION string holds 10 characters and the card `.bin` is ELUP-obfuscated, so check the name in the `.syx` (I124). `[hw]` / `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / KYOTI V1.8, Clyps and DIRECT JUMP V7.3 (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-13/16)
facts.text: Sample pool: KYOTI V1.8 (RELOAD + DIRECT JUMP) takes 11 pages, V1.8C and the CLYPS image 1,709 pages (~10 MB) of the 6 KB pages from the arena start `0x40a955e0`; the MEMORY page still reads 85.5 MB. A track-record copy (`0x40020898`) takes ~15-25 µs. `[doc]` {kyoti-1117}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam stock reading: save path, Parts, key layers, one-shot mask (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-16/18)
facts.text: One-shot trig mask: byte 40 of an audio track record in the bank file (RAM: `bank + pattern*0x8ed8 + 31 + 0x91a*k`, i.e. track record `+0x1f`) is the low byte of the track's one-shot trig mask, bit 0 = step 1 ... bit 7 = step 8. With the step layout of the other masks (byte 7 - s/8) this puts the one-shot mask at `+0x18..0x1f` (inferred). A test project with no one-shots on steps 1-8 reads it as zero, which is how PATTERN MUTE mistook it for spare (I146, O32). `[hw]` (MKI over REMOTE) / `[emu]` {octabam-pmute-1118}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam stock reading: save path, Parts, key layers, one-shot mask (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-16/18)
facts.text: Stock mute state: one per project, bits 8-15 of `0x80000008` for the audio tracks (FUNC+Tn toggles bit 8+n-1). The 22-byte state block at `0x80000000` is mirrored in battery RAM at `0x100b14cc` and restored at boot and by the new-project reset (`0x40025a90`); the power-up sanitiser is `0x4000fe20`. Byte `0x80000011` / `0x100b14dd` is referenced by nothing in the image (octabam uses bit 0 for its layer). A boot with empty battery RAM zeroes `0x100b14dc..df`; a boot with valid RAM writes nothing there. `[emu]` {octabam-pmute-1118}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam stock reading: save path, Parts, key layers, one-shot mask (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-16/18)
facts.text: FUNC press: FUNC's press records sit at `0x400bfc12` (MKI) and `0x400c01f6` (MKII) key tables; its handler gets edge 1 on each press, and stock's double-press filter `0x40040250` (edge 3) does not run for FUNC. facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam stock reading: save path, Parts, key layers, one-shot mask (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-16/18)
facts.text: SAVE PROJECT path: PROJECT > SAVE is row action `0x40063890`; `0x400255ec` tests whether the project is on the card (if not: SAVE TO NEW `0x40063618`, name keyboard), then a YES/NO popup. YES `0x40063c54` stops the sequencer (`0x400a10c8`) and `0x40022850` posts a static record `{17, 0x400232bc, 0x40022e80, 0x40022dc4}` to the engine queue. Engine job 17 (`0x40085736`) opens the progress window via the sys task (event 43), runs the bank write `0x400919e4` and the project store `0x4008ee74` on the engine task, then `0x40022e80` closes the window with DONE! or stock's error text. 16 banks take over 6 s of emulated card time. `[emu]` {octabam-1118}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam stock reading: save path, Parts, key layers, one-shot mask (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-16/18)
facts.text: Engine job 21 is not an engine job: `{21, fn}` on the engine queue (`0x40085ab6`) posts event 43 to the sys queue `0x460d17ae`, and `0x40062454` runs `fn(1)` on the sys task, which also handles the panel keys; a long file write there freezes every key. facts.text: Who holds the keys: with nothing open the key-layer list holds only the base layer (`0x400c090a` MKI, `0x400c091e` MKII). Pushed layers: MAIN MENU `0x400cbf2c`, YES/NO popup `0x400cdff8`, MIXER `0x400d0384`, TEMPO `0x400bb4ec`, PART window `0x400b9b24` and its menu `0x400ce0c4`, name keyboard `0x400d071c`, progress window `0x400d0bc4`, FUNC sub-map `0x400bfa32`, a page key `0x400bab6e`, a trig held in grid recording `0x400bee74`; SETUP windows SRC `0x400bb7b4`, LFO `0x400bbd22`, AMP `0x400bb960`, FX1 `0x400bc246`, FX2 `0x400bc470`. facts.text: PART window: cursor `0x460d10c8` is a cross (UP Part 1, RIGHT 2, DOWN 3, LEFT 4); YES selects and closes. FUNC + BANK over it opens a four-row edit menu: RENAME, RELOAD `0x4002dd50`, SAVE `0x4002dd0c`, SAVE ALL `0x4002dcd0` (labels `0x400b9b14`, callbacks `0x400b9b04`). facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk findings: stock delay cost, machine prices, card upgrades (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-17/18)
facts.text: Stock delay routine cost: `0x400031a0` runs once a frame for all eight tracks, whatever their FX2 and however silent: 44.9 µs of the 362.8 µs frame (12.4 % of the ColdFire), stopped or playing. About 43 µs is eDMA (two tap reads and one ring write per track) and waiting for it; the filter and mix are 1.6 µs. Each track has a 68-byte state record; the delay time is at `+0x2c`. `[hw]` (MKII)

facts.text: The Part validator `0x40002318` caps the recorder's LOOP (Part + `0x607` + 12t) at 1 (`0x40002cd2`) and SRC3 (+ `0x606` + 12t) at 10 (`0x40002cb2`), and forces XVOL (+ `0x125` + `0x18`t) to 127 (`0x40002d24`). The bank read `0x4008cea0` calls it and ignores the result, but the battery restore `0x40025770` treats a correction as failure: a bad XVOL gives BANK UNAVAILABLE (flag `0x4017d516 + bank*0x9b340`, read at `0x4007b2fc`). A mod value outside the stock range is silently reset on load and can cost the bank at power-up (rule A60). `[emu]`

Row type byte 0 pattern, 1 LOOP/JUMP/HALT, 2 REM; byte 3 the target, byte 2 the count (0-64); targets read unsigned. Arrangement number `0x100b14d1`, changed bits `0x1001614c` (the bank bit `0x100b14ce` is a different one). Clipboard `0x461078ec` (valid flag `0x461078e8`), undo row `0x46107902`. facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk findings: frame guard budget, claim refusals, field records (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-18/19)
facts.text: Frame guard budget (USB bases): the whole frame interrupt gets 80 % of a 363 µs frame (about 290 µs); stock playback and the other tracks spend that time too, and a track can get two render calls in one frame. When the predicted total passes the share plus saved credit, the guard renders silence for a machine track instead. The guard's skip count and track mask add up since boot, so measure a run by the difference of two reads. A release base logs a `shed` incident at most once every ten minutes (its value: skip count in the low 24 bits, tracks in the high 8), so a short run without a new incident can still have skipped. `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk findings: frame guard budget, claim refusals, field records (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-18/19)
facts.text: A "module memory" refusal can be a DSP claim meeting a delay buffer: SC Ringmod 0.2.1 claims Y `$7E00-$7FFF` on both cores (the key bus) and Y `$33DFE-$33FFF` in the shared window. The base checks claims against live and planned delay buffers and counts a module effect's whole 16,384-word FX2 block, so a module effect on FX2 of T1 or T5 (block at Y `$4000`) or T7 (shared window) meets the claims; the refusal said "module memory" (loader refusal 2). In the module pool the set used 161,344 of 786,432 bytes. Seen on a unit on base 0.7.8 (refusals began when Air Chorus sat on T5 FX2); the same may explain I129, whose records do not line up, so that stays unconfirmed. Base 0.7.10 is to give it its own code (12, "meets a buffer") and count reviewed buffer extents for E-Verb, Mini Verb, BBD Delay and Vibrato. `[hw]` (field log) / `[emu]`

facts.text: Key-bus buffer refusal has its own code (base 0.7.10): a DSP claim that meets a live or planned slot buffer is refused as `RUNTIME_BUFFER` (12), no longer as "module memory" (`RUNTIME_MEMORY`, 2), and the unit's log says which check refused a module at start and how much module memory was in use. So a key-bus reader (SC Ringmod) is refused only beside a module effect on FX2 of T1, T5 or T7 whose buffer reaches the bus. facts.text: USB Audio moves out of the base (base 0.7.12, USB Audio 0.3.0-experimental): until 0.7.11 each of six layouts and USB MIDI alone was a separate base, because the layout set the configuration descriptors, and every base kept a fixed reserve (8 KiB code, 2.5 KiB data, 96 KiB bss). Now a package contributes one USB function (1-4 interfaces on endpoint 3, the only endpoint left; four descriptor blocks in 512-byte slots). When the function changes, the base waits for EP0 to idle, leaves the bus for half a second, rewrites the configurations and comes back; the host then has 20 s to reach the vendor interface before the trial counts as unplugged. The 0.3.0 package holds 10,288 B of image and 94,152 B of bss from the 768 KiB module pool. `[hw]` / `[doc]`

facts.text: USB stock sites the base raises hooks from: the USB interrupt's transfer path (shim at `0x4001e606`), bus reset and session end (`0x4001e91c`, `0x4001e952`), stock's unknown-request tail before it stalls (`0x4001de64`, SETUP packet at `0x46c8ce08`), and the audio producer in the frame interrupt, every 16-sample block, at `0x4000d9a0` before stock clears `0x46104d4e`. facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam: DARK REV stall narrowed, window placement, DSP audit (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-19/22)
facts.text: The DARK REV stall needs MODULATION loaded: with MODULATION loaded and DARK REV picked, 5 of 7 runs stalled with DARK REV on 8 tracks, 1 of 6 on 4 tracks, 0 of 2 on 1 track; with SPECTRUM loaded instead, 0 in 25 cycles; a stock-effects image without the demand loader, 0 in 60 STARTs. Which core runs DARK REV made no clear difference. Cause still open: octabam's loader or a race that the ColdFire's load exposes. `[hw]` (MKII, [I170](../INCIDENTS.md#i170-dark-rev-picked-on-all-eight-tracks-while-modulation-was-loaded-stopped-the-dsp-octabam-build-05))

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam: DARK REV stall narrowed, window placement, DSP audit (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-19/22)
facts.text: What a START frame looks like: every START gave one frame interrupt of about 505 µs (normal frames about 362 µs). In a stall one frame is then skipped (a 726 µs gap) and the DSP count freezes 5-6 frames later. The ColdFire frame interrupt is driven by the DSP and stops with it (this corrects an earlier note that it kept running). `[hw]`

facts.text: KEYBUS words: X:`$37F60` + track (0-7) holds the peak of |(L+R)/2| over the track's 16-frame block; X:`$37F68` + track the mean of (L²+R²)/2. facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk findings: base 0.7.13 in the field, Grain 0.1.2, stock delay timing (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-22)
facts.text: Stock's delay routine delays the next frame: it runs from the eDMA interrupt with the mask lowered to IPL 5 (`0x40004b0e`), and the chain's last state unmasks the frame interrupt (`0x40004bc2`). Its time therefore pushes back the next frame interrupt. Code in that path can see a late call from the free-running DTIM3 count (`0xfc07c00c`, 132 MHz) without help from a base. `[doc]` (code reading) {modwerk-1123}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk findings: base 0.7.13 in the field, Grain 0.1.2, stock delay timing (OS 1.40C, 2026-11-22)
facts.text: Resting detours of table modules stayed patched: Modwerk's tables route (`--octabam-tables`, Mute Modes' route) dropped the `"rests"` list of a module's `runtime.json`. The detours stayed patched while the module rested and kept their frame cost. Fixed 2026-11-22; every published package rebuilt byte for byte. Tape Echo is the first DSP effect to ship detours that rest. `[doc]` {modwerk-1123}

facts.section: Syntakt / Recovery (SyntHack OS `RECOVERY.md`)
facts.text: Mod data written for defaults slows project load and save (Synfact, OS 1.41): a user saw a project load slowly when switched to from another project and save more slowly than usual; a reboot straight into it loaded normally. The export was valid. The ARP mod wrote and sealed a 320-byte carrier for every kit even with default settings, so load checked all 1,664 bindings; leaving default carriers absent cut the emulated serialization from 24.8 M to 4.8 M instructions (81 % fewer). The slowness is a user report; the cost is `[emu]`, the wall-clock gain not yet measured. `[doc]` {synfact-lifecycle} ([I50](../INCIDENTS.md#i50-mod-data-written-for-default-settings-slowed-project-load-and-save))
