facts.section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.41 static-analysis facts (Humgic/syntakt-machine45-research - README and handoff dated 2026-10-28; no hardware run, no firmware)
facts.text: Address rule `VA = file offset + 0x40000400`; ColdFire big-endian (ISA-C/EMAC). MAIN is 3,438,480 bytes, section 7 is 383,760 bytes. `[doc]` {machine45-handoff}

facts.section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.41 static-analysis facts (Humgic/syntakt-machine45-research - README and handoff dated 2026-10-28; no hardware run, no firmware)
facts.text: Stock public Machine IDs are 0-44, stored as a BYTE in each track's machine payload (`P[t]+0xA2`); runtime records `R[t] = model + 0x6C + 0x3C0*t`, `P[t] = *(R[t]+0x10)`; the setter is at `0x40025594` (store at `0x40025620`). 505 parameter descriptors of 52 bytes; only MAIN digital tracks 0-7. `[doc]` {machine45-handoff}

facts.section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.41 static-analysis facts (Humgic/syntakt-machine45-research - README and handoff dated 2026-10-28; no hardware run, no firmware)
facts.text: Section 7 selector: a signed BYTE with a 46-entry map (negative -> 0, 0-45 kept, above 45 clamped to 45); stock maps 0-7 to the same-numbered engine family and 36->8, 37->9, 38->10, 44->11, everything else (incl. 45) to family 0. Stock tables: render pointers `0x400148F0` (12 entries), prep pointers `0x40014920`, the 46-byte map at `0x40014950`. A compact handoff moves MAIN `[0x80002000,0x800021B0)` through a 27x16-byte eDMA transfer (TCD47, channel 47); each track then receives a 20-byte copy into `T[t] = 0x80003C40 + 0x8E*t`. Dslot is 8 x `0x708` = 14,400 bytes. `[doc]` {machine45-handoff}

facts.section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.41 static-analysis facts (Humgic/syntakt-machine45-research - README and handoff dated 2026-10-28; no hardware run, no firmware)
facts.text: Persistence confirmed statically: the current-kit Sound-v7 save/load keeps the machine byte (raw 0-45 and 255 retained, 46-254 map to 0); Pattern-v11 stores the byte at row `+0x2EC` and its restoration is not closed; Sound locks, p-locks, held trigs, migration, clipboard and undo not qualified. facts.text: Open: safe executable storage for native DSP on "CPU 2" (the loader boundary is unresolved); composition with SY FM4 (engine 4, A-table entry overlap) and other descriptor mods; resource IDs 254-261 are unclaimed in the registry but have MIDI CCs, 505+ have no native allocation. `[doc]` {machine45-handoff}

facts.section: Syntakt / Platform: two ColdFires, an FPGA, an analog mixer (SyntHack OS docs, OS 1.41)
facts.text: Two ColdFire MCF5441x (V4, EMAC, no FPU, ~250 MHz, so 166,667 cycles per 32-sample block), with 64 KB SRAM at `0x80000000`. RAM shared between the CPUs is at `0x10000000`. `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Platform: two ColdFires, an FPGA, an analog mixer (SyntHack OS docs, OS 1.41)
facts.text: Sections of OS 1.41, stored in the order 5, 2, 1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8: | Section | Content | Size | Note | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | FPGA bitstream | 149,516 B | never touch | | 2 | bootstrap with the STARTUP menu | 30,782 B | never touch | | 3 | MAIN OS for CPU #1, at `0x40000400` | 3,438,480 B | patched by mods | | 4 | updater | 32,776 B | raw; never touch | | 5 | meta | | | | 6 | ColdFire boot stub | 1,744 B | raw; never touch | | 7 | voice engine for CPU #2, at `0x40000400`, entry `0x40001070` | 383,760 B | raw; patchable | | 8 | the shared ARM Cortex-M image (not a second FPGA; CONFLICTS S15) | 159,948 B | identical in size to the DT1/DN2/Rytm/A4 image whose hash is known | Stock 1.41 SHA-256: `8e2488f4...b9ed19e`.

facts.section: Syntakt / Platform: two ColdFires, an FPGA, an analog mixer (SyntHack OS docs, OS 1.41)
facts.text: Signing conflict `[?]`: SyntHack describes an HMAC-SHA256 over the container for 1.41, with the key derived from the image. digikit found no HMAC trailer in 1.42 (the last 32 bytes are zero). Check the trailer of your own file before you decide.

facts.section: Syntakt / Platform: two ColdFires, an FPGA, an analog mixer (SyntHack OS docs, OS 1.41)
facts.text: Boot unpack limit: the bootstrap loads compressed section 3 at `0x40200000` and unpacks it to `0x40000400`. The margin (decompressed minus compressed) must stay below ~`0x1FFC00` at every point of the stream. Stock 1.41 has a margin of +99,938 B. A build padded with zeros to `0x40350000` (-8,751 B) did not boot, tested twice and hung on the logo. Zero padding is the worst case; already-compressed payloads raise the margin. SyntHack refuses builds under 4 KB of margin. `[hw]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Platform: two ColdFires, an FPGA, an analog mixer (SyntHack OS docs, OS 1.41)
facts.text: The Syntakt accepts rebuilt images (recompressed section 3) over USB and DIN. `[hw]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Memory map of CPU #1 (OS 1.41)
facts.text: Hardware lesson `[hw]`: SyntHack up to v0.8.0 kept mod code at `0x46000000`. Projects with SP TWINSHOT samples then crashed at boot. Since v0.8.1 the mod code (compressed, appended to section 3 at `0x40348000`) is unpacked into a 64 KB block that a hook at the end of heap init (`0x4010358E`) reserves first. ([I20](../INCIDENTS.md#i20-mod-code-at-a-free-address-crashed-projects-with-certain-samples))

facts.section: Syntakt / Memory map of CPU #1 (OS 1.41)
facts.text: Conflict to watch `[?]`: SY FM4 (OS 1.40A) copies its code to `0x47000000`, which it describes as "above the BSS end, below the stack, addressed by nothing". That is the region SyntHack found to be overwritten by sample loading on 1.41. Treat any use of RAM above the BSS as unsafe until it is tested with sample-heavy projects. Synfact's reading (2026-11-17) puts `0x47000000` inside the stock sample blob's span (`0x4584f2c5-0x4759b3c5` with all 64 slots full). `[emu]` {synfact-1118}

facts.section: Syntakt / Memory map of CPU #1 (OS 1.41)
facts.text: Boot: entry `0x400004E8`; static constructors loop `0x40082500` (136 entries); the intro animation task `0x40087E6A` gates boot, so never make the intro longer. Screen: 128x64 1 bpp, column-major, double buffer at `0x402D6DC4`/`0x402D6DC0`; frame loop `0x4000A0E6` redraws when `*(0x444E1334)+96` is set. `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Audio path
facts.text: CPU #2 (section 7): all work runs in the audio interrupt `0x40000934` (vector 96, DMA timer 0 capture). Per block it copies `0x1B0` bytes of parameters from shared RAM and renders 8 digital voices (`0x40004324`). It returns 8 x 32 int32 over eDMA channel 47 and does no mixing. 12 engines: tables at `0x400148F0` (render), `0x40014920` (update), `0x40014950` (machine id -> engine). Order: BD MODERN, SD BASIC, CY ALLOY, PC CARBON, SY TONE, SY CHORD, SD VINTAGE, CP VINTAGE, SY TOY, SY BITS, SY SWARM, SP TWINSHOT. SY CHORD reads a 512 x int32 wave at `0x4001A300`. `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Audio path
facts.text: CPU #1 (section 3): the per-block routine `0x400A3856` runs CV/gain, ADC deinterleave, then master/FX `0x4008F1CA`. Delay `0x40096890` and reverb `0x40096E3C` are the same code as on the Digitakt mk1. Buffers: digital tracks from CPU #2 at `0x80003D50`. ADC channels at `0x80003950`: 0-3 analog tracks, 4-5 external in, 6-7 the FX-track bus. USB/Overbridge: 20 channels per frame at `0x80004760`. The final mix is analog: digital buses go out through DACs into an analog mixer, with nothing digital after them. 40 control voltages go out over DSPI1 with eDMA channel 15; CV 35/36 are the FX-track bus VCAs. `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Audio path
facts.text: CPU #1 load: ~89 % at rest (sequencer stopped), measured on the device with DTIM0 (`0xFC07000C`) at interrupt entry and exit. The UI gets the rest, so a few thousand instructions per block make the UI lag. `[hw]` SY FM4 reports its main-CPU render at 85.8k of 166.7k cycles per block (stock 85.0k). That is a different span of the same interrupt. `[?]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Audio path
facts.text: Digital filter and amp run on CPU #2; the cutoff is computed on CPU #1. Analog voices and the FX track drive a hardware envelope generator with 20-bit rate codes. Measured curves: the digital biquad f0 = 4.918 Hz x e^(0.0655 x FREQ); the analog filter f = 14.645 Hz x e^(0.0574 x FREQ). Tempo is at `0x402D7010` (BPM x 120). `[hw]` (analog curves measured)

facts.section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
facts.text: Section 7 is byte-identical in 1.41 and 1.42 (SHA-256 `daf6451c...783bc2`). It is ColdFire ISA-C with EMAC, MCF5441x-class: compile with `-mcpu=54418`, disassemble with `-m m68k:isa-c:emac`. CPU #2 has its own 128 MB SDRAM at `0x40000000` (SP `0x48000000`, entry `0x40001070`). `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
facts.text: Only 39.8 KB is code (`0x40000404-0x40009f88`: boot, audio interrupt, voice loop, 12 engines, sample loader), followed by 284 KB of tables and data. Code room for mods is almost nil: ~318 bytes in small pieces remained after SynCrackd's images.

facts.section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
facts.text: CPU #2 configures its own FPGA: a packed bitstream at `0x40041060` is unpacked to `0x40042000` (54,664 bytes) at init. That is the same size as the Analog Heat +FX FPGA section, so it may be the same part `[?]`. Keep away from it (rule A22).

facts.section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
facts.text: The sample pool is in CPU #2's RAM: 64 MB from `0x4004f750`, in BSS zeroed at boot. A 64-entry slot table `{u32 frames, u32 pointer}` is at `0x4404f754`. Format: 64 times `u32 frames` + big-endian int16 mono. The main CPU fills it at boot in 2 KB chunks through the shared window `0x800`, with an unchecked 16-bit index. This is the slow boot the manual mentions. Per slot at most 524,287 frames (10.9 s; positions are 20.12 fixed point). The stock UI limits slots to 5 s and "32 MB".

facts.section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
facts.text: Above the BSS, `0x4404f980-0x48000000` (63.7 MB) is not referenced by any section-7 instruction and is used for SynCrackd's state. Leave the top megabyte for the stack (its depth is not measured). This is CPU #2's RAM, not the main CPU's region that sample loading overwrites (CONFLICTS O2). `[hw]` (alpha, one unit)

facts.section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
facts.text: Shared window (CPU #2 `0x0-0x1000` = main CPU `0x10000000`, chip select 0, 16-bit, one wait state): `0x000-0x1b0`: the parameter block, copied to `0x80008000` every block; `0x1b0-0x5b0`: 8 mono track buffers, sent by eDMA 47; `0x5b0-0x800`: unused by stock; `0x800-0x1000`: the sample chunk at boot.

facts.section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
facts.text: SRAM `0x80000000`: 8 voices of 1,800 B, 8 mono int32 output buffers, 8 parameter blocks of 142 B. The highest static reference is `0x8000f670`, so treat SRAM as full.

facts.section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
facts.text: Twinshot (engine 11, machine type 44) reads the parameter slots 18-25: TUN1, SMP1, FLT1, MIX, TUN2, SMP2, loop flag, DEC1. A sample select below the centre plays the slot in reverse. `[emu]`

facts.section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
facts.text: SynCrackd replaces Twinshot (and CY ALLOY) with a 64-slot stereo sampler, loops, slices, time stretch and transient triggers. It is OS 1.42 only, alpha, tested in emulation and on one unit, MIT.

facts.section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
facts.text: Synfact (OS 1.41; source builds on 1.42 from core 2.0, 2026-11-17) adds DT mk1 sample machines, a per-project pool, polyphony across tracks and a third LFO. It ships its firmware change as a zlib-compressed XOR mask against the official file, pinned by hash. It needs a second mods file (515,808 B) sent with its own transfer tool after the flash. Boot is confirmed on a unit (core 1.4 and 1.7.2, 2026-11-09); the safe-boot rollback is not yet tested on hardware. `[hw]` {synfact} {synfact-core}

facts.section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
facts.text: Each change is stored with the SHA-256 of the original bytes, so a different OS version fails the build instead of crashing. Every mod runs in a Unicorn emulator next to the original code before flashing. Stock Unicorn gets signed fractional EMAC wrong (the audio comes out silent), so EMAC instructions are trapped and executed in Python from the NXP manual. Use CPU model "ANY" (the code needs FF1, MVS/MVZ, SATS).

facts.section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
facts.text: Hooks: replace at least 6 bytes with `jsr` plus `nop` padding, and the trampoline replays the replaced instructions. Save every register; replay replaced EMAC instructions first. If your code uses EMAC, set MACSR yourself and leave ACC0 at 0, because the OS sum routines start from it. One-time setup goes in a hook in the page initializer (`0x401885D2...`), never in boot time.

facts.section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
facts.text: Mod code: gcc/as with `-mcpu=54418`, no `.bss` (put variables in `.data`), no libgcc (`nm -u` empty). ColdFire limits: `muls.l` takes no absolute address, there is no `exg`, `movem` takes only `(An)`/`d16(An)`, short branches reach ±127 B.

facts.section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
facts.text: Spare storage the OS saves without knowing: per track: engine word +106 (hidden id 72); per kit: unused words of the pattern kit at `*0x800030BC` (ids 0, 0x1A, 0x24, 0x27, 0x29, 0x2A, 0x37, 0x46, 0x38). Store values XOR their default, so old projects load with defaults; kit words 41-43 of the 12 per-track kit blocks (Digitakt MIDI-track data, unused here); 256 bytes in the project settings file. A "free" parameter id can be an alias the OS shows in some modes, so audit it.

facts.section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
facts.text: UI internals: parameter descriptors at `0x4022D59C + 52*id`; page objects at `0x41B9F3C8` (44 B, 8 slots); per-parameter `std::function` objects at `0x41B9FA24 + 84*id` (+20 text, +36 icon, +68 style). Page 25 ("OB8") is a free Digitakt leftover. Rewrite a `std::function` only from UI code, never from the audio interrupt.

facts.section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
facts.text: Audio mods: Hook the mix function; keep the OS's EMAC `msac` sign convention (the result is -Σ g·x). Do nothing when there is nothing to do. Compute at 24 kHz where the sound allows it. Ramps must snap to their target or the effect never goes idle. Limit how far a modulated delay moves per block. Keep a cost-per-block regression test (count instructions with `UC_HOOK_CODE` after `ctl_flush_tb()`).

facts.section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
facts.text: Where mod code lives at run time (SyntHack modarea, v0.8.1+): The OS image has only ~2 KB free, and everything after it is zeroed at boot. So mod code is appended to section 3 compressed (SHLZ, at `0x40348000 + offset`). At boot it is unpacked into the first 64 KB block of the OS heap: buddy allocator `0x4010350C`, 16 MB pool at `0x444E38C0`. The block is reserved by a call right after heap initialization, so it always gets index 0, and the OS never hands it out again. The earlier home above the BSS (`0x46000000`) was overwritten whenever samples loaded (SyntHack issue 4), which settles conflict O2. `[hw]` {synthack-mods}

facts.section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
facts.text: Kit and project storage that round-trips through stock code (SyntHack kitstore/projstore): Kit words 41-43 of the 12 per-track blocks go into 6 file bytes that stock's writer zeroes and its reader ignores. 256 bytes go into the project settings block (`+0x227..+0x3FF` is zeroed by the writer and ignored by the reader), behind an `SH` marker. Tests run the real writer and reader with and without the hooks. Zero must mean "default", because stock-saved files load as zero. `[emu]` {synthack-mods}

facts.section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
facts.text: Controlling the analog side digitally (SyntHack master-comp): a feed-forward compressor detects on ADC 6/7 (the FX-track bus before its VCAs) and applies gain through those VCAs' control voltages (CV 35/36), once per block (~1.5 kHz). Its UI uses the Digitakt MIDI-track "CC Select" ids 262-268, which the Syntakt never uses. Cost: ~100 instructions per block when off, ~600 when on. Checked on the device (v0.9). `[hw]` {synthack-mods}

facts.section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
facts.text: Projects: SyntHack OS (9 mods on hardware, MIT); SY FM4 (4-operator FM replacing SY TONE, which also patches CPU #2); Syntakt Firmware Workbench. The Workbench replaces SY CHORD's waves: 31 slots of 257 big-endian Q31 samples, measured on a unit within 1 %. It adds a Deja Vu LFO, DV-H. It refuses any file but 1.41 and checks that only the declared regions changed. `[hw]` {syntakt-workbench}

facts.section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.42 container and CPUs (digikit finding 70, static reading, 2026-10) `[doc]`
facts.text: `Syntakt_OS1.42.syx`: ELE3, 2,029,486 bytes, META stamp 2026-09-30 (same day as DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12), SHA-256 `ded3c59f...7f37c1`; SysEx transport id `0x16`, OS-stream byte `0x11`; same packing codec as DT2/DN2; per-packet checksum constant K = 0x11. `[doc]` {digikit-f70}

facts.section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.42 container and CPUs (digikit finding 70, static reading, 2026-10) `[doc]`
facts.text: No HMAC trailer - the Syntakt OS file is not signed (no SHA-256 constants in sections 2-4); only the content checksum applies. `[doc]` {digikit-f70} Correction 2026-11-18: there is no trailer slot at all; the container (2,029,392 bytes, the value in its length word) ends at the end of section 8 rounded up to 16, where DT2/DN2 add 32 bytes, and digikit's rebuild of the stock file matches it byte for byte. `[doc]` {digikit-st-1118}

facts.section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.42 container and CPUs (digikit finding 70, static reading, 2026-10) `[doc]`
facts.text: Sections: 5 META; 2 bootstrap (dest word `0x04000000`, ColdFire code at `0x8000xxxx`, 30,782 B); 1 present only on Syntakt: `0xFF` padding then a bitstream-like blob (149,516 B) - the FPGA configuration (~~the bootstrap configures a Xilinx-style FPGA via INIT_B/DONE; MAIN only reads a status word~~ corrected by digikit 2026-11-19: MAIN configures the FPGA from section 1, see the digikit-1121 section below {digikit-1121}); 3 MAIN at `0x40000400` (3,442,576 B, same reset path as DT2: entry `0x400004e8`, SP `0x48000000`); 4 UPDATER at `0x80000400` (32,768 raw); 6 present only on Syntakt (1,744 B; per digikit's newer reading the peer CPU's stage-1 loader, linked at SRAM `0x80000000` {digikit-st-1118}); 7 is not a SHARC stream here but a standalone ColdFire program linked at `0x40000400` (entry `0x40001070`, 383,760 B) driving a DSPI-like block at `0xFC05C000` - consistent with a second ColdFire that runs the digital machines `[?]`; 8 byte-identical to DT2/DN2's section 8. `[doc]` {digikit-f70}

facts.section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.42 container and CPUs (digikit finding 70, static reading, 2026-10) `[doc]`
facts.text: Peer link ("DSP boot"): a mailbox in the FlexBus window at `0x10000000` ("HO" hello / "NO" -> DSP_MEM error; `0xA5A5` at +4 for OK), a doorbell on GPIO PA bit 4, EPORT IRQ4 handshake, 2 KB chunks to `0x10000800`, DSPI2 with eDMA channel 29; status values WAIT, init fail, TIMEOUT, BUFSIZE, DSP_MEM, CF_MEM, OK; the OS shows "DSP BOOT FAILURE (TIMEOUT/CF/DSP/BUF)". Peer states include LOAD_OS, BOOT, RUNNING, UPLOAD_SAMPLES. `[doc]` {digikit-f70}

facts.section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.42 container and CPUs (digikit finding 70, static reading, 2026-10) `[doc]`
facts.text: ~~Only 27 of 172 digikit anchor rules hit on Syntakt 1.42~~ (withdrawn by digikit as not reproducible). New dry run 2026-11-18: 81 of 106 ColdFire anchor rules hit on 1.42 (controls DT2 1.17 225/225, DN2 1.12 180/180); misses are mostly view, window, `shared_ptr` string and USB functions. facts.text: digikit's scope rule, adopt it: never modify sections 1, 6 or 7 or the bootstrap (digikit's patchkit now refuses 1, 2, 4, 6, 7 and 8 {digikit-st-1118}), never reconfigure or emulate the FPGA (risk to the analog circuitry). `[doc]` {digikit-f70}

facts.text: Correction to earlier forum talk ("two ColdFires and an FPGA"): digikit's reading supports an FPGA and a second ColdFire program; SY FM4's "CPU #2" fits that.

facts.section: Syntakt / What the Syntakt shares with other boxes (merged from analog-emu's Syntakt port, OS 1.42, static plus emulator)
facts.text: The analog tracks reuse the Analog Rytm MKII's voice design. The voice control records have the Rytm MKII's format (command/depth word, start and target bytes, mode nibble, rate exponent and mantissa). The cymbal oscillator banks use the Rytm's scale (43.62 units per Hz) and load the Rytm's CH/CB CLASSIC values. So Rytm voice research applies here and back. `[doc]` (inferred from the shared formats)

facts.section: Syntakt / What the Syntakt shares with other boxes (merged from analog-emu's Syntakt port, OS 1.42, static plus emulator)
facts.text: Digital tracks: rendered on CPU #2, then handed over by mailbox and eDMA channel 47 to CPU #1, which mixes them and sends them to the SSI1 codec. This agrees with SyntHack's audio path above. `[emu]`

facts.section: Syntakt / What the Syntakt shares with other boxes (merged from analog-emu's Syntakt port, OS 1.42, static plus emulator)
facts.text: An emulator now boots 1.42 with both CPUs (analog-emu: stage 1 the main screen with a stand-in for CPU #2, stage 2 CPU #2 running for real). It is the only Syntakt 1.42 emulator in the catalogue; SyntHack's Unicorn harness targets 1.41. `[emu]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
facts.text: Bank store: two 8 MiB slots inside the old 16 MiB `/mods` reservation, metadata sectors at eMMC `0x02bffe00` and `0x033ffe00`; the legacy record at `0x03400000` is still read. `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
facts.text: Safe boot: a bank moves CANDIDATE -> TRYING (written before any bank code runs) -> GOOD, set once AUDIO and the sample pool are ready and 150 UI ticks (about 5 s) have passed; a crash or power-off before that boots the previous GOOD bank or stock machines. Each bank names an exact core contract, and the core checks the stock bytes that LFO3 and MODULATION SKIP patch before any initializer runs. `[doc]`, rollback `[?]` (not yet tested on hardware). The first trial crashed every boot (I62).

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
facts.text: Filter table: the stock base-width filter reads Q31 poles from `0x40040060` (508 poles, then a zero tail; indices up to 1023 are read). A mod window in that tail made BASE+WDTH of 128 or more read code as poles; core 1.7.2 bounds the index. `[hw]` (I63)

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
facts.text: Load: MAIN is about 88 % with a plain pattern and 91-92 % with three POLY voices; code fetched from DDR costs far more than its instruction count (I64). `[hw]` {synfact-chorus}

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
facts.text: Load after the MAIN optimisation (owner's unit, OS 1.41, stock pattern, 2026-11-13/14): a minimal bank (System Info + Modulation Skip) reads 81 % MAIN, the full bank 86 % before and 83 % after the optimisation release; about 2 points sat in LFO3's per-block callback, about 1 in the stereo audio callbacks. The meter rounds to whole percent; at 48 kHz and 32-sample blocks one MAIN point is about 6.7 µs per block. `[hw]` {synfact-main-opt}

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
facts.text: Appended boot storage is wiped at startup: on OS 1.41 the storage appended after the MAIN image is cleared and reused once the early resident copy is done, so code placed there is gone when the application runs; only the resident reserve (64 KiB in Synfact's core) is safe for code called after boot (I104). `[hw]` {synfact-main-opt}

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
facts.text: Stock track types: every stock digital track type has bit 6 clear; Synfact's machines use types 64-79, so a mod can tell that all tracks are stock from the type bytes alone. The MAIN audio interrupt calls the stock modulation routine `0x40097afc` for every track on every block (about 6,600 emulated instructions for the full body). `[doc]` / `[emu]` {synfact-main-opt}

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)

facts.section: Syntakt / SY SWARM read from the audio program (model27 notes/84, OS 1.42 section 7, same in 1.41, 2026-11-16)
facts.text: Engine 10 (SY SWARM): update `0x400092ec`, render `0x400096e8`. Seven sawtooths from band-limited tables, one per octave (`0x40006588` picks the table by note, `0x40006434` reads it with linear interpolation); a centre that SUB moves down 0, 1 or 2 octaves (its increment shifted right and its table picked again, nothing else), six detuned oscillators driven by six tables indexed by DET; ANIM is three slow sines (about 1, 2 and 5 Hz, `0x40006074`) that phase-modulate oscillator pairs in opposite directions; NMOD is a noise generator (`0x40003eb4`) that phase-modulates the six; MIX uses two gain tables; every oscillator gets a random phase at a trig. `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: sequencer, kit slots, views, mixer (OS 1.41, 2026-11-14/16)
facts.text: View manager (UI controller +`0x40`): list sentinel +`0x14`, tail +`0x18`, highest opaque node +`0x1c`; a node holds its view at +`0x8`; a view's closed flag is a byte at +`0x30`. facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: stock sample blob, OS 1.42 port (OS 1.41/1.42, 2026-11-17)
facts.text: Stock builds one sample blob in MAIN DDR at boot: the native builder (`0x400822bc` on 1.41, `0x40082334` on 1.42) reads each of the 64 stock slots through a temporary 512 KiB buffer and concatenates them at physical `0x4584f2c5` (used through the uncached alias `0x4d84f2c5`; same address on both OS versions): 64 `u32` frame counts, then 2 bytes per mono frame, no 64-byte SAMP header; an empty slot still takes its 4-byte count. With 64 five-second slots it is 30,720,256 bytes (29.30 MiB) and ends at `0x4759b3c5` (exclusive). The stock sender (`0x40082f90` on 1.42) then copies it in 2,048-byte pages through the mailbox at `0x10000800`; CPU #2 keeps its own copy. `[emu]` (Unicorn running each OS's own builder with file and heap stand-ins)

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: stock sample blob, OS 1.42 port (OS 1.41/1.42, 2026-11-17)
facts.text: So `0x45565490-0x48000000` is unsafe from about `0x4584f2c5` up: past 8,064,315 bytes of blob (84.000625 s of mono 48 kHz PCM16 in all, for example 17 five-second samples) it reaches `0x46000000`; in the reproduction the first overlapping write came from stock's memcpy (`0x40115f94` on 1.41, `0x40116158` on 1.42) while copying slot 17. This is the mechanism behind SyntHack's lesson at `0x46000000` (I20) and also covers SY FM4's `0x47000000`. Limiting each slot to 5 s does not keep it out. `[emu]` / `[hw]` (I145)

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: stock sample blob, OS 1.42 port (OS 1.41/1.42, 2026-11-17)
facts.text: CPU #2 reads the stock pool at `0x4004f750`: its receiver (`0x40000fba`) and descriptor parser (`0x40000d06`) use that base, unchanged from 1.41 to 1.42 (section 7 is identical). Synfact's 1.42 port first moved the base to `0x4004f7c8` by mistake; core 2.0.1 restores it. `[emu]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: stock sample blob, OS 1.42 port (OS 1.41/1.42, 2026-11-17)
facts.text: Stock per-slot limit as Synfact checks it: one sector per stock header, a SAMP header and at most 240,000 mono frames (5 s); a slot's on-disk body is at most 480,064 bytes (64-byte header plus PCM). All 64 full slots are 15,001 sender pages. `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: stock sample blob, OS 1.42 port (OS 1.41/1.42, 2026-11-17)
facts.text: Synfact core 2.0.1 streams instead: it no longer calls the stock builder; it plans the 64 slots from their headers and builds each sender page on demand from eMMC (byte-identical to the old blob), using 5,120 bytes of MAIN scratch freed by a task-only hook at `0x40083026` after the last mailbox copy. Waveform envelopes are read lazily (at most 4,096 PCM bytes per UI idle call); the cache is about 98 KiB for 128 entries, allocated on first use. The native heap is 16 MiB, too small for a 29.3 MiB blob anyway. Resident use: 65,116 of 65,536 bytes (420 free). `[emu]` (sender, page and parser code run in Unicorn); boot with 64 five-second samples `[hw]` (prototype, owner's unit)

Synfact found its 108 sites with masked byte-pattern contexts and then checked each one. Examples (1.41 -> 1.42): draw-all `0x401007ce` -> `0x40100992`; operator new `0x40103788` -> `0x4010394c`; menu item ctor `0x400fa688` -> `0x400fa84c`; menu add `0x400f9ebe` -> `0x400fa082`; app startup site `0x400826a6` -> `0x4008271e`; mixer call `0x400a4fce` -> `0x400a5046` (calls `0x4008f1ca` -> `0x4008f242`); modulation `0x40097afc` -> `0x40097b74`; LFO `0x40119266` -> `0x4011942a`; deferred view cleanup's clear `0x40100f2c` -> `0x401010f0`; trig preparation `0x4008b882` -> `0x4008b8fa`. facts.section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: How the peer CPU gets its program: MAIN reads ids 6 and 7 from the OS directory in NOR (`0x80000`, "ELE3", 16-byte entries from `0x80020`: id, offset, length) and streams them at every boot over DSPI2 (`0xEC038000`) in slave mode, eDMA channel 29 one byte per request. Buffers are `0xAA | big-endian length | payload`: id 6 at `0x4f8af2c1` after eight `0xFF` bytes (MAIN changes byte 1 from `0x01` to `0x0f`), id 7 at `0x4f84f2c1` (length limit `0x5fffb`, matching SY FM4's "0x60000 - 5"). Section 6 (stage 1, SRAM `0x80000000`) sets up DDR, takes the stream and jumps through `*(0x40000400)`. Who starts DSPI0 as master before stage 1 is open. `[doc]` (stream bytes `[emu]`: payload equals section 7 by SHA-256)

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: Two pins form the handshake: MAIN's doorbell (GPIO port A bit 4) is the peer's DTIM0 capture event (vector 96); the peer's pin (port 6 bit 2: set via `0xEC09401E`, cleared via `0xEC09402A`) is MAIN's EPORT IRQ4 (vector 68). Peer steps the window state `+8` from 1 to `0xC` (hello "HO"/"HA" at `+0/+2`, `0xA5A5` at `+4`, window RAM test with `0xAAAAAAAA`/`0x55555555`, sample chunks), then installs its frame handler `0x40000934`. MAIN status `0x41bbf448` and state `0x41bb32b0` reach 6. Without a peer, "DSP BOOT FAILURE (TIMEOUT)" follows after `0x12` poll periods (about 1.04 G emulated instructions). `[emu]`

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: MAIN mixes the digital voices and owns the audio clock: eDMA ch 54 (TCD `0xFC0456C0`) streams a 2 KB ring at SRAM `0x80000000` (64 frames x 8 words) to the SSI TX FIFO `0xFC0C8000`; its half-way interrupt is the 1500 Hz audio frame (32 samples at 48 kHz, SSI1 slave; vector 174, handler `0x400a2058`). That handler forces INTC1 source 63 to run the engine tick (vector 191, `0x400a38ce`, 7,550 bytes), which mixes the 8 voices from `0x80003d50` in Q31 and fills the other half. Main L/R sit in ring words 5 and 3 as 24-bit signed (the Q31 mix shifted right by 8). `[doc]`/`[emu]`

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: Frame budget numbers (emulator): MAIN needs about 117,000 instructions per frame; the peer's frame handler about 86,500 idle and up to 88,900 with a note. digikit runs MAIN at 189.9 M instructions/s (264 MHz core over a measured busy CPI of 1.39); at one instruction per 132 MHz bus tick (88,000 per frame) MAIN did not fit. The peer's hottest code is the voice oscillator `0x4000290e` (98 instructions, 18 call sites, 21-24 % of the frame handler). `[emu]`

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: Profiling clock: stock MAIN reads DTIM2's counter DTCN2 (`0xFC07800C`, started by the boot loader; MAIN never writes `0xFC078000-0xFC07800F`) and busy-waits on it; DT2/DN2 use DTIM0. `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: MAIN RAM map 1.42: reset path clears `0x4033a000..0x45566490` (bss end); nothing above. Heap: buddy allocator `0x401036d0` (free `0x401038d6`), descriptor `0x402d5324`, 16 MiB at `0x444e48c0..0x454e48c0` (1.41: `0x444E38C0`). DMA data through the `+0x08000000` alias: slots `0x45570000..0x45609000`, `0x45608000..0x4564f0a0`, eMMC bounce buffers `0x4582f080..0x4583f280`, the sample stage buffer from `0x4584f2c0`, the section-7 transmit buffer `0x4784f2c1..0x478af2cb`. `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: The top 4 MiB of DDR is a ring: `0x400966e0` memsets 4 MiB at uncached `0x4fc00000` at boot; `0x4009687a` and `0x4009748c` index it as `0x4fc00000 + 8*(i & 0x7ffff)`, advance by `0x20` per frame and hand it to eDMA. So cached `0x47c00000..0x48000000` is cleared at every boot and written every frame (that it is the delay memory is open; SyntHack called `0x4FC00000` delay/reverb lines on 1.41). digikit's first `cf.expansion` (`0x47e8b000..0x47fe0000`) sat inside it and was moved. `[doc]` (O35)

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: Why SyntHack's `0x46000000` code got overwritten (inferred): MAIN builds the 64 sample slots for upload at `0x4584f2c0` (`0x40082334`), and the section-7 buffer starts 32 MB later at `0x4784f2c1`; `0x46000000` and SY FM4's `0x47000000` fall in that stage buffer, and the stock UI's "32 MB" sample limit matches its size. `[?]` (ties to I20, I145)

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: digikit's proposed mod RAM on 1.42 (not canary-tested): `cf.expansion` `0x478c0000..0x47bf0000` (3.2 MiB, 64 KiB above the section-7 buffer, 64 KiB below the ring), keep area `0x47bf0000..0x47bf1000`, flash cave `0x40339730..0x4033a000` (2,256 zero bytes after the 136-entry init table; 1.41's cave was `0x40338740..0x40339000`). A 31 MiB unreferenced gap `0x458b0000..0x4784f2c1` is deliberately not used. `[doc]` (boot `[emu]`)

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: Board facts same as DT2/DN2: UART8 `0xEC070000` (same init and TX code), eSDHC `0xFC0CC000` (same driver, same 4-part eMMC whitelist at `0x402d5b40`), DDR 128 MiB at `0x40000000` (bootstrap SDRAM setup byte-identical; CACR `0xa50ce100`, ACR0 `0x4007e020`), soft reset `0x400058f4` (drain UART, `clr.l 0x48000000`, `0x80` to `0xEC090000`). facts.section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: Card layout 1.42 (512-byte sectors, MmcFs only, no path filesystem): header at 0 (magic `0xBEEFBACE`); write-protect bitmaps at `0x800` (272 B, no kit bitmap); 2,048 sound slots of 2 sectors at `0x1000`; 64 sample slots ("SAMP", `0x400` sectors) at `0x2000..0x12000`; two "COKi" arena copies at `0x7a000`/`0x7c000`; working project at `0x7e000`; 128 project slots of 4 MiB at `0x80000..0x180000`. MmcFs writes refuse sector >= `0x180000`. An emulated session (save project, save sound, format +Drive) wrote at most sector `0x81f7f` and erased up to `0x17ffff`. `[doc]`/`[emu]`

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: Host-controlled card offsets (stock, all three devices): the MidiRpc Read/Write/Clear/Copy/Move/Swap handler (`0x4010bd9a`) writes the card through `SafeMmcStreamWriter` at the offset the host sends; nothing bounds it except the card capacity. A host that sends a mod store's offset erases it. digikit lists bounding this as its first open item before any hardware use. `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: PCB revision byte and the "TOO OLD HARDWARE" screen: MAIN maps FlexBus CS1 at address 0 (128 KiB, read only) and reads a revision byte there (letter = bits 0-4, number - 1 = bits 5-7, self-test prints `PCBA0046%c%d`). Below letter D the boot shows "TOO OLD HARDWARE FOR THIS OS"; `0x23`, `0x43`, `0x82` give "WILL NOT BE COMPATIBLE"; `0x4008248c` takes a newer-board path from letter E. CS0 is the 128 KiB peer window at `0x10000000`. `[doc]`

facts.text: Analog calibration record (factory data): SPI NOR `0x300000`, `0x22d40` bytes, magic "RBOZ" (`0x52424f5a`), checksum at `+0xc` (sum of `i ^ byte`), u16 `+0x10 == 1`, eight marker bytes non-zero; a backup copy is read from NOR `0x340000`. facts.section: Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: Panel wire and firmware key index differ: wire code = channel*8 + bit + 1 (1-48, 49 = channel 6 bit 0, LEVEL push). Codes: 1-16 trigs, 17 FUNC, 18 TRK, 19 TRIG, 20 SYN, 21 none, 22 FLTR, 23 AMP, 24 LFO, 25 SETTINGS, 26 FX, 27 TEMPO, 28 NO, 29-31 LEFT/DOWN/RIGHT, 32 PAGE, 33 BANK, 34 PTN, 35 SONG/SOUND (three dots), 36 REC, 37 PLAY, 38 STOP, 39 YES, 40 UP, 41-48 encoder pushes G,F,E,B,A,D,C,H. The decoder `0x40103094` maps wire to key index through `0x401d7a48`, and `key_down` (`0x40102f40`) maps back through `0x401d7984`: trig keys 1-16 are firmware key indices 24-39 (on DT2/DN2 both tables are the identity). MAIN has no boot-time key reader. `[emu]` (sweep) / `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Upgrade receiver, transport state, native bitmaps (OS 1.42, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: The OS upgrade receiver checks only checksums: it copies the image into a 2 MB RAM buffer with no size check, so a larger image overruns the buffer, and then erases and programs NOR from `0x80000` for the full claimed length. The 2 MB bound ends 512 KB below the calibration record at `0x300000`, and it is the only guard (rule A76, O34). Traced in the code, not tried. `[doc]` {modwerk-1119}

facts.section: Syntakt / Upgrade receiver, transport state, native bitmaps (OS 1.42, 2026-11-18)
facts.text: Native Bitmap API (1.42 MAIN): constructor `0x400f72be(object, width, height, pixels, mask)`, clipped rectangle fill `0x400f7fb6`, masked blit `0x400f8f70(dst, src, x, y, flags)`; an eight-word object can borrow pixel and mask arrays with no heap allocation. A 128 x 64 bitmap is 256 big-endian words per array, two words per column; y = 0 is bit 31 of the first word, y = 63 bit 0 of the second; a zero mask bit keeps the destination pixel. This is the bitmap layer; the panel's own row order is a different layer (compare D13). `[emu]` (executed in Unicorn) {synfact-1119}

facts.section: Syntakt / trig-seedr's Syntakt notes: pattern data, locks, power-off save, free DDR (OS 1.42, analog-emu, 2026-11-18/19)
facts.text: The track record (`0x499` bytes, 13 per pattern, contiguous, then the lock store): 64 × u16 flag words at +`0x000` (bit `0x0001` a trig); per-step bytes VEL +`0x080`, LEN +`0x0C0`, micro timing +`0x100` (−23..+23), retrig fields +`0x140`/+`0x180`/+`0x1C0` (by the Rytm's order), condition +`0x200`, NOTE +`0x2C0`, NOT2-NOT4 +`0x300`/+`0x340`/+`0x380` (0xFF = track default); track length word +`0x3C9`; Euclidean mode +`0x3D1`, PL1 +`0x3D2`, the Euclidean pulse table +`0x3D8`. VEL, NOTE, EUC, PL1, the table and the length word `[emu]`; the rest from their setters `[doc]`.

facts.section: Syntakt / trig-seedr's Syntakt notes: pattern data, locks, power-off save, free DDR (OS 1.42, analog-emu, 2026-11-18/19)
facts.text: Parameter locks are a full matrix, no row pool: per track `0x2447` bytes, 64 steps × 72 int16 (ids 0..70, −1 none; word 71 the step's lock count) plus 71 per-id bytes; address `locks + 0x2447·track + 2·(72·step + id)`. Set `0x40017602`, clear `0x4001741e`, get `0x4001722a` (model level, no length check); `0x40027fa2` is the track-level set that refuses steps past the length. Nothing counts rows, so the Rytm's 72-row limit does not exist here. Layout `[doc]`, one lock measured `[emu]`.

facts.section: Syntakt / trig-seedr's Syntakt notes: pattern data, locks, power-off save, free DDR (OS 1.42, analog-emu, 2026-11-18/19)
facts.text: Power-off save: the power-sense interrupt (`0x40001d88`, PPDSDR_C bit 2, as on the Rytm) forces INTC1 source 30; its handler `0x40001d5e` calls `0x400bcf7a`, which writes the COKI working state to sectors `0x7a000`/`0x7c000` only when byte `0x43be3154` is set, else it only parks the card. `0x400bd8a0` sets that byte once PPDSDR_G bit 3 (supercap charged) reads high; the Rytm's signal is PPDSDR_A bit 5. An emulator that does not model the bit saves nothing at power off. `[emu]` On one unit running trig-seedr (2026-11-19) an applied take and a pending take were both on the track after a power off and on; the save path is stock's, but a plain stock unit and the supercap timing are not checked (H60). `[hw]` {trig-seedr-1121} (I184)

facts.text: Repacking a unit file: the bootloader stages packed MAIN at `0x40200000` and depacks it in place to `0x40000400`. elektron-firmware-tool levels 3 and 2 gave seedr's MAIN a negative in-place margin (would not boot); level 1 left 10,912 bytes, level 0 35,153. facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: AUDIO memory, MAIN CPU profile, project workers (OS 1.42, 2026-11-18/19)
facts.text: AUDIO image layout (traced from section 7's code, `tools/study_st_audio_memory.py`): entry word at `0x40000400` (-> `0x40001070`), code `0x40000404-0x40009f1c` (11,477 instructions reached), tables to `0x40040850`; `0x40040860-0x40041050` is zero in stock (Synfact's AUDIO services sit there); the packed FPGA stream at `0x40041060` unpacks to `0x40042000`. The image tail `0x4004f6e0-0x4005df10` holds SRAM's initial contents (copied to `0x80000000` and `0x80008000` at boot). VBR is `0x40000000` (the value is stored at `0x4004005c`); boot points all 256 vectors at an `rte`, then sets vector 96 and the block interrupt. `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: AUDIO memory, MAIN CPU profile, project workers (OS 1.42, 2026-11-18/19)
facts.text: The sample-page receiver has a forbidden page: MAIN writes a 16-bit page index at window `0x00c` and 2 KiB at `0x800`; AUDIO copies to `0x4004f750 + index * 0x800` with no bound. Index `0x8000` lands on `0x4404f750-0x4404ff50`, AUDIO's own variables and 64-entry sample table: never send it. Indices `0x8001-0xffff` reach `0x4404ff50-0x4804f750`, which runs past the stack top; keep pages below `0x47ff0000`. `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: AUDIO memory, MAIN CPU profile, project workers (OS 1.42, 2026-11-18/19)
facts.text: Nothing in the stock AUDIO image names an address above `0x4404f980` (the end of the zeroed data, named once by the clear; no allocator). The AUDIO stack starts at `0x48000000`, the main context idles and all work runs in the block interrupt: at most 3,140 bytes deep by static count. ACR0 `0x4007e020` caches `0x40000000-0x47ffffff`, so AUDIO has 128 MiB as MAIN does. That nothing writes the high zone at run time is not yet shown on a unit (Synfact's high-memory probe, type 70, is built for that check). `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: AUDIO memory, MAIN CPU profile, project workers (OS 1.42, 2026-11-18/19)
facts.text: Stock MAIN cost (emulator profile with a calibrated cache model, default project in PLAY, not meter readings): the block routine `0x400a38ce` is 97.5 % of MAIN's instructions. Per block about 72,400 instructions, 1,466 I-cache misses and 206 D-cache misses, modelled as 77 % of a 250 MHz MAIN; stopped gives nearly the same. About 22 KB of code runs every block against an 8 KB, 4-way, 16-byte-line I-cache, so almost every hot line misses once per block: 1 KB less code per block is about 1.5 MAIN points, 1,000 fewer instructions about 0.5. The model (cycles ~ 0.85 x instructions + 40 x misses) was fitted on a unit for AUDIO code and predicted the first Chorus port's jump from 88 % to 100 %. `[emu]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: FX-bus compressor, kit codecs, real-bank profile (OS 1.42, core 2.4.0, 2026-11-20)
facts.text: FX-bus VCA gains on 1.42: the two FX VCA gains sit in D1/D3 at `0x400905b6` (stock bytes `0c81 0000 ffff`, a clamp compare); the native clamp and stores run through `0x400905da` and write hardware context +70/+72 (decimal). The 1.41 site was `0x4009053e`. Changing only these two gains there compresses whatever reaches the FX track, after DRIVE and filter, and leaves direct track outputs and the MAIN mix alone. At this site the native MOVCLR leaves ACC0/ACC1 empty; a callback may use them but must keep ACC2/ACC3. `[doc]` (site and stores compared with stock 1.42); comp-st 0.2.0 using it reported working on the owner's unit `[hw]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: FX-bus compressor, kit codecs, real-bank profile (OS 1.42, core 2.4.0, 2026-11-20)
facts.text: FX ADC pair: the detector input for the FX bus is fixed at `0x80003c50` and `0x80003cd0`, 32 signed Q31 frames each (the ADC 6/7 capture SyntHack named on 1.41). `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: FX-bus compressor, kit codecs, real-bank profile (OS 1.42, core 2.4.0, 2026-11-20)
facts.text: The digital FX bus is not the whole FX input: `0x8000dad0` (Synfact's `ST_FX_TRACK_BUS`, the first of the six mixer buses) is the digital bus before the analog FX block. Processing it digitally does not cover what the analog circuit routes to FX; for that, detect on the ADC pair and act on the VCAs. `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: FX-bus compressor, kit codecs, real-bank profile (OS 1.42, core 2.4.0, 2026-11-20)
facts.text: Kit pointers and codecs on 1.42: live kits at `0x41ad6134 + k*0x1618`, k < 128 (1.41: `0x41ad5134`, the `+0x1000` DDR shift). `KitActive::kitChanged` is `0x40172414` (vtable `0x401c3694` +`0x5c`; object `0x40a713f0`, kits at its +`0x10`). Native Kit new `0x400b3384`, encode `0x400a78f4`, decode `0x400a78a0`; native memcpy `0x4011613c`; the global Kit model's has/get/set start at `0x4000d870`, `0x4000d94a`, `0x4000da32`. Core 2.4 takes these sites once and passes notifications to modules, so Chorus and LFO3 no longer patch them themselves. `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: FX-bus compressor, kit codecs, real-bank profile (OS 1.42, core 2.4.0, 2026-11-20)
facts.text: Kit slot tail, 1.42: native `[0, 0x14d2)`, LFO3 `[0x14e0, 0x15d0)`, comp-st `[0x15d0, 0x15e0)` (tag `0x4351`, six big-endian Q8 words, a 16-bit check), playhead-st `[0x15e0, 0x15f8)`; the tail is now full up to `0x15f8`. The native Kit SysEx uses a shorter layout, so tail data does not travel in a Kit SysEx dump. `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: FX-bus compressor, kit codecs, real-bank profile (OS 1.42, core 2.4.0, 2026-11-20)
facts.text: Compressor cost in Synfact's emulator (guest instructions per 32-frame block, not cycles): the Digitakt mk1 compressor ported literally would cost about 2,900-3,050 for the gain calculation alone; SyntHack's compact master-comp core 98 off, 564-611 on; comp-st 0.2.0 in the full bank 43 off, 377-379 below threshold, 484-509 compressing, against Chorus at about 2,180-4,040. `[emu]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact findings: FX-bus compressor, kit codecs, real-bank profile (OS 1.42, core 2.4.0, 2026-11-20)
facts.text: Profile of the real shipped bank (analog-emu with a patch that forces the 1.42 profile for a modified image): the per-block hot code is the stock audio block; the mods' code shows almost no cache misses. With an 8 KB I-cache against about 22 KB of code per block, any lock set covers at most about 16-19 %, so a better lock set than icache-lock-st's cannot recover much. The MAIN parameter smoother keeps its arrays in SRAM (uncached) and runs with `MACSR=0x28`; its one-pole has a history-dependent dead band, so "converged" is not one value. Only an A/B on the unit (same core, banks differing by one module) measures real CPU. `[emu]`

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: Two images boot on the unit: `device-peer` (only the section 7 packer below) and, after the repair below, the full `device` set (runtime, DIGIKIT menu, HEALTH, input, card guard, section 7 packer). The second CPU loads the unpacked section 7, the store works and a content module (digikit/remote) was installed from the workbench, selected, applied and ran with working keys. `[hw]`

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: The patched image did not fit without packing section 7: Elektron stores section 7 raw (383,760 B, SHA-256 `daf6451c...ec783bc2`); with it raw the patched container was 2,129,312 B, 32,672 B over the 2 MiB upgrade limit (`0x1FFE00`). Packed (aPLib with an 8-byte header: big-endian body length and byte sum) it is 264,194 B. The full set with the guard is 2,079,872 B (16.4 KB free). `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: How MAIN reads section 7 (no stage buffer): the peer thread (entry `0x40082c04`, made by `0x40082e9c` from the boot thread) loads A2 with the NOR read `0x40116d7a` (6-byte `lea` at `0x40082c24`), reads id 6 into `0x4f8af2c9` and id 7 straight into the transmit buffer at `0x4f84f2c6` (`0xAA` at `0x4f84f2c1`, big-endian length at `0x4f84f2c2`). The only length check is `length + 5 <= 0x60000` at `0x40082d66` (else "DSP BOOT FAILURE (BUF)"); a missing id gives status 1 at `0x40082e84`. No other code reads id 7; the bootstrap and the OS-upgrade receiver do not parse sections. The handshake timeout (about 5.1 s, 19 polls) starts only after both NOR reads and the DMA arm, so unpacking before the stream costs no timeout time. `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: digikit's peer-image hook: it replaces that `lea` so id 7 is read to the end of the buffer, checked (length, byte sum), unpacked forward with the firmware's own depacker `0x401181ec` (no output bound; returns the length in D0) and checked again (length, SHA-256 of the stock section). On any failure it takes the missing-section path: the second CPU gets no bytes and MAIN shows "OOPS! SOMETHING WENT WRONG, SWITCH OFF/ON TO BOOT AGAIN." The in-place margin of the packed stream is 9,444 B. Boot cost estimate 0.25-0.4 s (not measured on the unit). `[emu]` (proof with a one-byte-changed stream refused) / `[hw]` (boots)

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: The second CPU must get the exact stock bytes: section 7 carries a second FPGA bitstream (at `0x40041060`) that the peer loads through its own DSPI. MAIN configures the main FPGA itself from section 1: `0x400bd74e` reads id 1, unpacks it with `0x401181ec` to `0x43be315c` (length at `0x43be3158`, 149,516 B), and `0x400bcb4e` shifts it out over DSPI `0xFC03C000` after INIT goes high. This corrects the earlier "the bootstrap configures the FPGA" (section list above). `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: Bootstrap stage and in-place unpack: the Syntakt bootstrap copies packed MAIN to `0x40200000` and unpacks it in place to `0x40000400` (depacker `0x8000041c`; stage constant at `0x800005b2`, `0x800005d2`, `0x80000622`, `0x8000155c`, `0x8000157e`). It checks no bound and no checksum; when the output overtakes the unread stream the decoder runs away and MAIN never starts. Margins at this stage: stock +96,356 B, `device-peer` +67,676 B, the first full `device` image -42,486 B (it hung the unit, I183). digikit now refuses a margin under 8 KiB and writes the stream's last tokens as literals to reach it. The emulator had missed it because it installs MAIN directly and never runs the bootstrap's unpack. `[hw]` (hang) / `[doc]` (stage, margins) (I183, compare SyntHack's padded build above)

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: Key ids in key events differ from the Digitakt II/Digitone II: the id at +`0xc` of a key event is the firmware key index from the decoder table `0x401d7a48`: YES 12, NO 13, RIGHT 17, LEVEL push 48 (a second YES key in lists; the stock compact menu handler `0x400f5c82` treats 12 and `0x30` alike). On DT2/DN2 the same keys are 10, 12, 15 and 49. The flag bits look the same: bit 0 set on a press (cursor keys and RIGHT act on it), bit 4 on a release (YES acts on it). `[doc]` (I181)

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: The card capacity is a driver word: the eSDHC init (`0x4010ebea`, boot thread) stores the capacity in sectors at `0x444ba720` (from EXT_CSD SEC_COUNT, else the CSD); the 20-byte getter `0x4010f232` returns it, or `0xFFFFFFFF` while the driver is not ready (same hash on DT2 1.17 `0x4012ddd6`, DN2 1.12 `0x4012c49a`, DN2 1.11 `0x4012c1ba`). The part table (7 rows of 32 bytes at `0x402d5adc`) is checked at boot but not enforced on the Syntakt: only the self-test reads the result (the DT2 gates its mount on it). Only the self-test makes the pSLC (enhanced area) conversion. `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: One unit's card: INFO reports `0x3a4000` sectors (1.82 GiB): the `4FTE4R` part with the enhanced area set, the smallest capacity in the table. So do not assume the 32 GB `0x2e1a000` part the emulators model. `[hw]` (I182)

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: What stock touches on the card: nothing is sized from the capacity. FORMAT +DRIVE erases `0x80000-0x17ffff` and `0x1000-0x1fff` (with SAMPLES also `0x2000-0x11fff`), not the whole card; stock 1.42 touches only sectors below `0x180000`. digikit's Syntakt store is now the fixed area `0x200000-0x300000` (1-1.5 GiB, 512 MiB): 256 MiB above the last stock sector and below the smallest listed capacity. Store writes, listing and removal worked on the unit. `[doc]` / `[hw]` (store)

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: The eMMC write and erase entries: block write `0x4010f7f8` `(sector, bytes, buf)` and block erase `0x4010f52a` `(sector, count)` are the only MAIN code that writes or erases the user area, except the OS-upgrade finale's raw controller writes of the COKi copies (`0x400bcf7a`) and the CMD6 EXT_CSD writes in `0x4010f3d8` (one-time-programmable card setup: never call it). The write splits requests over 64 KiB by calling itself (return address entry + `0x36`) and is bounded only by the capacity; the erase checks nothing, and a count of 0 makes the end sector `sector - 1`. Both start with 8 bytes of `lea; movem.l` (no PC-relative operand); D0, D1, A0, A1 and the flags are dead at both entries; same hash and size on DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12 and 1.11. Five 1.42 callers ignore the result (the console command `0x40080646`, the COKi writer `0x400bcadc`, the Data API Clear `0x400b639a`, the COKi restore `0x400bd608` twice). `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: digikit's card write guard (built for the Syntakt, emulator only): `before` hooks at both entries refuse a request outside the row of its writer class (stock: `[0, 0x180000)`; the runtime's own write, known by its return address: the store) and return -10, the driver's own out-of-range code, before any lock is taken. The Data API then reports "Failed to write to eMMC". It cannot see the finale's raw writes or CMD6. The guard is on in both Syntakt sets; no refusal was reported from the unit. `[emu]` (SB35)

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: Hook sites found by hash on 1.42 (not checked on this image, `[?]`): project slot setter `0x4006f2ce`, slot byte `0x40653441`, save exit `0x4001a7d4`, clear-one exit `0x4005a81a`, clear-many exit `0x4005a898`, paste exit `0x400c2116`; USB EP0 setup dispatcher `0x400062e2`, EP0 send `0x4000621c`, setup packet `0x454e4bdc`. `[?]`

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: MidiRpc Ping reply: on 1.42 the payload is length-prefixed (`1e 16`, 22 request types, `"Syntakt" 00`, 32 bytes); read the name as the first NUL-terminated string after the blob. `[emu]`

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: Recovery path digikit gives: FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4 (OS UPGRADE), the stock file over 5-pin MIDI DIN; back up the +Drive card first and do not put samples or sounds into the stock slots with Transfer until the Data API guard exists. Whether the logo-hung unit came back through that menu is not stated. `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: Size baseline 2026-11-22: digikit's `device` set now stores 2,102,528 B against its cap of 2,096,640 B (`0x1FFE00`), 5,888 B over, after the 2026-11-21 set that booted on the unit was 2,079,872 B; growth on the development lane. About 69.8 KB of MAIN's tail is stored as literals because the unpack margin is small; the DIGIKIT menu (19,104 B stored) is to move to the card first. Measured with patchkit; nothing flashed. `[doc]` {digikit-1122}

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: The in-place unpack sets a hard floor on stored MAIN (finding 159, static): the room before the output reaches the stream start is `0x200000 - 0x400` = 2,096,128 B. Since only literals keep the slack constant, the binding point is the end of the stream: stored MAIN >= unpacked MAIN - 2,096,128 + margin floor + 8 (header). Checked against the hung image of I183: 3,683,064 B out, 1,544,457 B plain stream, -42,486 B margin (formula: -42,471). Stock MAIN is 3.44 MB; digikit's appended runtime is 274,498 B (was 215,583). `[doc]` {digikit-1123} ([I183](../INCIDENTS.md#i183-a-full-digikit-image-hung-a-syntakt-at-the-logo-the-bootstraps-unpack-overran-its-stream))

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: What follows for a Syntakt mod: each byte removed from unpacked MAIN saves one stored byte (not the about 0.54 the packer ratio suggests). Moving bytes around, splitting the stream, packer depth or choosing which bytes become literals cannot go below the floor; they only choose where the padding sits. digikit's 111,517 B literal tail costs 69,762 B because the plain stream was that far short of the floor. Only a smaller MAIN, a lower margin or code outside MAIN's stream helps. `[doc]` {digikit-1123}

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: The 8 KiB margin floor is a safety default, not a measurement: `main_margin_min` = 8192 in digikit's device data. If the depacker `0x8000041c` reads one byte at a time (read once, a second check is wanted), a slack of 0 or more after each token would do; a word prefetch would need 4 or more. Lowering the floor to 64 B would save 8,128 B. digikit plans this only as a fallback, after a second read of the loop and a run of the real bootstrap depacker on the exact stream (`depack_check`, length and SHA-256). Too low a floor hangs the unit at the logo ([I183](../INCIDENTS.md#i183-a-full-digikit-image-hung-a-syntakt-at-the-logo-the-bootstraps-unpack-overran-its-stream)). `[doc]` (open) {digikit-1123}

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: Other room for code: section 8 (103 KB stored, use unknown) and a section 4 repack are read-only for patchkit, with unknown consumers; whether the bootstrap walks a table of section ids and accepts an unknown one is unread. Code caves give only about 2 KB. The OS-upgrade stage (`0x403d10d0`) lies above and is not used at boot. `[doc]` / `[?]` (section 8, unknown ids) {digikit-1123}

facts.section: Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
facts.text: digikit's fix is deferred: the Syntakt fit waits for the resident core / system package split (about 167 KB of the runtime moves to the card, see digitakt-2.md). Until then the current `device` set does not fit, and the Syntakt container-overflow patchkit tests fail on main. Nothing new was flashed. `[doc]` {digikit-1123}

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact: screen redraw cost, stereo inside the AUDIO chain, eDMA self-link (OS 1.42, core 2.5.0, 2026-11-21/22)
facts.text: A redraw request recomposes the whole screen: the UI is double-buffered and every repaint redraws all visible views; the COMP page alone costs about 30,000 instructions per recompose. With drums, comp-st 0.2.0's GR meter asked for a repaint on 24-26 of the 30 UI ticks a second, and MAIN rose on the unit with the page open ([I196](../INCIDENTS.md#i196-a-compressors-gr-meter-raised-main-cpu-through-screen-repaints-synfact-comp-st-020-syntakt)). 0.3 repaints for the meter at most every third tick (10 Hz) and ignores 1-pixel moves except to zero: 8-10 a second with drums, none with a steady signal. The drop on the unit is not measured. `[hw]` (symptom) / `[emu]` (counts) {synfact-1123}

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact: screen redraw cost, stereo inside the AUDIO chain, eDMA self-link (OS 1.42, core 2.5.0, 2026-11-21/22)
facts.text: The AUDIO chain's multimode is one load away from replaceable: the stock chain loads its per-track multimode routine with `lea 0x400019d6,a4` at `0x40000a72`; core 2.5 changes it to `movea.l 0x40040f3c,a4` (chain directory word 3, which holds `0x400019d6` until a bank writes its own entry). The native routine's first part `0x400019d6-0x40001ea3` has no PC-relative operand and no call, and every exit joins at `0x40001ea4`, so it can be copied and run elsewhere. samplers-st copies it on the unit from its own AUDIO image only when the bytes match 1.42's fingerprint. `[doc]` {synfact-1123}

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact: screen redraw cost, stereo inside the AUDIO chain, eDMA self-link (OS 1.42, core 2.5.0, 2026-11-21/22)
facts.text: Negative frame word sends the multimode outside its tables: the first part indexes its tables with the frame word `0x80008188 + 4t` shifted right by 21 and 22; a negative value reads outside the tables, into AUDIO SRAM among other places. Seen in analog-emu with random words; keep it at or above zero. `[emu]` {synfact-1123}

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact: screen redraw cost, stereo inside the AUDIO chain, eDMA self-link (OS 1.42, core 2.5.0, 2026-11-21/22)
facts.text: AUDIO chain state: the drive's control state is 40 words at `0x800083b0`, written only by the chain; the base-width has no control state, only two words of memory per track at `0x800088a0 + 8t` and the row's poles. `[doc]` {synfact-1123}

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact: screen redraw cost, stereo inside the AUDIO chain, eDMA self-link (OS 1.42, core 2.5.0, 2026-11-21/22)
facts.text: A software-started eDMA channel runs one minor loop unless it is linked to itself: stock's channel 47 TCD links the channel to itself. Synfact's first try on AUDIO channel 46 (2026-11) set CITER 35 without the link, and on the unit only the first 16 bytes (sequence, mask, shifts) reached the shared window, never the tag ([I197](../INCIDENTS.md#i197-an-edma-block-without-a-self-link-moved-only-its-first-16-bytes-synfact-stereo-tracks-syntakt)). samplers-st 1.6 sets CITER/BITER `0xdc23` (ELINK to channel 46, 35 loops of 16 bytes); checked in emulation only. Channel 46 is free on both CPUs in stock; MAIN's eDMA controller arbitrates round robin (`CR` 6 at boot). From samplers-st 1.6 the stereo engine claims channel 46 on AUDIO and on MAIN. `[hw]` (16-byte failure) / `[emu]` (fix) {synfact-1123}

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact: screen redraw cost, stereo inside the AUDIO chain, eDMA self-link (OS 1.42, core 2.5.0, 2026-11-21/22)
facts.text: Stereo cost after the move into the chain (emulator, instructions per 32-frame block): R's chain work for eight stereo tracks 19,891 against 33,099 for a native R pass; the chain end's own code 4,954 (9,671 in samplers 1.5); PCM at whole-frame steps (unity pitch, octaves) mono 679 -> 344, stereo 969 -> 447; the stereo voice tail 2,581 -> 2,399 per track. Every change gives the same words as 1.5.2 in analog-emu. `[emu]` {synfact-1123}

facts.section: Syntakt / Synfact: screen redraw cost, stereo inside the AUDIO chain, eDMA self-link (OS 1.42, core 2.5.0, 2026-11-21/22)
facts.text: COMP's sidechain filter (SCF): a one-pole high-pass on the detector only, `lp += a(x - lp)`, `y = x - lp`, `a = 1 - exp(-2 pi fc / 48000)`, state in ACC0/ACC1 during the block; OFF plus 127 cutoffs log-spaced from 60 Hz to 1 kHz. Extra instructions per block: 43 with MIX at 0, 395-397 below threshold and 502-528 compressing with SCF off, 600 and 705-738 with SCF at 150 Hz; every cutoff costs the same. A 50 Hz kick is 3.8 dB lower to the detector at 60 Hz and 14.0 dB at 250 Hz. The position is stored in RAT's unused low byte; a 0.2.0 bank refuses such a Kit and restores COMP's defaults. Synfact does not trust Unicorn for EMAC arithmetic and checks the loop in analog-emu's cfbench (2,688 blocks against a 64-bit model). `[emu]` {synfact-1123}

facts.text: Before adding a code site to a mod, check whether the core already has an event, table or export for it. If another mod could want the same thing, build it in the core's shape in its own file so it can move into the core, tell the user and offer a pull request; use `lint`'s `core_candidates`, `sdk.coresites` and `sdk.bounties` to find hooks that belong in the core. `[doc]` {elekloader-agents}

facts.section: Agent workflow for firmware mods (distilled from the digitone-2-modding-skill) / Repo-level rules for agents (elekloader `AGENTS.md`, the only project we found that ships a formal agent file)
facts.text: Never commit firmware - no `.syx`, extracted sections, `.bin` images, built `.elemod` files or anything derived from a stock OS; run `git status` to check. Never weaken a check to make a test pass: the checks in `syx.verify`, `elemod` and `link` protect users (bootloader stays stock, mods must not collide); if a check wrongly refuses something, narrow the fix and test both sides. Keep device facts in `devices/`, not in code paths; the writer must stay byte-exact (`test_writer_matches_c_tool`, `test_writer_no_change_is_stock`); keep the JS engine in sync with the Python one; keep the web kit site-agnostic; the web page loads nothing from other origins, sends user files nowhere, holds no firmware or builds, and pins catalog entries by SHA-256. `[doc]` {elekloader-agents}

facts.section: Agent workflow for firmware mods (distilled from the digitone-2-modding-skill) / Repo-level rules for agents (elekloader `AGENTS.md`, the only project we found that ships a formal agent file)
facts.text: Tests: always `python tests/test_units.py` and `python tests/test_link_refusals.py`; others need firmware passed through environment variables (`ELEKLOADER_STOCK`, `ELEKLOADER_DN_SYX`, ...). A test with missing files is skipped, not passed - report which tests ran and never claim a skipped test passed. "Done" = all runnable tests pass, docs match the code, `git status` shows no firmware. `[doc]` {elekloader-agents}

facts.section: Agent workflow for firmware mods (distilled from the digitone-2-modding-skill) / Repo-level rules for agents (elekloader `AGENTS.md`, the only project we found that ships a formal agent file)
facts.text: Format rules worth copying: a mod stores a hash of stock bytes, never the bytes themselves; where its bytes repeat firmware it writes a `["stock", addr, len]` reference and the loader copies them from the user's own hash-checked image; a `code` site must cover whole instructions; the linker checks stock hashes, overlaps, memory regions within free areas, duplicates, unresolved imports and core versions, lays out the core first and then mods sorted by ID (output independent of input order), and verifies that the built image differs from stock only inside declared sites and appended code. `[doc]` {elekloader-format}

facts.section: Agent workflow for firmware mods (distilled from the digitone-2-modding-skill) / How digikit separates firmware from mods (ARCHITECTURE.md, worth copying)
facts.text: Layers, each depending only on the one below: content modules (`.dkm` machines/FX/tools, loaded from the card at run time); apps (menus); SDK contract; runtime (loads `.dkm`, links imports); adapters (one per firmware plug-in point: the only code that hooks the firmware); firmware, found by hash-pinned anchors.

facts.text: Everything version- or device-specific lives in anchors, device profiles and adapters. A new OS version means new anchors plus adapter fixes; modules and SDK stay unchanged. A checker (`layercheck`) enforces it.

facts.section: Agent workflow for firmware mods (distilled from the digitone-2-modding-skill) / How digikit separates firmware from mods (ARCHITECTURE.md, worth copying)
facts.text: Apps never patch. A hook costs at most one flag check on a hot path when no module uses it. Modules are never unloaded, so every pointer handed to the UI must be static.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 3. Time and DSP link
facts.text: DN2 has 16 voice slots chosen at note-on, not tied to tracks, so it has no fixed stereo pair. DT2 has 32 voices: even = L, odd = R. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 3. Time and DSP link
facts.text: digikit's run-time limits (its own, not the firmware's): 8 modules, 4 FX slots (3 since 2026-11-15, CONFLICTS O27 `[?]`), 512 KiB (DT2) / 320 KiB (DN2) DSP area in 64-byte granules, 64 KiB per module file (128 KiB since 2026-11-20, the upload stage buffer `stage_bytes` on DT2, DN2 and Syntakt; `[doc]` {digikit-1120}). The firmware would allow about 900 / 450 KiB. Every limit was filled in the emulator and the next module was refused with a clean error. `[emu]` {digikit-f57}

facts.section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 3. Time and DSP link
facts.text: digikit's planning budget (2026-11-14): a selection must fit 85 % of the 666,667-cycle block after the stock baseline, with emulator instruction counts projected to cycles by a high factor: that leaves 194,244 instructions per block on the DT2 and 92,796 on the DN2 (12,140 and 5,799 per voice at 16 voices). These are planning instructions, not the cycles measured free on a unit, so do not compare them with the `[hw]` headroom figures directly. On DN2 1.12 the whole DSP ran 332,039 instructions per block in the emulator with one note playing (stock baseline 334,529); the DT2 stock baseline is about 211,000. `[doc]` / `[emu]` {digikit-budget}

facts.section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 4. SHARC calling convention of the stock code (selcc emits the same)
facts.text: Call: `CALL (linked, delayed)` (Type 25a). Prologue `I7 = MODIFY(I7, -N)`, saves to `DM(I6 - n)`. Return `I12 = DM(I6, M7); JUMP (M14, I12) (DB)` with `RFRAME` in the delay slot.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 4. SHARC calling convention of the stock code (selcc emits the same)
facts.text: Arguments R4, R8, R12, then the stack (`DM(I6, M6)`). Result in R0 (F0; R0:R1 for 64-bit). Render kernels return nothing and write through pointers.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 4. SHARC calling convention of the stock code (selcc emits the same)
facts.text: Constant registers that voice code never writes: M5 = 0, M6 = 1, M7 = -1, M13 = 0, M14 = 1, M15 = -1. Indirect jumps use DAG2 (`JUMP (M13, I12)` relies on M13 = 0). The stock interrupt code also reads B7, L6 and L7 (a valid linear stack in I7, L6 = L7 = 0) and IMASK, IMASKP, IRPTL, MMASK, TPERIOD, TCOUNT and FLAGS at any instruction; never write them, even with a save and restore (digikit finding 130, [digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md section 7](../devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md)). `[doc]` {digikit-1116}

facts.section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 5. The DT2 audio chain per block (planar floats, 32 L then 32 R; voice blocks mono)
facts.text: At H2/H3 SIMD is off and no DO loop is active. The stock FX state lives in DDR: chorus `0x80459388`, delay `0x8005912c` (rings of 524,288 floats, max 8 s), reverb `0x80000018`. FX rings wrap by index arithmetic; FX units never write B or L registers, but the voice renderer does and restores them. Static FX cost: chorus 7.1k, delay 6.0k, reverb 17.2k instructions per block. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 5. The DT2 audio chain per block (planar floats, 32 L then 32 R; voice blocks mono)
facts.text: The stock machines share almost no code (each machine is one large function). Only the post-voice chain and a few maths helpers are shared between DT2 and DN2. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
facts.text: Clock and block: 1 GHz, 32 samples per block, 666,667 cycles nominal. Measured median per block: DT2 666,582, DN2 666,784 (digikit); DN2 666,706 (elekloader's idle-task meter); the owner's idle counter on a DT2 agrees. {digikit-f103} {elekloader-sharc-dn2} {own-dt2-notes}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
facts.text: Core behaviour: 59 value items (saturation with MODE1.ALUSAT, the short and multifunction compute forms, float rounding) and all cycle snippets equal, including the L2 conflict loads (2,769 vs 2,803 cycles for 4,096 loads); the 6,694 RECIPS/RSQRTS seed results are equal. So the cycle budget of rule A35 and the float rules in [`../devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md`](../devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md) section 6 hold on both. {digikit-f103} {digikit-f102}

facts.text: Core registers set by the boot code: IMASK, MODE2, SHDBG_REVID, cache configuration (`SHL1C_CFG`) read the same on both. The traps armed (illegal opcode, L1 parity) are therefore the same. {digikit-f103}

facts.text: Never store a DAG register through its own DAG (rule A33): hung a DT2 (Plaits port, digikit's "rung C"); the DN2 skill names the same pattern "the root cause of silent units" on its unit. {dt2-plaits} {dn2-skill-sharc}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
facts.text: NaN or Inf in stock FX feedback silences everything until reboot: on a DT2 from an LFO at large depth on TUNE (digikit) and in the owner's builds; on a DN2 from never-written DDR, which powers on as garbage such as `0xFFFFFFFF` (the DN2 skill). Same failure, two triggers: guard every value you feed into a feedback path, and fill new DDR in emulator tests with `0xFFFFFFFF`. {digikit-f51} {own-dt2-notes} {dn2-skill-firmware}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
facts.text: Shared stock DSP code, by the bytes: the DT2's six wavetable render stages are in the DN2 image too. Three are byte-identical; in the other three every differing byte is a PC-relative call offset (same target) or one table-pointer literal. All call the same reciprocal helper at sw `0x1c06ba` in both images (RECIPS plus Newton steps, the helper behind A35's divide cost). A fix or measurement on one of these stages carries over. `[doc]` {digikit-f11}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
facts.text: The unused frame tail carries DSP code on both (+23 instructions per block on DT2, +26 on DN2). `[doc]` {digikit-findings}

facts.text: How stock spends the block: the DN2 engine renders every voice every block (~63-65 % flat by dnfw's idle-task method, a held voice adds ~8k cycles; elekloader reads ~80 %, conflict O15). A test that settles it: provoke single late blocks on a DN2 the way the DT2 test did. {own-dt2-notes} {dn2mk2-reports}
