facts.text: The Digitone II 1.11 example file has 18,668 SysEx messages, 8-in-7 encoding, per-packet checksums, a container with model/version/overall checksum and an HMAC-SHA256 signature the tool recomputes on repack. Section 3 (MAIN OS) is the usual target; leave 2 (bootstrap) and 4 (updater) alone because the bootloader holds the recovery menu; section 8 appears as `?` (no known name); section IDs differ on other devices, so `-i` is authoritative. `.raw` sections are copied as-is, `.bin` sections are decompressed. `[doc]` {em-tutorial}

facts.section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / Safe byte-level editing rules (elektronmods tutorial by the forum admin, using elektron-firmware-tool)
facts.text: Editing rules: overwrite bytes only, the file size must not change (later addresses shift); replacement text must be the same length and use characters already present; keep the terminating zero byte; always edit a copy in `work/` and keep `extracted/` untouched; verify with `cmp -l` (exactly the intended number of changed bytes) and by re-extracting section 3 from the new file and comparing it byte-for-byte; `-V` must not exceed the original version string length (e.g. 4 characters like `1.11`). The repacked file is smaller than Elektron's because the tool compresses slightly better (level 3 took ~14 s, level 0 is ~18x faster and ~3 % larger). The author states the worked example (replacing "UNTITLED" with "ELEKMODS") was not tested on hardware. `[doc]` {em-tutorial}

facts.section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Sections
facts.text: Section 7 is a stream of ADI boot records (the ADSP-2156x hardware reference, boot chapter). Each header is four little-endian uint32s: block code, target, byte count, argument. The block code's top byte is `0xad`; its byte at offset 2 makes the XOR of all 16 header bytes zero; its low 16 bits are flags: `0x0001` LOAD (copy `count` bytes to the target), `0x0101` FILL (fill with the argument), `0x5001` FIRST + IGNORE (starts a boot image; target = entry in PC16, argument = distance from the end of this header to the next FIRST), `0x0801` INIT and `0x8001` FINAL (end the image and the stream). Later loads overwrite earlier ones in order, and stock relies on that (15 overlapping loads and fills on DN2 1.12). To add code, insert records before FINAL and grow only the last FIRST's argument and XOR byte; dt2-machine-lab used FILL records to keep a decoded stream under the size limit below. `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-boot} {dt2-lab-capicola}

facts.section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Sections
facts.text: Section 7 must stay under 1 MiB, stored and decoded (DT2 and DN2). At boot the ColdFire allocates two `0x100000`-byte buffers, copies the stored section into the first, writes a `0x03` byte at the start of the second and depacks the section after it. The decoded-size check (`len + 1 > 0x100000`, status 3) runs after depacking (DT2 1.16 `0x400cd20c`; the same 828-byte routine on DT2 1.17, DN2 1.11 and 1.12) {digikit-f06} {digikit-f01}. So an oversized stream is not refused cleanly: it overruns the buffer first. A dt2-machine-lab build with a 1,314,460-byte decoded stream hit a ColdFire exception on a unit and was withdrawn; the lab's repair encodes zero regions as fill blocks so the decoded stream fits {dt2-lab-capicola}. elekloader states the same limits for the DN2 ([`../devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md`](../devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md)). Count decoded bytes with a depacker, not the stored size (rule A46). `[hw]` The earlier README named sections 3 and 7 as patch targets. `[doc]` {digikit} {digikit-old}

The same 159,948-byte image (sha256 `6943b2f2...`) ships in Digitakt mk1 1.53, Digitone II 1.11, Analog Rytm MKII 1.73 and Analog Four 1.55D. Syntakt and Digitakt II carry a section 8 of the same size. It is not an FPGA bitstream (the FPGA is section 1, or inside section 7 on the Digitone mk1), and it is not code for the device's own CPU. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3} {analog-emu-a4} {rytm-fw-re}

facts.section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
facts.text: Preamble of the decoded byte stream: u32 container size + u32 content checksum, then the container (magic at offset 8). Container size: DN2 1,743,120, DN1 1,102,352 (the sizes of the file pair dnfw analysed). The content checksum is not a standard algorithm: a running 32-bit sum over big-endian words, each word XORed with its one-based index; trailing bytes that do not fill a word are excluded. Compressed sections carry a header with the stream length and a u32 sum of the stream bytes (padding excluded). `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

facts.section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
facts.text: SysEx transport: each message is `F0 ... F7`; the body is either a 126-byte data packet or a 14-byte marker; it starts with the manufacturer ID and a device ID: DN2 `0x15`, DT2 `0x14`, DN1 `0x0D`. Payloads use 8-in-7 encoding (116 encoded bytes carry 101 decoded bytes, last packet zero-padded); packet count = stream length / 101 + 1 (an exact division still adds a packet); a block and sequence counter starts from values in the start marker and wraps at 7 bits; the 7-bit packet checksum sits in the last body byte and uses a base value taken from the start marker, not a constant. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

facts.section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
facts.text: Trailer: the last 32 bytes of the declared container are an HMAC-SHA256 on the first 16-byte boundary at least 4 bytes past the last section (gap zeroed); it covers everything before it, padding included; the key is derived from material inside the image (a printable string in a decompressed section, found in the bootstrap, plus a fixed constant) - never edit that key material, the device likely verifies with its installed copy. DN1 1.42A is unsigned (trailer all zeros). `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

facts.section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
facts.text: Compression: each section is raw or aPLib-variant compressed (not flagged - inferred by whether the bytes depack): LZ77 with interlaced Elias-gamma codes, a biased offset, a last-offset reuse code and a length bonus for far matches, minimum match 2; Elektron's streams keep the furthest match within 1 MiB and the longest at 2,048 bytes. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

facts.section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
facts.text: DN1 vs DN2: bootstrap load address DN2 `0x02000000` / DN1 `0x02000800`; blob (id 7) compressed on DN2, raw on DN1; boot (id 6) absent on DN2, present (raw) on DN1; section 5 (meta) is 15 bytes, stored raw, no destination address, identical size on both; section 8 appears in OS 1.11 compressed (it is the Outbox 8 accessory firmware). `[doc]` {dn2-ele3} {dn2-cfw-handoff}

facts.section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
facts.text: After patching, recompute: re-encoded section data and its stream length/sum (+ padding to 4 bytes, table length includes the padding), section table offsets/lengths and 16-byte placement (and the count if sections change), the preamble (container size, content checksum), SysEx packet checksums/counters/packet count, and on DN2 the HMAC over everything before the trailer. The page does not say whether the product code, build string or version string must change, nor whether ids must be renumbered. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

facts.section: Flash procedure and link pitfalls (Digitone II, as practised by dn2mk2 and dnfw) / Numbers
facts.text: MIDI DIN runs at 31,250 baud, about 3,125 bytes/s; a 2,209,184-byte image needs at least ~12 minutes (derived, not timed). Do not interrupt. `[doc]` {dn2-flashing}

facts.section: Flash procedure and link pitfalls (Digitone II, as practised by dn2mk2 and dnfw) / Numbers
facts.text: Nothing is written until reception completes. The receiver has no error recovery: a bad sequence number or checksum freezes the progress bar with no message and no retransmit. Checksums and sequence counters are content-independent, so the receiver cannot tell a modified image from stock. `[doc]` {dn2-flashing} {dn2mk2-safety}

facts.section: Flash procedure and link pitfalls (Digitone II, as practised by dn2mk2 and dnfw) / The "stalls at ~80 %" problem
facts.text: Reported 2026-09-11: Transfer showed 100 % sent while the device bar froze near 80 %; stock 1.10E stalled over the same route, so the link was at fault, not the image. Root cause in that case: a Focusrite Scarlett 4i4's MIDI went idle mid-transfer and dropped packets; the stall point varied (30/70/80 %). `[hw]` {dn2-flashing}

facts.section: Flash procedure and link pitfalls (Digitone II, as practised by dn2mk2 and dnfw) / The "stalls at ~80 %" problem
facts.text: Fixes: prove the link with the stock firmware first; use a dedicated class-compliant USB-MIDI cable for long recovery transfers; disable Windows USB selective suspend and device power management; retry. `[hw]` {dn2-flashing} {dn2mk2-safety}

facts.section: Flash procedure and link pitfalls (Digitone II, as practised by dn2mk2 and dnfw) / The "stalls at ~80 %" problem

facts.text: CPU fingerprint: NXP MCF5441x (ColdFire V4m with EMAC) - UART8 `0xEC070000`, GPIO `0xEC094000`, eDMA `0xFC044000` (TCDs +0x1000), INTC0-2 `0xFC048000/0xFC04C000/0xFC050000`, DSPI0 `0xFC05C000`, PIT0-3 `0xFC080000-0xFC08C000`, EPORT `0xFC090000`. Stock Ghidra misdecodes EMAC line-A words; digikit uses a separate language spec. `[doc]` {digikit-f08}

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
facts.text: DDR is 128 MiB (DDRMC writes in the bootstrap; earlier 64 MiB claims are wrong): `0x40000000-0x47FFFFFF` cached (ACR0), `0x48000000-0x4FFFFFFF` an uncached alias of the same DDR used for DMA buffers; reset SP `0x48000000`; 32 MiB C++ heap above `0x44000000`. `[doc]` {digikit-f08}

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
facts.text: NOR flash 16 MiB, S25FL127S-class (RDID mfg 0x01, id 0x2018); the bootstrap's flash loop uses 512-byte pages and 256 KB erase blocks. The in-OS writer (finding 75) uses 0x100-byte pages and 0x10000 sectors from flash `0x80000` - two code paths, two geometries `[?]`. `[doc]` {digikit-f08} {digikit-f75}

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
facts.text: UART8 receive is done by eDMA (channel 34), not by reading the data register - an emulator must model eDMA, not just the UART. `[emu]` {digikit-f08}

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
facts.text: No ColdFire watchdog. Neither MAIN OS (DT2 1.16/1.17, DN2 1.11/1.12) nor the bootstrap names the core watchdog registers (CWCR `0xFC040016`, CWSR `0xFC04001B`), and the watchdog is off after reset. A ColdFire hang therefore stays hung until a power cycle; nothing resets the unit for you. Static reading; computed addresses are not excluded. Third-party MCF5441x code agrees that the core watchdog stays off after a power cycle unless software enables it, and CWCR can be written only once after reset (so a bootstrap write of 0 would also lock it off). `[doc]` {digikit-f17} {netburner-cwt} {nxp-mcf5441x-rm}

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
facts.text: eMMC part table: DT2 1.16 (`0x402b4a24`) and DN2 1.10E/1.11 (`0x4029f554`) accept the same seven 32-byte entries: Kingston parts `TX2932` and `TS0A32`, both 32 GB, matching the Kingston EMMC32G-TX29 on a DN2 board photo. Shared ColdFire storage code: the block driver, the MmcFs slot store and the transfer routing; the sample filesystem, its request handler and the sample manager are DT2-only. `[doc]` {dn2-drive}

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
facts.text: eMMC card (both, about 32 GB part, 0x2E1A000 sectors assumed): sectors `0x0-0x457FFF` belong to the firmware (boot, tables, projects, pools, presets); MmcFs refuses writes at `0x457FFF` and above. DT2 1.17: factory sample table "MaGj" at `0x458000` and 1,265 factory samples to `0x5D7FFF` - never touch; +Drive (ekFS) `0x5D8000-0x2DF017F`; `0x2DF0180` to the end unused. DN2 1.12: nothing stock writes at `0x458000` and up; FORMAT trims only up to `0x457FFF`. Unchecked bank ids in the Data API can reach every sector below `0x800000` over USB - put any private store above that line (digikit: DT2 `0x2DF1000+`, DN2 `0x800000+`). Not checked on a real card. `[doc]` {digikit-f59}

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
facts.text: Card pools inside the firmware area (MmcFs) `[emu]` {digikit-samples}: Fixed slots: projects 0-127 (16 MiB each on both), sounds 0-2047 (DT2 4 KiB, DN2 1 KiB), kits 0-1023 (DT2 64 KiB, DN2 32 KiB). The bitmaps at sector `0x800` are write-protect padlocks, not occupancy. The boot project (magic "COKi") has two copies at sectors `0x40000` and `0x48000`. The working project is at `0x50000` and is rewritten from the boot copy at every start. The DT2 has a path filesystem (ekFS +Drive) for samples. The DN2 has none: only the MmcFs pools. Card layouts are device data (digikit `devices/<device>.toml`).

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / ColdFire code caves and mod RAM (dnfw `code-caves.md`, `mod-memory-regions.md`, DN2 1.11)
facts.text: RAM aliases every `0x08000000`: a byte answers at nine addresses up to `0x8c000000`. ACR0 caches only the first window, and stock reaches its DMA buffers through the second (`0x4e......`). Scan all nine windows before you call RAM unreferenced. `[doc]`

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / ColdFire code caves and mod RAM (dnfw `code-caves.md`, `mod-memory-regions.md`, DN2 1.11)
facts.text: Flashed bytes above the reset clear do not survive a reset (DT2 1.16 clears from `0x40312000`; on the DN2 about 3,200 B separate the end of MAIN OS from the clear). Code placed there must be copied up by a loader *after* the clear. digikit, dnfw and elekloader all do this. `[hw]` (bytes lost on a DT2)

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / ColdFire code caves and mod RAM (dnfw `code-caves.md`, `mod-memory-regions.md`, DN2 1.11)
facts.text: The DN2's code region has no free run of even 24 bytes. Zero runs exist in the constants region, and code there does execute (a boot-path cave printed "CAVE RAN!!!" on a real DN2). One "free" run was an array the code fills at run time: patching it crashed the unit, and the emulator watch read zeros. Two static checks catch most cases: a fixed stride between equal gaps marks an array, and `lea`/`pea`/`move.l #` operands mark referenced space. On 1.11 only 13 runs (4,207 B) pass both, not the "~29 KB" first assumed. `[hw]` ([I19](../INCIDENTS.md#i19-patching-a-free-zero-run-crashed-the-unit))

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / ColdFire code caves and mod RAM (dnfw `code-caves.md`, `mod-memory-regions.md`, DN2 1.11)
facts.text: Displaced stock instructions are replayed at another address, so no PC-relative instructions in the displaced bytes. Pick hook sites whose first instructions are absolute. `[doc]`

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / ColdFire code caves and mod RAM (dnfw `code-caves.md`, `mod-memory-regions.md`, DN2 1.11)
facts.text: dnfw's mods take fixed RAM chunks in `0x46700000-0x47fe0000` (waverider 436 KB at `0x4670c000`/`0x467f0000`/`0x46a00000`, lfo4 `0x46800000`/`0x46900000`, ...). The alternative is the stock 32 MiB buddy heap (`0x4464abf0`), where the allocator records the use but a 12.9 MB project load takes half. Mods that store settings in unused pattern bits must not claim the same bits. `[doc]`

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Digitone II: who uses the RAM above the reset clear (compared across five projects, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: Stock does not touch `0x46710000-0x47ffffcc` in emulation. Three independent checks agree: dn2-cfw's write watches over `0x46800000-0x47f00000`, elekloader's canary over `0x46710000-0x48000000` (cold boot, two panel sessions), and digikit's reference scan (`0x4671a000-0x47fe0000` unreferenced, [`dt2-dn2-limits-and-audio-chain.md`](dt2-dn2-limits-and-audio-chain.md)). All three ran in an emulator, so rule A43 (canary on a unit) still applies. `[emu]`

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Digitone II: who uses the RAM above the reset clear (compared across five projects, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: The range from `0x46700000` up to `0x46710000` is not free. On 1.12 it holds the end of the DMA buffers; on 1.11 the MMC bounce buffer reaches `0x46701300`. dnfw's lfo4 state sat at `0x46700000` until 2026-10-11 and corrupted every project saved on an LFO4 unit (the bounce buffer carries each piece of a project on save and load); it now lives in the first block of stock's heap (`0x4464abf0`). dnfw's remaining `0x4670xxxx` chunks (from `0x46708000`) are above the 1.11 DMA section (`0x466b8000-0x46701340`) but inside the 1.12 one, so they must move for a 1.12 port. The "25.3 MB unclaimed above BSS" figure in dnfw's memory map missed these alias references. The skill's "`0x46700000..0x46900000` unused, hardware-confirmed" disagrees: see [CONFLICTS S17](../CONFLICTS.md). `[doc]`

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Digitone II: who uses the RAM above the reset clear (compared across five projects, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: The platforms collide. dnfw's lfo4 code, cfmod's default link address and the start of dn2-cfw's mod area are all `0x46800000`; cfkit's scratch at `0x46a00000` is Waverider's chunk. Only elekloader's `0x47f00000` and dn2-cfw's core `0x47e00000` are disjoint from the rest. A mod built for one platform cannot be dropped into another's image without moving its RAM (and its hooks: [`dt2-dn2-limits-and-audio-chain.md`](dt2-dn2-limits-and-audio-chain.md) section 6, [`agent-workflow.md`](agent-workflow.md)). Before picking an address, check this table and declare every range you use. The full register, with every platform's ranges per OS and the overlaps, is [`../RAM-TENANCY.md`](../RAM-TENANCY.md) (task T23).

facts.section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Acknowledgement and buffering
facts.text: The menu route sends no SysEx reply at all; only the screen shows progress. Pace by time: digikit uses 128-byte messages every 2 ms (about 29 s DT2, 37 s DN2) - 12x slower than the emulated ceiling; not run on hardware.

facts.section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Acknowledgement and buffering
facts.text: The whole container is staged in RAM; flash is untouched until the last message. A transfer cut before the footer leaves the screen on "Receiving" and nothing validated, erased or written. Power loss during the flash phase leaves the container area partly erased; the bootstrap (`0x40000`) is never written by this path, so FUNC boot menu and DIN OS UPGRADE stay usable (emulated).

facts.section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Validation (before any erase; run up to three times)
facts.text: No "UPGRADE OS NOW?" on the menu route in the emulator: the delegate returns "do not ask", so after the last message the screen goes ERASING FLASH... -> SUCCESS! REBOOTING -> reset with no key pressed. Real hardware may differ (no derived delegate class was found). NO while receiving asks "CANCEL OS UPGRADE?".

facts.section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Validation (before any erase; run up to three times)
facts.text: The flash writer ignores erase/program return codes - "Success" is shown whatever the chips did. It erases sector by sector from flash `0x80000` (default sector 0x10000) and programs 0x100-byte pages, waits 3 s, soft-resets via `0x80 -> 0xec090000`.

facts.section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Rules that follow
facts.text: Prefer the RPC route with explicit End; send End 0 on every abort. Do not resend Writes blindly; a failed run costs only a new Start.

facts.section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Rules that follow
facts.text: A "Success!" screen does not prove the flash was written correctly - verify by version string / behaviour after reboot.

facts.section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Rules that follow
facts.text: Never rely on the in-OS path for recovery; it needs a working MAIN OS. The bootstrap route (DIN) is the recovery.

facts.section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Rules that follow
facts.text: Digitone II has no build floor in the validator - an older signed image is accepted; Digitakt II refuses builds below 0060.

facts.section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / USB device side of Digitakt II / Digitone II (digikit finding 42, static, DT2 1.16)
facts.text: Controller: MCF5441x USB OTG at `0xFC0B0000`, device mode, external ULPI PHY, high speed (480 Mb/s; descriptors have 512-byte bulk packets; DEVICE_QUALIFIER stalled = HS-only). Only endpoints EP0-EP3 exist. VID `0x1935`. `[doc]` {digikit-f42}

facts.section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / USB device side of Digitakt II / Digitone II (digikit finding 42, static, DT2 1.16)
facts.text: Modes -> descriptors: USB MIDI PID `0x012b` (EP1 bulk pair, 2 cables); USB AUDIO/MIDI PID `0x102b` (UAC2 iso on EP2/EP3 + MIDI on EP1); OVERBRIDGE PID `0x0b2b` (vendor class 0xFF: interrupt EP3 in/out, EP2 OUT bulk 512 + EP2 IN interrupt 64, plus MIDI on EP1); a service mode PID `0xffff` with CDC-ACM. No MS-OS/BOS descriptors - Windows will not bind WinUSB on its own. `[doc]` {digikit-f42}

facts.section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / USB device side of Digitakt II / Digitone II (digikit finding 42, static, DT2 1.16)
facts.text: In USB AUDIO/MIDI mode on the DT2/DN2 EP2 OUT is unused; digikit adds a bulk OUT interface there at boot. `[hw]` {digikit-f123-bulk}

facts.section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / USB device side of Digitakt II / Digitone II (digikit finding 42, static, DT2 1.16)
facts.text: SysEx throughput is limited by the ColdFire's per-byte handling (about 32 instructions per wire byte just to split USB-MIDI events, two 512-byte receive buffers in flight); digikit estimates 0.8-1.4 MB/s at best for an own SysEx route. Transfer's file-write RPC: OpenFileForWrite `0x40`, WriteFileV1 `0x42` (handle, length, offset, data), CloseFileWriter `0x41`. `[doc]` {digikit-f42}

facts.section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / USB device side of Digitakt II / Digitone II (digikit finding 42, static, DT2 1.16)
facts.text: Samples are not converted on the device: the native file is a 0x40-byte header (+1 stereo flag, +4 length, +8 rate 48000) + big-endian int16 PCM + 16-byte trailer; no WAV parser in the image. The host must resample to 48 kHz and convert. `[doc]` {digikit-f42}

facts.section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / Overbridge refuses a mod whose version field changed (Digiwerk OB01, DN2 1.12)
facts.text: The container's 4-byte version field (header `+0x14`, `1.12` on stock) is sent to the computer by the main OS. A build that writes its own name there (e.g. `CMP1`) makes the Overbridge plugin answer "Device is not running compatible OS Version" and fail to open. The engine itself connects; the refusal comes from the plugin. `[hw]`

facts.section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / Overbridge refuses a mod whose version field changed (Digiwerk OB01, DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Fix: patch the two main-OS sites that send the version so they send a header copy with `1.12`. The flash and the power-on screen keep the build's name. Overbridge and Transfer work again on the unit (2026-10-22). `[hw]`

facts.section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / Overbridge refuses a mod whose version field changed (Digiwerk OB01, DN2 1.12)

facts.section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / Confirmed on a Digitakt mk1 with a Raspberry Pi as host (digitakt-sidecar-pi, OS 1.54)
facts.text: Alt setting 3: interrupt endpoint `0x83` IN, 368 bytes, and `0x03` OUT, 88 bytes. Seven frames per packet, a 32-byte header and big-endian int32 words, with input data 24-bit in 32-bit words. The measured cadence is 47,999.5 frames/s.

facts.section: Recovery and flashing / Rules of thumb (all from the sources above)
facts.text: A mod can break the normal USB update path without anyone noticing until the next update. On Overtone 1.0 (Digitone II), an OS sent with Transfer stopped at "Receiving" or "PREPARING..." and wrote nothing. The only way off it was the STARTUP menu over DIN, about 15 minutes. Test "install the next build over USB" as part of every release (rule A36). `[hw]` {overtone} ([I22](../INCIDENTS.md#i22-a-mod-broke-the-normal-usb-update-path))

facts.section: Recovery and flashing / Rules of thumb (all from the sources above)
facts.text: Test your DIN interface before you need it. On a DT2, a generic "USB2.0-MIDI" cable adapter (VID 1a86, PID 752d) delivered nothing, while a controller's DIN out worked. Cheap cable adapters are known to drop or mangle long SysEx; a stock-OS dry run with your exact cable is the only proof. `[hw]` {dt2-lab-coldfire-fix} ([I44](../INCIDENTS.md#i44-recovery-used-on-a-digitakt-ii-after-a-crashing-build-a-cheap-cable-delivered-nothing))

facts.section: Recovery and flashing / Additions from the "read everything" pass (2026-10-31)
facts.text: Digitakt II (digitakt-ii-research `RECOVERY.md`): keep an official stock `.syx`, a physical MIDI interface and cable ready; MIDI OUT of the interface to the Digitakt II's MIDI IN (USB MIDI cannot be used); hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4 = OS UPGRADE; in Elektron Transfer open the SYSEX TRANSFER page and choose "OS upgrade via device startup menu"; select the stock file and keep power on until the unit reboots. No durations are given and the author states recovery is not guaranteed if the startup menu or bootloader cannot run, power is lost during a critical write, or storage/hardware is damaged; the page reports no hardware test of the procedure. `[doc]` {dt2-recovery}

facts.section: Recovery and flashing / Additions from the "read everything" pass (2026-10-31)
facts.text: Syntakt (SyntHack OS `RECOVERY.md`): if the OS still boots, flash the stock `.syx` via Transfer's Drop page (works even if a mod misbehaved); if not, MIDI interface with a 5-pin OUT to the Syntakt's MIDI IN ("USB doesn't work from the startup menu"), FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4, Transfer SYSEX TRANSFER "OS Upgrade via device startup menu", tens of minutes at 31.25 kbit/s, the unit restarts itself. Avoid TRIG 2 (empty reset) and TRIG 3 (factory reset) in the startup menu - both erase data. Do a dry run of the DIN procedure with the stock OS before the first flash; flash only files for which `tools/unpack/eft.py info <file>` reports `checksums : ok`; no hardware results are reported on the page. `[doc]` {synthack-recovery}

facts.section: Recovery and flashing / Additions from the "read everything" pass (2026-10-31)
facts.text: Other Elektron devices, from elekloader's BUILDING.md (for reference): Analog Rytm MKII and Analog Four MKII - FUNC at power-on (STARTUP menu), TRIG 4, stock `.syx` over 5-pin DIN MIDI, USB does not work. Octatrack - hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 3 = MIDI UPGRADE, DIN MIDI; normal flashing from the card (PROJECT > SYSTEM > USB DISK MODE, copy the `.bin`, then PROJECT > SYSTEM > OS UPGRADE, power-cycle once more before judging). Digitakt mk1 / Digitone mk1: FUNC, TRIG 4, legacy mode; the connection is not stated for these two. Per-device notes: [`analog-rytm.md`](../devices/analog-rytm.md), [`digitakt.md`](../devices/digitakt.md), [`digitone.md`](../devices/digitone.md). `[doc]` {elekloader-building}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Official
facts.text: Each device's manual contains the MIDI implementation (CC and NRPN tables, "Appendix B" in the Digitakt II manual for OS 1.03 per the MCP project). The tables of the current Digitakt II, Digitone II and Analog Heat +FX manuals are transcribed below under "Official CC and NRPN tables". These are the only vendor-documented parts. `[doc]` {digitakt-midi-mcp}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Official
facts.text: Elektron Transfer is the official tool for dumps, backups and OS upgrades; its legacy OS-upgrade mode is the DIN-MIDI path. {elektron-dt2-notes}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Framing and encoding
facts.text: SysEx frame starts `F0 00 20 3C` (Elektron manufacturer ID `00 20 3C`), then device ID and command. `[doc]` {digitakt-midi-mcp} {syxgrid}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Framing and encoding
facts.text: Elektron uses its own 7-bit encoding of 8-bit data, ported from elk-herd into SYXGRID and digi-roll-studio. Decode before analysing dumps, otherwise nothing makes sense. `[doc]` {syxgrid} {digi-roll-studio}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Framing and encoding
facts.text: Digitone mk1 device ID is `0x0D`; its pattern format differs from Digitone II and SYXGRID rejects it. The DN2's is `0x15`. All known device bytes: [firmware-container.md](firmware-container.md#sysex-device-byte-per-device-merged-from-the-projects-that-decode-these-files). `[doc]` {syxgrid}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Framing and encoding
facts.text: Two protocol generations: the Digitakt II / Digitone II speak "gen-2"; Analog Four speaks "gen-1" with a different pattern format and a slower wire. `[doc]` {digi-roll-studio}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Framing and encoding
facts.text: Digitone II library contains Digitone mk1 preset files, which use a second container format (refuse foreign formats by magic bytes). `[doc]` {digi-roll-studio}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Framing and encoding
facts.text: Container structure and checksums for older machines are best documented in libanalogrytm (Analog Rytm only; no Analog Heat); the frame, packing and checksum match the newer devices, the type bytes do not (section "Dump messages and device ids across generations" below). `[doc]` {libanalogrytm}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: One dump frame for every generation compared: `F0 00 20 3C <device> <dev id> <type> 01 01 <index> <packed payload> <checksum hi lo> <count hi lo> F7`. The Rytm writes the same `01 01` version field ("OS 1.02c" in libanalogrytm), the same index byte and the same trailer. `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: The same 7-bit packing: groups of one header byte plus up to 7 data bytes; header bit 6 holds the MSB of the first data byte, bit 0 that of the seventh; a short last group keeps its header. syxgrid's DN2 field "control byte 101506, mask `0x40`, payload 101507" is exactly this rule (first byte of a group). `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol} {syxgrid-map}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: The same checksum and count: checksum = sum of the packed payload bytes (header bytes included) mod 2^14, sent as two 7-bit bytes, high first; count = packed length + 5 (checksum, count and `F7`), also mod 2^14. syxgrid recomputed the checksum over raw bytes `[10, 114113)` and matched the DN2's own on every fixture. A DN2 pattern message is 114,118 bytes, so its count field wraps; tools must not use it as a length. `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol} {syxgrid-map}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: Requests: an empty payload, trailer `00 00 00 05` (checksum 0, count 5) on both generations; the Rytm's request is 15 bytes, `F0 00 20 3C 07 00 <id> 01 01 <nr> 00 00 00 05 F7`. `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: The type bytes differ, so never reuse a type table across devices: Rytm: dumps `0x52` kit, `0x53` sound, `0x54` pattern, `0x55` song, `0x56` settings, `0x57` global; `0x58-0x5D` the same objects from the unsaved work buffer; requests `0x62-0x6D` the same way. Digitakt / Digitakt II / Digitone II: `0x50` pattern plus kit in one message, `0x51` pattern, `0x52` kit, `0x53` sound, `0x54` project settings; requests `0x60-0x64`, and `0x6F` asks for the whole project. So `0x54` is a Rytm pattern but a DT2/DN2 project-settings message. syxgrid's guess "`0x53` = kit" for the DN2 (graded D, unknown) is a sound dump by digi-roll's table. `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol} {syxgrid-map}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: The index byte on receive: a DN2 stores a received pattern in the slot armed on the device, not in the index the message carries (syxgrid, on a unit). libanalogrytm does not say what a Rytm does with it. `[hw]` {syxgrid-map}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: Device byte in dumps: Rytm (libanalogrytm's era, MKI) `0x07`; Digitakt `0x0A`; Digitakt II `0x14`; Digitone II `0x15`. A DN2 answered only `0x15` in a sweep and ignored `0x0B-0x0E`, `0x14` and `0x16`. The same bytes appear in the OS files ([`firmware-container.md`](firmware-container.md)). `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol} Three different device ids. They are easy to mix up, and the same number means different devices in different namespaces:

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: `0x14` is the Digitakt II's SysEx byte but the Digitone mk1's product id; `0x0A` is the Digitakt's SysEx byte but the Analog Heat's product id. Name the namespace whenever you write an id down.

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: Elektroid reads the product id from byte 5 of the decoded `Device` (Ping) reply and looks it up in its device table; digi-roll captured 42 and 43 from a DT2 and a DN2 the same way. The FAQ table on elektron.se (Heat `000A`, Digitakt `000C`, Digitone `0014`, Heat MKII `0016`, Model:Samples `0019`, Model:Cycles `001B`, Digitone Keys `001C`) matches Elektroid's table entry for entry, so that table lists product ids. `[doc]` {elektroid-devices} {digi-roll-protocol} {elektron-faq}

facts.text: Elektroid's further product ids: Analog Four `0x04`, Analog Keys `0x06`, Analog Rytm `0x08`, Analog Four MKII `0x0E`, Analog Rytm MKII `0x10`, Syntakt `0x1E`. facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Digitone II pattern dump: hardware-confirmed offsets (syxgrid's map v1.13.0, CC BY 4.0, facts restated)
facts.text: Message: product byte `0x15`, message type `0x50` (pattern). A pattern dump is 114,118 bytes. The body from raw byte 10 to 114113 is 7-bit packed (one control byte per 7 payload bytes); "decoded" offsets below are into the unpacked payload.

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Digitone II pattern dump: hardware-confirmed offsets (syxgrid's map v1.13.0, CC BY 4.0, facts restated)
facts.text: Slot: raw byte 9 is the slot the device dumped from (0 = A01 ... 127 = H16), not a destination. A received pattern is stored in the slot armed on the device, advancing by one per pattern.

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Digitone II pattern dump: hardware-confirmed offsets (syxgrid's map v1.13.0, CC BY 4.0, facts restated)
facts.text: Step states: at decoded `4 + 1187*(track-1) + 2*(step-1)`, two bytes per step, 16 tracks x 128 steps. Odd-step trig `03 81`, even-step trig `03 91`. `03 90` / `03 80` (bit 0 clear) is not an occupied step. First byte `0x78` = trigless trig (parameter automation, no note).

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Digitone II pattern dump: hardware-confirmed offsets (syxgrid's map v1.13.0, CC BY 4.0, facts restated)
facts.text: Trigger records: at decoded `18996`, 6 bytes each, up to 8,192 records. Fields: track, step, note, velocity (`0xFF` = track default), length index (`0xFF` = inherit), and a signed micro-timing byte (1/384 note, -23..+23). A record is free when its track byte is `0xFF`; nothing terminates the table, so skip and keep scanning. Chords are stored as all primary notes first, then all chord extras.

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / The panel wire protocol (digikit finding 58, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12) `[doc]`
facts.text: Remote control without touching the UART: the firmware's button decoder `f(channel, new_mask)` (DT2 1.17 `0x4011e318`, DN2 1.12 `0x4011fc8c`) and encoder decoder `f(encoder0, delta)` (`0x4011e598` / `0x4011ff0c`) can be called from a mod. Mask SR to `0x2700` around the call; the decoders do unprotected read-modify-write. Neither checks the channel (safe: buttons 0-6, encoders 0-8). An encoder turn is ignored for 40 ticks after its click key is released. `[emu]`

facts.text: DIN MIDI runs on UART9 (`0xec074000`, 31,250 baud, receive by eDMA channel 36). The front panel talks over UART8 (`0xec070000`). Panel key codes used by emulators: SETTINGS 8, FUNC 17, YES 10, NO 12, UP 11, DOWN 14, LEFT 13, RIGHT 15. `[emu]`

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Hardware ports and the hidden service console (DT2 1.16 / DN2 1.11)
facts.text: Maintenance mode (a power-on key combination, or a reboot marker) presents a USB CDC-ACM serial port, VID `0x1935` PID `0xFFFF`. It speaks a line protocol: `#COMMAND\n` text lines, `!` + 4-byte big-endian length for binary frames. About 60 factory commands. Read-only examples: `#HELLO` (answers "HOW DO YOU DO?"), `#STATUS` (reports `PLATFORM PCBA0109..`, `PRODUCT 52;5;15;Digitone II`), `#READ_SERIAL` (the "SERI" record at flash `0x3C0000`). Writing commands change persistent state: `#WRITE_SERIAL`, `#WRITE_TESTED`, `#WRITE_UI_TESTED`, `#WRITE_AUDIO_TESTED`, `#MMC_RECONFIGURE`, `#WRITE`, `#UPGRADE`, `#FULL_UPGRADE` (unchecked flash path, see `os-update-protocol.md`). Agents never send these. `[doc]` (digi-roll-studio's ceremony - copy it) 1. Re-read and back up the whole destination pattern first; abort if the backup fails. 2. The target's OS build must be on an allowlist. 3. The user confirms a dialog listing the changes. 4. Change only the bytes that must change. 5. Read the result back and byte-compare. Also: keep a local stash of overwritten patterns (50) plus pre-restore snapshots (10). `[hw]` {digi-roll-studio}

A forum user reports that the Digitakt II manual lists no CC values for the Euclidean sequencer parameters and that some Euclidean NRPNs misbehaved before OS 1.10 ("Some NRPN parameters regarding the Euclidean sequencer didn't work as intended" is in the 1.10 notes). The Octatrack is said to be the only Elektron device that answers a CC request. Manuals are updated with every OS - always use the one for the OS in hand. `[?]` {elektronauts-dt2-sample-slot} {elektronauts-heat-midi} {elektron-dt2-notes}

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / Compilers and builders
facts.text: selache pitfalls that halt a real DSP but run in the emulator (elekloader ADAPTING.md, Nov 2026; the first matches 70b185's DT2 finding): A shift by a negative immediate (`LSHIFT R1 BY -16`) is encoded without sign extension. Put the count in a register (`R2 = -16; R1 = LSHIFT R1 BY R2;`). elekloader's lint flags candidates, but it cannot see instruction boundaries, so check each one in the listing. A C function whose locals sit more than ~63 words from the frame pointer is compiled wrongly. One large local array is enough. Keep large buffers static or in the voice state. `[hw]` {elekloader-adapting} {own-dt2-notes}

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / Compilers and builders
facts.text: Two projects compared selache's VISA decoder with digikit's table decoder on the DN2 stock program, and agree on where each is wrong. The test: walk instruction by instruction between known starts (branch targets, `cjump` sites, DO-loop ends) and see who lands exactly. `[doc]` {dn2-selache} {dn2-cfw-t31} selache's disassembler gives some 48-bit forms as 32-bit (Type 3a `59be`, Type 4a `6a3e`, Type 7a `043e`, Type 16a `9980`) and one 32-bit form as 48-bit (Type 3b `593e`); DO-loop ends land on the table decoder's starts 85 of 85 times, on selache's 64 of 85, and selache prints most DO offsets with bit 23 set. digikit's table had Type 2b wrong (the programming guide's `000000011`, not the reference's `110000000`; selache won 119 to 0) and wrongly ruled out `Type10a_rel` in VISA; both fixed in digikit#31. Its `undoc16/48` forms are still provisional. A two-byte-late start still lands 94.9 % of spans, because VISA resynchronises within a few instructions. A decoder's score means something only against that control.

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / Compilers and builders
facts.text: Disassembled text is not a patch format. 11,440 distinct encodings from the DN2's L2 program, each disassembled with selmap and reassembled alone with selas: 83.9 % came back identical; 1,265 kept their width but lost register fields the text does not show (`bitrev`, `modify`, `dm` moves); 216 changed width; 320 printed forms could not be parsed; 40 crashed the assembler. A 48-bit `nop` reassembles as the 16-bit one. Patch from source, and compare bytes (rule A41). `[doc]` {dn2-selache}

facts.text: Family covered: MCF54410 and MCF54415-MCF54418. Peripherals with drivers: GPIO, PIT, INTC, eDMA, UART, DSPI, eSDHC (eMMC block reads via eDMA), SSI (I2S/network audio, full-duplex eDMA rings), USB OTG device mode (high speed via ULPI PHY; 54415-54418 only). Not implemented there: eSDHC writes, EPORT, DMA timers, I2C, RTC, PWM, ADC/DAC, FlexCAN, Ethernet, NAND, USB host.

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / Writing fast ColdFire C (digigrain's measured notes, Digitakt mk1, gcc `-mcpu=54455 -O2`)
facts.text: Shift immediates only reach 8. A shift by 14 or 15 costs a `moveq` plus a register shift; a shift by 16 is `swap` (+ `ext.l`). Arrange fixed-point products to land on a 16-bit boundary (e.g. store tables as unsigned Q16 so that `(s*w16) >> 16` equals `(s*w15) >> 15` exactly).

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / Writing fast ColdFire C (digigrain's measured notes, Digitakt mk1, gcc `-mcpu=54455 -O2`)
facts.text: `muls.l` and hardware divide are there; libgcc is not linked, so avoid 64-bit math (hand-write it).

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / Writing fast ColdFire C (digigrain's measured notes, Digitakt mk1, gcc `-mcpu=54455 -O2`)
facts.text: Prove the bounds once per block, then run a loop without checks, with state in locals. Keep the checked loop as the fallback near buffer ends.

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / Writing fast ColdFire C (digigrain's measured notes, Digitakt mk1, gcc `-mcpu=54455 -O2`)
facts.text: Mark hot loops `noinline`: an inlined, merged loop kept a branch inside and spilled to the stack (~45 instructions per sample). `do { } while (--n)` saves the count test.

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / Writing fast ColdFire C (digigrain's measured notes, Digitakt mk1, gcc `-mcpu=54455 -O2`)
facts.text: Specialise on loop-invariant cases: unity-speed grains skip interpolation (13 vs ~26 instructions per sample); a cached per-voice window table replaces per-sample shape blending.

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / Writing fast ColdFire C (digigrain's measured notes, Digitakt mk1, gcc `-mcpu=54455 -O2`)
facts.text: EMAC in fractional mode (MACSR `0x20`: signed fractional, truncating, no saturation): save and restore MACSR, ACC0 and ACCEXT01, and clear ACC0 first. Bit-exact Python models must truncate each product as `floor(x*y/2^23)`, keeping 8 bits below the LSB.

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / Writing fast ColdFire C (digigrain's measured notes, Digitakt mk1, gcc `-mcpu=54455 -O2`)
facts.text: Hooks must preserve every register the caller relies on. Real bugs: a chord hook missed a4-a6, a callee clobbered a0, and a restoring `movem` lost a decision kept in d7. Test hooks with a stub that junks all scratch registers.

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / Writing fast ColdFire C (digigrain's measured notes, Digitakt mk1, gcc `-mcpu=54455 -O2`)
facts.text: Write a C reference and a bit-exact Python model first, and optimise only while the model's tests stay green.

facts.text: Entry point for firmware questions: `coldfire/fw.py` (commands `fn`, `decomp`, `disasm`, `callers`, `callees`, `xref`, `path`, `str`, `class`, `port`, `search`, `atlas`, `sql`, `batch`) on top of `coldfire/atlas.py build IMAGE...`, which builds a SQLite atlas (machines, parameters, classes, UI strings, structs, manual terms; every row with provenance and confidence). facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / digikit tool index in short (docs/TOOLS.md) - what an agent can reuse
facts.text: Facts: sections `section_3_MAIN_OS.bin` (ColdFire) and `section_7_BLOB.bin` (SHARC+ loader stream); the DSP firmware is a stream of writes to mapped memory, not one flat executable - address mapping and last-write order matter; SHARC import uses `SHARC_VISA:LE:32:default`, DM data addresses are byte addresses; default DSP stack range DM `[0x26f000, 0x2c0000)` (derived from an untouched gap, an assumption); example eDMA facts: `TCD50.CITER` at `0xfc045654`, DMA channel 50 connects SSI0 TFE0 to vector 170, vector 191 is an unassigned source with an `INTFRCH1` software-force bit; images named `dt2-1.16`, `dt2-1.17`, `dn2`. `[doc]` {digikit-tools}

facts.text: digiemu patches Unicorn (six patches) - details in [`../devices/digitakt.md`](../devices/digitakt.md); dn2mk2 reports that stock Unicorn's destructive SR read corrupts condition flags, so a patched Unicorn is mandatory for any ColdFire work. `[doc]` {digiemu-readme} {dn2mk2-emulator}

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / More emulators and directory snapshots (2026-10-31)
facts.text: Stock Unicorn 2.1.4 (and QEMU master as of 2026-09-15) gets ColdFire wrong in ways that change results (emu-elektron's patch notes) `[doc]` {emu-elektron-patches}: Condition codes: they are committed lazily, so a hook or a counted stop in mid-block sees stale flags, and the next branch goes the wrong way. MAC/MSAC with load is decoded wrongly in four ways: Ry with bit 0 or 1 set faults as "dual accumulate" on a CFV4E; Rx is always D2; MSAC adds instead of subtracting (this also hits MSAC without load); MASK is applied to every load address. The DT2 main OS reaches one of these at `0x400db9e0`. EMAC fractional and signed arithmetic is wrong (as found by SyntHack and octabam). EMAC saturation with MACSR.OMC gets its sign and constants wrong. Any ColdFire emulator built on Unicorn needs these fixes before its audio or branch results mean anything. emu-elektron carries all of them as patches for five devices.

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / More emulators and directory snapshots (2026-10-31)
facts.text: Directory views of the tools: {alt-tools} lists digikit, elekloader, digiscreen (Android page mirroring the 128x64 screen over USB MIDI), Elektron Emu, digiemu, ghidra-dsp56300, digi-roll, Elektroid, Overwitch and elektron-firmware-tool (the page names no source for the last one). elektronmods' Mod List ({em-list}) has 59 entries; its Analog Heat filter shows only Overwitch and elektron-firmware-tool.

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / More emulators and directory snapshots (2026-10-31)
facts.text: Unicorn's `emu_start(count=N)` puts a hidden code hook on every address. With a code hook covering every address, every instruction also walks all other code hooks (dn2mk2's gate has about 330). Replacing `count=` with a budget in translated blocks took dn2mk2's longest ColdFire gate step from 3,250 s to 161 s, with every report byte-identical; running out of the budget now raises instead of stopping silently. Not usable where the instruction count is the measurement (digikit's boot counts instructions on purpose). `[emu]` {dn2mk2-gatespeed}

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / More emulators and directory snapshots (2026-10-31)
facts.text: A pure-Python SHARC emulator runs about 4x faster under PyPy (dn2mk2's ten SHARC runner parts: about 181 to 44 min) with every emulated value identical; only numpy results computed after the run differ in the last digits. dn2mk2 re-runs those steps under CPython after each release as a cross-check. `[emu]` {dn2mk2-gatespeed}

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / More emulators and directory snapshots (2026-10-31)
facts.text: CPU readings from an instruction-counting emulator sit far under the unit's. analog-emu's unit timing (`DTEMU_TIMING`, "unit" sampled at about real time, "exact" at about 0.6x) charges the core's cycles and memory waits. On the Rytm MKII the unit's readings were all taken with the Sidecar Pi streaming Overbridge both ways (about 6,857 blocks of 368 bytes a second each way), and elekloader's core 0.10/0.11 memcpy/memset wrappers also run for that stream's handlers. Without the stream the emulator read core 0.11 builds about 14 points low; with it, nine of eleven calibration builds came within about 3.6 points of the unit. elkbench fails an emulator run at 95 % CPU or more and warns above 90 %. `[emu]`, calibrated against units {elkbench-timing}

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / More emulators and directory snapshots (2026-10-31)
facts.text: Ghidra and EMAC `[?]`: digikit found that stock Ghidra misdecodes the EMAC line-A words of the MCF5441x and uses a separate language (`68000:BE:32:ColdfireEMAC`). The owner's Heat research notes that Ghidra has known EMAC variants since GP-2197. Check the EMAC decode of your Ghidra version on a known MAC instruction before you trust it. {digikit-f08} {own-heatfx-notes}

hypotheses.inference: Each unit has three different ids: SysEx device byte, product id, Overbridge USB id. Expected: DT2 `0x14` / `0x2A` / USB `0x0B2B`; DT1 `0x0A` / `0x0C` / `0x0B2C`; DN2 `0x15` / `0x2B` / `0x0B34`; Heat +FX `0x13` / `0x20` / `0x0B53`. The USB id's low byte changes with the USB mode (`0x012B` MIDI, `0x102B` audio/MIDI on the DT2).
hypotheses.test: Read the USB ids in each USB mode (`lsusb` on Linux, System Information on a Mac, Device Manager on Windows). Read the product id with Elektroid's device info.

hypotheses.inference: Unsaved edits survive a power cycle on the DT2 and the DT1 as on the DN2, because the stock edit writer stores each edit in the sound record at once.
hypotheses.test: On a throwaway project, turn a filter knob, do not save, power-cycle. Is the value still there? Also try a parameter lock.

hypotheses.inference: A received pattern dump lands in the slot armed on the unit, not in the slot its index byte names (shown on the DN2 by syxgrid).
hypotheses.test: On a throwaway project, send a pattern dump with index A05 while A02 is armed, using Elektroid or digi-roll. Where does it land?

hypotheses.inference: The DT1 recorder holds at most 33.0 s (1,584,000 frames at 48 kHz, mono).
hypotheses.test: Record with free length until it stops; time it.

hypotheses.inference: Overbridge rejects a modified OS whose container version field differs from stock (shown on the DN2, Digiwerk OB01).
hypotheses.test: No new flash needed if you already have builds: does Overbridge connect to a build whose version field was changed, and to one where it was kept?

hypotheses.inference: The Heat +FX answers the screen request (RPC framing `F0 00 20 3C 10 00`), as the Heat MKII does, so its screen can be mirrored and read without a mod.
hypotheses.test: Open Elek View (bluesgl.github.io/Elek_View) with nothing else on the MIDI port, select the unit, Start.

hypotheses.inference: The stock start-up animation runs at 30 frames per second, so it lasts about 5.8 s (175 frames), not about 11.7 s at 15 fps (O20).
hypotheses.derived_from: digikit f117 (timer model) vs digikit f07 (derived)
hypotheses.test: Film a cold start with your phone, three times, and time the animation from its first frame to its last; also say whether it looked the same each time (one of five animations is picked at random, the first about 99.9 % of the time).

hypotheses.inference: The ~4 KB cut in long MidiRpc LIST replies is in the stock reply router, not in a mod: an unpaged listing of a 256-entry table store on a modded DN2 came back as 3,997 bytes, correct up to entry 125 and garbage after; pages of 64 were clean.
hypotheses.test: On stock, list a +Drive folder with more than 130 entries in one unpaged request (DNX or Elektroid) and compare the reply length and the tail with a paged listing. Until settled, page listings at 64 entries or fewer.

hypotheses.inference: The Digitakt II and Digitone II hang on LOAD TO PROJECT of a +Drive file that is not a sample, as the Analog Rytm MKII does (SB19), since their sample browsers list every file too.
hypotheses.derived_from: elekloader Drive Loader (Rytm) {elekloader-drive}, digikit f120 (DT2 file layout)
hypotheses.test: Back up first. On a throwaway project, put a small non-audio file on the +Drive with Elektroid, LOAD TO PROJECT, note what happens; then power-cycle, delete the file and run CREATE NEW before the next OS update.

hypotheses.inference: The Digitakt II on OS 1.17 answers midi.guide's NRPN numbers (track mute 1:108, track level 1:110, pattern mute 1:109, master overdrive 2:50), not the manual's (1:101, 1:100, 1:104, 2:37) (O24).
hypotheses.test: On a throwaway project, send each NRPN pair from a DAW or a MIDI tool on the auto channel with value 0 and then 127, and watch which parameter moves on the screen.

hypotheses.inference: On a stock Analog Rytm MKII (OS 1.74) the first note right after a boot can be silent.
hypotheses.test: Power the stock unit on, wait for the main screen, play one pad or trig once and note whether it sounds; repeat over ten boots.

hypotheses.inference: A Digitakt II or Digitone II drops stock MidiRpc / Transfer requests while its boot intro still plays, and answers them once the main screen is up (digikit's emulator, 2026-11-16; I114).
hypotheses.test: Power on with Elektron Transfer (or another MidiRpc tool) connected and start a file listing as soon as USB appears; note whether the request fails or hangs during the intro and works after it.

hypotheses.inference: Stock TRACK COPY / PASTE on the Octatrack does not carry the LFO designer (SB26).
hypotheses.test: On T1 set an LFO WAVE to the designer, draw an obvious shape, aim it at volume with high depth; give T2 a different designer; GRID REC copy T1, paste onto T2: does T2 follow T1's shape?

hypotheses.inference: With SILENCE TRACKS on, stock also pops at a Part-changing pattern change when a ringing track has no trig on the new pattern's step 0 (the hard kill `0x40006820`; I119).
hypotheses.test: OT DEMO, SILENCE TRACKS on: let a sample ring on T4, T5 or T7, change A05 -> A03 with CHAIN AFTER 2; listen for a pop; repeat with SILENCE TRACKS off.

hypotheses.inference: The brief "new settings on the old sound" heard at a FULL load (Clyps) is stock's single sound path per track, not the mod: a retriggered voice fades through a path that already carries the new Part.
hypotheses.test: Stock [PTN] + trig between two patterns on different Parts with clearly different settings on one track and a sample ringing up to the change; the same blip on stock settles it.

hypotheses.inference: On Analog Rytm MKII OS 1.74 the OS version field of a flashed build shows only on the boot screen; no GLOBAL menu shows it (trig-seedr's corrected check 1).
hypotheses.test: Boot a stock 1.74 unit, look through GLOBAL > SYSTEM for an OS INFO entry; note what the boot screen shows.

hypotheses.inference: The Rytm MKI boot-flash writers lie at `0x40096A6C-0x40096B3E` and BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE ends at `0x4011AA7A` in OS 1.74; the upgrade buffer is `0x40366570` (2 MiB; SB21).
hypotheses.test: Static: disassemble the stock MKI 1.74 image at those addresses and check the callers of the erase and program routines. No flashing needed.

hypotheses.inference: The Digitakt II's stock USB MIDI transmit path (OS 1.17) waits indefinitely for buffer space when the host stops reading.
hypotheses.test: Send a SysEx request whose reply is large, keep the port open but stop reading, and watch whether the UI and sequencer keep running.

hypotheses.inference: Octatrack stock LFO-design Invert maps v to -1 - v and Clear sets all steps to 0 and stepped.
hypotheses.test: Invert and clear a custom LFO on the unit, save, and read the Part's 16 values and interpolation mask.

hypotheses.inference: On stock DN2 OS 1.11 the chord MODEs' per-scale chord table is built in RAM at start-up from the five stock scale tables, with one row per SCALE value 0-34.
hypotheses.test: Dump the RAM table after boot in the emulator and on a unit (read-only), compare row count and content per scale.

hypotheses.inference: On a Model:Cycles with stock OS 1.13, a project track holding an out-of-range machine number plays CHORD with wrong settings, shows *Error* on MACHINES, and is repaired by turning LEVEL/DATA, without any crash.
hypotheses.test: Save a project with an added machine on a mod, flash stock, open it and play; then turn LEVEL/DATA on MACHINES.

hypotheses.inference: A Monomachine (OS 1.32B) sometimes reads a pattern status request sent right after a kit dump and never answers it; the same request sent again is answered.
hypotheses.test: Send a kit dump, then a pattern status request at once, 50 times; count requests with no reply within 3 s.

hypotheses.inference: A Model:Samples running a Cycles OS that checks with the Cycles key refuses a Samples-signed OS file at the last block, after all packets were sent (the check covers the whole file).
hypotheses.test: Only with a recovery path ready (MIDI startup menu): on a Samples with such an OS, send a Samples-signed OS by USB with a tool that logs each reply; note which block gets an error, and what the screen says.

hypotheses.inference: A Model:Cycles OS `.syx` with more than 16,270 packets (packet numbers past 16,383) is refused or fails during the update.
hypotheses.test: Do not flash such a file. Instead count the packets of your build and check that each packet number's two bytes are below 0x80.

hypotheses.inference: On a Rytm MKII (OS 1.74), Transfer's progress bar goes wrong while reading a file over 4,294,967 bytes from the unit (SB28).
hypotheses.test: Read a sample larger than 4.3 MB back from the unit with Transfer and watch the progress.

hypotheses.inference: A `.wav` saved by a stock Octatrack holds the file size, not size - 8, in its RIFF header (bytes 4-7).
hypotheses.test: Save any sample or recorder buffer on a unit; read bytes 4-7 as little endian and compare with the file size.

hypotheses.inference: With several .bin files at the CF card's top level, Octatrack OS UPGRADE picks one by a fixed rule (name order or file date), not the newest.
hypotheses.test: Put two copies of the stock 1.40C .bin with different names and dates on the card (both stock, so nothing changes), run OS UPGRADE and note which file it names or reads; swap names and repeat.

hypotheses.inference: On stock Rytm MKII 1.74, TRK SEND MIDI sends only a step's first message on time; later notes of the same step leave 5-30 ms late, more on p-locked steps.
hypotheses.test: Stock OS: TRK SEND MIDI on BD and SD, trigs on the same steps, one p-lock on BD; record DIN out on a computer MIDI monitor and compare each note's time to the step grid.

hypotheses.inference: On stock Digitone II 1.12, after NEW project the LFOs of a MIDI track send nothing until a note trig plays on that track; lock-only trigs do not start them.
hypotheses.test: Stock OS 1.12: NEW project, a MIDI track with LFO1 in FRE mode on a CC, no trigs; PLAY and watch a MIDI monitor. Then add a lock-only trig, then a note trig. Which one starts the CCs?

hypotheses.inference: On Syntakt OS 1.42 the top 4 MiB of DDR (`0x47c00000-0x48000000`) is rewritten every frame while delay and reverb are in use, so Modwerk's freed `0x47fe0000-0x48000000` is not free then.
hypotheses.test: Fill `0x47fe0000-0x48000000` and `0x478c0000-0x47bf0000` with a pattern after boot, play a pattern with heavy delay and reverb sends, load a sample-heavy project, then read back. Settles O35. The lower range is done for one unit: trig-seedr's canary over `0x478b0000-0x47bf0000` held with all 64 sample slots loaded (2026-11-19, I184) {trig-seedr-1121}; the top 4 MiB is still open.

hypotheses.inference: Holding TRIG 16 at power-on on a Syntakt with stock OS 1.42 does nothing else than (at most) toggle step 16 of the first pattern; MAIN has no boot-time key reader.
hypotheses.test: Hold TRIG 16 while powering on a stock unit; check the boot and step 16.

hypotheses.inference: On a stock Digitakt II (OS 1.17), changing a track's filter type sends the same MIDI parameter as a machine change (`0xea`, the "Machine Type" row, or (`0xf`, type) in the other send mode), because the stock filter setter `0x40051886` is a copy of the machine setter `0x40051712` (O39). What a receiving unit does with it is unknown.
hypotheses.test: Stock OS, MIDI out (CC/NRPN) to a computer MIDI monitor: change the filter type on the FLTR page, then the machine; compare the messages. Optionally send the captured message into a second unit and see what changes.

hypotheses.inference: A stock project rename on a Digitakt II or Digitone II keeps the save stamp (32-bit word at slot record +`0x18`), so a tool keyed on the stamp follows a renamed project. The rename callback (DT2 `0x400a1246`, DN2 `0x4009b3bc`) does not call the stamp builder directly; what its change notice triggers is not traced. Partly answered 2026-11-21: in the DN2 1.12 emulator a menu rename of the *current* project gave it a new live stamp, written at the next save; a non-current slot keeps its stamp by static reading. `[emu]`
hypotheses.test: Read the slot listing (with a tool that reads it) before and after a rename in PROJECT MANAGER; compare the stamp.

hypotheses.inference: Stock Model:Cycles OS 1.13 plays an LFO WAVE value past RND (a sound saved by the Techno Edition with its T3-T16 waves) as RND and does not crash.
hypotheses.test: Load such a sound on the official OS (back up first); check the LFO page and listen.

hypotheses.inference: On stock Model:Cycles OS 1.13, muting a track does not stop a note already sounding; only later trigs are held back (I162).
hypotheses.test: Play a long-decay note (CHORD or TONE), mute the track mid-note, listen.

hypotheses.inference: Stock Octatrack OS 1.40C reads a trig condition above 64 (octabam's TRIG MUTE stores condition + 65) as no condition: it plays the trig, shows ERR, and the bank still loads (no BANK UNAVAILABLE, cf. A60).
hypotheses.test: Load a project saved with a TRIG MUTE build on stock 1.40C (back up first): does the muted trig play, does its condition read ERR, does the bank load?

hypotheses.inference: A stock Octatrack power-up never parses `project.work`; it restores the project from battery RAM (I168).
hypotheses.test: With the unit off, edit the tempo in `project.work` on the card (keep a copy), power on: the old tempo should stay until LOAD PROJECT.

hypotheses.inference: A stock Syntakt (OS 1.42) keeps an unsaved trig edit across a power-off once its supercap is charged: the power-off handler writes the working state only when byte `0x43be3154` is set, which happens when PPDSDR_G bit 3 (supercap charged) reads high.
hypotheses.test: Leave the unit on for a few minutes, add a trig without saving, switch off and on: is the trig there? Repeat right after a cold start. Partly seen 2026-11-19: on one unit running trig-seedr (stock save path) an applied and a pending take survived a power off {trig-seedr-1121}; a plain stock unit and a power off right after a cold start are still open.

hypotheses.inference: Syntakt OS 1.42 has no parameter-lock row limit (unlike the Rytm's 72 rows a pattern): each track's lock store is a full 64-step x 71-id matrix and the set routine counts no rows.
hypotheses.test: Lock several SYN, FLTR and AMP parameters on every step of several tracks; look for any refusal.

hypotheses.inference: A Syntakt (OS 1.42) whose MAIN unpack runs away in the bootstrap (I183, a hang at the logo) still reaches the STARTUP menu with FUNC held at power-on, because the bootstrap reads the keys before it copies and unpacks section 3 (read on the DT2 bootstrap, finding 01).
hypotheses.test: Next time a build hangs at the logo: hold FUNC at power-on, choose TRIG 4 and send stock over DIN; report whether the menu came up. Do not provoke the hang for this.

hypotheses.inference: The DT2's SHARC DDR above the sample pool window (`0x9d22b9c8` up to `0xa0000000`, about 46 MB) is never written by stock, as the DN2's tail `0x80531000-0xa0000000` is not.
hypotheses.derived_from: dnfw dn2-ddr method; dt2-machine-lab pool window
hypotheses.test: dnfw's method: fill the range with a pattern at boot, then scan it during heavy playback, pattern and kit changes, FX extremes, sample loads and a save. Expect a reserved top part for Capicola builds only.

hypotheses.inference: The DT2's ColdFire runs the same FreeRTOS layout as the DN2: higher priority numbers run first, prio 0 never runs, prio 1 is the idle loop; the main task's stack is barely used.
hypotheses.test: With the USB probe: find the ready table and the running-task pointer, sample them 60 times.

hypotheses.inference: The DN2's digikit flash cave `0x402fb7a8` (2,136 B on 1.11) keeps its bytes through a cold boot, as the DT2's `0x403117c4` does.
hypotheses.test: A canary in the cave, read back after a cold boot and after playback. Combine with H9.

hypotheses.inference: The DT2 flash cave `0x403117c4-0x40312000` is safe on a stock image; the freeze report (O18) came from something else in that build.
hypotheses.derived_from: Deja Vu, 70b185's builds vs dt2-capicola's comment
hypotheses.test: A stock image plus a canary in the cave, read back after a cold start after a long power-off (A40).

hypotheses.inference: DN2 L2 `0x200918c0-0x200c2000` is not written by stock in normal use (O19).
hypotheses.derived_from: DN2 skill, elekloader vs dnfw, Digiwerk
hypotheses.test: A canary or a write watch over the range during playback, pattern changes and a save (T24).

hypotheses.inference: DN2 RAM `0x46700000-0x46701300` is written by stock only when a +Drive transfer is over 60,672 bytes (S17: project save and load reach it).
hypotheses.test: A canary at `0x46700000`, read back after loading a large sample or project from +Drive.

hypotheses.inference: Direct hook writes may race reply publication on a DN2. Digikit measured 3,995 of 4,000 zero diagnostic words on a DT2; its own diagnostic clears overwrote the previous block's record in the DN2 emulator. Silicon DMA timing remains unmeasured.
hypotheses.test: Compare a hook's direct counter writes with static-word publication at block tail, without clearing prior reply records; count arrivals on the ColdFire side.

hypotheses.inference: On a project load, `write_live_project` (DT2 `0x400df95a`) and `fx_array.load` (`0x400daf54`) run in the project-load task (stack `0x4039beac` + `0x4000`), not in the UI task (stack `0x4096775c` + `0x28000`); finding 135 shows reachability only.
hypotheses.test: PC probe at those addresses logging A7 and SR while a project loads; A7 in the first range = project task.

hypotheses.inference: A stock Analog Rytm MKII (OS 1.74) spends CPU on silence until a power cycle: from a slot's first SYN trig the render calls that slot's machine every block whether it sounds or not (no idle test at `0x40121208`), and delay and reverb once used never decay to exact zero and run at full cost with every send at 0. STOP, a kit load or a project load do not clear it.
hypotheses.test: Read the render load with a probe at boot, after triggering all eight voices once, after one delay and reverb use, after STOP and after a kit reload. Does it stay up until a power cycle?

hypotheses.inference: The stock Digitone mk1 (OS 1.44) bank select swallows the release of the trig key used to pick a bank, as digiemu shows; Drum Mode 0.9.2 works around it with a 1.5 s timeout.
hypotheses.test: With a key-event logger build, press BANK + trig 9 and release: does a release event arrive? If it does, it is a digiemu artefact.

hypotheses.inference: On a Syntakt (OS 1.42) nothing writes AUDIO RAM `0x4404ff50-0x47ff0000` in normal use, and the AUDIO stack stays well under 64 KiB (O43).
hypotheses.test: Run Synfact's HIGH MEM PROBE for several minutes with samplers, FM, POLY, ARP, chorus, the recorder and a project load and save; HIGH BAD must stay 0; read STACK PEAK.

hypotheses.inference: SIMD loads or stores into L2 byte space hang the DN2's DSP as they hang the DT2's (same core, same IMASK).
hypotheses.test: A one-variable probe image with one SIMD L2 access behind a key press; recovery by power cycle.

hypotheses.inference: The SHARC's IIR0/FIR0 accelerators compute on the DT2 exactly as measured on the DN2 (output from stored word 5, FIR sums in pairs, INIDX/OUTIDX written the other way round).
hypotheses.test: Port the accelprobe image to the DT2 and compare the 76 result words.

hypotheses.inference: On the DN2, a single late DSP block is a one-block dropout that recovers, as on the DT2; the "silence until power cycle" reports came from sustained overload.
hypotheses.test: Provoke single late blocks (a burn loop on a key press) and count them on the DSP side; then hold an overload for seconds.

hypotheses.inference: Heat +FX builds need a cold-start test like other ColdFire units: a startup change can pass quick restarts and fail after minutes off (A40).
hypotheses.test: For the next startup-touching build: power off for 10 minutes before judging.

hypotheses.inference: Code costs on the Heat +FX follow the DT1's ColdFire lessons (EMAC mode switches, D16 hot-path hooks), since both run audio on an MCF5441x ColdFire.
hypotheses.test: Measure an audio-ISR hook with and without a MACSR switch per block.

hypotheses.inference: DT2 OS 1.17 saves only the kits the user changed, so a module's own kit data that changes by itself is lost unless a stock parameter of that kit changes too.
hypotheses.test: Modwerk publishes a unit procedure: change only module data, save, power-cycle, reload.

hypotheses.inference: The Octatrack stall after a PROJECT > SYSTEM walk on Modwerk builds is Modwerk's DSP stall watchdog firing while stock itself holds the frames (USB DISK MODE), not a stock fault.
hypotheses.test: Make the same walk on a unit with nothing installed, then with the watchdog off.

hypotheses.inference: The total freeze in octabam's demand-loader soak (I57) is the ColdFire spinning in one of the frame interrupt's waits that have no time limit, after the DSP stopped taking host words.
hypotheses.test: Add time limits (with a counter) to both waits and repeat the 118-switch soak.

hypotheses.inference: On the Octatrack's ColdFire (MCF5445x), a byte push to `-(sp)` moves SP by 2 and `move.b (a0)+,(0,a0,a1)` uses the incremented a0, as ot_emu models it (GCC assumes otherwise; I117).
hypotheses.test: Run a tiny probe that executes both forms and logs SP and the written address to the card or a battery-RAM word.

hypotheses.inference: The Octatrack comes back up normally from a ColdFire soft reset (RCR `0xFC0A0000` = `0x80`) started on the engine task; stock never restarts itself.
hypotheses.test: Trigger the reset from a minimal mod on a unit with a known recovery path; check boot, card mount and project load.

hypotheses.inference: Clocking an Octatrack on a USB-MIDI mod base (Modwerk, octabam) from USB and DIN at once doubles the tempo and saves it into the project, because the base passes every USB clock tick to stock's clock handler without checking for DIN clock.
hypotheses.test: Send 120 BPM clock on DIN and USB together for 30 s; read the tempo, then reload the project.

hypotheses.inference: The Digitone mk1 trig-key LED palette indices 2 dark, 3 red, 5 dim red, 20 white, 21 dim white (from digiemu's copy of the panel's colour table) give those colours on a unit.
hypotheses.test: Set each index with the setter `0x40016e62` on a unit and compare with the stock trig and dim-white LEDs.

hypotheses.inference: The Drum Mode UI hang (Mod Menu opened with YES right after releasing the track key, after trig key 1 with Drum Mode off) is an emulator artefact and does not happen on a unit.
hypotheses.test: Run the same key sequence on a unit with Drum Mode 0.8; check YES/NO/page keys in the Mod Menu.

hypotheses.inference: On a Digitone mk1 (OS 1.44), a mod page inserted right after MIDI page 20 (MIDI Source) breaks FUNC + push A (CHAN enable) on a unit too, as measured in digiemu.
hypotheses.test: Build with the extra page after 20, try FUNC + push A on a MIDI track's SRC page.

hypotheses.inference: On stock Octatrack OS 1.40C, erasing a MIDI trigless lock's trigs in LIVE REC ([NO] + [TRACK] while the playhead passes) leaves the step's trigless-lock flag (`+0x10`) set over an empty lock row, and the trig row keeps showing a trigless lock there, while the same gesture on an audio track clears it.
hypotheses.derived_from: KYOTI NOTES 2026-11-19/20 (emulator, stock's MIDI clear path) {octatrack-kyoti-fw-1121}
hypotheses.test: On a stock unit, place a MIDI trigless lock with a locked CC, erase it with [NO] + [TRACK] in LIVE REC and look at the step in GRID REC; repeat on an audio track.

hypotheses.inference: Binding a DSP module at about 95 % CPU stalls the Octatrack's DSP frame exchange: four field stalls on Modwerk bases before 0.7.9 had the manager binding, core 0's last packet a BIND, every earlier frame on time.
hypotheses.test: On base 0.7.9 or later, bind a module at about 95 % CPU and read the stall record; the emulator cannot show it (it never places DSP code).

incidents.title: Stock eMMC TRIM fails with TRIM ERROR on a busy card
incidents.unit: Digitone II, OS 1.11 (dn2mk2 v0.39, erasing mod data), 2026-11-05
incidents.seen: TRIM ERROR at sector 817905, after a restart further on at CB1905.
incidents.cause: after CMD38 the stock busy wait arms the DAT0 edge interrupt before it tests DAT0; a short TRIM that finishes in between leaves a stale semaphore post, so the next TRIM on a really busy card returns at once and the call after it gets no answer. The driver has no timeout.
incidents.cause_found_by: read statically from stock code, not seen on the bus
incidents.fix: read `PRSSTAT` `0xfc0cc024` before every TRIM and verify read, call only when idle; retry five times; ERASE PAUSED and resume on request (v0.40).
incidents.status: fixed in the mod; the stock race remains.

incidents.title: Stock song LOAD trusts a stored row count
incidents.unit: Digitone II, OS 1.11
incidents.seen: one project crashed stock and modded builds alike when opened.
incidents.cause: song LOAD `0x400dea6a` copies `count` stored rows without checking it; the project held 21,503 rows instead of at most 99.
incidents.cause_found_by: read statically and confirmed on the project file
incidents.fix: repair the project (row count at record `+0x147`, storage version 4); mods must keep every count in range.

incidents.title: USB upgrade receiver does not check the 2 MiB limit
incidents.unit: Digitone II
incidents.seen: an oversized image stalls at the end; nothing is written; a power cycle clears it.
incidents.cause: the receive buffer is 2 MiB and the receiver does not check the size.
incidents.fix: keep the container under `0x200000` bytes.

incidents.title: Auto-commit upload loses its "complete" event on the first upload after boot
incidents.unit: Digitone II, OS 1.11
incidents.seen: the unit sits on "OS UPGRADE / Receiving".
incidents.cause: with auto-commit the OS posts "upload complete" while the upgrade view is not open yet; the event is lost.
incidents.cause_found_by: read from stock code, seen on the unit
incidents.fix: upload without auto-commit, then send End(1), which checks the bytes and posts the event itself.

incidents.title: EP0 data stages of a multiple of 64 bytes stall or freeze (stock USB driver)
