incidents.status: fixed in 8650bb8a (KR17 passed on the same unit)

incidents.title: Powering off on a mod page broke the stock Euclidean page at the next boot (Euclidean Scale)
incidents.unit: Digitakt II, OS 1.17, Modwerk base with Euclidean Scale build P117, 2026-11-08
incidents.seen: after powering off on the SCF/RNN page, the next boot showed the stock Euclidean page without its page indicators; FUNC + AMP did nothing until the tester changed page and came back.
incidents.cause: at startup the stock Euclidean view's track-editor cache is unset; the module read the track from that cache.
incidents.fix: read the track through the stock Euclidean view's own accessor (S117); confirmed on the unit.

incidents.title: A Rytm MKII mod read a 32-bit kit index as 16 bits and played the old sound (MIDI Engine)
incidents.unit: Analog Rytm MKII, OS 1.74, MIDI Engine build ME08 (flashed), early November 2026
incidents.seen: on a project whose current kit was not kit 1, a track switched to the MIDI machine kept playing its previous sound from pads and sequencer, and its AMP page showed stock values.
incidents.cause: the current kit's index is a 32-bit word; the build read its top half, which is 0, so it always used kit 1.
incidents.fix: read the whole word (ME09); reproduced and cleared in rytm-emu with kit 2 current.

incidents.title: A project load dropped installed effects from the next start's list (Modwerk Octatrack base up to 0.7.8)
incidents.unit: Octatrack (MKII units in the shared diagnostics), OS 1.40C, Modwerk bases up to 0.7.8, reported 2026-11-18
incidents.seen: at the next start Tape Echo, BBD Delay and Euclid were refused with NO ROOM FOR IT; the shared diagnostics of four units show it.
incidents.cause: a project load replaced the base's effect map; a module that stayed on its handle was left unnamed, so the save dropped its line. Found from the diagnostics and reproduced in a host test.
incidents.fix: base 0.7.9 names every module that stays on its handle and gives legacy projects the catalogue's handle.
incidents.status: fixed in 0.7.9, not yet tried on a unit; may explain I129

incidents.title: Arr Rows drew its selection wrong and pasted as an insert (Modwerk draft, Octatrack MKI)
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKI, OS 1.40C, Arr Rows 0.1.0-experimental draft, 2026-11-17
incidents.seen: selection marks were drawn on the wrong rows; paste acted as an insert; once, MIDI to external synths stopped during a many-row copy while playing.
incidents.cause: the module read `0x460d16e8` as the first row shown (stock's is `0x460d1c64`), and judged CUE from its own key count, which a missed release left stuck. Found on the unit, diagnosed in the emulator. The MIDI stop is unexplained. An earlier build had marked the bank bit `0x100b14ce` instead of the arrangement bit `0x100b14d1`; the emulator caught that, the host test could not.
incidents.fix: the stock row variable, and CUE state read from stock.
incidents.status: two fixed; the MIDI stop open

incidents.title: FM+ knobs moved the wrong parameters (dn2mk2 v0.59)
incidents.unit: Digitone II, OS 1.11, dn2mk2 v0.59 FMPLUS, testers' units, 2026-11-18
incidents.seen: on FM+ STAT, PAR and DYN the knobs moved other parameters and some read "unused"; the sound engine itself was fine.
incidents.cause: the page lookup skipped over BOUNCE's machine number, so STAT got PAR's page, PAR got DYN's and DYN read past the table. Found from the testers' reports; the 57-step gate had no check for which knob reaches which parameter.
incidents.fix: v0.60 finds each Monomachine machine's page by an explicit test; a new gate step `mnmpages` checks that each type's page record is its own.
incidents.status: fixed in v0.60 (gated; unit report pending)

incidents.title: A mis-encoded DSP multiply put garbage on the Octatrack's headphones (AERIA OS)
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKII, AERIA OS builds of 2026-11-13..15
incidents.seen: the headphones carried garbage: far too loud, never negative, the same level whatever the volume; main was fine. Earlier (2026-11-13) the owner heard "stereo, then right only, then left only, then cut out".
incidents.cause: a multiply in the DSP engine had its operands in an order the assembler silently encodes as the signed-by-unsigned `mpysu`, so the sample was read as unsigned.
incidents.cause_found_by: found by the author, read from the listing
incidents.fix: operands reordered (builds of 2026-11-15, tested and flashed on the unit); the build script now refuses a DSP listing with an `mpysu`-encoded multiply or with unassembled lines.

incidents.title: Headphones silent after flashing, though every RAM-boot bench test passed (AERIA OS)
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKII, AERIA OS releases of 2026-11-15/16, flashed; reported 2026-11-17
incidents.seen: no sound from the headphone output after flashing; main worked. The bench tests (RAM boot, 2026-11-15) had passed.
incidents.cause: at a cold start core 0 started the ESAI and lined its output rings up with the converter before core 1 set the shared PLL; the PLL lock then stalled it, and the eight output words could sit shifted in the converter's slots (a shift of two puts main on the main jacks and unused words on the headphones). A RAM boot runs with the PLL already locked, so no bench test could see it. Also found: AERIA's MKII headphone left and right were swapped against stock.
incidents.cause_found_by: likely, read from code; not confirmed on the unit
incidents.fix: v0.9.5-beta (2026-11-19): the engine waits for a host flag raised 20 ms after core 1 and the PLL are set; the MKII phones order follows stock (right in word 4). Simulator-tested only; the simulator does not model the cold-start clock. The owner's check: cold power-on, sound on main and headphones; if still silent, listen on CUE (main there means the slots are still shifted).
incidents.status: open (fix not yet run on the unit)

incidents.title: A chord set just before a live note slid in from the old chord (model27 Chord Joy, Model:Cycles)
incidents.unit: Model:Cycles, OS 1.13, model27 release 0.76 full build, 2026-11-19
incidents.seen: some Chord Joy chords sounded broken: the note started on the chord held before and slid to the new one, worst on TRIG 6-8; also with keys played one after another. SHAPE turned by hand between trigs played cleanly.
incidents.cause: the set reaches the voice target at once, but the audio side smooths every target per block, and CHORD reads the smoothed word. The OS snaps the smoothing state only when a note brings another sound, not for a live note on the track's own sound. A second bug found while reading: a degree pressed while another was held released the wrong root.
incidents.fix: after each SHAPE set, Chord Joy also writes the smoothing state of that parameter before the note's event; the sounding root is tracked. The fixed build passed on the unit the same day.

incidents.title: Held chord notes were cut when a melody played over them (RIFT v0.10 and earlier, Digitone II)
incidents.unit: Digitone II, OS 1.11, RIFT v0.10 or earlier, user report on Discord, 2026-11-19
incidents.seen: on a busy FASCIA or SILT track a held chord lost notes when a melody played over it, or when one of its notes was struck again (voice mode REUSE).
incidents.cause: the frame guard renders voices in ORDER and leaves out, then steals, those that no longer fit. ORDER was newest first (inherited from dn2mk2 v0.29), so new and re-struck notes took the DSP time ahead of held ones.
incidents.cause_found_by: read from code, shown in the emulator
incidents.fix: v0.11 marks a voice released at its note-off until its next note and orders all released voices after all held ones; an emulator test holds two notes under a melody with the clock squeezed to about three voices.
incidents.status: fix gated in the emulators 2026-11-19, no unit result yet; the REUSE case did not reproduce at the emulator's CPU level. More held notes than the DSP can run still lose the oldest.

incidents.title: A drone kept sounding on a muted track (Modded Cycles Techno Edition ATMOS, before v1.9)
incidents.unit: Model:Cycles, OS 1.13, Techno Edition v1.8 or earlier, user report, 2026-11-19
incidents.seen: ATMOS with GATE on kept droning after its track was muted, even across a pattern change.
incidents.cause: the Cycles' mute only holds back the sequencer's trigs; the GATE drone plays without a trig.
incidents.fix: v1.9 ends the drone on mute (FUNC + track or latched mute) and fades its reverb tail in about a second; unmute starts it again.
incidents.status: fixed in v1.9 (emulation only, not yet played on a unit)

incidents.title: An Octatrack froze while playing after the walk PROJ, DOWN, YES, YES (Modwerk base 0.7.9)
incidents.unit: Octatrack (model not stated), Modwerk base 0.7.9 (`c889442d`), eight modules (E-Verb, BBD Delay, LOFI2, Recorder Loop, DirectJmp Kyoti, Deja Vu, Temp Save, Repitch), field diagnostics 2026-11-18/19
incidents.seen: froze until a restart while playing at 58 % CPU; the last keys were PROJ, DOWN, YES, YES (four times), the last followed by PLAY. Earlier the same night it froze while stopped after the same walk. All eight modules came back at the next start.
incidents.cause: unknown. Freezes while stopped after this walk were read earlier as OS upgrades or USB DISK MODE seen by the freeze watch, but this one was playing and kept its base.
incidents.fix: none yet. Modwerk's test: on 0.7.9 with that set, play, repeat the walk and read the log.

incidents.title: A 303 voice lost its last step, popped and played a blip at Part and pattern changes (KYOTI BLACKPYRAMIDS_303)
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKI, OS 1.40C, octabam test images OCTABAM40-43 with KYOTI's blackpyramids-303 module, 2026-11-19
incidents.seen: OCTABAM40: a quiet pop at a cued Part switch into a Part whose 303 track had no trig on step 1, and the outgoing pattern's last-step note never sounded. OCTABAM41: a note tied to the end of a pattern was cut at a change to a pattern starting with ties. OCTABAM42: the first note after a load or into another Part was a blip or cut short.
incidents.cause: the voice asked the UI Part, which stock moves about 7 ticks before the switch, so the outgoing track changed a step early; a note's gate was worked out a step ahead from its own pattern only; and GATE was read from the live SETUP byte, which stock re-stages only at the track's trig (0 after a load).
incidents.cause_found_by: shown in ot_emu after each report
incidents.fix: read stock's per-track Part pair, re-time a tied note from the next pattern's first steps, and read GATE from the scheduled pattern's Part. OCTABAM43 passed all checks; the same code is in KYOTI V1.8BC FINAL (2026-11-19). All three bugs were in the earlier FINAL too.
incidents.status: fixed (confirmed on the unit in the octabam form, not in V1.8BC itself)

incidents.title: A FLEX SRC page pasted onto a 303 track left a 303 with FLEX's numbers (KYOTI V1.8BC)
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKI, OS 1.40C, KYOTI V1.8BC first test image, 2026-11-18
incidents.seen: a FLEX track's SRC page pasted onto a 303 track left it a 303 with VOL 0 and the other FLEX values.
incidents.cause: the 303 machine is stored as FLEX in the machine bytes plus a signature in NEIGHBOR's bytes; a page paste writes one machine's twelve bytes and the machine byte, never the signature.
incidents.fix: hooks at the page copy core, the page paste and the page UNDO set the machine before stock writes. The rebuilt image behaved as intended on the unit, 2026-11-19.

incidents.title: The sequencer stayed on step 1 after a 303 track was pasted into another Part's pattern (KYOTI V1.8BC, seen once)
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKI, OS 1.40C, KYOTI V1.8BC test image, 2026-11-18/19
incidents.seen: while setting up a test by TRACK COPY of a 303 track and TRACK PASTE onto T2 or T5 of a pattern on another Part, PLAY left step 1 lit and the sequencer did not advance.
incidents.cause: unknown; the author could not repeat it, and an ot_emu replay of the steps ran normally in every variant.
incidents.fix: none; if it comes back, record the steps and build a diagnostic image.

incidents.title: Holding a step again deleted its trig (octabam LOCK EDIT)
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKI, OS 1.40C, a contributor's LOCK EDIT build, 2026-11-17
incidents.seen: with the audio editor opened by [TRIG] + [BANK], holding the same step again and releasing it removed the step's trig while the editor stayed open.
incidents.cause: LOCK EDIT's hold hook kept the lock popup closed but returned before stock's hold handler cleared the key's hold bit; the release toggles the trig while that bit is set.
incidents.fix: the hook clears the bit itself and still keeps the popup closed; a gate holds again for 400 ms and checks that the step survives.
incidents.status: fixed (port gate; a unit re-run is not stated)

incidents.title: Per-track trig modes were saved but gone after a power cycle (TRACK TRIG MODE)
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKI, OS 1.40C, test images ACCLOOP14 and ACCLOOP16 (Hteah's TRACK TRIG MODE), 2026-10-27/28
incidents.seen: ACCLOOP14: the modes survived SAVE but were gone after a power cycle. ACCLOOP16: leaving QUICK MUTE with FUNC + UP/DOWN wrote the mode it passed over onto the track (T1's SLICES became CHROMATIC).
incidents.cause: a power-up restores the project from battery RAM and never parses `project.work`, and the mode table was in DRAM. The QUICK MUTE exit treated the passing mode as a pick.
incidents.cause_found_by: read from code, shown in the emulator
incidents.fix: the table moved to 8 bytes of battery RAM; a step out of TRACKS, QUICK MUTE or DELAY CONTROL never overwrites a track's mode. ACCLOOP15 passed switching, save, reload and a power cycle on the MKI.

incidents.title: A project reload after a demand-loader phase left the DSP frame count stopped (octabam BUILD 05)
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKII, OS 1.40C, `octabam` and `octabam-verbs` BUILD 05 (`5b991c85`), 2026-11-18/19
incidents.seen: a project reload over USB (DISK MODE, copy, then the reload command) right after a scripted demand-loader phase left the DSP's frame count fixed, still so after 90 s and after 20 minutes; the ColdFire frame interrupt ran on and USB answered. Seen three times; never after a reload straight after boot, nor after the FX phases.
incidents.cause: unknown.
incidents.fix: none; workaround: boot the image again (REMOTE command 3) after each loader phase, which restarted the count without a power cycle.

incidents.title: DARK REV picked on all eight tracks while MODULATION was loaded stopped the DSP (octabam BUILD 05)
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKII, OS 1.40C, `octabam` BUILD 05 (`5b991c85`), seeded fuzz soak (seed 3401), 2026-11-19/20
incidents.seen: the DSP frame count stopped 1,612 s into the run, at a START after a program change; panel, USB and the ColdFire frame interrupt went on. A commanded boot did not bring it back (boot screen, I110); a power cycle did. A 573 s replay stalled 2 of 2 times at the same START; with the last program change set to MODULATION, PLATE or SPRING REV instead of DARK REV it did not (one run each). Three diagnostic builds still stalled; in all, 6 of 9 runs stalled. ot_emu did not stall.
incidents.cause: it needs MODULATION loaded by the demand loader and live on FX2 when DARK REV, whose buffer reaches the demand effect's code, is picked on every track and START follows. An earlier overwrite of the frame guard's cells is not the cause.
incidents.fix: none

incidents.title: A third LFO page showed ERR labels when the bank held only modules (Synfact core 2.1.1, Syntakt)
incidents.unit: Syntakt, OS 1.42, Synfact core 2.1.1 with a bank of LFO3 only (one module, no machine), 2026-11-19
incidents.seen: the third LFO page appeared, but its parameters showed ERR labels, no ranges and no editor data.
incidents.cause: the machine binder returned early for a bank with no machines and never set the registry active. The LFO3 page hooks still ran, but every provider lookup was skipped while the registry was inactive, so LFO3's ids fell through to stock's fallbacks. Every earlier test had at least one machine in the bank.
incidents.cause_found_by: read from code, reproduced in a host test
incidents.fix: core 2.1.2 drops the early return; an empty registry gets valid storage before it becomes active. A host regression and a Unicorn test with two module-only banks cover it, with the old core as a negative control.
incidents.status: fixed in 2.1.2 (the owner ran the old and the new core with the LFO3-only bank and confirmed the fix on the unit, 2026-11-19)

incidents.title: A 303 chosen on a FLEX track was silent until switched away and back (KYOTI V1.8BC RC1)
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKI, OS 1.40C, KYOTI V1.8BC release candidate RC1 (`KY18BC RC1`), 2026-11-20
incidents.seen: a BLKPYRAMD (the 303 voice) chosen from the machine chooser often made no sound; switching to NEIGHBOR or THRU and back once or twice woke it.
incidents.cause: the 303 is stored as FLEX, so FLEX to BLKPYRAMD is FLEX to FLEX for stock, and stock's machine commit re-stages a track's live machine bytes only for PICKUP; otherwise they follow at the track's next trig after a real machine change, or at a Part apply. The voice played FLEX's live values (VOL = FLEX's TSTR byte: OFF gives silence). The project's checks seeded the bytes before PLAY, so none caught it. The same was in V1.8BC FINAL.
incidents.fix: after a machine commit on the current Part, call stock's seed when the stored machine is FLEX and set the track's Part pair to `0xff`, but not while the track still carries the old Part's note. `KY18BC RC2` passed every item on the unit, 2026-11-20.
incidents.status: fixed in RC2 (not yet promoted; waits for RC3)

incidents.title: A fix for erased trigless locks covered audio tracks only (KYOTI ERASE_EMPTY_TRIGLESS_LOCKS)
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKI, OS 1.40C, KYOTI V1.8C and V1.8BC RC1, 2026-11-20
incidents.seen: on a MIDI track, erasing the last lock of a trigless lock left the step lit, as on stock (SB12); audio tracks were fixed.
incidents.cause: the LIVE erase calls a separate MIDI twin of the audio worker; the fix had only hooked the audio one. The emulator showed the bug on the FINAL and RC1 images once a MIDI case was added.
incidents.fix: one shared rule behind two hooks, one per worker (240 B). `KY18BC RC2` passed every MIDI and audio item on the unit, 2026-11-20; promoted the same day.

incidents.title: A track that stopped being a 303 played a burst of its FLEX sample (KYOTI V1.8BC RC2)
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKI, OS 1.40C, `KY18BC RC2`, sequencer running, 2026-11-20
incidents.seen: switching a track with samples between BLKPYRAMD and FLEX, STATIC or NEIGHBOR played a bit of the FLEX or STATIC sample at the switch, often a very short fast loop.
incidents.cause: the 303 rides on a hidden stock FLEX voice. After the switch the frame's renderer for the track stays the 303's until the track's next trig, and it handed the hidden voice to stock's sample renderer, which played it for about 300 ms. Present since V1.8BC FINAL.
incidents.fix: while a track that was a 303 waits for its trig (also when it yields at a cued Part switch), render stock's idle record instead. RC3 carries it.
incidents.status: fixed in the emulator; RC3 not yet flashed

incidents.title: QUAN read 5/4 instead of 1/1 on entering VARI; VARISPEED and the 303 shared spare bytes (KYOTI VARISPEED)
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKI, OS 1.40C, `KY18C VRG1` test image, 2026-11-19
incidents.seen: setting TSTR to VARI showed QUAN `5/4` instead of `1/1`, also on a track that seemed fresh.
incidents.cause: which meaning a parked byte had (PTCH or QUAN) lived only in RAM and was forgotten at every Part apply, so the next poll read the PTCH park as QUAN (PTCH +12 = `5/4`), and that value was then saved with the Part. Present in every FINAL VARISPEED, VARISPEED_EMUS and KYOTI. A follow-up probe found that VARISPEED parked PTCH in NEIGHBOR's spare bytes, which BLACKPYRAMIDS_303 also used: PTCH was lost or changed, a track that had been a 303 entered VARI at `5/4`, and a real 303's signature could break. A flag in bit 7 was also zeroed by stock's Part validator on every load.
incidents.fix: VRG3 keeps VARISPEED's state in four Part bytes nobody else uses, each below 128, with the meaning in the bytes; older projects are migrated at first sight, and VARISPEED never touches a 303 track. Confirmed on the unit in RC1 (VARI entry, QUAN across a save, a project from the old build, a 303 beside VARI), 2026-11-20; promoted.

incidents.title: A USB Audio Undo froze the panel and left the Octatrack off USB (Modwerk 0.7.11 candidates)
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKII, OS 1.40C, owner's unit, RAM-booted Modwerk 0.7.11 release candidates with USB Audio 0.3.0-experimental as a package, macOS host, 2026-11-20
incidents.seen: (1) on candidate `a2ae64eb`, Undo of a 16-channel POST LEVEL trial was acknowledged, then the unit left USB and its panel froze; the log kept a freeze (UI tick stopped at least 5 s while the frame interrupt ran, CPU 38 %), and the Mac's port reset failed to enable the port. (2) On the rebuilt `e0cbd717`, seven trials passed; the eighth (Track 8/Master) acknowledged its set and the unit vanished from USB before the host read the new descriptors, while the panel still answered keys. Both times a cold start with USB unplugged brought back the flashed base and all ten kept modules, checksum for checksum.
incidents.cause: (1) after a descriptor change only the UI tick could switch the USB controller back on (host test); (2) not proven: the base started its host deadline when it set the controller's run bit and never checked that the controller attached.
incidents.fix: a one-second fallback in the frame interrupt re-enables the controller; later the base checks attach, suspend and reset after three seconds and offers the descriptors once more if VBUS is valid and the port stayed disconnected. Release base 0.7.12 then passed eight trials (2 to 20 channels, Track 8/Master twice), Keep, a power cycle and a restore from the card.
incidents.status: fixed in 0.7.12 (the retry itself did not fire on the unit; it runs in a controller model only)

incidents.title: A paired browser tab rolled back USB Audio trials at the reconnect (Modwerk)
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKII, OS 1.40C, development base with the USB function slot, macOS host with a Modwerk page open in a browser, 2026-11-20
incidents.seen: four-channel USB Audio trials driven by a native test tool rolled back during the reconnect that follows the descriptor change, two of three times; once the unit came back with the audio configuration live but its module row gone.
incidents.cause: the macOS USB log showed the browser opening the vendor interface about 200 ms before the test tool; the site's link undoes an unfinished trial when a paired page reconnects. The log does not show an Undo command from the browser.
incidents.fix: with the browser closed, Main + Cue passed three times in a row and all six layouts recorded; Modwerk's guide says to close paired tabs before a native USB Audio trial, and the site now leaves another session's USB Audio trial running when the unit reconnects.

incidents.title: Analog BD stayed silent after a rolled-back trial until a power cycle (Modwerk base 0.7.9)
incidents.unit: Octatrack (field report #1736), Modwerk base 0.7.9; reproduced on an MKII with a development copy of the beta base, 2026-11-19
incidents.seen: a trial that took out Analog BD (or Sidechain, or Output Matrix) to make room for another module was rolled back; Analog BD was listed again and could be picked but made no sound until a power cycle.
incidents.cause: the base released the module's DSP engine for good while the trial was still open.
incidents.fix: base 0.7.10 keeps the module ready to come back until the trial is kept or rolled back, while still giving its DSP room to the trial. Release candidate on an MKII: the kick measured -19.3 dBFS on T4 before and after a 60 s trial that removed Analog BD and added Vibrato.

incidents.title: A VECTOR trial's Undo left the loader in recovery until a power cycle (Modwerk 0.7.11 development image)
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKII, OS 1.40C, 0.7.11 development image `fac15232`, VECTOR 0.3.2 alone in a 30 s stopped whole-set trial, 2026-11-20
incidents.seen: the rollback left the loader in recovery; a fresh connection and `recover` failed too. After the owner's power cycle the flashed 0.7.9 base and its ten modules were intact.
incidents.cause: before removing a departing track machine the loader checked its stock menu definitions as they read with the machine still patched in, so it saw the machine as still in use. The log did not name the reference that blocked.
incidents.fix: the loader now judges a departing machine's menu entries as they will read after its stock handlers return, and still checks cached callbacks and every Part live. Five later VECTOR trials (stopped and after playback, three builds, the release candidate included) rolled back normally.

incidents.title: A project load after a card restore stalled the DSP (Modwerk 0.7.9 development base)
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKII, OS 1.40C, 0.7.9 Tracks Post development base `c6345a32`, six modules (Tape Echo, Euclid, LOFI2, Sidechain Compressor, POLY8, Slow LFO) restored from the card, 2026-11-19
incidents.seen: the first load from one project to another (stock SPRING REV on T1 FX2 and SPATIALIZER on T5 FX1 in both) stalled the DSP twice before PLAY. The same load passed once without modules and four times with the same modules sent over USB.
incidents.cause: the base's DSP manager began changing which effects the DSP held while the bank and Parts were still loading: at the stall core 0 had bound SPATIALIZER and the manager waited for core 1's SPRING REV bind, with the incoming effect map not yet published. Why the frame edge went missing is open.
incidents.fix: a gate that continues open requests but starts no new plan until the whole effect map is loaded (base 0.7.11). On 0.7.11 two restoring boots loaded with no extra DSP packet or commit; shipped 0.7.10 did not stall in two tries either but made the same residency changes the stall trace had shown.
incidents.status: fixed in 0.7.11; the stall itself did not reproduce on 0.7.10

incidents.title: The digikit MODULES page froze a Syntakt: it used the Digitakt II key ids
incidents.unit: Syntakt, OS 1.42, digikit `device` image, 2026-11-20
incidents.seen: DIGIKIT > MODULES showed an empty list ("NO STORE") and afterwards no key worked, not even NO; the unit needed a power cycle.
incidents.cause: the list page replaces the stock key handler and compared key ids with the Digitakt II values (YES 10, NO 12, RIGHT 15). An empty list passes only NO to the stock handler. On the Syntakt the firmware key index 12 is YES and NO is 13 (decoder table `0x401d7a48`), so NO was swallowed with every other key.
incidents.cause_found_by: reproduced in the emulator, also on a blank card
incidents.fix: key ids and flag bits per device in the device file (Syntakt YES 12, NO 13, RIGHT 17, LEVEL push 48); an empty list now swallows only YES and RIGHT and passes every other key to the stock handler; the build refuses a device file without the key table. A test compares the ids with the stock decoder table.
incidents.status: fixed; the fix ran in the emulator, a flash of the fixed build is not reported as the cause check

incidents.title: The first digikit store on a Syntakt lay beyond the unit's card
incidents.unit: Syntakt, OS 1.42, first digikit `device` build, 2026-11-19/20
incidents.seen: the runtime reported `CARD_TOO_SMALL` and had no store; nothing was written (the check refuses every write before a sector is touched).
incidents.cause: the store reused the Digitone II range (sectors `0x800000-0x2e1a000`, made for the 32 GB part the emulators model), but the unit's eMMC is the 1.82 GiB part (`0x3a4000` sectors, the smallest the firmware's part table lists; the table is not enforced at boot).
incidents.fix: a fixed 512 MiB store at `0x200000-0x300000`, above every stock sector (below `0x180000`) and below the smallest listed capacity, checked at boot against the driver's capacity getter; INFO and HEALTH show the capacity. On the unit the new store took uploads, listing and removal, and a content module ran from it.

incidents.title: The emulator undercounted DSP time by 2x to 12x
incidents.unit: Digitakt II (70b185's project; digimod's Plaits mod)
incidents.seen: device cycles about 2x the emulator's instruction count for code reading DDR; a hard stop the emulator showed overshooting by ~25k overshot by ~75k on the unit; digimod reports 7-12x on hardware for one case.
incidents.cause: the emulators model no memory stalls.
incidents.fix: budget with silicon costs; leave a margin; measure once per project on the unit.

incidents.title: A SHARC emulator shifted every fractional multiply
incidents.unit: Digitone II (complex-ping's emulator)
incidents.seen: found when the emulator was checked against stock routines.
incidents.cause: the emulator shifted every fractional multiply left; the PRM shifts only signed x signed.
incidents.fix: fixed in the emulator; `sharc_checks.py` calls stock routines and compares.

incidents.title: Low-window flash pointers boot in the emulator and hang on the unit
incidents.unit: Machinedrum / Monomachine (Gearmulator board model)
incidents.seen: images boot in the emulator and hang on the unit.
incidents.cause: after the OS remaps CS0, nothing decodes the low window on hardware; the emulator maps flash at `0x0` and `0x10000000`.
incidents.fix: link and point through `0x10000000`; scan images for low pointers.

incidents.title: The default compression level corrupted a DN2 image
incidents.unit: Digitone II
incidents.seen: corrupt image.
incidents.cause: section 4's in-place loader has a stock margin of +31,182 bytes; elektron-firmware-tool's `-l 3` gives -39,318. Stock DT2 1.17 also fails the in-place path (margin -31,912).
incidents.fix: check the margin at every loader stage; a dense packer.

incidents.title: A "no change" rebuild came out 2 bytes short
incidents.unit: Analog Rytm MK1
incidents.seen: the null repack failed.
incidents.cause: elektron-firmware-tool padded ELE2 containers to 2 bytes; stock pads to 4.
incidents.fix: pad to 4; always null-repack the stock file first.

incidents.title: A label defined twice resolved to the wrong file
incidents.unit: Digitakt II (Plaits kernels, caught before a unit)
incidents.seen: each kernel's own test passed; the merged image jumped into the wrong file.
incidents.cause: a label defined in two sources resolves to one of them in the merged object.
incidents.fix: unique label prefixes per file.

incidents.title: Checks reported success about work they never did
incidents.unit: Digitone II (dnfw LFO4 bridge)
incidents.seen: the build passed every check and faulted on the unit.
incidents.cause: snapshot harnesses cleared code no real boot ran; a boot gate printed "Safe to flash" after its coverage section was deleted; an emulator call returned 0 for a present value.
incidents.fix: every check gets a control that must fail.

incidents.title: Boot-screen frames were upright in the emulator and flipped on the panel
incidents.unit: Digitakt II, OS 1.17 (digikit, branch image), 2026-11-08
incidents.seen: a boot screen whose bar was at the bottom in the preview and the emulator appeared at the top on the panel; left-to-right fill was unchanged.
incidents.cause: the emulator decodes the intro bitmap as if the intro flush flipped like the main-UI blit. On the panel, intro rows are stored top-down mirrored. Why the intro path differs (flush routine or panel scan direction) is not established.
incidents.cause_found_by: shown on the unit, plus a comparison of the stock logo with the bootloader picture: 0 mismatching pixels after a vertical flip
incidents.fix: digikit's `.dkbs` frames, safe screen and pixel helper use the panel's layout. The emulator decoder is not fixed yet.
incidents.status: worked around; emulator still wrong for intro frames.

incidents.title: A test plan pressed the wrong key, and the emulator reference did not match the unit
incidents.unit: Analog Rytm MKII, OS 1.74 (Modwerk, Kit A/B runs KBH7 and KBH8), 2026-11-08/09
incidents.seen: two runs tested only the KIT-menu path; another run stopped because the unit's kit list draws markers after kits 02-16 that the emulator's reference image lacks.
incidents.cause: rytm2_mods' documentation gives the reload key as NO + PLAY, so the remote-key plan pressed transport PLAY; the OS 1.74 manual says NO + PLAY MODE.
incidents.fix: rerun with NO + PLAY MODE and narrow the screen check to the cursor row.

incidents.title: Odd jump targets froze a Digitakt II at boot; the emulator kept running
incidents.unit: Digitakt II, OS 1.17 (elekloader core-dt2 2.0), fixed 2026-11-08
incidents.seen: the unit froze at boot.
incidents.cause: byte-aligned code sections put routines at odd addresses; a jsr/jmp to an odd address stops the ColdFire with an address error (vector 3), while the emulator keeps running.
incidents.fix: the linker refuses an odd-target absolute jsr/jmp into mod RAM; each code section starts with a 2-byte alignment.

incidents.title: Code built into .bss crashed a Digitakt II at boot; the emulator ran the zeros
incidents.unit: Digitakt II, OS 1.17 (gdeo607's Digi2Core, core-dt2 2.4-2.6), fixed in 2.6.1 on 2026-11-09
incidents.seen: right after boot the unit stopped with an illegal-instruction exception.
incidents.cause: two new routines were placed in `.bss` instead of the code section, so the unit jumped into zero-filled memory. The emulator executed the zeros as no-ops and booted.
incidents.fix: the routines are code again in 2.6.1. The README says not to flash a 2.4, 2.5 or 2.6 build; Digi2MacroOSC and Digi2ElixirPotionsDRUM still name core 2.4.

incidents.title: A feature that crosses ColdFire and DSP passed the gate and failed on units
incidents.unit: Digitone II, OS 1.11 (dn2mk2 v0.45/v0.46, BOUNCE), 2026-11-08/09
incidents.seen: on testers' units BOUNCE recorded nothing, or recorded and never played back.
incidents.cause: unknown. The gate never ran the ColdFire and the DSP together. Per the v0.48 notes the recorder trigs fired and takes were made, but the track never played its buffer.
incidents.fix: BOUNCE removed from the menu in v0.47 and its code removed in v0.48 (old projects load, the track silent). v0.48 adds a coupled emulator that runs both processors one audio block at a time (faithful in order and content, not in timing margins) and the first gate step on it; FLEX, the replacement, is to be tested from recording to playback on it.

incidents.title: Uninitialised shared-window memory crashed DSP core 1 on a cold boot; the emulator starts it at zero
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKII, AERIA OS bring-up builds, 2026-11-11
incidents.seen: after a cold boot core 1 sent one report and crashed; a crashed core 1 then blocked a DSP reload over USB until a power cycle.
incidents.cause: core 1's slot table in the shared window held random values at power-on; the emulator zeroes that memory.
incidents.fix: core 1 clears its table before it starts.

incidents.title: MIDI hits on a software voice were silent on a Rytm; the emulator could not show it
incidents.unit: Analog Rytm MKII, OS 1.74 (BD ANALOG development builds), 2026-11-05
incidents.seen: 39 of 40 MIDI hits were silent.
incidents.cause: a MIDI trig sets the voice timer to a start tick of 0-15 or later, but the base took a hit only when it read 0; rytm-emu does not trigger track 1 from pads or MIDI, so only sequencer trigs had been tested.
incidents.cause_found_by: found on the unit, then from stock's code
incidents.fix: the voice waits for the scheduled tick, as stock BD CLASSIC does (`0x40110a06`).

incidents.title: A UI pointer the emulator filled stayed 0 on a Digitakt II
incidents.unit: Digitakt II, OS 1.17 (Modwerk's Track Names, first build, the author's unit), 2026-11-13
incidents.seen: the module loaded but never recognised the Internal Mixer, so no track names were drawn; in digikit's emulator it worked.
incidents.cause: the module found the mixer through the view controller's page-set pointer at `+0x9c`, which was non-zero in the emulator and 0 on the unit.
incidents.fix: 0.1.3 recognises the mixer from the frame the OS has just drawn; about 2 h on the unit with core 1.0.

incidents.title: The compiler merged two stores and broke a step move (trig-seedr, emulator)
incidents.unit: none (analog-emu), trig-seedr 0.4.0 for Analog Rytm MKII OS 1.74, 2026-11-15
incidents.seen: a moved step lost its note and velocity and corrupted the step before it.
incidents.cause: Homebrew m68k-elf-gcc 16.2 at -O2 miscompiled a struct copy followed by stores to its fields; with store merging one 4-byte store landed 6 bytes early.
incidents.cause_found_by: found in the emulator and the compiler output
incidents.fix: from 0.4.1 every ColdFire build (the mod, core-ar2, the device checks) uses `-fno-store-merging`. 0.4.0 had passed every emulator check, so the same fault may sit in code the checks do not reach.
incidents.status: fixed in 0.4.1; not run on a unit.

incidents.title: Two ColdFire instruction forms where GCC and ot_emu disagree (Octatrack, emulator)
incidents.unit: none (octabam's ot_emu), TELOS 0.1 for Octatrack OS 1.40C, 2026-11-14
incidents.seen: the boot linker misbehaved in the emulator until two code patterns were removed.
incidents.cause: for `move.b (a0)+,(0,a0,a1)` GCC assumes the destination uses the old a0 and ot_emu the new one; for a byte push to `-(sp)` GCC assumes SP moves by 1 and ot_emu by 2.
incidents.cause_found_by: found in the emulator and the compiler output
incidents.fix: `dl_memcpy` kept out of line and `-fno-ipa-sra`, so neither form is in the build.
incidents.status: avoided; which reading the ColdFire takes is not checked on a unit (H29).

incidents.title: A landing on the boundary tick was exact in the emulator and sometimes a step off on the unit
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKI, OS 1.40C (KYOTI with Clyps, CL25), 2026-11-12
incidents.seen: with DIRECT JUMP on, a loaded sequence now and then came in one step off and fell into phase at the next step.
incidents.cause: CL25 landed on the boundary tick and purged the old boundary event only if its fire time was at or after the sample clock; on the unit that clock runs in audio frames, so the comparison flipped by a frame and the old step stayed. Tick-level oracles in the emulator had passed.
incidents.cause_found_by: from the report and the code; the emulator's exact clock never shows it
incidents.fix: CL26 lands a tick before the boundary (ahead 2) and purges a full tick ahead (measured margin: one tick in every purge); RELOAD_FROM_PROJECT and DIRECT JUMP V7.1 took the same rule. CL29 "timing correct" on the unit.

incidents.title: Two lock lanes on one parameter lost one lane's locks (trig-seedr, emulator)
incidents.unit: none (analog-emu), trig-seedr 0.5 for Analog Rytm MKII OS 1.74, found 2026-11-16 by the host fuzzer and the emulator sample
incidents.seen: a recipe with lane 1 at 100 % on the sample slot and lane 2 left on the sample slot too: the emulated Rytm stored lane 2's value (the original locks) and lane 1's new locks were lost, with no error; the host reference showed a lock on every trig.
incidents.cause: the Rytm keeps one lock per parameter and step; the second write replaced the first.
incidents.fix: 0.6.0 refuses such a recipe (SETTING OUT OF RANGE, nothing written) and LOCK's PARM skips the other lane's parameter; host test `test_found_lanes`.
incidents.status: fixed before any unit ran it.

incidents.title: Idle CPU cost overstated five times: an instruction budget read as one second (trig-seedr, analog-emu)
incidents.unit: none (analog-emu), trig-seedr 0.4-0.5 for Analog Rytm MKII OS 1.74, found 2026-11-16 (status M2.3)
incidents.seen: the screen's idle cost was reported as 7.8 % and 9 % of the CPU and planned around.
incidents.cause: `dtboot --instr 1000M` at the default `--ips 200M` runs 5 emulated seconds; the count was divided by one second.
incidents.fix: measured again per emulated second: 1.9 %, then 0.25 % after redrawing only on change; F10's status file carries a correction.

incidents.title: A function without a return value passed the emulator by chance (trig-seedr 0.7.0)
incidents.unit: Analog Rytm MKII OS 1.74 in analog-emu, trig-seedr 0.7.0, found 2026-11-17
incidents.seen: no failure seen; a code review for the manual found that `take()` is declared `int` but falls off its end on success, and YOLO tests its result. A successful roll could be treated as failed and the old recipe put back, depending on a leftover register value. Every emulator test passed.
incidents.cause: undefined return value in C (m68k-elf-gcc gives no error by default); the register happened to hold a non-zero value in the emulator runs.
incidents.fix: `return 1;` added; the mod builds with `-Werror=return-type`.
incidents.status: fixed in 0.7.1 (0.7.1 passed on a unit, 2026-11-17).

incidents.title: Gearmulator's DSP56300 JIT misexecuted `cmpm` and X/Y half writes (gearmulator-md-mm)
incidents.unit: Machinedrum / Monomachine emulator (gearmulator-md-mm before mdmm-v0.1.0-alpha.15; the same JIT is upstream Gearmulator's), 2026-11-10 to 2026-11-17
incidents.seen: two wrong results inside one JIT block: after `cmpm a,b` or `cmpm b,a` the source accumulator held its magnitude, so later instructions in the block read |S1|; and after a write to x0/x1 (or y0/y1) followed by a read of the whole 48-bit x (or y) in the same block, the halves were never stored back, so the next block read a stale x.
incidents.cause: JIT code generation bugs (the interpreter was right; the `cmpm` fix came from upstream dsp56300).
incidents.fix: dsp56300 submodule moved to the fixed release branch; an interpreter-versus-JIT test for X/Y half writes was added.

incidents.title: Live-recorded beats went into pattern A01: every emulator test had run on A01 (Drum Mode 0.8/0.8.1)
incidents.unit: Digitone MKI, OS 1.44, Drum Mode 0.8 and 0.8.1 on elekloader, 2026-11-17/18
incidents.seen: the pads, notes, pages and mutes worked, but beats recorded live on a Drum Mode track never played back; in the emulator they did.
incidents.cause: the project holds one set of track edit objects per pattern (128 sets `0x38c` apart); 0.8 always wrote through A01's set, 0.8.1 through A01's or A02's, so on H02 the beats went into A01. Found with three debug builds that printed the playback path's view on the unit's screen, then by hooking the stock trig setter in digiemu on the same pattern.
incidents.fix: 0.8.2 uses the active pattern's own set (checked by its data pointer, all 128 searched otherwise); a test now records on H02.

incidents.title: A full digikit image hung a Syntakt at the logo: the bootstrap's unpack overran its stream
incidents.unit: Syntakt, OS 1.42, digikit full `device` set (runtime, menu, HEALTH, input, section 7 packer), 2026-11-19
incidents.seen: after the flash the unit restarted and stayed at the Elektron logo on every power cycle. The smaller `device-peer` image (the section 7 packer only) booted. Every emulator boot of the same image had passed.
incidents.cause: the Syntakt bootstrap stages packed MAIN at `0x40200000`, not at the `0x40400000` of the Digitakt II and Digitone II, and unpacks it in place with no bound. The full image's stream had an in-place margin of -42,486 bytes at that stage (stock +96,356), so the output overwrote unread stream bytes and the decoder ran away before MAIN started. The emulator installs MAIN directly and never runs that unpack; the device file had copied the Digitakt II stage value; the margin was checked only for the repacked section 7.
incidents.cause_found_by: read from the bootstrap, reproduced by running its own depacker on the emulator core
incidents.fix: the stage is per-device data read from section 2; patchkit writes the stream's last tokens as literals until the margin is at least 8 KiB and refuses an image below that in `verify`, `preflight` and `flash`, printing the margin. The repaired full image boots on the unit. Finding 159 (2026-11-23, static) adds that the 8 KiB floor is a safety default, not measured, and that the stored MAIN cannot go below unpacked MAIN - 2,096,128 B + floor whatever the packer does {digikit-1123}.
incidents.status: fixed (confirmed on the unit). How the hung unit was brought back is not stated; digikit's documented path is the startup menu (FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4, stock file over DIN).

incidents.title: Recovery stalled at ~80 %: the MIDI link, not the image
incidents.unit: Digitone II (dn2_firmware_explore), 2026-09-11

incidents.unit: Digitakt II, OS 1.16 (dt2-machine-lab), 2026-10-06

incidents.unit: Digitone II, OS 1.11 (armio)

incidents.title: Safe mode by REC at power-on, tested on a Digitakt II
incidents.unit: Digitakt II, OS 1.17 (digikit, branch image with loadable boot screens), 2026-11-08
incidents.seen: REC held from power-on gave digikit's safe mode (no modules loaded; the DIGIKIT menu showed "safe mode key held"). Without REC, the selected boot screen played about 1.8 s after the stock intro started, and the module setting survived power cycles.
incidents.cause: test. In the emulator, digikit's earlier queue scan missed the key (`safe:0`); reading the stock key state fixed it. On the unit, a key held at power-on does produce a report.

incidents.title: A loader base update over USB said Done but did not stick
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKII, OS 1.40C (Modwerk beta base, the author's unit), 2026-11-09

In the same trials the loader's diagnostic log once showed a "hot" record (CPU 98.9 %) with the transport stopped, not explained.

incidents.title: A Windows PC could not open the Octatrack's vendor interface
incidents.unit: Octatrack MKII with the Modwerk base and a Windows 11 PC, 2026-11-12/13, after member reports
incidents.seen: with `DeviceInterfaceGUIDs` missing from the interface's registry key the USB bridge could not open the unit; a replug did not help.
incidents.cause: Windows writes that value only at an interface's first setup; why it was missing on members' PCs is unknown.
incidents.fix: the base reports `bcdDevice` 0x0101, which made Windows write the value again.
incidents.status: fixed by hand on one PC; not confirmed on an affected member's PC.

incidents.title: A repacked stock image ran on an Analog Rytm MKI, and stock came back over USB and DIN
incidents.unit: Analog Rytm MKI, OS 1.74 (elekloader's new ELE2 writer), reported 2026-11-13

incidents.title: The first USB OS send to a Model:Samples stalls at 0-1 % (Modded-Cycles protocol flashers)
incidents.unit: Model:Samples, OS update over USB with model27's flasher and other flashers of the same protocol, a tester's report, 2026-11-18
incidents.seen: the first send stalls at 0-1 % with every such flasher; the second send always works.
incidents.cause: unknown; the guess is that the first reply after the MIDI ports are reopened is lost (macOS/Chrome), or that the unit answers slowly on its first start.
incidents.fix: model27 0.73 waits 2 s, reopens the ports, identifies the unit again and resends the whole file once (nothing is written before the user confirms on the unit).

incidents.title: A memory canary held with all 64 sample slots loaded, then trig-seedr passed its first checks (Syntakt)
incidents.unit: Syntakt, OS 1.42, trig-seedr 0.7.1-labelled build (same code as 0.8.0) on a minimal elekloader hook-bus core, one unit, 2026-11-19
incidents.seen: in order: the STARTUP menu (FUNC at power-on) with TRIG 4 = OS UPGRADE was checked on stock; the stock file round-tripped by elektron-firmware-tool (`-r`, byte-identical) flashed and booted as stock; a canary build kept a pattern over `0x478b0000-0x47bf0000` intact (OK and a growing pass count) through a session with all 64 sample slots loaded, project load and save and a power cycle; then trig-seedr passed its 15 first checks, including an applied and a pending take kept across a power off.
